summary: Target-level blueprint of Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (stages R01.1–R01.6 and G7). R01.1 builds the carrier: continuous representations of profinite groups on finite projective modules over topological coefficient rings, with jointly continuous action, framed coordinates, coefficient extension, restriction, duals, tensor products, twists, the Tate twist and continuous induction with the Mackey decomposition and the determinant of an induced representation; finite-coefficient factorisation, descent of residual and Q̄_ℓ-valued representations to finite coefficient fields, stable lattices by compactness, integral models, semisimplification, absolute irreducibility, the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem obtained from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1, lattice-independence of the residual semisimplification, Ribet's lattice lemma, self-dual lattices and the reductive (Ĝ-valued) integral-model theorem of Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne. R01.2 restricts to decomposition and inertia groups through chosen embeddings, defines unramified representations and Frobenius characteristic polynomials in the arithmetic normalisation, the unramified characters λ(α), cyclotomic and Dirichlet characters, the tame and fundamental characters of Serre, Grothendieck's quasi-unipotence, Weil–Deligne representations with Deligne's normalisation, the Weil–Deligne functor and its independence of choices, Frobenius semisimplification, local Euler and ε-factors and purity. R01.3 defines breaks, Swan and Artin conductors (mixed and equal characteristic), the conductor with its monodromy term, global and prime-to-p conductors, their additivity, induction and reduction behaviour, Artin–Schreier examples, the conductor of an elliptic curve with the Ogg–Saito formula and the local exponent bounds. R01.4 treats oddness, absolute irreducibility of odd irreducible residual representations for odd p, Dickson's classification with the coefficient field visible, Cartan subgroups, dihedral and bad-dihedral images, images under restriction and characteristic two. R01.5 proves density of Frobenius elements and recognition of semisimple representations by Frobenius characteristic polynomials after a common coefficient extension, coefficient descent with its Brauer obstruction, Haar-measure Chebotarev and recognition of lifts over local rings. R01.6 constructs ℓ-adic Tate modules of abelian varieties with torsion, isogeny, Weil-pairing, determinant, oddness, good-reduction Frobenius polynomial, endomorphism-coefficient and local Euler interfaces. G7 provides the dimension-general API: symmetric and exterior powers, tensor induction, restriction of scalars, adjoint representations with the p | n corrections, polarizations with actual pairings, multipliers and signs, oddness at real places, the group 𝒢_n and the GSp₄ branch, monodromy groups, adequacy, enormous image and the Taylor–Wiles image conditions with their verification lemmas.

nodes.title: Continuous representations on finite projective modules
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group (for a field F, Γ = G_F := Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F with its Krull topology) and A a commutative topological ring with continuous ring operations (IsTopologicalRing). A continuous representation (ContinuousRep Γ A M) is a pair (M, ρ) where M is a finitely generated projective A-module (Module.Finite A M, Module.Projective A M) carrying the module topology (IsModuleTopology A M) and ρ : Γ →* (M →ₗ[A] M) is a Mathlib Representation A Γ M, such that the action map Γ × M → M, (g, m) ↦ ρ(g)m, is continuous for the product topology (joint continuity). A morphism (M, ρ) → (N, σ) is an A-linear map f with f ∘ ρ(g) = σ(g) ∘ f for all g ∈ Γ; it is automatically continuous. Standard coefficient cases: (i) A = E a finite extension of Q_ℓ with its valuation topology (M a finite-dimensional E-vector space); (ii) A = k a finite field, or F̄_p = AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p), with the discrete topology; (iii) A a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field and the m_A-adic topology (M is then finite free, since finite projective modules over a local ring are free); (iv) A = Q̄_ℓ := PadicAlgCl ℓ with the topology of its absolute value; (v) A = ℂ with its usual topology (Artin representations). If M has constant rank r, the determinant det ρ : Γ → A^× is the character through which Γ acts on the rank-one projective module ⋀^r_A M (End_A(⋀^r_A M) = A); it is continuous, and for M free it equals LinearMap.det ∘ ρ. Every continuous representation defines a Mathlib ContRepresentation A Γ M (each ρ(g) is a continuous linear map); the converse fails, so ContRepresentation is a compatibility target, not the carrier.
hypotheses: Γ is profinite: compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group.
A is a commutative topological ring with continuous addition, multiplication and negation; Hausdorffness is not required for the definition but holds in all standard cases (i)–(v).
M is finitely generated projective over A and carries the module topology; the condition is JOINT continuity of Γ × M → M, which is strictly stronger than continuity of each operator ρ(g).
Frobenius, inertia and decomposition groups are not part of this definition; they are R01.2's.
proofSteps: Data: the underlying Representation A Γ M, the instances Module.Finite, Module.Projective, IsModuleTopology A M, and a proof that the uncurried action is continuous.

Compatibility with Mathlib's ContRepresentation: by mathlib:IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap every A-linear map M → M is continuous, so ρ(g) lifts to M →L[A] M and ContRepresentation.ofMonoidHom applies. The same lemma makes every morphism of representations continuous.

Matrix criterion: choose a surjection A^n → M with a section s (projectivity). Then M is a direct summand of A^n, the module topology of M is the subspace and the quotient topology (mathlib:IsModuleTopology.instPi, mathlib:IsModuleTopology.instQuot), and joint continuity of ρ is equivalent to continuity of g ↦ (matrix of e ∘ ρ(g) ∘ s) into M_n(A) ≅ A^{n²}: evaluation End × A^n → A^n is bilinear on a finite module, hence continuous (mathlib:IsModuleTopology.continuous_bilinear_of_finite_left), and conversely matrix coefficients are evaluations of the action at basis vectors followed by coordinate projections.

Determinant: ⋀^r_A M (mathlib:ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower) of a finite projective module of constant rank r is finite projective of rank one, so End_A(⋀^r M) = A and ⋀^r ρ(g) is multiplication by a unit det ρ(g). When M is free, this unit is LinearMap.det(ρ(g)) (mathlib:LinearMap.det, the Mathlib determinant, which is defined to be 1 when no finite basis exists and therefore must NOT be used for non-free projective M). Continuity: det is a polynomial in the matrix coefficients of ρ on a free cover, so det ρ is continuous.
Rank: over a local ring A (cases (i)–(iv)), M is free by mathlib:Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing (projective implies flat), and rank_A M = n is well defined.
acceptance: The ℓ-adic cyclotomic character χ_ℓ : G_F → Z_ℓ^× (char F ≠ ℓ; mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter, continuous by mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter.continuous) defines a rank-one ContinuousRep of G_F on Z_ℓ, whose determinant is χ_ℓ.

For Γ = Z_ℓ and A = Q_ℓ with the DISCRETE topology, the character a ↦ (1 + ℓ)^a gives a Mathlib ContRepresentation (every operator of a discrete module is continuous) that is not a ContinuousRep: its kernel {0} is not open, and with A discrete joint continuity forces an open kernel (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients).

nodes.title: Framed continuous representations Γ → GL_n(A)
nodes.statement: For Γ profinite, A a commutative topological ring and n ≥ 0, a framed continuous representation is a continuous group homomorphism ρ : Γ → GL_n(A) = Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) A, where GL_n(A) carries the units topology (the topology induced by g ↦ (g, g⁻¹) into M_n(A) × M_n(A), with M_n(A) ≅ A^{n²}). Because g ↦ ρ(g⁻¹) is continuous whenever g ↦ ρ(g) is, a homomorphism ρ is continuous into GL_n(A) iff its composite with GL_n(A) → M_n(A) is continuous. (a) ofFramed ρ := (A^n, ρ) is a ContinuousRep; (b) a ContinuousRep (M, ρ) with an A-basis b of M gives a framed representation frame_b ρ, and frame_{b'} ρ = P⁻¹ (frame_b ρ) P for the change-of-basis matrix P; (c) ofFramed ρ ≅ ofFramed ρ' as ContinuousReps iff ρ' = g ρ g⁻¹ for some g ∈ GL_n(A). Hence isomorphism classes of ContinuousReps on modules isomorphic to A^n are in bijection with GL_n(A)-conjugacy classes of framed representations Γ → GL_n(A). The bijection depends on A: GL_n(B)-conjugacy for B ⊃ A is coarser.
hypotheses: Γ profinite; A commutative topological ring; n ≥ 0.
GL_n(A) has the units topology; continuity into GL_n(A) is equivalent to continuity into M_n(A) for homomorphisms from a topological group.
Conjugacy is by GL_n(A), not by GL_n of a larger ring.
proofSteps: (a) is R01.1/continuous-representation's matrix criterion for M = A^n.
(b) Matrix coefficients with respect to b are continuous by the same criterion; change of basis conjugates by P = matrix of b' in b.
(c) An isomorphism A^n → A^n of representations is an invertible matrix g with g ρ(h) = ρ'(h) g; conversely such g is Γ-equivariant, hence an isomorphism (continuity is automatic).
Continuity of the inverse: ρ(h)⁻¹ = ρ(h⁻¹) and inversion on Γ is continuous, so continuity into M_n(A) implies continuity into GL_n(A) with the units topology.
acceptance: For Γ = Z_ℓ, ρ_1(a) = (1 a; 0 1) and ρ_2(a) = (1 ℓa; 0 1) are conjugate by diag(ℓ, 1) in GL_2(Q_ℓ) but not in GL_2(Z_ℓ): ρ_1 mod ℓ is nontrivial and ρ_2 mod ℓ is trivial.
n = 1: framed representations are exactly continuous characters Γ → A^×, and conjugation is trivial.

nodes.title: Extension of coefficients
nodes.statement: Let f : A → B be a continuous homomorphism of commutative topological rings and (M, ρ) a ContinuousRep of Γ over A. The base change M_B := B ⊗_A M with ρ_B(g) := id_B ⊗ ρ(g) is a ContinuousRep of Γ over B (finite projective over B, module topology over B), and m ↦ 1 ⊗ m is a continuous Γ-equivariant f-semilinear map. Properties: (a) base change along id is canonically isomorphic to the identity and (M_B)_C ≅ M_C for A → B → C, compatibly with morphisms; (b) det(ρ_B) = f ∘ det ρ; for M free, charpoly ρ_B(g) = Polynomial.map f (charpoly ρ(g)); (c) base change commutes with direct sums, tensor products, duals, Hom, restriction and induction (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist, R01.1/continuous-induction); (d) for an extension of coefficient fields E ⊂ E′ (finite over Q_ℓ, or finite fields k ⊂ k′), Hom_Γ(V, W) ⊗_E E′ ≅ Hom_Γ(V_{E′}, W_{E′}) and (V_{E′})^Γ = V^Γ ⊗_E E′; (e) Q̄_ℓ-coefficients: every ContinuousRep over a coefficient field E ⊂ Q̄_ℓ = PadicAlgCl ℓ extends to Q̄_ℓ, and every ContinuousRep over Q̄_ℓ is isomorphic to such an extension (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field), so the category over Q̄_ℓ is the 2-colimit of the categories over the coefficient fields E. Special cases: O_E → E (generic fibre) and O_E → k_E (reduction, R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification).
hypotheses: f is continuous; the construction fails for discontinuous ring maps.
In (d), E′/E is a field extension; invariants and Hom commute with field extension because they are kernels of finitely many linear maps on finite-dimensional spaces.
In (e), Q̄_ℓ carries the topology of its absolute value.
proofSteps: Module side: B ⊗_A M is finite projective over B (base change of a direct summand of A^n is a direct summand of B^n), with the module topology over B.
Continuity: on a free cover A^n, the matrix coefficients of ρ_B are f applied to those of ρ, continuous since f is continuous; apply the matrix criterion of R01.1/continuous-representation.
Determinant and characteristic polynomial: ⋀^r(B ⊗ M) = B ⊗ ⋀^r M, and Matrix.charpoly commutes with Polynomial.map of a ring homomorphism.

Invariants over fields: V^Γ = ∩_{g} ker(ρ(g) − 1) is cut out by finitely many g (finite dimension), and kernels of linear maps commute with the flat extension E → E′; Hom_Γ(V, W) = Hom(V, W)^Γ (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist).

Q̄_ℓ: every finite subset of Q̄_ℓ lies in a coefficient field; morphisms and isomorphisms over Q̄_ℓ between representations defined over E are defined over a finite extension of E by (d), and objects descend by R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field.
acceptance: Base change of Z_ℓ(1) along Z_ℓ → Q_ℓ is Q_ℓ(1), with the same character χ_ℓ.

For the rotation representation of Z/4 on Q² (through a quotient of Γ), base change to Q(i) splits into the two characters i ↦ ±i; irreducibility over Q is not preserved, absolute irreducibility is (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible).

nodes.title: Restriction, duals, tensor products, Hom and twists
nodes.statement: Let Γ, Γ′ be profinite groups and A a commutative topological ring. (a) Restriction: for a continuous homomorphism φ : Γ′ → Γ (inclusion of an open or closed subgroup; Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.mapOfAlgebra : G_L → G_K for a field extension L/K with compatible algebraic closures, e.g. a decomposition group G_{F_v} → G_F once an embedding is fixed), Res_φ(M, ρ) := (M, ρ ∘ φ) is a ContinuousRep of Γ′. (b) For ContinuousReps M, N of Γ over A: the direct sum M ⊕ N; the tensor product M ⊗_A N with g ↦ ρ_M(g) ⊗ ρ_N(g); the dual M^∨ := Hom_A(M, A) with g ↦ ρ_M(g⁻¹)^∨ (inverse transpose); the internal Hom Hom_A(M, N) with g·f := ρ_N(g) ∘ f ∘ ρ_M(g)⁻¹; and for a continuous character χ : Γ → A^× the twist M(χ) := M ⊗_A A(χ). Each is a ContinuousRep (finite projective, module topology, jointly continuous). (c) Canonical isomorphisms, all continuous and Γ-equivariant: Hom_A(M, N) ≅ M^∨ ⊗_A N; M ≅ M^∨∨; (M(χ))(ψ) ≅ M(χψ); M(1) ≅ M; Hom_A(M, N)^Γ = Hom_Γ(M, N); evaluation M^∨ ⊗ M → A and coevaluation are morphisms. (d) Determinants for M, N of constant ranks m, n: det(M ⊕ N) = det M · det N, det(M ⊗ N) = (det M)^n (det N)^m, det(M^∨) = (det M)⁻¹, det(M(χ)) = det M · χ^m; det is unchanged by restriction (det Res_φ M = det M ∘ φ). (e) All constructions commute with restriction along φ and with coefficient extension.
hypotheses: φ is a continuous group homomorphism of profinite groups.
χ is a continuous character with values in A^× (units topology).
The dual uses the inverse transpose, so that evaluation is Γ-invariant.
proofSteps: Algebraic structures are Mathlib's: mathlib:Representation.tprod, mathlib:Representation.dual, mathlib:Representation.linHom; restriction is ContRepresentation.restrict (mathlib:ContRepresentation.restrict) on the underlying operators.
Finite projectivity: tensor products, duals and Hom-modules of finite projective modules are finite projective; all carry the module topology.

Joint continuity by the matrix criterion of R01.1/continuous-representation: on free covers the matrix coefficients of ρ_M ⊗ ρ_N are products of matrix coefficients, those of the dual are matrix coefficients of ρ_M(g⁻¹) (continuous because inversion on Γ is continuous), and Hom = dual ⊗ N.
Canonical maps are A-linear, hence continuous (mathlib:IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap); equivariance is the usual computation.
Determinants: ⋀^{top} of sums, tensors and duals (locally on a free cover these are the classical identities for block-diagonal matrices, Kronecker products and inverse transposes).

For normed coefficient fields, Tau Ceti's tauceti:ContRepresentation.linHom with tauceti:ContRepresentation.continuous_linHom builds the Hom representation on V →L[𝕜] W when g ↦ π(g) is continuous in operator norm; for finite-dimensional V, W over a coefficient field this agrees with the construction here (operator-norm continuity of g ↦ ρ(g) is equivalent to joint continuity in finite dimension).
acceptance: det(M ⊗ M^∨) = 1 and det(M(χ)) = det(M)·χ^{rank M}; e.g. det(Z_ℓ² ⊗ Z_ℓ(1)) = χ_ℓ².
For F′/F finite inside F̄ and χ_ℓ the cyclotomic character, Res_{G_{F′}} Z_ℓ(1)_F = Z_ℓ(1)_{F′}.

nodes.title: The Tate module Z_ℓ(1) and Tate twists
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, F̄ := AlgebraicClosure F, ℓ a prime with ℓ ≠ char F, and χ_ℓ : G_F → Z_ℓ^× the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter F̄ ℓ composed with G_F → Aut(F̄)), characterised by σ(ζ) = ζ^{χ_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n} for every ζ ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}(F̄). Define Z_ℓ(1) := ofCharacter χ_ℓ, the rank-one ContinuousRep of G_F over Z_ℓ; it is canonically isomorphic to lim_n μ_{ℓ^n}(F̄) (transition maps ζ ↦ ζ^ℓ) with its Galois action, and Z_ℓ(1)/ℓ^n ≅ μ_{ℓ^n}(F̄) as G_F-modules. For n ∈ Z put Z_ℓ(n) := Z_ℓ(1)^{⊗n} for n ≥ 0 and Z_ℓ(n) := Z_ℓ(−n)^∨ for n < 0, so Z_ℓ(n) ≅ ofCharacter χ_ℓ^n; for a ContinuousRep M of G_F over a topological Z_ℓ-algebra A (continuous structure map), M(n) := M ⊗_{Z_ℓ} Z_ℓ(n) = M(χ_ℓ^n). Then M(m)(n) ≅ M(m + n), M(0) = M, M(n)^∨ ≅ M^∨(−n), det M(n) = det M · χ_ℓ^{n·rank M}, and for a finite extension F′/F, Res_{G_{F′}} Z_ℓ(1)_F = Z_ℓ(1)_{F′}. Conventions: the Hodge–Tate weight and the Frobenius value χ_ℓ(arithmetic Frob_v) = q_v (v ∤ ℓ) are recorded by R01.2 and PadicHodgeTheory; here only the module and its action.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char F. When char F = ℓ, Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter is the trivial character by definition and Z_ℓ(1) is not defined by this node.
F̄ is Mathlib's AlgebraicClosure F; μ_{ℓ^n}(F̄) lies in the separable closure since ℓ ≠ char F.
proofSteps: χ_ℓ and its continuity for the Krull topology: mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter, mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter.continuous (stated for Gal(L/K); apply with L = AlgebraicClosure F), and the characterising congruence mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter.spec.

Z_ℓ(1) := ofCharacter χ_ℓ (R01.1/continuous-representation). The comparison with lim μ_{ℓ^n}: choose a compatible system (ζ_{ℓ^n}) of primitive roots (ζ_{ℓ^{n+1}}^ℓ = ζ_{ℓ^n}); a ↦ (ζ_{ℓ^n}^{a mod ℓ^n})_n is a Z_ℓ-isomorphism Z_ℓ → lim μ_{ℓ^n} intertwining χ_ℓ with the Galois action by mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter.spec; reduction mod ℓ^n gives Z_ℓ(1)/ℓ^n ≅ μ_{ℓ^n} (Mathlib modularCyclotomicCharacter).
Twists and their identities: R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist with χ = χ_ℓ^n.
Restriction: χ_ℓ for F′ is the restriction of χ_ℓ for F along G_{F′} → G_F, since both are determined by the action on the same roots of unity in F̄.
acceptance: For F = Q and complex conjugation c ∈ G_Q, c acts on Z_ℓ(1) by −1 (c(ζ) = ζ⁻¹).
For F a finite field F_q (ℓ ∤ q), arithmetic Frobenius x ↦ x^q acts on Z_ℓ(1) by q, and Z_ℓ(1)/ℓ ≅ μ_ℓ is trivial iff q ≡ 1 mod ℓ.

nodes.title: Induction from open subgroups
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, H ≤ Γ an open subgroup (so of finite index m = [Γ : H]) and (U, σ) a ContinuousRep of H over A. Define Ind_H^Γ U := {f : Γ → U | f(hx) = σ(h) f(x) for all h ∈ H, x ∈ Γ} with (g·f)(x) := f(xg). Then: (a) Ind_H^Γ U is a ContinuousRep of Γ; for any right transversal g_1, …, g_m (Γ = ⊔ H g_i), f ↦ (f(g_i))_i is an A-linear isomorphism onto U^m, so Ind U is finite projective of rank m·rank U; a change of transversal changes the coordinates by a block-monomial matrix with blocks in σ(H), and the module Ind U itself involves no choice; (b) Frobenius reciprocity: Hom_Γ(M, Ind_H^Γ U) ≅ Hom_H(Res_H M, U) (f ↦ ev_1 ∘ f) and Hom_Γ(Ind_H^Γ U, M) ≅ Hom_H(U, Res_H M), naturally; (c) Shapiro on invariants: (Ind_H^Γ U)^Γ ≅ U^H, f ↦ f(1); (d) transitivity: for K ≤ H ≤ Γ open, Ind_H^Γ Ind_K^H W ≅ Ind_K^Γ W, f ↦ (x ↦ f(x)(1)); (e) projection formula Ind_H^Γ(Res_H M ⊗ U) ≅ M ⊗ Ind_H^Γ U; (f) Ind commutes with duals ((Ind U)^∨ ≅ Ind(U^∨)), direct sums and coefficient extension; (g) the underlying Representation is Mathlib's coinduced representation along H.subtype, isomorphic to Mathlib's Representation.ind (Rep.indCoindIso, finite index); with topologies it is Mathlib's ContRepresentation.coind along the inclusion (every equivariant f : Γ → U is continuous, since f(hg_i) = σ(h)f(g_i) on each open coset Hg_i). Galois case: for a finite separable extension L/F inside F̄, G_L ≤ G_F is open and Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} is defined.
hypotheses: H is OPEN in Γ; for closed subgroups of infinite index the induced module is not finitely generated and is not a ContinuousRep.
Left-module convention: f(hx) = σ(h)f(x), Γ acting by right translation.
proofSteps: Algebra: this is Mathlib's coinduction Representation.coind along H.subtype; Rep.indCoindIso (mathlib:Rep.indCoindIso) identifies it with Representation.ind (mathlib:Representation.ind) for finite index, and Mathlib's adjunctions mathlib:Rep.resCoindAdjunction and mathlib:Rep.indResAdjunction give (b) on underlying representations; morphisms are automatically continuous, so (b) holds for ContinuousReps.

Finiteness: Γ/H is finite (mathlib:Subgroup.quotient_finite_of_isOpen, applied to H, whose left and right coset spaces correspond by inversion), and evaluation at a right transversal is an isomorphism Ind U ≅ U^m.

Continuity: let N ⊆ H be an open normal subgroup of Γ (mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one). For g ∈ N, g_i g g_i⁻¹ ∈ N ⊆ H, so in the coordinates (f(g_i)) the element g acts block-diagonally by σ(g_i g g_i⁻¹), continuous in g; Γ is a finite union of cosets N x, on each of which g ↦ action is the composite of a fixed permutation matrix with this continuous family. Joint continuity follows from the matrix criterion of R01.1/continuous-representation.

With topologies, the underlying ContRepresentation is mathlib:ContRepresentation.coind along the inclusion H → Γ (functions in C(Γ, U) satisfying the equivariance); every equivariant f : Γ → U is continuous because f(hg_i) = σ(h)f(g_i) and the sets Hg_i are open.
(c) is (b) with M the trivial representation A; (d) and (e) are the standard explicit isomorphisms, checked on transversals; (f) by evaluation at a transversal and R01.1/coefficient-extension.
acceptance: Ind_H^Γ 1 is the permutation representation A[H\Γ]; for Γ = G_Q and H = G_K with K quadratic, Ind 1 ≅ 1 ⊕ ε_K with ε_K the quadratic character of K.
For H = Γ, Ind_Γ^Γ U ≅ U.

nodes.title: The Mackey decomposition
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, H ≤ Γ open, D ≤ Γ closed, and (U, σ) a ContinuousRep of H over A. The double coset space H\Γ/D is finite. For s ∈ Γ put D_s := D ∩ s⁻¹Hs, an open subgroup of D, and let U^s be the representation of s⁻¹Hs on U given by y ↦ σ(sys⁻¹). Then for any choice of representatives s of the double cosets HsD there is an isomorphism of ContinuousReps of D, Res^Γ_D Ind_H^Γ U ≅ ⊕_{HsD ∈ H\Γ/D} Ind_{D_s}^D (Res^{s⁻¹Hs}_{D_s} U^s), the summand for s being the functions supported on HsD, sent to d ↦ f(sd). Changing the representative s to hsd changes the summand by a canonical isomorphism, so the isomorphism class of the right side is independent of the choices. (With the left-translation model of induction the index set is D\Γ/H, via s ↦ s⁻¹.)
hypotheses: H open, D closed: D_s is then open in D and the summands are inductions from open subgroups.
The isomorphism is stated for a fixed choice of representatives.
proofSteps: H\Γ is finite (Γ compact, H open: mathlib:Subgroup.quotient_finite_of_isOpen after inversion), so H\Γ/D is a finite quotient of it; double cosets are Mathlib's mathlib:DoubleCoset.Quotient.
Ind_H^Γ U = ⊕_{HsD} (functions supported on HsD), each summand D-stable because D acts by right translation and HsD is a union of right H-cosets permuted by D.

For f supported on HsD, φ_s(f)(d) := f(sd) satisfies φ_s(f)(yd) = f(s y s⁻¹ · s d) = σ(sys⁻¹) φ_s(f)(d) for y ∈ D_s, so φ_s(f) ∈ Ind_{D_s}^D U^s; φ_s is D-equivariant and bijective (its inverse extends a function on D to HsD by f(hsd) := σ(h)φ(d), well defined because hsd = h′sd′ forces d′d⁻¹ ∈ D_s).

Continuity is automatic (A-linear maps between module-topology modules). The finite-group case is the Mackey isomorphism of Tau Ceti InductionRestriction Layer 3a (fixed representatives via Quotient.out); the profinite statement is proved by the same splitting along double cosets.
acceptance: D = Γ: one double coset, Res_Γ Ind_H^Γ U = Ind_H^Γ U.
D = H normal in Γ: Res_H Ind_H^Γ U ≅ ⊕_{s ∈ H\Γ} U^s, the sum of the Γ-conjugates of U (used for Clifford theory in R01.1/semisimplicity-under-restriction-and-induction).

nodes.title: The determinant of an induced representation
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, H ≤ Γ open of index m, and U a ContinuousRep of H over A, finite projective of constant rank r. Let sgn_{Γ/H} : Γ → {±1} ⊂ A^× be the sign of the permutation action of Γ on the finite set H\Γ (equivalently on Γ/H; the two permutation actions of g are conjugate up to g ↦ g⁻¹, so have the same sign), and Ver_{Γ→H} the transfer, so that det U ∘ Ver := MonoidHom.transfer (det U) : Γ → A^× (A^× is commutative). Then det(Ind_H^Γ U) = sgn_{Γ/H}^r · (det U ∘ Ver_{Γ→H}) as continuous characters of Γ. In particular det Ind_H^Γ 1 = sgn_{Γ/H}, and for U of rank r with det U = 1 one gets sgn_{Γ/H}^r.
hypotheses: H open in Γ (finite index).
U of constant rank r (e.g. free of rank r; over a local ring A always).
Sign of the permutation of H\Γ; transfer in Mathlib's normalisation (left transversals, diff of transversals).
proofSteps: Choose a transversal; by R01.1/continuous-induction, g acts on Ind U ≅ U^m by a block-monomial matrix: the block pattern is the permutation π_g of H\Γ and the nonzero blocks are σ(h_i(g)) with h_i(g) ∈ H determined by the transversal.

det of a block-monomial matrix with r × r blocks = sgn(π_g)^r · ∏_i det σ(h_i(g)); this holds over any commutative ring (permute block columns, Laplace), and for projective U locally on a free cover or on ⋀^{top}.

∏_i h_i(g) taken in H^ab is the transfer Ver(g): this is Mathlib's definition of MonoidHom.transfer through mathlib:MonoidHom.transfer (diff of left transversals), after matching right with left transversals by inversion.
Continuity is automatic from R01.1/continuous-representation; the sign is Mathlib's mathlib:Equiv.Perm.sign of the permutation action on the finite quotient.
This is Gallagher's theorem as stated in Deligne 1973, Proposition 1.2, there for representations over a field; the block-monomial computation gives it over any commutative ring.
acceptance: Γ = G_Q, H = G_K with K/Q quadratic, U = 1: det Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q} 1 = sgn_{G_Q/G_K} is the quadratic character with kernel G_K.

Γ = S_3 (as a finite quotient), H = A_3, U a faithful character ψ of order 3: Ver(τ) = τ² = 1 for a transposition τ and Ver(c) = c·τcτ⁻¹ = 1 for a 3-cycle c, so ψ ∘ Ver = 1 and det Ind ψ = sgn, the determinant of the 2-dimensional irreducible representation of S_3.

sources.locator: §1, Proposition 1.2 and the following display, Del-8 = printed p. 508 (read on the page image)

nodes.title: Discrete coefficients, open kernels and finite Galois quotients
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, A a commutative ring with the DISCRETE topology (a finite ring, a finite field k, or F̄_p), M a finite projective A-module (so M is discrete for its module topology) and ρ : Γ → Aut_A(M) a homomorphism. The following are equivalent: (i) (M, ρ) is a ContinuousRep; (ii) every stabiliser {g ∈ Γ : ρ(g)m = m}, m ∈ M, is open; (iii) ker ρ is open; (iv) ρ factors through Γ/N for an open normal subgroup N, i.e. through a finite quotient of Γ. If A is finite, ρ(Γ) is then finite. For Γ = G_F, F a field, (iv) is equivalent to: ρ factors through Gal(L/F) for a finite Galois extension L/F inside F̄ (L the fixed field of ker ρ). Complement (Artin representations): for A = ℂ with its usual topology (more generally any A such that GL_n(A) has a neighbourhood of 1 containing no nontrivial subgroup), every continuous ρ : Γ → GL_n(ℂ) has open kernel and finite image.
hypotheses: A discrete; M finite projective (finitely generated suffices for (ii) ⇒ (iii)).
Γ profinite; for (iv) with Galois groups, Γ = G_F with the Krull topology.
The Artin complement uses the no-small-subgroups property of GL_n(ℂ), not discreteness.
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii): the orbit map g ↦ ρ(g)m is continuous into the discrete M, so the stabiliser is open.
(ii) ⇒ (iii): tauceti:Representation.isOpen_ker_of_finite (the kernel is the intersection of the stabilisers of a finite generating family).

(iii) ⇒ (iv): an open subgroup of the profinite Γ contains an open normal subgroup (mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one), and Γ/N is finite (mathlib:Subgroup.quotient_finite_of_isOpen). (iv) ⇒ (i): Γ × M → M factors through the discrete finite Γ/N × M.

Galois form: an open subgroup of G_F contains the fixing subgroup of a finite-dimensional normal subextension E/F (tauceti:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.exists_finiteDimensional_normal_fixingSubgroup_le); the maximal separable subextension L of E is finite Galois over F and Gal(E/F) = Gal(L/F); the quotient is finite by tauceti:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.finite_quotient_of_isOpen.

Artin complement: let U = {g ∈ GL_n(ℂ) : ‖g − 1‖ < 1/2}; a subgroup inside U is trivial (if g ≠ 1 has ‖g − 1‖ < 1/2, some power g^k leaves U, by considering an eigenvalue λ ≠ 1 or a nontrivial unipotent part); ρ⁻¹(U) contains an open normal N, and ρ(N) is a subgroup inside U, hence trivial.
acceptance: The mod ℓ cyclotomic character G_Q → F_ℓ^× factors through Gal(Q(μ_ℓ)/Q).
Non-example of a discrete-coefficient hypothesis: for A = Z_ℓ with the ℓ-adic topology, χ_ℓ is continuous with infinite image and kernel G_{Q(μ_{ℓ^∞})}, which is closed but not open.

nodes.title: Descent of residual representations to a finite field
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, p a prime, F̄_p := AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p) with the discrete topology, n ≥ 1 and ρ : Γ → GL_n(F̄_p) a continuous homomorphism. Then ρ(Γ) is finite, and the subfield k ⊂ F̄_p generated over F_p by the matrix entries of the elements of ρ(Γ) is finite, with ρ(Γ) ⊂ GL_n(k). Equivalently, every ContinuousRep V of Γ over F̄_p of dimension n is isomorphic to V_k ⊗_k F̄_p for a ContinuousRep V_k over a finite subfield k; any finite subfield k′ ⊃ k also works, and V_{k′} ≅ V_k ⊗_k k′. For the smallest field over which V can be realised after conjugation (the field generated by the characteristic polynomial coefficients, Serre's trace-field statement), see ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/finite-field-realisability, which is not part of this node.
hypotheses: F̄_p carries the discrete topology; with any non-discrete topology the statement is not implied.
The field k here is generated by matrix entries in the given frame; it depends on the frame, the class of realisability fields does not.
proofSteps: By R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients, ker ρ is open, so ρ(Γ) ≅ Γ/ker ρ is finite.

The finitely many matrix entries are algebraic over F_p; the subfield they generate is finite-dimensional over F_p (mathlib:IntermediateField.adjoin.finiteDimensional, iterated), hence a finite field k, and ρ(Γ) ⊂ GL_n(k) because the entries lie in k.

Module form: choose a basis, apply the framed statement (R01.1/framed-representation), and use R01.1/coefficient-extension for k ⊂ k′ ⊂ F̄_p; continuity over k is automatic since k is discrete and the kernel is unchanged.
acceptance: A continuous ρ̄ : G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) has image isomorphic to a subgroup of GL_2(F_q) for a power q of p (Serre 1987, 1.1).
For ρ̄ = ω̄ ⊕ 1 with ω̄ the mod p cyclotomic character, k = F_p.

nodes.title: Baire descent of ℓ-adic representations to a coefficient field
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group (more generally a compact Hausdorff group), ℓ a prime, Q̄_ℓ := PadicAlgCl ℓ with the topology of its absolute value, and ρ : Γ → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ) a continuous homomorphism. Then there is a coefficient field E (a finite extension of Q_ℓ inside Q̄_ℓ) with ρ(Γ) ⊂ GL_n(E). Consequently every ContinuousRep V of Γ over Q̄_ℓ is isomorphic to V_E ⊗_E Q̄_ℓ for a ContinuousRep V_E over some coefficient field E, and E may be enlarged at will. For any finite extension K/Q_ℓ, a continuous Γ → GL_n(K̄) (K̄ = Q̄_ℓ) takes values in GL_n(K′) with K′/K finite (the form used by Calegari–Geraghty).
hypotheses: Q̄_ℓ with its absolute-value (not discrete) topology; it is not locally compact, and the argument uses compactness of ρ(Γ) instead.
Γ compact Hausdorff, so ρ(Γ) is a compact Hausdorff, hence Baire, space.
proofSteps: Countability: the coefficient fields E ⊂ Q̄_ℓ form a countable set. By Krasner's lemma (mathlib:IsKrasner.krasner) every finite E = Q_ℓ(α) equals Q_ℓ(β) for β algebraic over Q close enough to α (approximate the minimal polynomial of α by one with rational coefficients; roots move continuously), and the algebraic closure of Q in Q̄_ℓ is countable.
Each GL_n(E) ∩ ρ(Γ) is a closed subgroup of ρ(Γ): E is complete, hence closed in Q̄_ℓ.

ρ(Γ) is compact Hausdorff, so a Baire space (mathlib:BaireSpace; the instance BaireSpace.of_t2Space_locallyCompactSpace in Mathlib/Topology/Baire/LocallyCompactRegular.lean makes locally compact R₁ spaces Baire), and ρ(Γ) = ⋃_E (ρ(Γ) ∩ GL_n(E)) is a countable union of closed sets; by mathlib:nonempty_interior_of_iUnion_of_closed one of them has nonempty interior, so it is an open subgroup of ρ(Γ), hence of finite index (compactness).
The finitely many coset representatives have entries in a finite extension; the compositum E′ of E with it satisfies ρ(Γ) ⊂ GL_n(E′).
Module form: choose a basis and use R01.1/coefficient-extension and R01.1/framed-representation; continuity over E holds because the topology of E is the subspace topology from Q̄_ℓ.
acceptance: The λ-adic representation of a weight-k eigenform, constructed over K_λ, is already defined over a coefficient field; conversely a representation obtained over Q̄_ℓ by base change from E descends back to E.
For n = 1, Γ = Z_ℓ and u ∈ Z_ℓ^×, the character a ↦ u^a takes values in Q_ℓ (E = Q_ℓ); for u ∈ O_E^× with E/Q_ℓ ramified of degree e, the smallest coefficient field is Q_ℓ(u).

nodes.title: Compact subgroups stabilise lattices
nodes.statement: Let E be a nonarchimedean local field (IsNonarchimedeanLocalField; e.g. a coefficient field E/Q_ℓ) with valuation ring O_E and uniformiser ϖ, and V a finite-dimensional E-vector space with its module topology, n = dim V. An O_E-lattice in V is a finitely generated O_E-submodule Λ ⊂ V spanning V over E (equivalently, a free O_E-submodule of rank n spanning V). (a) Every lattice Λ is compact and open in V, and GL(Λ) := {g ∈ GL(V) : gΛ = Λ} ≅ GL_n(O_E) is a compact open subgroup of GL(V). (b) A subgroup K ⊂ GL(V) stabilises some lattice iff its closure is compact; precisely, if K̄ is compact and Λ is any lattice, the stabiliser of Λ in K̄ is open of finite index and Λ′ := Σ_{k ∈ K} kΛ = Σ_{i=1}^{s} k_iΛ (k_i coset representatives) is a K-stable lattice. (c) Hence if Γ is profinite and V is a ContinuousRep of Γ over E, then V has a Γ-stable O_E-lattice; with a basis of it, ρ is GL_n(E)-conjugate to a continuous Γ → GL_n(O_E). The hypothesis of compact closure cannot be dropped: n ↦ ℓ^n on Q_ℓ (Γ = Z, not compact) stabilises no lattice.
hypotheses: E nonarchimedean local field (locally compact, discretely valued); O_E compact.
Γ compact (profinite) and ρ continuous in (c).
Lattices are finitely generated and spanning; E itself is not a lattice.
proofSteps: (a) Λ ≅ O_E^n is compact since O_E is (mathlib:IsNonarchimedeanLocalField.isCompact_closedBall with radius 1), and open since it contains ϖ^k O_E^n-neighbourhoods; GL(Λ) = {g ∈ M_n(O_E) : det g ∈ O_E^×} in a basis of Λ is open (preimage of the open O_E^× under the continuous det) and compact (closed in M_n(O_E) × M_n(O_E) via g ↦ (g, g⁻¹)).

(b ⇐) K̄ ∩ GL(Λ) is an open subgroup of the compact group K̄, hence of finite index (mathlib:Subgroup.quotient_finite_of_isOpen); the translates kΛ, k ∈ K̄, are finitely many, so Λ′ = Σ k_iΛ is finitely generated, contains Λ (so spans), and is K-stable because K permutes the translates. (b ⇒) K ⊂ GL(Λ′), which is compact by (a).

(c) ρ(Γ) is compact as a continuous image of the compact Γ (R01.1/continuous-representation, framed form R01.1/framed-representation); apply (b). The restriction of ρ to the lattice is a ContinuousRep over O_E (see R01.1/integral-model).
acceptance: For V = Q_ℓ(1) (G_Q acting through χ_ℓ), every Z_ℓ-lattice ℓ^k Z_ℓ is stable.
For Γ = Z_ℓ acting on Q_ℓ² by a ↦ (1 a; 0 1), the lattices Z_ℓ e_1 ⊕ ℓ^k Z_ℓ e_2 (k ≥ 0) are stable and pairwise non-homothetic; a stable lattice exists but is not unique up to homothety.
For the Tate-curve local system with monodromy p^Z (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0), the image is not relatively compact and no global lattice exists.

nodes.title: Integral models: Γ-stable lattices
nodes.statement: Let E be a coefficient field (nonarchimedean local field) with O_E, ϖ, k_E = O_E/ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep of a profinite Γ over E of dimension n. An integral model of V is a Γ-stable O_E-lattice Λ ⊂ V (finitely generated, spanning, ρ(g)Λ = Λ for all g); then Λ is free of rank n, (Λ, ρ|_Λ) is a ContinuousRep of Γ over O_E (ϖ-adic topology = subspace topology), and Λ ⊗_{O_E} E ≅ V canonically. The set L(V)^Γ of integral models is nonempty (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices) and is stable under: homothety Λ ↦ cΛ (c ∈ E^×), sums and intersections, and saturation W ∩ Λ for a Γ-stable subspace W ⊂ V (an integral model of W, with Λ/(W ∩ Λ) torsion-free, an integral model of V/W). Any two lattices satisfy ϖ^aΛ ⊂ Λ′ ⊂ ϖ^{−a}Λ for some a ≥ 0. The dual lattice Λ^∨ := {λ ∈ V^∨ : λ(Λ) ⊂ O_E} is an integral model of V^∨. Homothety classes of integral models are the vertices of the Bruhat–Tits tree/building of GL(V) fixed by ρ(Γ) (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2's GL_n model); this identification is a comparison, not used for existence.
hypotheses: E a nonarchimedean local field; V finite-dimensional with the module topology; Γ profinite.
Integral models are not unique, even up to homothety (unless the residual representation is irreducible, R01.1/self-dual-lattice-for-absolutely-irreducible-residual).
proofSteps: Finitely generated torsion-free modules over the DVR O_E are free; spanning gives rank n.
Continuity over O_E: the module topology of Λ ≅ O_E^n is the ϖ-adic product topology, which is the subspace topology from V; joint continuity is inherited.

Closure properties: sums and intersections of finitely many lattices are lattices (finitely generated because O_E is Noetherian; spanning because each contains ϖ^a of the other); saturation W ∩ Λ is a lattice in W and Λ/(W ∩ Λ) embeds in V/W as a lattice.
Dual lattice: λ(gx) for λ ∈ Λ^∨ and x ∈ Λ is in O_E, so Λ^∨ is stable for the dual action (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist).
acceptance: For G_Q acting on Q_ℓ(1), the integral models are exactly ℓ^k Z_ℓ(1), one homothety class.
For Z_ℓ acting on Q_ℓ² unipotently by a ↦ (1 a; 0 1), Λ_k = Z_ℓ e_1 ⊕ ℓ^k Z_ℓ e_2 (k ≥ 0) are integral models in distinct homothety classes.

nodes.title: Semisimplification over a field
nodes.statement: Let k be a topological field (a coefficient field, a finite or algebraically closed field with the discrete topology, Q̄_ℓ) and V a ContinuousRep of a profinite Γ over k. Every Γ-stable subspace W ⊂ V, with the subspace topology (= its module topology, W being a direct summand of V as a k-vector space), is a ContinuousRep, and so is V/W. V has a composition series 0 = V_0 ⊂ V_1 ⊂ … ⊂ V_r = V of Γ-stable subspaces with irreducible quotients (Mathlib Representation.IsIrreducible). The semisimplification V^ss := ⊕_{i=1}^r V_i/V_{i−1} is a semisimple ContinuousRep (IsSemisimpleRepresentation) whose isomorphism class is independent of the composition series (Jordan–Hölder: the composition factors with multiplicities are well defined). Properties: V^ss ≅ V iff V is semisimple; (V^ss)^ss ≅ V^ss; for an exact sequence 0 → W → V → V/W → 0 of ContinuousReps, V^ss ≅ W^ss ⊕ (V/W)^ss; charpoly ρ_{V^ss}(g) = charpoly ρ_V(g) and det V^ss = det V; for a field extension k ⊂ k′, (V ⊗ k′)^ss ≅ (V^ss ⊗ k′)^ss, and if k is perfect then V^ss ⊗ k′ is already semisimple.
hypotheses: k a field; V finite-dimensional, so of finite length.
Isomorphism classes, not subspaces: V^ss is defined up to isomorphism, as a choice of composition series is made.
proofSteps: Subrepresentations and quotients are ContinuousReps: a Γ-stable subspace has a k-linear complement, so V ≅ W × W′ topologically (mathlib:IsModuleTopology.instProd), the action on W is the restriction of a jointly continuous action, and V/W carries the quotient = module topology (mathlib:IsModuleTopology.instQuot).

Composition series exist by finite dimension; the lattice of subrepresentations is modular, so Mathlib's JordanHolderLattice instance applies and mathlib:CompositionSeries.jordan_holder gives uniqueness of composition factors up to permutation and isomorphism (mathlib:Subrepresentation for the lattice, mathlib:Representation.IsIrreducible for the factors).
Semisimplicity of V^ss: a finite direct sum of irreducibles is semisimple (mathlib:Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation, mathlib:IsSemisimpleModule).
Characteristic polynomials: in a basis adapted to the composition series ρ(g) is block upper triangular with diagonal blocks the factors (mathlib:LinearMap.charpoly).

Field extension: a composition series of V gives a filtration of V ⊗ k′ whose subquotients are V_i/V_{i−1} ⊗ k′; refine. If k is perfect, each simple factor S has End_Γ(S) a division algebra whose centre is separable over k, so S ⊗ k′ is semisimple (separable algebras stay semisimple).
acceptance: For Γ = Z_p acting on F_p² through Z/p by a ↦ (1 a; 0 1), V^ss ≅ 1 ⊕ 1 while V is not semisimple.
For V irreducible, V^ss ≅ V.

nodes.title: Absolutely irreducible representations
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and V ≠ 0 a ContinuousRep of Γ over k (dim V = n). V is irreducible if its only Γ-stable subspaces are 0 and V (Representation.IsIrreducible), and absolutely irreducible if V ⊗_k k̄ is irreducible for an algebraic closure k̄. Equivalent conditions: (i) V absolutely irreducible; (ii) V ⊗_k k′ is irreducible for every field extension k′/k; (iii) the k-span of ρ(Γ) in End_k(V) is all of End_k(V) (Burnside); (iv) V is irreducible and End_Γ(V) = k (for V irreducible over a finite field this holds iff V ⊗ k′ is irreducible for all finite k′). Invariance: for a field extension k ⊂ k′, V is absolutely irreducible iff V ⊗_k k′ is, and the notion does not depend on the choice of k̄. For a representation over F̄_p descended to a finite field k (R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field), absolute irreducibility of V_k, of V_{k′} (k′ ⊃ k finite) and of V are equivalent.
hypotheses: k any field; the topology plays no role (Γ-stable subspaces are closed).
V ≠ 0 (the zero representation is not irreducible).
proofSteps: (iii) is invariant under field extension: span_{k′}(ρ(Γ)) = k′ ⊗_k span_k(ρ(Γ)) in End_{k′}(V ⊗ k′) = k′ ⊗ End_k(V), so dimensions agree; hence (i) ⇔ (ii) ⇔ (iii) once (iii) ⇔ irreducibility over an algebraically closed field is known.

Over k̄ algebraically closed: V irreducible ⇒ End_Γ(V) = k̄ (Schur) and V is a simple module over the image algebra R, which is then a simple Artinian algebra with simple module V and commutant k̄; by Mathlib's mathlib:jacobson_density (or Wedderburn–Artin over algebraically closed fields, mathlib:IsSemisimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_of_isAlgClosed) R = End(V). Conversely R = End(V) has no proper nonzero invariant subspaces.

(iv): End_Γ(V) ⊗ k̄ = End_Γ(V ⊗ k̄) (R01.1/coefficient-extension); if V ⊗ k̄ is irreducible this is k̄, so End_Γ(V) = k; the converse uses that the image algebra is central simple with commutant k, hence End_k(V) by double centraliser, for V irreducible over a perfect field (finite fields).
Independence of k̄: any two algebraic closures are isomorphic over k, and the span criterion (iii) is intrinsic.
acceptance: Every one-dimensional V is absolutely irreducible.
Γ = Ẑ acting on Q² through Z/4 by rotation (0 −1; 1 0): irreducible over Q, splits over Q(i) into the characters with values ±i, so not absolutely irreducible.

nodes.title: The Brauer–Nesbitt theorem
nodes.statement: Let k be any field, Γ any group (no topology needed), and V, W finite-dimensional representations of Γ over k. (a) If charpoly ρ_V(g) = charpoly ρ_W(g) in k[X] for every g ∈ Γ, then V^ss ≅ W^ss; in particular semisimple V and W with the same characteristic polynomials are isomorphic. (b) If char k = 0 or char k > dim V, equality of traces tr ρ_V(g) = tr ρ_W(g) for all g ∈ Γ (with dim V = dim W) suffices. (c) If V and W are ContinuousReps, the isomorphisms in (a), (b) are isomorphisms of ContinuousReps. In characteristic p ≤ dim V, traces do not suffice.
hypotheses: k arbitrary (finite residue fields are the main case); Γ arbitrary group or monoid.
Characteristic polynomials of the group elements g ∈ Γ, not merely of elements of a generating set.
(b) needs dim! invertible in k.
proofSteps: Step 1 (determinants): the determinant laws det ∘ ρ_V and det ∘ ρ_W on k[Γ] (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation) have the same characteristic-polynomial coefficients Λ_i(g) for g ∈ Γ; by Amitsur's formula (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/amitsur-formula) Λ_i of any k-linear combination of group elements is a polynomial in Λ_j of words in those elements, which are again elements of Γ, so the two determinants coincide.

Step 2 (algebraic closure): extend scalars to k̄ (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-base-change, R01.1/coefficient-extension). The determinants of (V ⊗ k̄)^ss and (W ⊗ k̄)^ss equal those of V ⊗ k̄ and W ⊗ k̄ (R01.1/semisimplification), hence coincide.

Step 3 (reconstruction over k̄, RT-AREA-langlands-1/17): by the uniqueness half of the reconstruction theorem over algebraically closed fields (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1, Chenevier Theorem 2.12: a d-dimensional determinant on k̄[Γ] is det ∘ ρ for a semisimple ρ, unique up to isomorphism), (V ⊗ k̄)^ss ≅ (W ⊗ k̄)^ss. IHG.1 must prove this uniqueness directly (e.g. evaluating the characteristic polynomial on elements of k̄[Γ] mapping to a rank-one idempotent of one matrix factor of the image algebra), since Chenevier's own proof quotes Brauer–Nesbitt.

Step 4 (descent from k̄ to k): write V^ss = ⊕ S_i^{m_i} and W^ss = ⊕ S_i^{n_i} over pairwise non-isomorphic simple k[Γ]-modules S_i. The image of k[Γ] in ∏_i End_k(S_i) is ∏_i of simple algebras (Jacobson density, mathlib:jacobson_density, and Wedderburn–Artin), so it contains central idempotents e_i acting as 1 on S_i and 0 on S_j (j ≠ i). Then e_i acts as 1 on every composition factor of S_i ⊗ k̄ and as 0 on every factor of S_j ⊗ k̄, so the (nonempty) sets of composition factors of the S_i ⊗ k̄ are pairwise disjoint; comparing multiplicities in (V ⊗ k̄)^ss ≅ (W ⊗ k̄)^ss gives m_i = n_i. This works for every field; for perfect k (finite fields) one may instead use that S_i ⊗ k̄ is semisimple together with Noether–Deuring descent.

(b): when d! is invertible a determinant is determined by its trace (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-trace-injective; equivalently Newton's identities recover the characteristic polynomial from tr ρ(g^j), j ≤ d), so (b) reduces to (a).
(c): an A-linear isomorphism between ContinuousReps is continuous with continuous inverse (R01.1/continuous-representation).
acceptance: Over F_p (p ≥ 3), with Γ = Z/(p−1) and χ a faithful character to F_p^×, V = 1^{⊕p} and W = χ^{⊕p} have equal traces (both identically 0 in F_p) but are non-isomorphic semisimple representations; their characteristic polynomials (X − 1)^p and (X − χ(g))^p differ, as (a) requires.
For Γ = Z_p acting on F_p² unipotently, V and 1 ⊕ 1 have equal characteristic polynomials, V^ss ≅ 1 ⊕ 1, but V ≇ 1 ⊕ 1: semisimplicity is needed for the isomorphism of V itself.

nodes.title: Reduction of an integral model and the residual semisimplification
nodes.statement: (a) General reduction: for a ContinuousRep (M, ρ) of Γ over a topological local ring A whose maximal ideal m_A is open (k_A := A/m_A discrete), M ⊗_A k_A is a ContinuousRep over k_A with charpoly ρ̄(g) = charpoly ρ(g) mod m_A and det ρ̄ = det ρ mod m_A. (b) For a coefficient field E (O_E, ϖ, k_E) and an integral model Λ of a ContinuousRep V over E (R01.1/integral-model), the reduction is ρ̄_Λ := Λ/ϖΛ = Λ ⊗_{O_E} k_E, a ContinuousRep of Γ over the finite field k_E with finite image; in a basis of Λ, ρ̄_Λ = ρ mod ϖ : Γ → GL_n(k_E). Its semisimplification ρ̄_Λ^ss is the residual semisimplification attached to Λ. (c) Over Q̄_ℓ: for V over Q̄_ℓ, choose E with V ≅ V_E ⊗ Q̄_ℓ (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field) and an integral model Λ of V_E, and put ρ̄ := (ρ̄_Λ ⊗_{k_E} F̄_ℓ)^ss, a semisimple ContinuousRep over F̄_ℓ (discrete), F̄_ℓ the residue field of Q̄_ℓ. Compatibilities: reduction commutes with coefficient extension E ⊂ E′ (Λ ⊗ O_{E′} reduces to ρ̄_Λ ⊗ k_{E′}), with direct sums, tensor products, duals (Λ^∨/ϖΛ^∨ ≅ (Λ/ϖΛ)^∨), twists and restriction. The reduction ρ̄_Λ itself depends on Λ; its semisimplification does not (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence).
hypotheses: m_A open in A, so the residue field is discrete and the reduction has open kernel.
E a nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field k_E.
Q̄_ℓ case: the residue field of the valuation ring of Q̄_ℓ is an algebraic closure F̄_ℓ of F_ℓ.
proofSteps: (a) M ⊗_A k_A is finite projective (free) over k_A; joint continuity holds because ϖ- or m_A-adic neighbourhoods are open, so the action on M/m_A M factors through an open subgroup (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients). Characteristic polynomials and determinants commute with the ring homomorphism A → k_A (R01.1/coefficient-extension).
(b) is (a) for A = O_E and M = Λ; finiteness of the image from R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients since k_E is finite.
(c) uses R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field for E, R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices for Λ, and R01.1/semisimplification over F̄_ℓ.
Compatibilities with operations: (Λ ⊗ Λ′)/ϖ = Λ/ϖ ⊗ Λ′/ϖ, Hom_{O_E}(Λ, O_E)/ϖ = Hom_{k_E}(Λ/ϖ, k_E) since Λ is free; restriction and twists are evident.
acceptance: Reduction of Z_ℓ(1) is μ_ℓ(F̄) with the mod ℓ cyclotomic character ω̄ = χ_ℓ mod ℓ.
For Z_ℓ acting on Q_ℓ² by (1 a; 0 1), Λ_0 = Z_ℓ² reduces to the nontrivial (1 ā; 0 1) and Λ_1 = Z_ℓ e_1 ⊕ ℓZ_ℓ e_2 to the trivial representation; both have semisimplification 1 ⊕ 1.

nodes.title: Lattice independence of the residual semisimplification
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field (O_E, ϖ, k_E) and V a ContinuousRep of Γ over E of dimension n. (a) V has an integral model. (b) For any two integral models Λ, Λ′ of V, (Λ/ϖΛ)^ss ≅ (Λ′/ϖΛ′)^ss as ContinuousReps of Γ over k_E; the reductions themselves may be non-isomorphic. (c) For coefficient fields E ⊂ E′ and Λ an integral model of V, Λ ⊗ O_{E′} is an integral model of V ⊗ E′ with reduction (Λ/ϖΛ) ⊗_{k_E} k_{E′}; hence for V over Q̄_ℓ the residual representation ρ̄ := ((Λ/ϖ_EΛ) ⊗ F̄_ℓ)^ss (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification) is independent of E and Λ up to isomorphism. (d) ρ̄ is a continuous semisimple representation with finite image, defined over a finite field, and charpoly ρ̄(g) is the reduction of charpoly ρ(g) for every g; ρ̄ depends only on these characteristic polynomials. Isomorphic V give isomorphic ρ̄.
hypotheses: Γ compact (profinite) — this is what gives integral models.
Independence holds only after semisimplification.
F̄_ℓ carries the discrete topology.
proofSteps: (a) R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices.

(b) Choose a basis of V; charpoly ρ(g) ∈ E[X] does not depend on the lattice, and in a basis of an integral model it has coefficients in O_E, so charpoly ρ̄_Λ(g) = charpoly ρ(g) mod ϖ = charpoly ρ̄_{Λ′}(g) (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification). Apply the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem over k_E (R01.1/brauer-nesbitt) to the semisimplifications.

Alternative argument avoiding Brauer–Nesbitt (recorded as a check): after homothety ϖΛ ⊂ Λ′ ⊂ Λ for adjacent lattices, [Λ/ϖΛ] = [Λ/Λ′] + [Λ′/ϖΛ] and [Λ′/ϖΛ′] = [Λ′/ϖΛ] + [ϖΛ/ϖΛ′] in the Grothendieck group of finite-length k_E[Γ]-modules, with ϖΛ/ϖΛ′ ≅ Λ/Λ′; a chain of adjacent stable lattices (Λ_i = Λ′ + ϖ^iΛ) connects any two. This gives the same conclusion by Jordan–Hölder.

(c) R01.1/coefficient-extension and R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification; the semisimplification over F̄_ℓ of a representation already semisimple over the perfect field k_E is the base change (R01.1/semisimplification).

(d) Finite image and descent: R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients and R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field; dependence on characteristic polynomials only: R01.1/brauer-nesbitt over F̄_ℓ.

nodes.title: Twisting coefficients by field automorphisms; the residual coefficient Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative topological ring, σ a continuous ring automorphism of A, and (M, ρ) a ContinuousRep of Γ over A. The coefficient twist is ρ^σ := baseChange σ M (R01.1/coefficient-extension); in framed form ρ^σ(g) = σ(ρ(g)) entrywise. It satisfies ρ^{id} = ρ, (ρ^τ)^σ ≅ ρ^{στ}, charpoly ρ^σ(g) = σ(charpoly ρ(g)), det ρ^σ = σ ∘ det ρ, and commutes with ⊕, ⊗, duals, twists and restriction. (a) Residual coefficient Frobenius: for A = F̄_p or a finite field k (discrete) and σ = Frob_p : x ↦ x^p (Mathlib frobeniusEquiv), ρ̄^{(p)} := ρ̄^{Frob_p}; for k = F_p it is ρ̄ itself. (b) Galois conjugation of ℓ-adic coefficients: for γ ∈ G_{Q_ℓ} = Gal(Q̄_ℓ/Q_ℓ) (continuous on Q̄_ℓ) and V over Q̄_ℓ, V^γ is a ContinuousRep; if V = V_E ⊗ Q̄_ℓ with integral model Λ then γ(Λ) is an integral model of V^γ over O_{γE}, and the residual representations satisfy ρ̄(V^γ) ≅ ρ̄(V)^{γ̄}, where γ̄ ∈ Gal(F̄_ℓ/F_ℓ) is the image of γ. Consequently: (i) if γ lies in the inertia subgroup I_{Q_ℓ} (γ̄ = 1), then ρ̄(V^γ) ≅ ρ̄(V); (ii) if γ is a lift of arithmetic Frobenius (γ̄ = Frob_ℓ), then ρ̄(V^γ) ≅ ρ̄(V)^{(ℓ)}, independently of the chosen lift. This twists the coefficients; it is not restriction of the Galois representation along a Frobenius element of the base field.
hypotheses: σ continuous (automatic for automorphisms of a discrete field and for G_{Q_ℓ} acting on Q̄_ℓ).
In (b), the surjection G_{Q_ℓ} → Gal(F̄_ℓ/F_ℓ), its kernel I_{Q_ℓ} and arithmetic Frobenius lifts are those of Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2 and 4.
Arbitrary Frobenius lifts are NOT inertia: (i) and (ii) differ unless ρ̄ is defined over F_ℓ.
proofSteps: Twist = base change along σ: R01.1/coefficient-extension, with the functoriality isomorphisms there; charpoly and det by the same compatibilities.
(a) mathlib:frobeniusEquiv gives the automorphism x ↦ x^p of the perfect field F̄_p (or k); it fixes F_p pointwise.

(b) γ is an isometry of Q̄_ℓ, so it maps O_E to O_{γE} and the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal, inducing γ̄ on residue fields; γ(Λ) is stable under ρ^γ(Γ) and (γΛ)/ϖ(γΛ) ≅ (Λ/ϖΛ)^{γ̄}. The action of G_{Q_ℓ} on the residue field and its kernel come from Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2 and 4 (stage prerequisites, with requests).

(i) γ̄ = 1 gives the claim after semisimplification (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence); (ii) two Frobenius lifts differ by inertia, so their residual twists agree, both being Frob_ℓ-twists.
acceptance: For a character χ̄ : Γ → F_{p²}^× of order p² − 1, χ̄^{(p)} = χ̄^p ≠ χ̄; for χ̄ with values in F_p^×, χ̄^{(p)} = χ̄.
Newton–Thorne (1.1): Sym^{p+r−1} r̄ ≅^{ss} ((det r̄)^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1} r̄) ⊕ (r̄^{(p)} ⊗ Sym^{r−1} r̄), where the second summand uses the residual coefficient Frobenius of this node.

nodes.title: Teichmüller lifts of residual characters
nodes.statement: Let E be a nonarchimedean local field (a coefficient field) with residue field k_E of cardinality q, and teichmuller E : k_E^× →* O_E^× the Teichmüller lift (Tau Ceti), the unique multiplicative section of reduction with values in μ_{q−1}(O_E). For a continuous character ψ̄ : Γ → k_E^× (k_E discrete), its Teichmüller lift is [ψ̄] := teichmuller E ∘ ψ̄ : Γ → O_E^×. Then [ψ̄] is a continuous character of finite order equal to the order of ψ̄ (dividing q − 1), [ψ̄] mod ϖ = ψ̄, and [ψ̄] is the unique lift of ψ̄ with values in μ_{q−1}(O_E) (equivalently, of finite order prime to p); [ψ̄φ̄] = [ψ̄][φ̄], [ψ̄⁻¹] = [ψ̄]⁻¹, [1] = 1; for E ⊂ E′ the Teichmüller lift over E′ restricts to the one over E on k_E^×, so [ψ̄] is independent of the coefficient field. For ψ̄ : Γ → F̄_ℓ^× (discrete), [ψ̄] is defined through any finite subfield containing the image (R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field), with values in Q̄_ℓ^×. Example: ω := [ω̄] for the mod p cyclotomic character ω̄ = χ_p mod p, and for p odd χ_p = ω · ⟨χ_p⟩ with ⟨χ_p⟩ := χ_p ω⁻¹ valued in 1 + pZ_p.
hypotheses: E nonarchimedean local field; k_E finite of cardinality q.
ψ̄ continuous for the discrete topology on k_E^× (open kernel).
proofSteps: Definition and section property: tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller with tauceti:TauCeti.residue_teichmuller; values in μ_{q−1}: tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller_pow.
Continuity: ψ̄ has open kernel (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients), and ker[ψ̄] = ker ψ̄ because teichmuller E is injective (tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller_injective).
Uniqueness among (q−1)-torsion lifts: tauceti:TauCeti.eq_teichmuller applied pointwise (a lift χ with χ^{q−1} = 1 and χ mod ϖ = ψ̄).

Compatibility with E ⊂ E′: the Teichmüller lift over E′ of α ∈ k_E^× is a (q′−1)-torsion lift of α; since α^{q−1} = 1 and reduction is injective on prime-to-p roots of unity, it equals the E-lift (uniqueness again).
As a ContinuousRep: ofCharacter [ψ̄] (R01.1/continuous-representation); its reduction is ofCharacter ψ̄ (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification).
acceptance: The Teichmüller lift of the mod p cyclotomic character of G_Q is the finite-order character ω : G_Q → Z_p^× through Gal(Q(μ_p)/Q) with ω ≡ χ_p mod p.
The Teichmüller lift of the trivial character is trivial.

nodes.title: Ribet's lemma: a lattice with nonsplit reduction
nodes.statement: Let E be a coefficient field (Ribet: K finite over Q_p) with O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue field k, Γ a group, and V a two-dimensional E-representation of Γ that is irreducible over E and leaves some lattice stable (e.g. Γ profinite and V a ContinuousRep). Suppose the reductions of V are reducible over k, so their semisimplifications are φ_1 ⊕ φ_2 for characters φ_1, φ_2 : Γ → k^× (independent of the lattice by R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence). Then there is a Γ-stable lattice L ⊂ V whose reduction is of the form (φ_1 *; 0 φ_2) and is not semisimple, i.e. a nonsplit extension 0 → φ_1 → L/ϖL → φ_2 → 0. By symmetry there is also a stable lattice with nonsplit reduction (φ_2 *; 0 φ_1).
hypotheses: dim V = 2 and V irreducible over E; the conclusion is false for V = ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 reducible.
The reductions are reducible over the residue field k itself (otherwise first extend E by an unramified extension).
Completeness of O_E is used (the limit lattice).
proofSteps: Choose a stable lattice and an O_E-basis, so ρ : Γ → GL_2(O_E) (R01.1/integral-model, R01.1/framed-representation); after conjugating by (0 1; 1 0) and by P = diag(1, ϖ) as needed, the reduction has the form (φ_1 *; 0 φ_2) (Ribet: if it is (φ_1 0; * φ_2), divide upper-right entries by ϖ and multiply lower-left ones using P(a ϖb; c d)P⁻¹ = (a b; ϖc d)).

Suppose, for contradiction, that every lattice whose reduction is of the form (φ_1 *; 0 φ_2) has semisimple reduction. Ribet constructs inductively M_i = (1 t_i; 0 1) such that M_iρ(Γ)M_i⁻¹ has lower-left entries divisible by ϖ and upper-right entries divisible by ϖ^i: conjugating by P^i reduces to the hypothesis, the diagonalising matrix U = (1 u; 0 1) of the semisimple reduction gives t_{i+1} = t_i + ϖ^i u.
t_i converges in O_E (completeness), and M = (1 t; 0 1) with t = lim t_i makes all upper-right entries of Mρ(Γ)M⁻¹ zero, so ρ is reducible over E — a contradiction.
The second assertion follows by exchanging the roles of φ_1 and φ_2 (conjugating by (0 1; 1 0)).
acceptance: For V = ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 a sum of two characters of Γ = Z_ℓ with distinct reductions, every stable lattice is ϖ^aO e_1 ⊕ ϖ^bO e_2 and every reduction is split: irreducibility is necessary.

Ribet's application: for p | B_k, the p-adic representation attached to a cusp form congruent to an Eisenstein series has reducible reductions with characters 1 and χ^{k−1}, and Proposition 2.1 produces ρ̄ = (1 *; 0 χ^{k−1}) nonsplit (Ribet 1976, Theorem 1.3).

nodes.title: Self-dual integral models when the residual representation is irreducible
nodes.statement: Let E be a coefficient field (O_E, ϖ, k_E), Γ profinite, V a ContinuousRep of Γ over E of dimension n, and suppose the residual representation (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence) is irreducible over k_E (in particular if it is absolutely irreducible). (a) The integral models of V are exactly the homothety class {ϖ^kΛ_0 : k ∈ Z} of one of them. (b) Let ⟨ , ⟩ : V × V → E be a perfect pairing, symmetric or alternating, with ⟨ρ(g)x, ρ(g)y⟩ = µ(g)⟨x, y⟩ for a continuous character µ : Γ → E^×. Then µ takes values in O_E^×, and there are an integral model Λ and c ∈ {1, ϖ} such that c⟨ , ⟩ restricts to a perfect O_E-valued pairing on Λ (if the dual lattice is Λ^⊥ = ϖ^{2j}Λ one may take c = 1 after replacing Λ by ϖ^jΛ). (c) In the alternating case (n = 2g), Λ has a symplectic O_E-basis for c⟨ , ⟩, so ρ is GSp_{2g}(E)-conjugate to a continuous representation Γ → GSp_{2g}(O_E) with multiplier µ. This supplies the integral GSp_4(O_{K′}) models used by Calegari–Geraghty.
hypotheses: Residual irreducibility over k_E (absolute irreducibility is the hypothesis in Calegari–Geraghty and implies it).
⟨ , ⟩ perfect over E and Γ-equivariant up to the continuous similitude character µ.
Γ compact, so µ(Γ) is a compact subgroup of E^×.
proofSteps: (a) Given integral models Λ, Λ′, rescale Λ′ so that Λ′ ⊂ Λ and Λ′ ⊄ ϖΛ. The image of Λ′ in Λ/ϖΛ is a nonzero Γ-stable subspace, hence everything by residual irreducibility; so Λ′ + ϖΛ = Λ and Λ′ = Λ by Nakayama (R01.1/integral-model).

(b) µ(Γ) is compact in E^×, hence contained in O_E^× (its valuation is a compact subgroup of Z). For an integral model Λ, the orthogonal Λ^⊥ := {x ∈ V : ⟨x, Λ⟩ ⊂ O_E} is an integral model (the dual lattice transported along the perfect pairing; Γ-stable because µ is unit-valued), so Λ^⊥ = ϖ^mΛ by (a). Replacing Λ by ϖ^jΛ changes m by −2j; if m is odd replace ⟨ , ⟩ by ϖ⟨ , ⟩. Then Λ^⊥ = Λ, i.e. the pairing is perfect on Λ.

(c) A perfect alternating form on a free module over the local ring O_E has a symplectic basis: choose x with ⟨x, y⟩ ∈ O_E^× for some y (perfectness), split off the hyperbolic plane O_E x ⊕ O_E y and induct on the orthogonal complement; the matrix of ρ(g) in this basis lies in GSp_{2g}(O_E) with multiplier µ(g).
This fills the step used without proof by Calegari–Geraghty on p. 843 (recorded as ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E101).
acceptance: If ρ̄ is irreducible, V = Q_ℓ² with the action of a group with image GL_2(Z_ℓ) has the single homothety class of Z_ℓ²; the standard alternating form is perfect on Z_ℓ² with µ = det.
Without residual irreducibility (a) fails: Z_ℓ acting by (1 a; 0 1) has non-homothetic integral models (R01.1/integral-model).

nodes.title: Semisimplicity under restriction and induction
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H ≤ Γ open with normal core N := ∩_{g ∈ Γ} gHg⁻¹ (an open normal subgroup of Γ), V a ContinuousRep of Γ over k and U a ContinuousRep of H over k. (a) Clifford (any characteristic): if H is normal in Γ and V is semisimple, then Res_H V is semisimple; if moreover V is irreducible, Res_H V ≅ (W_1 ⊕ … ⊕ W_t)^{⊕e} with W_1, …, W_t the distinct Γ-conjugates of one irreducible constituent W_1, t the index of the (open) stabiliser of the isomorphism class of W_1. (b) Averaging: if [Γ : H] is invertible in k and Res_H V is semisimple, then V is semisimple. (c) If [H : N] is invertible in k and V is semisimple, then Res_H V is semisimple. (d) If [Γ : N] is invertible in k and U is semisimple, then Ind_H^Γ U is semisimple. In characteristic 0 all hypotheses on indices hold, so semisimplicity is preserved by restriction to and induction from open subgroups, and detected by restriction to open subgroups. In characteristic p dividing the indices, (b), (c) and (d) fail.
hypotheses: H open in Γ, so N is open of finite index.
(b), (c), (d) need the stated indices invertible in k; (a) holds in every characteristic.
proofSteps: (a): for an irreducible Γ-subrepresentation V′ ⊂ V and an irreducible H-subspace W ⊂ V′ (finite dimension), Σ_{g ∈ Γ/H} ρ(g)W is Γ-stable (H normal), hence equals V′; each ρ(g)W is an irreducible H-representation (the conjugate W^g), so Res_H V′ is a sum of irreducibles, hence semisimple; grouping isomorphic conjugates gives the isotypic shape, the stabiliser of the class of W_1 containing the open subgroup H.

(b): given a Γ-stable W ⊂ V, choose an H-equivariant projection p : V → W (Res_H V semisimple) and put p′ := [Γ : H]⁻¹ Σ_{gH ∈ Γ/H} ρ(g) p ρ(g)⁻¹; each summand depends only on the coset gH because p is H-equivariant, and p′ is a Γ-equivariant projection onto W, so W has a Γ-stable complement (mathlib:Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation is the complemented-lattice condition).
(c): Res_N V is semisimple by (a) applied to N ◁ Γ; then Res_H V is semisimple by (b) applied to the pair N ◁ H (index [H : N] invertible).

(d): by R01.1/mackey-decomposition with D = N (normal, so N ∩ s⁻¹Hs = N for all s), Res_N Ind_H^Γ U ≅ ⊕_{s ∈ H\Γ/N} Ind_N^N (U^s|_N) = ⊕_s U^s|_N; each U^s|_N is semisimple by (a) applied to N ◁ s⁻¹Hs, so Res_N Ind U is semisimple and Ind U is semisimple by (b) for N ◁ Γ.

Continuity plays no role beyond R01.1/continuous-induction. The finite-group case over splitting fields is Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction Layer 5 (Clifford theory); this node extends the statements needed here to open subgroups of profinite groups.
acceptance: For Γ = Z_p acting on F_p² through Z/p by (1 a; 0 1) and H = pZ_p, Res_H V is trivial, hence semisimple, while V is not: (b) fails when p divides [Γ : H].

For Γ = GL_2(Z_p) acting on F_p² through reduction (irreducible, hence semisimple) and H the open preimage of the upper unipotent subgroup of GL_2(F_p), Res_H V is the nonsplit unipotent representation: (c) fails when p divides [H : N].
BCGP25 Lemma 10.2.3: for ρ irreducible and potentially abelian over L/F, ρ|_{G_L} ≅ ⊕ χ_i^{⊕a} with the χ_i one Gal(L/F)-orbit — the shape in (a).

sources.match: Clifford theory is the standard technique for restricting Galois representations to normal subgroups (cited to Curtis–Reiner §11).
An irreducible representation restricted to the open normal subgroup G_L is a sum of one Galois orbit of characters with common multiplicity a, the conclusion of (a).
Averaging over a finite group in characteristic 0 gives semisimplicity, the mechanism of (b).

nodes.title: Integral models and reduction for Ĝ-valued representations
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a prime, Ĝ a split connected reductive group scheme over Z, Γ profinite, Q̄_ℓ = PadicAlgCl ℓ and F̄_ℓ its residue field (discrete). (i) If ρ : Γ → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) is continuous, there are a coefficient field E ⊂ Q̄_ℓ and g ∈ Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) with gρg⁻¹(Γ) ⊂ Ĝ(O_E). (ii) For any conjugate ρ′ of ρ with values in Ĝ(O_E) for some coefficient field E, the Ĝ-semisimplification ρ̄ : Γ → Ĝ(F̄_ℓ) of ρ′ mod ϖ_E is continuous and, up to Ĝ(F̄_ℓ)-conjugacy, independent of all choices (the reduction modulo ℓ of ρ). No hypothesis on ℓ is needed. (iii) For Ĝ = GL_n these are the statements of this layer: Ĝ(O_E)-valued conjugates are integral models with a basis (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices, R01.1/framed-representation, R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field), GL_n-semisimplification is semisimplification, and (ii) is R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence. The pseudocharacter statement of Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne Theorem 4.8(i) is not part of this node.
hypotheses: Ĝ split connected reductive over Z (dual groups in BHKT's convention).
Γ profinite; F̄_ℓ discrete.
Ĝ-semisimplification and the bijection between Ĝ-completely reducible representations and Ĝ-pseudocharacters over algebraically closed fields (BHKT Theorem 4.5) are inputs recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Baire step: ρ(Γ) is compact, and the Baire argument of R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field (closed subgroups ρ(Γ) ∩ Ĝ(E), countably many E) gives ρ(Γ) ⊂ Ĝ(E) for a coefficient field E.

Bruhat–Tits step (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2): ρ(Γ) lies in Ĝ(E)^0 (all characters O_E^×-valued, by compactness), acts on the building B(DĜ, E) of the derived group with bounded orbits, hence fixes a point; maximal compact subgroups of Ĝ(E)^0 are stabilisers of centroids of facets, and the hyperspecial point x_0 has stabiliser Ĝ(O_E).

Larsen's lemma (Larsen 1995, Lemma 2.4, recorded as a gap): there are a totally ramified E′/E and a ρ(Γ)-stable point x with i_{E,E′}(x) hyperspecial in B(DĜ, E′). Hyperspecial vertices are conjugate under Ĝ^ad(E′); lifting the conjugating element to Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) gives (i).

(ii): reduce modulo ϖ_{E′} and Ĝ-semisimplify; continuity is inherited from ρ′ mod ϖ (open kernel). Independence: the pseudocharacter of ρ̄ is the reduction of tr ρ, which depends only on ρ, and Ĝ-completely reducible representations over F̄_ℓ are determined by their pseudocharacters (BHKT Theorem 4.5, after V. Lafforgue) — gap.

(iii) For Ĝ = GL_n everything is proved in this layer without buildings or pseudocharacters: R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices for (i) and R01.1/brauer-nesbitt with R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence for (ii); the stabiliser of a lattice is a vertex stabiliser of the GL_n building (RG2.2's lattice model), which is the comparison between the two proofs.
acceptance: Ĝ = GL_n recovers lattice existence and lattice independence of ρ̄ (Definition 4.9: 'the familiar ones').

Ĝ = GSp_4: for ρ with absolutely irreducible residual representation, R01.1/self-dual-lattice-for-absolutely-irreducible-residual gives the integral GSp_4(O_E) model directly; the general case requires the building argument.

nodes.title: Decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at a place of a number field
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, F̄ = AlgebraicClosure F, G_F = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F with its Krull topology, and O_{F̄} the integral closure of O_F in F̄, on which G_F acts. For a finite place v of F (v : HeightOneSpectrum O_F) let F_v = v.adicCompletion F, k_v its residue field, q_v = #k_v, F̄_v = AlgebraicClosure F_v and G_{F_v} = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F_v. A place of F̄ above v is a maximal ideal w̄ of O_{F̄} with w̄ ∩ O_F = v. Define the decomposition group D_{w̄} = MulAction.stabilizer G_F w̄, the inertia group I_{w̄} = Ideal.inertia G_F w̄ = {σ ∈ G_F : σx − x ∈ w̄ for all x ∈ O_{F̄}} (a subgroup of D_{w̄}), and the wild inertia group P_{w̄} ⊂ I_{w̄} as the image of P_{F_v} below. For every field embedding ι : F̄ → F̄_v over F → F_v, let ι^* : G_{F_v} → G_F, τ ↦ ι^{-1} ∘ τ ∘ ι (the map Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map for the closure embedding ι), and let w̄(ι) be the place of F̄ pulled back from the maximal ideal of the integral closure of O_{F_v} in F̄_v. Then: (i) ι^* is a continuous injective group homomorphism and a homeomorphism onto its image, which is the closed subgroup D_{w̄(ι)}; (ii) ι^* maps the inertia group I_{F_v} = Gal(F̄_v/F_v^{ur}) and the wild inertia group P_{F_v} of Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 onto I_{w̄(ι)} and P_{w̄(ι)}, and induces D_{w̄}/I_{w̄} ≅ Gal(k̄_v/k_v) ≅ Ẑ; (iii) every place above v is w̄(ι) for some ι; for σ ∈ G_F, w̄(ι∘σ) = σ^{-1}w̄(ι) and (ι∘σ)^* = σ^{-1}·ι^*(−)·σ; two embeddings with the same place differ by an element τ_0 of G_{F_v} (ι' = τ_0∘ι), and then ι'^* = ι^* ∘ (conjugation by τ_0^{-1}); hence D_{σw̄} = σD_{w̄}σ^{-1}, I_{σw̄} = σI_{w̄}σ^{-1}, and the conjugacy classes of these subgroups depend only on v; (iv) the arithmetic Frobenius lifts at w̄ are the σ ∈ D_{w̄} with IsArithFrobAt O_F σ w̄ (σx ≡ x^{q_v} mod w̄ for x ∈ O_{F̄}); they exist and form one coset of I_{w̄} in D_{w̄}, and Frob_{σw̄} = σ Frob_{w̄} σ^{-1} modulo I_{σw̄}; geometric Frobenius lifts are their inverses; (v) for a finite Galois subextension L/F with w = w̄ ∩ O_L, the restriction of D_{w̄} to L is the stabilizer of w in Gal(L/F), and G_{F_v} → Gal(L/F) through ι^* is the composite of restriction G_{F_v} → Gal(L_w/F_v) with the inverse of the bijection decompositionHom of Tau Ceti NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5.6. At a real place v, an embedding ι : F̄ → C over the real embedding gives D = {1, c_ι} with c_ι = ι^{-1}∘(complex conjugation)∘ι, an element of order 2, and changing ι conjugates c_ι in G_F.
hypotheses: F is a number field; v is a finite place for (i)–(v) and a real place for the last sentence
the embedding ι is a choice: Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map documents that it depends on an arbitrary embedding of algebraic closures, and only conjugacy classes are canonical
inertia is defined globally through the action on O_{F̄} and locally as Gal(F̄_v/F_v^{ur}); statement (ii) is the comparison
proofSteps: Continuity and the homomorphism property are Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map (via mapOfAlgebra) for the algebra structure given by ι.

Injectivity: F̄_v = F_v·ι(F̄) because every element of F̄_v is algebraic over F_v and Krasner's lemma (Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layer 0) approximates it by elements of ι(F̄); an F_v-automorphism fixing ι(F̄) is the identity.

Image: ι^*τ preserves the pulled-back valuation, hence stabilises w̄(ι). Conversely, for each finite Galois L/F the restriction of D_{w̄} to L is the stabilizer of w, and NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5.6 shows decompositionHom is a bijection onto Gal(L_w/F_v); compactness of G_{F_v} and the inverse limit over L give surjectivity onto D_{w̄}. The image of a compact group in a Hausdorff group is closed, and a continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.

Inertia: τ ∈ G_{F_v} acts trivially on the residue field of F̄_v iff ι^*τ acts trivially on O_{F̄}/w̄, since the residue field of F̄_v is the algebraic closure of k_v and equals O_{F̄}/w̄ via ι. Wild inertia is the pro-p Sylow subgroup of inertia on both sides (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4).

Change of ι: direct computation of ι'^{-1}∘τ∘ι'; transitivity of G_F on places above v follows from transitivity of Gal(L/F) on the primes of L above v at every finite Galois level (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 2) and compactness.

Frobenius lifts: at each finite level Mathlib's IsArithFrobAt.exists_of_isInvariant and NumberFieldArithmetic layer 2 give Frobenius elements, IsArithFrobAt.mul_inv_mem_inertia shows two lifts differ by inertia and IsArithFrobAt.conj gives the conjugation rule; compactness passes to G_F (Deligne 3.12 works with exactly this choice of a place of F̄ above v).
acceptance: For F = Q, v = p and L = Q(i): the image of D_{w̄} in Gal(Q(i)/Q) is trivial when p ≡ 1 mod 4 and is the whole group when p ≡ 3 mod 4 or p = 2, and the image of I_{w̄} is nontrivial only for p = 2.

For F = Q and two embeddings ι, ι' = ι∘σ, the subgroups ι^*(G_{Q_p}) and ι'^*(G_{Q_p}) are conjugate by σ and are different whenever σ ∉ D_{w̄(ι)}, so the decomposition group is not a normal subgroup.
The restriction of D_{w̄} to a finite Galois L/F agrees with MulAction.stabilizer (L ≃ₐ[F] L) w used by Tau Ceti's Ideal.zpowers_eq_stabilizer_of_isArithFrobAt at unramified w.

nodes.title: Restriction of a global representation to a decomposition group, and its independence of the embedding
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G_F → Aut_A(M) be a continuous representation (R01.1 carrier: M finite projective over a topological coefficient ring A with the module topology, jointly continuous action) of the absolute Galois group of a number field F, and v a finite place. For an embedding ι : F̄ → F̄_v over F → F_v (decomposition-group-at-a-place) define the local restriction ρ_ι := ρ ∘ ι^* : G_{F_v} → Aut_A(M), a continuous representation of G_{F_v} (restriction along the continuous homomorphism ι^*, R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist). Independence: (a) for σ ∈ G_F, ρ(σ) is an isomorphism of G_{F_v}-representations (M, ρ_{ι∘σ}) → (M, ρ_ι); (b) for τ_0 ∈ G_{F_v}, ρ_ι(τ_0) is an isomorphism (M, ρ_{τ_0∘ι}) → (M, ρ_ι); since any two embeddings are related by (a) and (b), the isomorphism class of ρ|_{G_{F_v}} := [ρ_ι] depends only on ρ and v, but the isomorphism depends on the chosen σ, τ_0 (it is canonical only up to the automorphisms ρ(D_{w̄}) of ρ_ι). The restriction is compatible with the R01.1 operations: (ρ ⊗ ρ')_ι = ρ_ι ⊗ ρ'_ι, (ρ^∨)_ι = (ρ_ι)^∨, (ρ ⊗ χ)_ι = ρ_ι ⊗ χ_ι, coefficient extension along A → B, and for L/F finite and w̄ above w | v, (ρ|_{G_L})_{ι} = (ρ_ι)|_{G_{L_w}}; for induction from an open G_L, (Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ρ)_ι ≅ ⊕_{w | v} Ind_{G_{L_w}}^{G_{F_v}} (ρ_{ι_w}) (R01.1/mackey-decomposition with D = ι^*(G_{F_v}), double cosets G_L\G_F/D ↔ places w of L above v). For ρ with finite image and kernel field K_ρ (finite Galois over F), ρ_ι factors through an injective homomorphism Gal(K_{ρ,𝔭}/F_v) → Aut_A(M), 𝔭 = w̄(ι) ∩ O_{K_ρ}, carrying the inertia and wild inertia subgroups of Gal(K_{ρ,𝔭}/F_v) onto ρ(I_{w̄}) and ρ(P_{w̄}).
hypotheses: F is a number field and v a finite place; the same construction applies at real places with D = {1, c_ι}
A, M as in R01.1 (finite projective M with the module topology)
independence is up to non-canonical isomorphism; statements that depend on the isomorphism (for example extension classes compared at two places above v) must carry ι
proofSteps: Continuity: composite of the continuous action map with ι^* × id (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist).
(a): ρ_{ι∘σ}(τ) = ρ(σ^{-1}ι^*(τ)σ) = ρ(σ)^{-1}ρ_ι(τ)ρ(σ) by decomposition-group-at-a-place (iii); (b) likewise with τ_0.
Any two embeddings ι, ι' satisfy ι' = τ_0∘ι∘σ for some σ ∈ G_F, τ_0 ∈ G_{F_v}: choose σ with w̄(ι') = σ^{-1}w̄(ι) by transitivity, then use decomposition-group-at-a-place (iii).

Operations commute with restriction along a group homomorphism by definition; the induction formula is R01.1/mackey-decomposition for the closed subgroup D_{w̄} and open G_L, with the double cosets identified with places of L above v (finite level: NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5).

Finite image: ρ factors through Gal(K_ρ/F), ι^* restricted to Gal(K_{ρ,𝔭}/F_v) is decompositionHom^{-1} (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5.6), injective; the inertia statement is decomposition-group-at-a-place (ii) at finite level.
acceptance: For the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ of G_Q and p ≠ ℓ, χ_ℓ ∘ ι^* is the cyclotomic character of G_{Q_p}, for every ι (the restriction of a character does not depend on ι at all, since conjugation acts trivially on an abelian target).

For ρ = Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} 1 and p ≡ 1 mod 4 the restriction ρ_ι is the trivial two-dimensional representation, while for p ≡ 3 mod 4 it is 1 ⊕ (unramified quadratic character), matching the Mackey formula with two places, respectively one place, above p.

identifies ρ̄|_{D_p} with an injective Gal(K_𝔭/Q_p) → GL_2(F) carrying inertia and wild inertia to their images
local Weil–Deligne data are computed from local restrictions of twists, restrictions and inductions
local conductors are invariants of ρ|_{G_{F_v}}
V_v is the restriction of V to the decomposition group of a chosen place of K̄ above v
