nodes.title: Unramified and tamely ramified representations, and the ramification set
nodes.statement: Local: for K a nonarchimedean local field with inertia I_K and wild inertia P_K (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4) and a continuous representation ρ of G_K (or of the Weil group W_K) on M, ρ is unramified if ρ(I_K) = 1 and tamely ramified if ρ(P_K) = 1. Global: for ρ a continuous representation of G_F (F a number field) and v a finite place, ρ is unramified at v if ρ(I_{w̄}) = 1 for one, equivalently every, place w̄ of F̄ above v (equivalently ρ_ι is unramified for one, equivalently every, ι). Ram(ρ) is the set of finite places at which ρ is ramified; for p a prime, Ram^{(p)}(ρ) = Ram(ρ) minus the places above p (the set S(r̄) of CG20 when F = Q). ρ is unramified outside a set S of places if Ram(ρ) ⊂ S; equivalently ρ factors through G_{F,S} = Gal(F_S/F), F_S the maximal extension unramified outside S. If ρ has finite image (in particular if A is finite discrete), Ram(ρ) is the finite set of places ramified in the kernel field; for ℓ-adic ρ finiteness of Ram(ρ) is a hypothesis and is carried explicitly by consumers.
hypotheses: unramifiedness at v is independent of w̄ because the I_{w̄} for w̄ | v are conjugate in G_F
Ram(ρ) contains only finite places; real places are handled by complex conjugation (R01.4, G7)
Ram(ρ) need not be finite without a hypothesis; finiteness is automatic only for finite image
proofSteps: Independence of w̄: decomposition-group-at-a-place (iii).
Factorisation through G_{F,S}: the closed normal subgroup generated by the I_{w̄}, v ∉ S, is the kernel of G_F → G_{F,S}; ρ kills it iff ρ is unramified outside S.

Finite image: ρ factors through Gal(K_ρ/F) (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients) and is unramified at v iff the inertia group at a prime of K_ρ above v is trivial, i.e. iff K_ρ/F is unramified at v (Tau Ceti Ideal.isUnramifiedAt_iff_inertia_eq_bot); a number field has finitely many ramified primes.
acceptance: Ram(χ_ℓ) is the set of places above ℓ, for F = Q and any prime ℓ.
For E/Q with split multiplicative reduction at p and ℓ ≠ p with ℓ | v_p(q_E), the residual E[ℓ] is unramified at p while V_ℓE is ramified at p: unramifiedness of ρ̄ does not imply that of ρ.

nodes.title: The Frobenius characteristic polynomial P_v(ρ, X) at an unramified place
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative coefficient ring, ρ : G_F → Aut_A(M) continuous with M finite free of rank n over A (over the local coefficient rings of R01.1 every finite projective module is free; in general P_v is defined Zariski-locally on A and glues), and v a finite place at which ρ is unramified. P_v(ρ, X) := LinearMap.charpoly(ρ(Frob_{w̄})) = det(X − ρ(Frob_{w̄}) | M) ∈ A[X], where Frob_{w̄} is any ARITHMETIC Frobenius lift at any place w̄ above v (σx ≡ x^{q_v} mod w̄). It is well defined: lifts at one w̄ differ by elements of I_{w̄}, which act trivially, and lifts at σw̄ are conjugate by σ. Its trace tr ρ(Frob_v) and determinant det ρ(Frob_v) are coefficients up to sign. The geometric variant is P_v^{geom}(ρ, X) := det(X − ρ(Frob_{w̄}^{-1})) = P_v(ρ^∨, X), and the local Euler factor at an unramified v is L_v(ρ, X) = det(1 − Xρ(Frob_{w̄}^{-1})) = X^n·P_v(ρ^∨, X^{-1}) = Polynomial.reverse (P_v(ρ^∨, X)).
hypotheses: ρ unramified at v
arithmetic Frobenius (x ↦ x^{q_v}), following the plan; consumers using geometric-Frobenius polynomials (WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.1) use P_v^{geom} = P_v(ρ^∨, −)
M free of finite rank (charpoly is defined for finite free modules)
proofSteps: Independence of the lift: decomposition-group-at-a-place (iv) and unramifiedness (Mathlib IsArithFrobAt.mul_inv_mem_inertia).

Independence of w̄: conjugate endomorphisms have equal characteristic polynomials (LinearMap.charpoly is invariant under conjugation; LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix compares with Matrix.charpoly in any basis).

Geometric variant: ρ^∨(g) is the transpose-inverse of ρ(g), so det(X − ρ^∨(Frob)) = det(X − ρ(Frob)^{-1}); reversing gives the Euler-factor identity (Polynomial.reverse, using that the constant term det(−ρ(Frob)) is a unit).
acceptance: P_v(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q_v for v ∤ ℓ, and P_v^{geom}(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q_v^{-1}.
For an elliptic curve E/Q with good reduction at p ≠ ℓ, P_p(V_ℓE, X) = X² − a_pX + p (R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial), and L_p(V_ℓE^∨, X) = 1 − a_pX + pX².

nodes.title: Unramified characters λ(α) with prescribed Frobenius value, and the geometric variant
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, R a topological commutative ring and α ∈ R^×. λ(α) : G_K → R^× is the continuous homomorphism, trivial on I_K, with λ(α)(Frob) = α for one (equivalently every) arithmetic Frobenius lift Frob, when such a homomorphism exists (CG18). It exists iff the homomorphism Z → R^×, n ↦ α^n, is continuous for the profinite topology of Z (equivalently extends continuously to Ẑ = Gal(K^{ur}/K)), and it is then unique. Sufficient: the closure of α^Z in R^× is a profinite group, e.g. R^× profinite, as for R a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field, R = O_E, or R finite discrete; then λ(α) = (lift of n ↦ α^n to the profinite completion of Z) ∘ (G_K ↠ Gal(K^{ur}/K) ≅ Ẑ). For R = E finite over Q_ℓ, λ(α) exists iff α ∈ O_E^×; for R = C (complex topology) iff α is a root of unity. The geometric variant (CG20) λ^{geom}(γ) sends a geometric Frobenius to γ: λ^{geom}(γ) = λ(γ^{-1}). On the Weil group no condition is needed: λ_W(α)(w) = α^{weilDegree(w)} defines an unramified character W_K → R^× for every α ∈ R^×, and λ_W(α) extends to G_K iff λ(α) exists. For a number field F and finite place v, λ_v(α) denotes λ(α) on G_{F_v}, transported to D_{w̄} by ι^*.
hypotheses: arithmetic normalisation for λ (CG18), geometric for λ^{geom} (CG20); the two differ by inversion
existence is a condition on α and the topology of R, not automatic
proofSteps: G_K/I_K ≅ Gal(K^{ur}/K) ≅ Ẑ with Frob ↦ 1 (LocalFieldsRamification layers 2 and 4), Ẑ being Mathlib's profinite completion of Z.
If the closure H of α^Z is profinite, Mathlib's ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.lift extends n ↦ α^n to Ẑ → H, and lift_eta gives λ(α)(Frob) = α; uniqueness is lift_unique (Z is dense in Ẑ).

Necessity: a continuous extension restricts to the profinite topology on Z. For R = E: the image of the compact group Ẑ is bounded, forcing |α| = 1; conversely O_E^× is profinite. For R = C: a continuous homomorphism from a profinite group to C^× has finite image (C^× has no small subgroups), so α has finite order.
The Weil-group version uses W_K/I_K ≅ Z via weilDegree (ClassFieldTheory layer 9) and needs no extension.
acceptance: For ℓ ≠ p and K/Q_p finite, λ(q) : G_K → Z_ℓ^× equals the restriction of the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character χ_ℓ to G_K.
λ(ℓ) : G_K → Q_ℓ^× does not exist, while λ_W(ℓ) : W_K → Q_ℓ^× does.

uses.how: λ(α) : G_v → R^× sends the arithmetic Frob_v to α; used in ordinary local shapes
λ(γ) sends geometric Frobenius to γ; r̄|_{G_p} is conjugate to an upper-triangular matrix with λ(α), λ(β), ν(r̄)λ(β^{-1}), ν(r̄)λ(α^{-1})
the unramified character ω with ω(arithmetic Frobenius) = q on W_K

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic cyclotomic character, Dirichlet characters as Galois characters, and their Frobenius values
nodes.statement: (a) For a field F of characteristic ≠ ℓ, χ_ℓ : G_F → Z_ℓ^× is Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter (AlgebraicClosure F) ℓ composed with G_F → RingAut(F̄); it is continuous (cyclotomicCharacter.continuous) and σ(ζ) = ζ^{χ_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n} for ζ ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}(F̄) (cyclotomicCharacter.spec); its reduction mod ℓ^n is modularCyclotomicCharacter; Z_ℓ(1) of R01.1/tate-twist is A = Z_ℓ with this action. (b) For K a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p ≠ ℓ, χ_ℓ|_{G_K} is unramified with χ_ℓ(Frob) = q for arithmetic Frobenius, i.e. χ_ℓ|_{G_K} = λ(q); for F a number field and v ∤ ℓ finite, χ_ℓ is unramified at v and P_v(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q_v. (c) For N ≥ 1 and a Dirichlet character ε : (Z/N)^× → R^× (Mathlib DirichletCharacter R N on units), ε_Gal := ε ∘ galEquivZMod ∘ (restriction G_Q → Gal(Q(ζ_N)/Q)) is a continuous finite-order character of G_Q (any topology on R); it is unramified at every p ∤ N with ε_Gal(Frob_p) = ε(p mod N) for arithmetic Frobenius, Ram(ε_Gal) is the set of primes dividing the conductor of ε, and ε_Gal(c) = ε(−1) for complex conjugation c. Characters induced from divisors of N give the same Galois character. (d) Every continuous finite-order character of G_Q is ε_Gal for a unique primitive ε (Kronecker–Weber, Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 13). (e) The mod-p cyclotomic character χ̄_p = χ_p mod p equals ε_Gal for ε = (Z/p)^× → F_p^× the identity; its Teichmüller lift ω_p : G_Q → Z_p^× (R01.1/teichmuller-lift-of-a-residual-character) satisfies χ_p = ω_p·⟨χ_p⟩ with ⟨χ_p⟩ valued in 1 + pZ_p (1 + 4Z_2 for p = 2, where ω_2 is taken modulo 4).
hypotheses: χ_ℓ is valued in Z_ℓ^× and is trivial when F̄ lacks ℓ-power roots of unity (never for char F ≠ ℓ)
arithmetic Frobenius throughout; the Hodge–Tate weight of χ_p (+1 in the plan, −1 in CG20) is PadicHodgeTheory's convention, not fixed here
for p = 2 the Teichmüller decomposition uses (Z/4)^× (the torsion of Z_2^× is {±1})
proofSteps: (a) is Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter with spec, toZModPow and continuous.

(b): an arithmetic Frobenius lift acts on μ_{ℓ^n} ⊂ O_{K̄}^× by ζ ↦ ζ' with ζ' ≡ ζ^q mod the maximal ideal; reduction is injective on μ_{ℓ^n} for ℓ ≠ p, so ζ' = ζ^q; inertia acts trivially because the extension K(μ_{ℓ^∞})/K is unramified (LocalFieldsRamification layer 2).

(c): galEquivZMod_apply_of_pow_eq gives σ(ζ) = ζ^{a(σ)}; the Frobenius at p ∤ N in Q(ζ_N) is ζ ↦ ζ^p (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 2 cyclotomic examples), so ε_Gal(Frob_p) = ε(p); complex conjugation inverts ζ, so ε_Gal(c) = ε(−1); Q(ζ_N)/Q is ramified exactly at p | N, and ε_Gal is ramified at p iff ε is not trivial on the p-part, i.e. iff p divides the conductor.
(d) is Kronecker–Weber with the identification of Gal(Q^{ab}/Q) with Ẑ^× through cyclotomicCharacter.
(e): Teichmüller splitting Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) (Tau Ceti teichmuller for Q_p) applied pointwise.
acceptance: For the character ε = χ_{−4} of (Z/4)^×: ε_Gal(Frob_p) = (−1)^{(p−1)/2} for odd p, ε_Gal(c) = −1, and ε_Gal is the character of Q(i)/Q.
χ_ℓ(Frob_p) = p for every prime p ≠ ℓ, and χ_ℓ is ramified at ℓ with χ_ℓ(I_ℓ) = Z_ℓ^×.

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic tame character t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ(1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of characteristic p and cardinality q, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. Let θ : I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1) = lim_{p ∤ m} μ_m(K̄) be the tame character of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 and Z_ℓ(1) = lim_n μ_{ℓ^n}(K̄) (R01.1/tate-twist). Define t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ(1) as θ composed with the projection to the ℓ-component; explicitly t_ℓ(σ) = (σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n})_n for a uniformiser π and a compatible system of roots. Then: (i) t_ℓ is a continuous surjective homomorphism, independent of π and the roots, trivial on P_K; (ii) Kummer reductions: t_ℓ mod ℓ^n is σ ↦ σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n} ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}; (iii) equivariance: t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)·t_ℓ(σ) for w ∈ G_K, σ ∈ I_K; for w ∈ W_K this is q^{weilDegree(w)}·t_ℓ(σ); (iv) every continuous homomorphism from I_K (or from an open subgroup J of I_K) to a pro-ℓ group factors through t_ℓ (through t_ℓ|_J); in particular I_K has exactly one quotient of order ℓ, namely t_ℓ mod ℓ : I_K ↠ μ_ℓ; (v) for L/K finite with ramification index e, t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L}; (vi) a trivialisation T : Z_ℓ(1) ≅ Z_ℓ (a choice of compatible primitive ℓ^n-th roots of unity) gives T∘t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ, and changing T multiplies it by a unit of Z_ℓ. t_ℓ does not extend to a homomorphism on G_K or W_K (by (iii) such an extension would be invariant under conjugation by Frobenius, which multiplies t_ℓ by q ≠ 1).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p
K has finite residue field (a nonarchimedean local field); the construction for henselian traits with other residue fields stays with LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0
t_ℓ is a character of inertia only
proofSteps: (i)–(ii): LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 (the tame character, its independence of choices, its finite-level form) followed by the projection Ẑ^{(p')}(1) → Z_ℓ(1).

(iii): the G_K-equivariance statement of layer 4 (conjugation acts through the cyclotomic action), with χ_ℓ from cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters; on W_K, χ_ℓ(w) = q^{weilDegree w} because χ_ℓ = λ(q) on G_K.

(iv): a pro-ℓ quotient kills the pro-p group P_K and factors through the abelian group I_K/P_K ≅ ∏_{ℓ' ≠ p} Z_{ℓ'}(1), whose maximal pro-ℓ quotient is the ℓ-factor; the order-ℓ quotients correspond to Hom(Z_ℓ(1), Z/ℓ), a line over F_ℓ.
(v): with π_K = u·π_L^e, σ ∈ I_L fixes the ℓ^n-th roots of the unit u (they generate an unramified extension), so σ(π_K^{1/ℓ^n})/π_K^{1/ℓ^n} = (σ(π_L^{1/ℓ^n})/π_L^{1/ℓ^n})^e.
acceptance: For K = Q_p and σ ∈ I with σ(p^{1/ℓ}) = ζ_ℓ p^{1/ℓ}, t_ℓ(σ) ≡ ζ_ℓ in μ_ℓ.

For K = Q_2 and ℓ = 3, the unique quotient of order 3 of I_2 is t_3 mod 3 : I_2 ↠ μ_3, through which every unipotent action of I_2 on an F_3-vector space factors (ClassicalSerreModularity R33.3 at (q, N) = (3, 2)).

nodes.title: Tame inertia, the level of a character, and the fundamental characters of levels one and two
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of characteristic p, I_K ⊃ P_K and I_t = I_K/P_K (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4), k̄ the residue field of K̄. For n ≥ 1 and Q = p^n, the fundamental character of level n is θ_{Q−1} : I_t → μ_{Q−1}(K̄) ≅ F_Q^× ⊂ k̄^× (reduction modulo the maximal ideal), σ ↦ σ(π^{1/(Q−1)})/π^{1/(Q−1)}, independent of the uniformiser and the root; the fundamental characters of level n are its n conjugates θ_{Q−1}^{p^i}, 0 ≤ i < n, and, for a field k_1 of characteristic p, a character I_t → k_1^× is fundamental of level n if it is θ_{Q−1} followed by an embedding F_Q ↪ k_1. These induce I_t ≅ lim F_{p^n}^× (transition maps the norms). A character of I_t is of level n if it factors through F_{p^n}^× (via θ_{p^n−1}) and through no F_{p^m}^× with m a proper divisor of n. Conjugation by an arithmetic Frobenius lift s acts on I_t by u ↦ u^{#k}, so θ(sus^{-1}) = θ(u)^{#k} for every fundamental character θ. For K = Q_p: the level-1 fundamental character is ω = θ_{p−1} = χ̄_p|_{I}; the two level-2 fundamental characters ψ = ω_2, ψ' = ω_2^p satisfy ψψ' = ω_2^{p+1} = ω; for a finite extension K/Q_p with ramification index e, χ̄_p|_{I_K} = θ_{p−1}^e. The residual character ω_{p,2}, its Teichmüller lift [ω_{p,2}] : I_t → W(F_{p^2})^× (TauCeti.teichmuller) and its ℓ-adic incarnations are three distinct declarations, although the sources use one symbol.
hypotheses: level is a property of a character of I_t, not of a representation of G_K
the level-1/level-2 dichotomy is specific to dimension two (tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations)
the comparison with local class field theory has a sign: Serre 1972 Proposition 3 shows the tame character and the reciprocity map on units are opposite
proofSteps: θ_{Q−1} is the Q−1 component of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4's tame character I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1), read in the residue field: reduction μ_{Q−1}(K̄) ≅ F_Q^× is the bijection of TauCeti.rootsOfUnityEquivResidueFieldUnits (inverse of the Teichmüller map); the inverse limit statement is Serre 1972 Proposition 2.
Conjugation: layer 4's equivariance (conjugation acts through the cyclotomic action), with the cyclotomic character of an arithmetic Frobenius acting on prime-to-p roots of unity by the #k-th power.
ω = θ_{p−1} on I_{Q_p}: K(μ_p) = K((−p)^{1/(p−1)}) and (ζ^a − 1)/(ζ − 1) ≡ a modulo the maximal ideal (Serre 1972 Proposition 8, recorded there as the e-th power for ramification index e).
ψψ' = ψ^{1+p} = θ_{p²−1}^{(p²−1)/(p−1)} = θ_{p−1} by the norm compatibility of the θ's.
acceptance: The product of the two level-2 fundamental characters of I_{Q_p} is the restriction of the mod-p cyclotomic character.
On an explicit supersingular elliptic curve over Q_p with good reduction (p odd), the tame characters of E[p] are the two level-2 fundamental characters (Serre 1972 1.11; R01.6 supplies the curve).

nodes.title: Semisimple residual local representations are tame; levels and induced representations in dimension two
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, k_1 a field of characteristic p with the discrete topology and ρ̄ : G_K → GL(V) a continuous representation on a finite-dimensional k_1-vector space. (a) If ρ̄ is semisimple then ρ̄(P_K) = 1; hence for any ρ̄, P_K acts trivially on the semisimplification V^{ss} (R01.1/semisimplification) and I_K acts on V^{ss} through I_t; ρ̄(I_t) is cyclic of order prime to p, and over k̄_1 the action of I_t on V^{ss} is a sum of characters, each a product of powers of fundamental characters, the multiset of which is stable under χ ↦ χ^{#k}. (b) (K = Q_p, dim V = 2, k_1 = F̄_p) The two characters φ, φ' of I_t on V^{ss} are of level 1 or 2; if of level 2 they are conjugate: φ' = φ^p, φ = φ'^p, φ ≠ φ'. (c) If φ, φ' are of level 2, V is irreducible; conversely an irreducible two-dimensional ρ̄ has level 2. (d) Let Q_{p²} ⊂ Q̄_p be the unramified quadratic extension and χ : G_{Q_{p²}} → F̄_p^× continuous with χ|_{I} = ω_2^j. Then ind(χ) := Ind_{G_{Q_{p²}}}^{G_{Q_p}} χ restricted to I_{Q_p} is ω_2^j ⊕ ω_2^{pj}, and ind(χ) is irreducible iff (p+1) ∤ j; every irreducible two-dimensional ρ̄ is of this form. When (p+1) | j, χ extends to G_{Q_p} and ind(χ) ≅ χ̃ ⊕ χ̃η with η the unramified quadratic character.
hypotheses: k_1 has characteristic p equal to the residue characteristic (residual representations at p)
semisimplicity in (a) is with respect to G_K; P_K need not act trivially on V itself
(b)–(d) are two-dimensional statements over Q_p; for K with residue field F_{p^f} the Frobenius acts by the p^f-th power
proofSteps: (a) Serre 1972 Proposition 4: ρ̄(P_K) is a finite p-group (open kernel), its invariants V' ≠ 0 form a G_K-stable subspace because P_K is normal; semisimplicity and induction on dimension give ρ̄(P_K) = 1. Then I_t acts through a finite cyclic group of order prime to p (I_t is procyclic of order prime to p), hence diagonalisably over k̄_1, through characters which are powers of fundamental characters (tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters); stability under the #k-th power is conjugation by a Frobenius lift.

(b) Serre 1987 Proposition 1: conjugation by a Frobenius lift s satisfies sus^{-1} ≡ u^p mod I_p, so {φ, φ'} is stable under the p-th power; either both are fixed (level 1) or they are swapped (level 2).

(c) Serre 1987 2.2: a stable line would give a character of I_t extending to G_p, hence of level 1. Conversely let ρ̄ be irreducible (hence semisimple, so (a) applies) with φ, φ' of level 1: if φ = φ', twisting by a power of χ̄_p extending φ makes ρ̄ unramified, with procyclic image, hence reducible over F̄_p; if φ ≠ φ', conjugation by a Frobenius lift maps the φ-eigenline of I_t to the φ^{1/p} = φ eigenline, so both eigenlines are G_p-stable; either way ρ̄ is reducible.

(d) Mackey: Res_I Ind χ = χ|_I ⊕ χ^s|_I with s a Frobenius lift, and χ^s|_I = ω_2^{pj} by the conjugation rule; the Mackey irreducibility criterion (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction layer 4, applied to the finite image) gives irreducibility iff χ ≠ χ^s, i.e. iff ω_2^j ≠ ω_2^{pj} on I (unramified characters of G_{Q_{p²}} are s-invariant), i.e. iff (p² − 1) ∤ j(p − 1), i.e. (p+1) ∤ j. If (p+1) | j then ω_2^j = ω^{j/(p+1)} on I and χ = ω^{j/(p+1)}μ with μ unramified, which extends. Every irreducible ρ̄ has level 2 by (c), so I_t acts by ω_2^j ⊕ ω_2^{pj} with distinct characters; the Frobenius of Q_{p²} acts on I_t by the p²-th power and fixes both, so G_{Q_{p²}} preserves the two eigenlines, ρ̄|_{G_{Q_{p²}}} = χ ⊕ χ^s, and Frobenius reciprocity gives ρ̄ ≅ ind(χ).

nodes.title: Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem (arithmetic quasi-unipotence)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q, q = p^f, W_K its Weil group with the Weil topology (ClassFieldTheory layer 9), ℓ ≠ p a prime, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ, V a finite-dimensional E-vector space and ρ : W_K → GL(V) continuous for the Weil topology and the ℓ-adic topology (for instance the restriction of a continuous representation of G_K). Then there is a unique nilpotent N ∈ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(Z_ℓ(1), End_E V) = End(V)(−1) and an open subgroup J ⊂ I_K such that ρ(σ) = exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) for all σ ∈ J (exp of a nilpotent endomorphism, a finite sum). Moreover ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) for w ∈ W_K, x ∈ Z_ℓ(1); after a trivialisation T of Z_ℓ(1), N' := N(T^{-1}1) satisfies ρ(w)N'ρ(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N', i.e. ρ(Φ)N'ρ(Φ)^{-1} = qN' for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ and ρ(F)N'ρ(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N' for a geometric one. Consequences: every ρ(σ), σ ∈ I_K, is quasi-unipotent (eigenvalues roots of unity); ρ(I_K) is finite iff N = 0; N is the same for ρ and for every restriction ρ|_{W_L}, L/K finite, up to the factor e(L/K) of t_ℓ (N_L = e·N_K); coefficients in Q̄_ℓ are covered after descent to a finite E (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field).
hypotheses: ℓ different from the residue characteristic p

finite residue field: the argument uses that Frobenius multiplies t_ℓ by q, which is not a root of unity; for K = C((t)) the character σ ↦ (1+ℓ)^{T(t_ℓ(σ))} of I_K = G_K is continuous and not quasi-unipotent, so the statement fails for algebraically closed residue fields (where LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.1 supplies the geometric theorem)
quasi-unipotence holds on an open subgroup only; ρ need not be unipotent on I_K
N is Tate-twisted; the untwisted N' depends on T and changes by a unit under a change of T
proofSteps: Deligne states the theorem as 8.2 and refers to Serre–Tate for the proof (not read); the argument planned here is the standard one.
Lattice: ρ(I_K) is compact, so it stabilises an O_E-lattice (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices); J := ρ|_{I_K}^{-1}(1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E)) is open in I_K and ρ(J) is pro-ℓ.

Factorisation: by ell-adic-tame-character (iv), ρ|_J = h ∘ t_ℓ|_J for a continuous h : t_ℓ(J) → 1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E); t_ℓ(J) = ℓ^m Z_ℓ(1) is procyclic, and N(x) := ℓ^{-m} log h(ℓ^m x) (ℓ-adic logarithm, convergent on 1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E)) is Z_ℓ-linear with exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) = ρ(σ) on J.

Nilpotence: for w ∈ W_K, conjugation by w preserves an open subgroup of J and t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)t_ℓ(σ) (ell-adic-tame-character (iii)), so ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x); with w an arithmetic Frobenius lift, N' is conjugate to qN', so its eigenvalues are stable under multiplication by q and are all 0.
Uniqueness: two pairs (N_1, J_1), (N_2, J_2) agree on J_1 ∩ J_2 because log is injective on unipotent elements, and linearity in x gives N_1 = N_2.
ρ(I_K) finite iff N = 0: if N = 0, ρ is trivial on the open J; if ρ(I_K) is finite, exp(N(x)) has finite order and is unipotent, hence trivial, and N = log of it is 0.
acceptance: For the Tate curve E_q over K with v(q) > 0, the representation on V_ℓE_q has N ≠ 0 with image the line Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q, and ρ(I_K) is infinite.
For an abelian variety with potentially good reduction, or for any representation with finite image on inertia (e.g. a finite-order character), N = 0.

nodes.title: Weil–Deligne representations of a local Weil group (arithmetic normalisation)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, W_K its Weil group with weilDegree : W_K → Z (kernel I_K, arithmetic Frobenius lifts of degree 1; ClassFieldTheory layer 9), and Ω a field of characteristic 0. A Weil–Deligne representation of W_K over Ω is a triple (V, r, N): V a finite-dimensional Ω-vector space, r : W_K → GL(V) a homomorphism whose restriction to I_K has open kernel (equivalently r is continuous for the discrete topology on GL(V)), and N ∈ End_Ω(V) nilpotent with r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N for all w ∈ W_K (Deligne (8.4.1.1)); equivalently r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ and r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N for a geometric lift F. Morphisms are Ω-linear maps f with f∘r(w) = r'(w)∘f and f∘N = N'∘f; they form an Ω-linear abelian category WD_Ω(K) with direct sums, tensor products (r⊗r', N⊗1 + 1⊗N'), internal Hom and duals (r^∨, −N^∨), determinant (det r, 0), coefficient extension Ω → Ω', restriction to W_L for L/K finite inside K̄ and induction from W_L (Ind r, with N acting on the induced space through the coset decomposition). The unramified character ω : W_K → Ω^×, ω(w) = q^{weilDegree(w)} (ω(Φ) = q), corresponds to Deligne's ω_1 = ‖·‖ and to Q_ℓ(1); the special representation Sp(n) has basis e_0, …, e_{n−1}, r(w)e_i = ω(w)^i e_i and Ne_i = e_{i+1} (Ne_{n−1} = 0). The inertial type of (V, r, N) is r|_{I_K} up to isomorphism.
hypotheses: arithmetic normalisation (8.4.1.1); copying a geometric-Frobenius formula with q instead of q^{-1} gives the wrong objects
r is required to have open kernel on inertia; the ℓ-adic topology of Ω plays no role (Deligne 8.3–8.4: the description is independent of the topology of E_λ)
Ω has characteristic 0, needed for exp/log in the comparison with ℓ-adic representations
proofSteps: Category: kernels and cokernels of morphisms carry the restricted r and N, the relation is preserved; tensor products: r⊗r'(w)(N⊗1 + 1⊗N')r⊗r'(w)^{-1} = q^{deg w}(N⊗1 + 1⊗N'), and N⊗1 + 1⊗N' is nilpotent as a sum of commuting nilpotents.
Duals: with r^∨(w) the transpose of r(w)^{-1}, r^∨(w)X^∨r^∨(w)^{-1} = (r(w)Xr(w)^{-1})^∨ for X ∈ End V, so r^∨(w)(−N^∨)r^∨(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}(−N^∨).
Restriction to W_L: weilDegree_K = f(L/K)·weilDegree_L on W_L (ClassFieldTheory layer 9 weilDegree_weilTransfer) and q_L = q^{f(L/K)}, so the relation is preserved.
acceptance: Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N e_0 = e_1) satisfies the relation, and its kernel of N is the line on which arithmetic Frobenius acts by q, matching Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓ(E_q) for a Tate curve.
The pair (ω ⊕ 1, N e_0 = e_1), i.e. N lowering the ω-exponent, violates the relation: r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{-weilDegree(w)}N.

nodes.title: The Weil–Deligne representation of an ℓ-adic representation and its independence of choices
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ and (V, ρ) a continuous representation of W_K (or of G_K, restricted to W_K) on a finite-dimensional E-vector space, with monodromy N ∈ End(V)(−1) from grothendieck-quasi-unipotence. Choose a geometric Frobenius lift F ∈ W_K and an isomorphism T : Q_ℓ(1) → Q_ℓ (Deligne 8.4.2). Define WD_{F,T}(ρ) = (V, ρ', N') by ρ'(F^nσ) = ρ(F^nσ)·exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N) for n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K (every w ∈ W_K is uniquely F^nσ), and N' ∈ End(V) the image of N under T. Then (V, ρ', N') is a Weil–Deligne representation over E in the sense of weil-deligne-representation (ρ'|_{I_K} has open kernel and ρ'(w)N'ρ'(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N'), and its isomorphism class WD(ρ) depends only on ρ, not on F or T (Lemme 8.4.3): changing F to Fτ (τ ∈ I_K) conjugates by A = exp((1−q^{-1})^{-1}t_ℓ(τ)N), and changing T to aT replaces N' by aN', isomorphic to (ρ', N') for every a ∈ E^×. The construction is a functor from continuous ℓ-adic representations of W_K to WD_E(K), it is exact, faithful, compatible with ⊗, duals, det, direct sums, twists (WD(ρ⊗χ) = WD(ρ)⊗WD(χ)), coefficient extension, restriction to W_L and induction from W_L, and with V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N')^{ρ'(I_K)}; it induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of continuous ℓ-adic representations of W_K over E and isomorphism classes of Weil–Deligne representations over E (Deligne 8.3.7, in the form 8.4); a continuous representation of W_K extends continuously to G_K iff its image is bounded, i.e. iff the eigenvalues of r(Φ) are ℓ-adic units.
hypotheses: λ must have residue characteristic different from that of K; this is the ℓ ≠ p hypothesis of the stage
the nilpotent N of Theorem 8.2 lies in End(V)(−1), i.e. it is Tate-twisted; the untwisted N' of 8.4.2 depends on the choice of T, and changing T to aT replaces N' by aN'
quasi-unipotence is only on a subgroup of finite index of inertia; ρ itself need not be unipotent on all of I
the construction 8.4.2 depends on choosing a GEOMETRIC Frobenius F and a trivialization T of Z_ℓ(1); Lemme 8.4.3 removes the dependence only up to isomorphism

the source's proof of Lemme 8.4.3 changes F to F.ρ (ρ in I), giving an isomorphic pair via conjugation by A = exp((1−q^{−1})^{−1} t_ℓ(ρ)), and T to aT, and shows (ρ', N') is isomorphic to (ρ', aN') for every a (printed 'a ∈ E', meaning a nonzero) by decomposing V into generalized eigenspaces V^α of F^n, with N V^α contained in V^{q^{−n} α}
the bijection is for representations of W_K; Weil–Deligne representations whose Frobenius has non-unit eigenvalues come from representations of W_K that do not extend to G_K
proofSteps: The source states 8.2 as Grothendieck's theorem and refers to [13] = Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968), for the proof, which was NOT read here; grothendieck-quasi-unipotence plans that proof.

The exponent convention is fixed by the notation of 2.2.2–2.2.4: v' is reduction to Gal(k̄/k), whose Weil subgroup W(k̄/k) = Z is generated by the ARITHMETIC Frobenius φ, and F = φ^{-1} is the geometric Frobenius; so the displayed relation reads ρ(Φ)Nρ(Φ)^{-1} = qN for arithmetic Φ. This agrees with the stage text 'With arithmetic Frobenius the relation is r(F)Nr(F)^{-1}=qN'.

ρ' is a homomorphism because ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) and t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)t_ℓ(σ) (grothendieck-quasi-unipotence, ell-adic-tame-character (iii)), so the correction factors exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N) multiply compatibly; ρ' is trivial on the open J where ρ = exp(t_ℓN).
8.4.2 produces (ρ', N') from (V, ρ), and Lemme 8.4.3 proves independence of the choices of F and T up to isomorphism; 8.3.7 follows.

Compatibilities: N is unique, so the N of ρ⊗ρ' is N⊗1 + 1⊗N' and the N of ρ^∨ is −N^∨; restriction to W_L uses t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L} (ell-adic-tame-character (v)); induction: the monodromy of Ind ρ is the induced N because N is unique and Ind ρ restricted to an open subgroup of I_K is a sum of conjugates of ρ.
Invariants: σ ∈ I_K fixes v under ρ iff ρ'(σ)exp(t_ℓ(σ)N)v = v for all σ; taking σ ∈ J gives Nv = 0, and then ρ'(σ)v = v (Deligne 8.12, FSY §5.3.1).
acceptance: Check the conjugation relation against a chosen normalization by computing it for a Tate curve, where N is nonzero and the Frobenius eigenvalues differ by q: WD(V_ℓE_q) ≅ Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N ≠ 0), arithmetic Frobenius acting by q on ker N.

Check that the Frobenius semisimplification, the semisimplification and the full object are three different things by exhibiting a representation where they differ: V_ℓE_q ⊕ U with U unramified and Frobenius a nontrivial unipotent Jordan block (frobenius-semisimplification).

nodes.title: Frobenius semisimplification, semisimplification, and the three objects attached to a Weil–Deligne representation
nodes.statement: Let (V, r, N) be a Weil–Deligne representation over a field Ω of characteristic 0 and F ∈ W_K a geometric Frobenius lift. Let r(F) = s·u be the multiplicative Jordan–Chevalley decomposition (s semisimple, u unipotent, commuting; Tau Ceti LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.jordanDecomposition, Ω perfect). Then u commutes with r(W_K) and with N (Deligne 8.5: u is a polynomial in r(F), a power r(F)^m is central in r(W_K) because F^m acts trivially on I_K modulo the open kernel of r, and N is an eigenvector of conjugation by r(F)); the Frobenius semisimplification is (V, r^{F-ss}, N) with r^{F-ss}(F^nσ) := r(F^nσ)u^{-n} (n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K) (Deligne (8.5.1)). It is a Weil–Deligne representation, independent of the choice of F, with r^{F-ss}(F) = s. (V, r, N) is Frobenius-semisimple if r = r^{F-ss}, equivalently if r(w) is semisimple for one (equivalently every) w ∈ W_K ∖ I_K. Three objects are distinguished: (1) the full (V, r, N); (2) its Frobenius semisimplification (V, r^{F-ss}, N), which keeps N; (3) its semisimplification in the abelian category WD_Ω(K), which is (V^{ss}, r^{ss}, 0): the simple objects have N = 0 because ker N is a sub-object, and r^{ss} is the semisimplification of r as a representation of W_K. On the Galois side, for an ℓ-adic ρ, WD(ρ^{ss}) is (3) for WD(ρ), whereas WD(ρ)^{F-ss} is (2). Every Frobenius-semisimple indecomposable Weil–Deligne representation over an algebraically closed Ω is r_0 ⊗ Sp(n) for an irreducible representation r_0 of W_K and n ≥ 1, and the decomposition of a Frobenius-semisimple object into such is unique up to order.
hypotheses: Ω of characteristic 0 (perfect, so the Jordan decomposition exists over Ω)
Frobenius semisimplification semisimplifies only Frobenius; it does not kill N and is not the semisimplification of the Weil–Deligne representation
the classification of indecomposables needs Ω algebraically closed
proofSteps: Deligne 8.5: u is a polynomial in r(F) (Tau Ceti coe_semisimplePart_mem_adjoin); r(F)^m is central in r(W_K) modulo the open kernel I' of r on I_K for m with F^m acting trivially on I_K/I', so u (the unipotent part of r(F)^m to the power 1/m in the unipotent group) centralises r(W_K); N is an eigenvector of conjugation by r(F) (eigenvalue q^{-1}), so u commutes with N.

r^{F-ss} is a homomorphism with the same restriction to I_K and the relation for N holds because u commutes with N; independence of F: for w_1, w_2 ∉ I_K, r(w_1), r(w_2) have a common power up to the finite kernel, so u^n is the unipotent part of r(F^nσ) for every σ (Deligne 8.5).
Semisimplification: ker N is r-stable by the relation, so simple objects have N = 0; Jordan–Hölder in the finite-length category WD_Ω(K).

Classification: on an F-semisimple object, the monodromy filtration of N (the unique increasing filtration with N M_k ⊂ M_{k−2} and N^k : gr_k ≅ gr_{−k}) is r-stable with r(F) acting on the primitive parts; Deligne Proposition 8.9 uses the graded pieces; the decomposition r_0 ⊗ Sp(n) follows from the Jacobson–Morozov form of N (Ω characteristic 0).
acceptance: For V = Sp(2) ⊕ U, U two-dimensional unramified with r(F) a nontrivial unipotent Jordan block and N = 0 on U: the full object, its Frobenius semisimplification Sp(2) ⊕ 1² and its semisimplification (1 ⊕ ω ⊕ 1², 0) are pairwise non-isomorphic.
For WD(V_ℓA) of an abelian variety, the representation is already Frobenius-semisimple (Deligne Exemple 8.10).

nodes.title: The local Euler factor of a Weil–Deligne or ℓ-adic representation (geometric Frobenius)
nodes.statement: For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) over Ω and a geometric Frobenius lift Φ ∈ W_K, L(V, X) := det(1 − X·r(Φ) | (ker N)^{r(I_K)}) ∈ Ω[X], a polynomial with constant term 1 and degree dim (ker N)^{I_K}, independent of Φ (inertia acts trivially on the invariants); for Ω = C, L(V, s) = L(V, q^{-s})^{-1}. In Deligne's notation (3.5.1) Z(V; t) = det(1 − Ft^d, V^I)^{-1} with d = [k : F_p], so X = t^d = q^{-s}. For a continuous ℓ-adic representation ρ of G_K or W_K (ℓ ≠ p), L(ρ, X) := det(1 − Xρ(Φ) | V^{ρ(I_K)}) = L(WD(ρ), X) (Deligne 8.12). For F a number field, a finite place v and ρ a continuous representation of G_F over a field of characteristic 0 with v ∤ ℓ, L_v(ρ, X) := L(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}, X), independent of ι; if ρ is unramified at v, L_v(ρ, X) = det(1 − Xρ(Frob_v)^{-1}) = X^{dim V}·P_v(ρ^∨, X^{-1}). For a Tate module V_ℓA with H^1 = V_ℓA^∨: (V_ℓA^∨)^{I_v} is the dual of the coinvariants (V_ℓA)_{I_v}, so L_v(V_ℓA^∨, X) = det(1 − X·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v}) with arithmetic Frob_v; this equals det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓA^{I_v}) when I_v acts through a finite quotient, but not in general (Tate curve: 1 − X from coinvariants, 1 − qX from invariants).
hypotheses: GEOMETRIC Frobenius in the Euler factor, arithmetic Frobenius in P_v; the two are related by duality
(ker N)^{I} on the Weil–Deligne side, V^{ρ(I)} on the Galois side; these agree by the Weil–Deligne functor
taking inertia invariants does not commute with reduction modulo ℓ, so L_v of a residual representation is not the reduction of L_v of a lift
proofSteps: Independence of Φ: two geometric lifts differ by an element of I_K, which acts trivially on (ker N)^{I_K}; (ker N)^{I_K} is r(W_K)-stable because I_K is normal and r(w) preserves ker N by the relation.
L(ρ) = L(WD(ρ)): grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor gives V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N')^{ρ'(I_K)}, and ρ' = ρ on it.
Unramified case: ρ(Frob^{-1}) acts on V and det(1 − Xρ(Frob)^{-1}) = X^n det(X^{-1} − ρ^∨(Frob)) by transposition (frobenius-characteristic-polynomial).
acceptance: L(Q_ℓ(1), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X; for a Tate curve E_q over K, L(V_ℓE_q, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X and L(V_ℓE_q^∨, X) = 1 − X, the split multiplicative Euler factor.
For a totally ramified character χ (χ|_{I_K} ≠ 1), L(χ, X) = 1.

nodes.title: Local factors and Weil–Deligne representations of induced representations
nodes.statement: (a) Local: let L/K be a finite separable extension of nonarchimedean local fields with residue degree f, and (V, r, N) a Weil–Deligne representation of W_L over Ω. Then L(Ind_{W_L}^{W_K}(V, r, N), X) = L((V, r, N), X^f), and for an ℓ-adic representation ρ of W_L (or G_L), WD(Ind ρ) ≅ Ind WD(ρ), so L(Ind ρ, X) = L(ρ, X^f). (b) Global: let L/F be a finite extension of number fields, ρ a continuous representation of G_L over a field of characteristic 0 and v a finite place of F with v ∤ ℓ. Then L_v(Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ρ, X) = ∏_{w | v} L_w(ρ, X^{f(w|v)}). If ρ is unramified at every w | v and L/F is unramified at v, Ind ρ is unramified at v and P_v(Ind ρ, X) = ∏_{w | v} P_w(ρ, X^{f(w|v)}).
hypotheses: L/F finite (open subgroup G_L), places w of L above v with residue degrees f(w|v)
for the P_v formula: L/F unramified at v and ρ unramified at all w | v; otherwise only the L-factor statement holds
proofSteps: (a) Deligne Proposition 3.8(ii): (Ind V)^{I_K} = Ind_{W(k̄/ℓ)}^{W(k̄/k)}(V^{I_L}) as W(k̄/k)-representations (both are covariant functions on W(k̄/k) with values in V^{I_L}), and Lemme 3.9: for F_n the endomorphism of V^{⊕n} permuting cyclically and applying F once, det(1 − F_n X) = det(1 − F X^n). On the Weil–Deligne side the monodromy of the induced object is induced, and ker of the induced N is induced from ker N.
WD(Ind ρ) ≅ Ind WD(ρ): grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor (compatibility with induction).
(b) local-restriction gives (Ind ρ)_ι ≅ ⊕_{w|v} Ind_{G_{L_w}}^{G_{F_v}} ρ_{ι_w} (Mackey); apply (a) to each summand with f = f(w|v) and multiplicativity of L on direct sums.
P_v formula: at unramified v, L_v = reverse of P_v of the dual; apply the L-formula to ρ^∨ (Ind commutes with duals) and reverse, using that reversal is multiplicative and X ↦ X^f commutes with it.
acceptance: For L = Q(i), F = Q, ρ = 1: P_p(Ind 1, X) = (X − 1)² for p ≡ 1 mod 4 and X² − 1 = (X − 1)(X + 1) for p ≡ 3 mod 4.
For K'/K unramified of degree f and ρ = 1, L(Ind 1, X) = 1 − X^f.

nodes.title: The monodromy filtration and purity of Weil–Deligne representations
nodes.statement: Let (V, r, N) be a Weil–Deligne representation over Ω, ι : Ω → C an embedding (or Ω = Q̄_ℓ with a fixed ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C), F a geometric Frobenius lift and w ∈ Z. The monodromy filtration M_• of N is the unique increasing filtration of V with N M_a ⊂ M_{a−2} and N^a : gr^M_a V ≅ gr^M_{−a} V for all a ≥ 0; it is stable under r(W_K), so W_K acts on each gr^M_a V. An element α ∈ Ω^× is a q-Weil number of weight m if α is algebraic over Q and |τ(α)| = q^{m/2} for every field embedding τ : Q(α) → C. (V, r, N) is pure of weight w if, for every a, every eigenvalue of r(F) on gr^M_a V is a q-Weil number of weight w + a (FSY §5.3.2, geometric Frobenius). An ℓ-adic representation ρ of G_K (ℓ ≠ p) is pure of weight w if WD(ρ) is; mixed if V has an r-stable filtration with pure graded pieces.
hypotheses: geometric Frobenius: weights are measured with F, so Q_ℓ(1) = (ω, 0) is pure of weight −2
purity depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of the monodromy filtration for a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space (Deligne, Weil II 1.6.1; Jordan normal form in characteristic 0); its r-stability follows from uniqueness because r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} is a scalar multiple of N, which has the same monodromy filtration.
The Weil-number condition does not depend on the choice of F: two lifts differ by inertia, which acts through a finite group on each graded piece (N = 0 there).
acceptance: Sp(2) is pure of weight −1: a geometric Frobenius acts by q^{-1} (weight −2 = −1 + (−1)) on gr^M_{−1} = ker N and by 1 (weight 0 = −1 + 1) on gr^M_1 = V/ker N; hence V_ℓ(E_q) is pure of weight −1 and V_ℓ(E_q)^∨ of weight 1.
1 ⊕ ω with N = 0 is not pure (weights 0 and −2 on gr_0).

nodes.title: A representation with pure graded Weil–Deligne representation is pure, with the same L- and ε-factors (FSY Lemma 5.40)
nodes.statement: Let p ≠ ℓ be primes, K/Q_p finite (FSY: K = Q_p) and r : G_K → GL(V) a continuous ℓ-adic representation with a filtration 0 = V_0 ⊂ V_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_c = V by G_K-stable subspaces such that the Weil–Deligne representation of r̄ on V̄ = ⊕_i V_i/V_{i−1} is pure of weight w. Then WD(r) is pure of weight w, and r and r̄ have the same local L-factor and the same ε-factor: L(r, X) = L(r̄, X) and ε(WD(r), ψ, dx) = ε(WD(r̄), ψ, dx) (local-epsilon-factor).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p
the filtration is by G_K-stable subspaces; V̄ is the associated graded, not the semisimplification (though the conclusion passes to it)
the ε-statement is for complex coefficients after an embedding ι : Q̄_ℓ → C
proofSteps: FSY's proof (from a referee's sketch): the ε-factor of the Weil representation ρ in (5.33) depends only on the semisimplification of r by multiplicativity (local-epsilon-factor (1)).
With φ = ρ(F_p), the relation Nφ = pφN shows an eigenvalue α of φ on gr^M_a gives αp^{-b} on gr^M_{a−2b} with at least the same multiplicity, 0 ≤ b ≤ a.

By uniqueness of the monodromy operator (grothendieck-quasi-unipotence), N restricts to the monodromy of each V_i and induces the monodromy N̄ of V̄; det(1 − φT) = det(1 − φ̄T), and purity of (ρ̄, N̄) forces the monodromy filtrations of N and N̄ to have the same graded dimensions, so (ρ, N) is pure.

ρ|_{ker N} and ρ̄|_{ker N̄} have the same semisimplification; taking I_p-invariants is exact on Weil representations (I_p acts through finite quotients), giving equal det(1 − φT | ker(N)^{I}) and equal det(φT | V^{I}/ker(N)^{I}); hence equal L- and ε-factors by local-euler-factor and local-epsilon-factor.
acceptance: For the Tate curve, the filtration Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q has associated graded (1 ⊕ ω, 0), which is not pure, so the lemma does not apply; and indeed L(V_ℓE_q, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X differs from L(1 ⊕ ω, X) = (1 − X)(1 − q^{-1}X): the purity hypothesis cannot be dropped.
FSY apply the lemma for even k to replace {r_{k,ℓ}} by its semisimplification in the functional equation.

nodes.title: Deligne–Langlands local constants ε(V, ψ, dx) of Weil and Weil–Deligne representations
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, ψ : K → C^× a nontrivial continuous additive character, dx a Haar measure on K, and W_K the Weil group, with local class field theory normalised as in Deligne 2.3 (Art_K : K^× ≅ W_K^{ab} sending uniformisers to GEOMETRIC Frobenius lifts; the inverse of Tau Ceti's arithmetic artinMap normalisation). (Deligne Théorème 4.1) There is a unique function ε assigning to each isomorphism class of (K, K̄, ψ, dx, V, ρ), V a finite-dimensional complex representation of W_K with open kernel on I_K, a number ε(V, ψ, dx) ∈ C^×, such that: (1) ε is multiplicative in short exact sequences (hence defined on virtual representations); (2) ε(V, ψ, a·dx) = a^{dim V}ε(V, ψ, dx), so ε(V, ψ) is defined for virtual V of dimension 0; (3) for L/K finite inside K̄ and a virtual representation V_L of W_L of dimension 0, ε(Ind_{W_L}^{W_K} V_L, ψ) = ε(V_L, ψ ∘ Tr_{L/K}); (4) for dim V = 1, given by the quasi-character χ of K^× through Art_K, ε(V, ψ, dx) is Tate's local constant ε(χ, ψ, dx) (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1, translated from its ε(s, ω, ψ) normalisation). For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) over C: ε((V, r, N), ψ, dx) := ε(r, ψ, dx)·det(−r(Φ) | V^{r(I_K)}/(ker N)^{r(I_K)}) with Φ a geometric Frobenius lift (equivalently Deligne (8.12.4) ε = ε_0(r)·det(−F | V^I)^{-1}, V^I = (ker N)^{r(I)}); with the s-variable, ε(V, s) = ε(V ⊗ ω_s) (FSY (5.31)–(5.33)). For an ℓ-adic representation ρ (ℓ ≠ p) and ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C, ε(ρ, ψ, dx) := ε(ι WD(ρ), ψ, dx); it depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification and its ε_0-part only on the semisimplification.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (finite over Q_p): the Tau Ceti reciprocity isomorphism of ClassFieldTheory layer 9 is available only there; Deligne's theorem itself also covers archimedean and equal-characteristic local fields, which are recorded as a gap
normalisation of local class field theory: uniformiser ↔ geometric Frobenius (Deligne 2.3, CG18); Tau Ceti's artinMap must be inverted
uniqueness is local (Brauer induction); existence (Deligne §4) is global and uses Artin L-functions of number fields, whose functional equation has no owner (gap)
proofSteps: Uniqueness: every irreducible representation of W_K is r_0 ⊗ χ with r_0 of finite image (Deligne 4.10) and the finite-image part factors through Gal(L/K) for L/K finite Galois; Brauer's induction theorem (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction layer 6) writes any virtual representation of a finite group as a Z-combination of representations induced from one-dimensional characters of subgroups; (1), (3), (4) then determine ε (Deligne 4.1–4.3).
Reduction for existence: Deligne 4.10–4.11 reduce by the type decomposition to the existence of an α-theory of constants for each finite Galois K'/K and each quasi-character α (4.9 (*)).

Existence (Deligne 4.12–4.16): globalise K'/K as the completion of a Galois extension of number fields at a non-split place (Lemme 4.13, Krasner and weak approximation), choose an idele class character with prescribed ramification (Lemme 4.14), and define the local constant at v as the global constant of 3.12 (functional equation of Artin L-functions, from Brauer induction and Hecke's functional equation, AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation) divided by the product of the local constants at the other places, known by induction on ramification (Lemmes 4.15, 4.16 for unramified and highly ramified twists).

Weil–Deligne extension: the factor det(−r(Φ) | V^{I}/(ker N)^{I}) is multiplicative on Frobenius semisimplifications; FSY (5.33) and Deligne (8.12.4) agree because Deligne's ε_0(r) = ε(r)·det(−r(Φ) | V^{r(I)}) (Deligne (3.4.3.3) for characters).
acceptance: For an unramified character χ with n(ψ) = 0 and ∫_{O_K} dx = 1, ε(χ, ψ, dx) = 1 (Deligne (3.4.3.1)); for the WD representation Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N), ε(Sp(2), ψ, dx) = ε(1)ε(ω)·det(−r(Φ) | V/ker N) = −1 (Φ acts by 1 on V/ker N).
Unramified twists: ε(χω, ψ, dx) = ω(π^{n(ψ)+a(χ)})ε(χ, ψ, dx) for ω unramified (Deligne (3.4.3.5)), which must agree with AL.1's ε(s, ω, ψ) = ω(ϖ^ν)q^{(1/2−s)ν} after the change of normalisation.

nodes.title: Required examples: the cyclotomic character, an unramified character, and the Tate curve
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite with residue cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, Φ an arithmetic and F = Φ^{-1} a geometric Frobenius lift. (1) Cyclotomic: WD(Q_ℓ(1)) = (ω, 0) with ω(Φ) = q; P(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q, L(Q_ℓ(1), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, pure of weight −2; for K = Q_p and p ≠ ℓ this is the place-p component of χ_ℓ of G_Q. (2) Unramified character: for α ∈ O_E^×, WD(λ(α)) = (λ_W(α), 0), L(λ(α), X) = 1 − α^{-1}X, and λ^{geom}(γ) = λ(γ^{-1}). (3) Tate curve: for q_E ∈ K^× with v(q_E) > 0 and E = E_{q_E} the Tate curve, V_ℓE sits in 0 → Q_ℓ(1) → V_ℓE → Q_ℓ → 0, ρ(I_K) is infinite, and WD(V_ℓE) ≅ Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N) with N ≠ 0 mapping the quotient onto ker N = Q_ℓ(1) (N is v(q_E) times a generator, up to the scaling of Lemme 8.4.3); it is Frobenius-semisimple, not semisimple; its Frobenius semisimplification is itself and its semisimplification is (1 ⊕ ω, 0); L(V_ℓE, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, L(V_ℓE^∨, X) = 1 − X; it is pure of weight −1 (V_ℓE^∨ = H^1 of weight 1); the non-split twist by the unramified quadratic character η gives Sp(2) ⊗ η with L(V^∨, X) = 1 + X. (4) For ℓ | v(q_E) the residual E[ℓ] is unramified while V_ℓE is not.
hypotheses: the Tate curve and its Tate module are owned by Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 4 and R01.6; this node computes their Weil–Deligne data
ℓ ≠ p
proofSteps: (1): cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters (b) and grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor (unramified case).
(2): unramified-character-lambda and the unramified case of the functor.

(3): the Tate parametrisation K̄^×/q_E^Z ≅ E(K̄) (EllipticCurves layer 4) gives E[ℓ^n] as an extension of Z/ℓ^n by μ_{ℓ^n} whose extension class is the Kummer class of q_E; σ ∈ I_K acts by e_2 ↦ e_2 + v(q_E)t_ℓ(σ)e_1 (Kummer theory with t_ℓ), so ρ(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) with N e_2 = v(q_E)e_1; Frobenius acts by q on e_1 and by 1 on the quotient; then local-euler-factor, purity-of-weil-deligne-representations, frobenius-semisimplification.
(4): the Kummer class of q_E in K^×/K^{×ℓ} is unramified iff ℓ | v(q_E).
acceptance: The three Euler factors 1 − q^{-1}X, 1 − X, 1 + X are recovered for Q_ℓ(1), the split and the non-split multiplicative H^1.

The relation r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN is verified on the Tate curve with Φ arithmetic, and r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N with F geometric, matching PadicHodgeTheory R06.3's p-adic computation r(Φ) = diag(p, 1).

nodes.title: Upper-numbering breaks and the Swan conductor of a representation with finite wild image
nodes.statement: Local setting (fixed throughout R01.3): K is a field complete for a discrete valuation v_K normalised by v_K(K^×) = Z, with ring of integers O_K, maximal ideal m_K and PERFECT residue field k of characteristic p > 0; K has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic (0, p)) or p (equal characteristic, e.g. k((t))). Tier (F): k finite, i.e. K is a nonarchimedean local field (Mathlib IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, which covers finite extensions of Q_p and of F_p((t))). Tier (P): k perfect and arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed, as for F̄_q((t)) or the completion of K^ur). G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K with its Krull topology; I_K ⊇ P_K are inertia and wild inertia (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4). Coefficients: F is a field of characteristic different from p (characteristic 0, e.g. C, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ; or a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p), V a finite-dimensional F-vector space and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation in the sense of R01.1 (discrete topology for finite F, the ℓ-adic topology for E, the usual topology for C) such that ρ(P_K) is finite. Finiteness of ρ(P_K) is automatic for finite F, for F = C (continuity forces finite image) and for F = E finite over Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (ρ(G_K) lies in a compact GL(Λ) whose open pro-ℓ subgroup meets the pro-p group ρ(P_K) trivially); it is a hypothesis when ℓ = p. (i) Absolute upper filtration. For real u ≥ −1 let G_K^u ⊆ G_K be the closed normal subgroup of those σ whose restriction to every finite Galois L/K inside the fixed algebraic closure lies in Gal(L/K)^u, the upper-numbering group of LocalFieldsRamification layer 3; put G_K^{u+} := closure of ⋃_{w>u} G_K^w. Then G_K^{−1} = G_K, G_K^0 = I_K, G_K^{0+} = P_K, the image of G_K^u in Gal(L/K) is Gal(L/K)^u, and ⋂_u G_K^u = 1. (ii) Breaks. There is a unique decomposition V = ⊕_{λ ∈ Q, λ ≥ 0} V(λ) into G_K-stable subspaces, almost all zero, with V(0) = V^{ρ(P_K)} and, for λ > 0, V(λ)^{ρ(G_K^λ)} = 0 and V(λ)^{ρ(G_K^{λ+})} = V(λ). The λ with V(λ) ≠ 0 are the breaks (slopes) of V; the largest is the highest break. (iii) Swan conductor. Sw(V) := Σ_λ λ·dim_F V(λ) = ∫_0^∞ codim_V V^{ρ(G_K^u)} du = Σ_{i ≥ 1} (|G_i|/|G_0|)·codim_V V^{ρ(G_i)}, where in the last expression G = Gal(L/K) for any finite Galois L/K with ρ trivial on Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ P_K, G_i are its lower-numbering groups (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3), and G_i (i ≥ 1) acts on V through lifts in P_K, which is well defined because G_i is the image of G_K^{φ_{L/K}(i)} ⊆ P_K. Sw(V) ∈ Q_{≥0}; its integrality is R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality. Sw depends only on the restriction of ρ to P_K together with the filtration, and is an isomorphism invariant.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued with perfect residue field of characteristic p; tier (F) is supplied by LocalFieldsRamification layers 3–4, tier (P) rests on the gap 'ramification filtration over a perfect infinite residue field'
char F ≠ p and ρ(P_K) finite; for F a finite extension of Q_p with p the residue characteristic and ρ(P_K) infinite, Sw is NOT defined here (p-adic Hodge theory owns that case)
the upper numbering is the one compatible with quotients; the lower-numbering sum is taken over a finite Galois L/K large enough for ρ|P_K, never over Gal(L/K) for an arbitrary L
proofSteps: Construct G_K^u as the intersection over finite Galois L/K of the preimages of Gal(L/K)^u; compatibility of these preimages in towers is upperRamificationGroup_quotient (Herbrand's theorem, LocalFieldsRamification layer 3); G_K^0 = I_K and G_K^{0+} = P_K follow from the layer-4 identifications of the images of I_K and P_K in finite quotients with G_0 and G_1.

Break decomposition: ρ(P_K) = H is a finite p-group and char F ≠ p, so V|_H is semisimple; the subgroups ρ(G_K^u), u > 0, form a decreasing family of normal subgroups of ρ(G_K) contained in H with finitely many jumps, and V(λ) is the image of the idempotent e_{G^{λ+}} − e_{G^λ} (e_N = |N|^{-1} Σ_{n∈N} n), which commutes with ρ(G_K) because each ρ(G_K^u) is normal; uniqueness from the defining invariant conditions (Ulmer 2016 §2; Katz's slope decomposition).

Equality of the three expressions for Sw: on V(λ) the function u ↦ codim V^{ρ(G^u)} is dim V(λ) on [0, λ] and 0 after, giving the integral; the substitution u = φ_{L/K}(t), dφ/dt = |G_t|/|G_0| (Herbrand function, LocalFieldsRamification layer 3) turns the integral into the lower-numbering sum, which is therefore independent of L (DDT §1.1 gives the integral form; Serre 1987 (1.2.1)–(1.2.2) the lower form).
acceptance: Q_2(√−1)/Q_2: the nontrivial character χ_{−4} has upper break 1 and Sw = 1 (lower filtration G_1 = G, G_2 = 1 for the uniformiser 1 + i); Q_2(√2)/Q_2: the character χ_8 has break 2 and Sw = 2 (v(σ√2 − √2) = 3), matching the LocalFieldsRamification example in which Q_2(√2) has different exponent 3

Over L = Q_2(ζ_8) (lower jumps 1 and 3, |G_0| = |G_1| = 4, |G_2| = |G_3| = 2), the weighted sum for χ_8 is 1 + 2/4 + 2/4 = 2 = Sw(χ_8), the same value as over Q_2(√2): independence of the finite quotient on a wild example at 2
A tamely ramified character (p ∤ order of χ(I_K)) has the single break 0 and Sw = 0

nodes.title: The Artin conductor exponent and its wild part
nodes.statement: Local setting (fixed throughout R01.3): K is a field complete for a discrete valuation v_K normalised by v_K(K^×) = Z, with ring of integers O_K, maximal ideal m_K and PERFECT residue field k of characteristic p > 0; K has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic (0, p)) or p (equal characteristic, e.g. k((t))). Tier (F): k finite, i.e. K is a nonarchimedean local field (Mathlib IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, which covers finite extensions of Q_p and of F_p((t))). Tier (P): k perfect and arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed, as for F̄_q((t)) or the completion of K^ur). G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K with its Krull topology; I_K ⊇ P_K are inertia and wild inertia (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4). Coefficients: F is a field of characteristic different from p (characteristic 0, e.g. C, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ; or a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p), V a finite-dimensional F-vector space and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation in the sense of R01.1 (discrete topology for finite F, the ℓ-adic topology for E, the usual topology for C) such that ρ(P_K) is finite. Finiteness of ρ(P_K) is automatic for finite F, for F = C (continuity forces finite image) and for F = E finite over Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (ρ(G_K) lies in a compact GL(Λ) whose open pro-ℓ subgroup meets the pro-p group ρ(P_K) trivially); it is a hypothesis when ℓ = p. The Artin conductor exponent is a(V) := codim_V V^{ρ(I_K)} + Sw(V) = (dim V − dim V^{ρ(I_K)}) + Sw(V), with Sw from R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor; ε(V) := codim V^{ρ(I_K)} is the tame part and Sw(V) = b(V) the wild part. When ρ(I_K) is finite and G = Gal(L/K) for a finite Galois L/K with ρ trivial on Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ I_K, a(V) = Σ_{i ≥ 0} (|G_i|/|G_0|)·dim_F(V/V^{G_i}) (Serre (1.2.1)) = dim V/V^{G_0} + b(V) (Serre (1.2.2)). For an ℓ-adic representation (ℓ ≠ p) with infinite inertia image, V^{ρ(I_K)} is the actual subspace of inertia invariants; it equals (ker N)^{r(I_K)} for the Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) of R01.2, which is where the monodromy term enters (R01.3/conductor-of-a-weil-deligne-representation). For a residual representation ρ̄ over a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, a(ρ̄) uses ρ̄'s own (finite) inertia action, never that of a lift. Representations over fields of characteristic p (for instance mod p representations of G_K with K of residue characteristic p) are excluded, as in Serre 1987, which restricts N to places prime to p. a(V) ∈ Q_{≥0}; it is a nonnegative integer by R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality, and the exponent used in every global conductor.
hypotheses: same local setting and coefficients as R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor
the tame part is the codimension of the invariants of the ACTUAL inertia image (for ℓ-adic ρ this already contains the monodromy contribution)
integrality is a theorem (R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality), not visible from the formula; the wild term is never omitted at p = 2 or 3
proofSteps: Define a(V) by the displayed formula; for finite inertia image the identity with Serre's lower-numbering sum is the i = 0 term (|G_0|/|G_0|)·codim V^{G_0} plus the Swan sum of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor (Serre 1987 §1.2).
Independence of L and of the extension of the valuation: inherited from the Swan term (Herbrand) and from I_K being normal in G_K (conjugate subspaces of invariants have equal dimension).

For ℓ-adic ρ = (r, N) after R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor: a vector fixed by ρ(I_K) is fixed by the open subgroup J ⊆ I_K on which r is trivial, where ρ(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) with t_ℓ(σ) ≠ 0 for some σ ∈ J, so Nv = 0, and then r(σ)v = v for σ ∈ I_K; conversely; hence V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N)^{r(I_K)} (Ulmer 2016 §3).

nodes.title: Integrality and independence of choices of Artin and Swan conductors
nodes.statement: Local setting (fixed throughout R01.3): K is a field complete for a discrete valuation v_K normalised by v_K(K^×) = Z, with ring of integers O_K, maximal ideal m_K and PERFECT residue field k of characteristic p > 0; K has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic (0, p)) or p (equal characteristic, e.g. k((t))). Tier (F): k finite, i.e. K is a nonarchimedean local field (Mathlib IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, which covers finite extensions of Q_p and of F_p((t))). Tier (P): k perfect and arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed, as for F̄_q((t)) or the completion of K^ur). G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K with its Krull topology; I_K ⊇ P_K are inertia and wild inertia (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4). Coefficients: F is a field of characteristic different from p (characteristic 0, e.g. C, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ; or a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p), V a finite-dimensional F-vector space and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation in the sense of R01.1 (discrete topology for finite F, the ℓ-adic topology for E, the usual topology for C) such that ρ(P_K) is finite. Finiteness of ρ(P_K) is automatic for finite F, for F = C (continuity forces finite image) and for F = E finite over Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (ρ(G_K) lies in a compact GL(Λ) whose open pro-ℓ subgroup meets the pro-p group ρ(P_K) trivially); it is a hypothesis when ℓ = p. Then: (a) Sw(V) and a(V) are nonnegative integers. (b) They do not depend on the finite Galois extension used to compute them, on the choice of algebraic closure of K or of the extension of v_K, and are invariant under isomorphism and under extension of the coefficient field. (c) a(V) = 0 iff ρ(I_K) = 1 (unramified); a(V) = codim V^{ρ(I_K)} iff Sw(V) = 0 iff ρ(P_K) = 1 (tamely ramified). (d) Dimension one: for a continuous character χ: G_K → F^× with χ(P_K) finite, a(χ) = 0 if χ is unramified and a(χ) = 1 + u(χ) otherwise, where u(χ) := max{u ≥ 0 : χ(G_K^u) ≠ 1} (and u(χ) = 0 when χ is tamely ramified) is the upper break, an integer by the Hasse–Arf theorem.
hypotheses: tier (F): all inputs exist (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3 Hasse–Arf); tier (P): Hasse–Arf and Herbrand's quotient theorem over a perfect infinite residue field are the recorded gap
char F ≠ p; for char F = ℓ > 0 the reduction to characteristic 0 uses ℓ ≠ p
proofSteps: Independence (b): the integral formula of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor is intrinsic to G_K; changing the algebraic closure conjugates ρ by an isomorphism, and conjugate subgroups have invariant subspaces of equal dimension.
(c) is read off the formula: every term is ≥ 0, the i = 0 term vanishes iff G_0 acts trivially, and the wild sum vanishes iff G_1 = image of P_K acts trivially (Serre 1987 (b), (c)).

(d): χ factors through Gal(L/K) with L/K finite abelian (cyclic) and Sw(χ) = u(χ) by the integral formula; the Hasse–Arf theorem (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3, hasseArf, Serre LF V §7) makes the upper jump an integer.

Reduction of (a) to a finite Galois group: a(V) depends only on ρ|_{I_K}; with L/K finite Galois such that ρ is trivial on Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ I_K and L_0 = L ∩ K^ur, the restriction W of ρ to I_K is a representation of Gal(L/L_0) = G_0, and a_K(V) = a_{L_0}(W) because L_0/K is unramified (R01.3/additivity-twist-and-unramified-invariance (d) applied before integrality, which only uses the rational-valued formula). So it suffices to treat representations of G = Gal(L/K) of a finite Galois extension.

Characteristic 0 (Artin's theorem, Serre LF VI §2 Thm 1; Serre 1961 Théorème 2): by Brauer's induction theorem (InductionRestriction layer 6) the character of V is a Z-combination of Ind_H^G ψ with ψ one-dimensional; a(Ind_H^G ψ) = δ(L^H/K)ψ(1) + f(L^H/K)a(ψ) by the restriction identity a_G|_H = δ(L^H/K)·r_H + f(L^H/K)·a_H for the Artin character (proved from the Hilbert different formula of LocalFieldsRamification layer 3 and Frobenius reciprocity, the local argument recorded in R01.3/induction-formula-for-conductors, which does not use integrality), an integer by (d) for the abelian quotient cut out by ψ. Hence a(V) ∈ Z, and a(V) ≥ 0 from the formula.

Characteristic ℓ ≠ p: W|_{G_1} is semisimple (ℓ ∤ |G_1|) and Sw(W) depends only on it. Group the G_1-isotypic components of W into G_0-orbits; for θ in an orbit with stabiliser T ⊇ G_1, T/G_1 is cyclic, so the characteristic-zero lift θ̃ of θ extends to T (Clifford theory and the vanishing of the Schur multiplier of a cyclic group, InductionRestriction layers 5 and 7), and the orbit contributes (multiplicity of θ)·Sw(Ind_T^{G_0} θ̃), an integer by the characteristic-0 case; the tame part is an integer dimension (Serre 1987 cites Serre, Linear representations §19.3, for this integrality of b(V)).
acceptance: Wild at 2: Sw(χ_{−4}) = 1 and Sw(χ_8) = 2 are integers although the lower-numbering weights over Q_2(ζ_8) are 1/2
Wild at 3: the cubic character of Q_3 cutting out the degree-3 subfield of Q_3(ζ_9) has a = 2 (conductor 9) and Sw = 1
Equal characteristic: the Artin–Schreier character of R01.3/artin-schreier-swan-conductor has Sw = m ∈ Z (Deligne 1974 (8.13))

nodes.title: The conductor of a Weil–Deligne representation, with its monodromy term
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field (tier (F) of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor) with residue cardinality q, W_K its Weil group (ClassFieldTheory layer 9) and (r, N) a Weil–Deligne representation of W_K on a finite-dimensional vector space V over a field F of characteristic 0 (R01.2/weil-deligne-representation: r continuous with r(I_K) finite, N nilpotent, r(w) N r(w)^{-1} = q^{v'(w)} N with v'(arithmetic Frobenius lift) = 1). ker N is r(W_K)-stable and r(I_K) acts on it. Define a(r, N) := Sw(r) + dim V − dim (ker N)^{r(I_K)}, where Sw(r) is the Swan conductor of r|_{P_K} (R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor, which only uses G_K^u ⊆ P_K ⊆ W_K for u > 0). Equivalently a(r, N) = a(r) + dim V^{r(I_K)} − dim (ker N)^{r(I_K)}, with a(r) = codim V^{r(I_K)} + Sw(r) the conductor of r alone. Comparison: for ℓ ≠ p, F = E finite over Q_ℓ (or Q̄_ℓ) and ρ: G_K → GL(V) continuous with WD(ρ) = (r, N) (R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor), a(ρ) = a(r, N), independently of the Frobenius lift and of the homomorphism t_ℓ used to build WD(ρ); and a(r, N) = a(r^{F-ss}, N) for the Frobenius semisimplification (R01.2/frobenius-semisimplification).
hypotheses: finite residue field (the Weil group needs the Frobenius); characteristic-0 coefficients
the monodromy term is dim V^{r(I_K)} − dim (ker N)^{r(I_K)} ≥ 0; it is not dim V − dim ker N
proofSteps: (ker N) is stable: r(w)N r(w)^{-1} is a nonzero multiple of N. For σ ∈ I_K, v'(σ) = 0, so r(σ) commutes with N.

a(ρ) = a(WD(ρ)): Sw(ρ) = Sw(r) because ρ and r agree on P_K (t_ℓ is trivial on P_K); and V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N)^{r(I_K)} (R01.3/artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part), so codim V^{ρ(I_K)} = dim V − dim (ker N)^{r(I_K)} (Ulmer 2016 §3: the definitions of Deligne and Serre agree).
Independence of choices and Frobenius semisimplification: both only change r on W_K \ I_K or by conjugation, and the formula only involves r|_{I_K} and ker N.
acceptance: sp(2): r unramified and N ≠ 0 (rank one): a = 0 + 2 − 1 = 1 (Steinberg exponent 1); sp(n) ⊗ (unramified χ): a = n − 1
sp(2) ⊗ χ with χ ramified: (ker N)^{r(I_K)} = 0, so a = 2·a(χ) (e.g. = 2 for χ tamely ramified)
The ℓ-adic Tate module of a Tate curve has WD = sp(2)-type with a = 1, agreeing with R01.3/artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part

uses.how: a(r, N) = a(r) + dim V^{I} − dim (ker N)^{I}; a = 1 for the Steinberg parameter, giving KW I §8.4's dyadic bound

nodes.title: Global conductors and the prime-to-p conductor N(ρ̄)
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and ρ: G_F → GL(V) a continuous representation (R01.1) on a finite-dimensional vector space over a field C_ρ, unramified outside a finite set of places (R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set). Let Σ be a finite set of finite places of F containing every finite place whose residue characteristic is the characteristic of C_ρ if that characteristic is positive, and every place above ℓ if ρ is ℓ-adic (C_ρ ⊆ Q̄_ℓ with the ℓ-adic topology); Σ may be empty for an Artin representation (C_ρ = C, finite image). For v ∉ Σ let a_v(ρ) := a(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) (R01.2/local-restriction, R01.3/artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part; ρ(P_{F_v}) is finite at such v). The Σ-conductor is the ideal N^Σ(ρ) := ∏_{v ∉ Σ finite} 𝔭_v^{a_v(ρ)} of O_F (a finite product); N(ρ) := N^∅(ρ) for Artin representations; for ℓ-adic ρ, N^{(ℓ)}(ρ) := N^{{v | ℓ}}(ρ) is the prime-to-ℓ conductor (the exponent at v | ℓ is not defined in this layer). For ρ̄ over a finite field of characteristic p, N(ρ̄) := N^{{v | p}}(ρ̄) is the prime-to-p conductor; it is prime to p by construction. For F = Q every such ideal is identified with its positive generator, e.g. N(ρ̄) = ∏_{l ≠ p} l^{n(l, ρ̄)} (Serre 1987 (1.2.3)).
hypotheses: the local exponent at v uses ρ restricted to a decomposition group through a chosen embedding ι_v; conjugate embeddings give isomorphic local representations and equal exponents
places in Σ are omitted, not given exponent 0 by convention: N(ρ̄) says nothing about ramification at p
proofSteps: a_v(ρ) = 0 for v unramified (R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality (c)), so the product is finite; integrality of each a_v from R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality.
Independence of ι_v: a different embedding conjugates the decomposition group, and the local conductor is an isomorphism invariant.
Over Q identify ideals of Z with positive integers through Ideal.absNorm / the generator.
acceptance: For the nontrivial character of Gal(Q(√−1)/Q), N = 4; for Ind_{G_{Q(√−1)}}^{G_Q} 1 = 1 ⊕ χ_{−4}, N = 4 = |d_{Q(√−1)}|
For E = 11a1 and ℓ = 5: N_E = 11 but N(ρ̄_{E,5}) = 1, because 5 divides v_11(Δ_min) = 5 (R01.3/residual-elliptic-conductor-away-from-ell)

nodes.title: Additivity, duality, twists and base change of conductors
nodes.statement: Local setting (fixed throughout R01.3): K is a field complete for a discrete valuation v_K normalised by v_K(K^×) = Z, with ring of integers O_K, maximal ideal m_K and PERFECT residue field k of characteristic p > 0; K has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic (0, p)) or p (equal characteristic, e.g. k((t))). Tier (F): k finite, i.e. K is a nonarchimedean local field (Mathlib IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, which covers finite extensions of Q_p and of F_p((t))). Tier (P): k perfect and arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed, as for F̄_q((t)) or the completion of K^ur). G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K with its Krull topology; I_K ⊇ P_K are inertia and wild inertia (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4). Coefficients: F is a field of characteristic different from p (characteristic 0, e.g. C, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ; or a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p), V a finite-dimensional F-vector space and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation in the sense of R01.1 (discrete topology for finite F, the ℓ-adic topology for E, the usual topology for C) such that ρ(P_K) is finite. Finiteness of ρ(P_K) is automatic for finite F, for F = C (continuity forces finite image) and for F = E finite over Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (ρ(G_K) lies in a compact GL(Λ) whose open pro-ℓ subgroup meets the pro-p group ρ(P_K) trivially); it is a hypothesis when ℓ = p. (a) Exact sequences: for 0 → V′ → V → V″ → 0 of such representations, Sw(V) = Sw(V′) + Sw(V″) and a(V) ≥ a(V′) + a(V″), with equality iff V^{I_K} → V″^{I_K} is surjective, in particular when ρ(I_K) is finite of order invertible in F; a is additive on direct sums; a(V) ≥ a(V^ss) and Sw(V) = Sw(V^ss). (b) Duals: Sw(V^∨) = Sw(V); if ρ(I_K) is finite of order invertible in F, a(V^∨) = a(V). (c) Twists by a continuous character χ: G_K → F^× with χ(P_K) finite: if χ is unramified, a(V ⊗ χ) = a(V) and Sw(V ⊗ χ) = Sw(V); if χ is tamely ramified, the breaks and Sw of V ⊗ χ equal those of V; if the break u(χ) > 0 exceeds every break of V, then every break of V ⊗ χ equals u(χ), Sw(V ⊗ χ) = u(χ)·dim V and a(V ⊗ χ) = a(χ)·dim V. (d) Base change: for K′/K finite unramified (tier (F)), or K′ the completion of K^ur (tier (P)), a_{K′}(V|_{G_{K′}}) = a_K(V) and Sw likewise; for K′/K finite and tamely ramified with ramification index e, every break is multiplied by e and Sw_{K′}(V|_{G_{K′}}) = e·Sw_K(V). (e) Coefficients: a and Sw are unchanged by extension of F.
hypotheses: same local setting and coefficients as R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor; (d) for the completion of K^ur needs tier (P)
proofSteps: (a): V|_{P_K} is semisimple (|ρ(P_K)| invertible in F), so dim V^{ρ(G_K^u)} is additive for u > 0 and the integral formula gives additivity of Sw; for inertia invariants 0 → V′^I → V^I → V″^I is exact, hence codim V^I ≥ codim V′^I + codim V″^I, with equality iff the last map is onto (always when |ρ(I_K)| is invertible, by averaging). Iterating along a composition series gives a(V) ≥ a(V^ss).
(b): for a finite group H of order invertible in F, dim (V^∨)^H = dim V^H (the averaging idempotent is self-dual).

(c): unramified χ is trivial on I_K; tame χ is trivial on G_K^u for u > 0; for u(χ) larger than the breaks of V, G_K^{u(χ)} acts trivially on V and by a nontrivial scalar on V ⊗ χ, while G_K^{u(χ)+} acts trivially on both (Ulmer 2016 §4, a(ρ ⊗ χ) = deg(ρ) a(χ)).

(d): I_{K′} = I_K and G_{K′}^u = G_K^u for K′/K unramified (ψ_{K′/K} = id); for K′/K tame of index e, P_K ⊆ G_{K′} and G_{K′}^{eu} = G_K^u for u > 0 (Herbrand functions of LocalFieldsRamification layer 3; Serre 1970 §2.1 remarks).
(e): invariant subspaces commute with extension of scalars.
acceptance: Strict inequality in (a): the ℓ-adic Steinberg representation has a = 1 while both one-dimensional graded pieces of its monodromy filtration are unramified (a = 0)
Twist: for V unramified of dimension n and χ = χ_8 over Q_2, a(V ⊗ χ_8) = 3n
Tame base change: for K′ = Q_3(√3), totally and tamely ramified of degree 2 over Q_3, the cubic character of conductor 9 has break 1 over Q_3 and break 2 over K′

nodes.title: The induction (conductor–discriminant) formula
nodes.statement: Local: in the local setting of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor, let L/K be a finite separable extension inside K^sep, with residue degree f = f(L/K), and let V be a representation of G_L as in R01.3 (char F ≠ p, finite wild image). Then Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V (R01.1/continuous-induction) has finite wild image and a_K(Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V) = δ(L/K)·dim V + f·a_L(V), where δ(L/K) = v_K(𝔡_{L/K}) = f·d(L/K) is the discriminant exponent (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3); equivalently dim (Ind V)^{I_K} = f·dim V^{I_L} and Sw_K(Ind V) = f·Sw_L(V) + (δ(L/K) − [L:K] + f)·dim V. In particular a_K(Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} 1) = δ(L/K) (conductor–discriminant formula). Global: for a finite extension F′/F of number fields, a representation ρ of G_{F′} as in R01.3/global-conductor-and-prime-to-p-conductor and Σ, Σ′ = places above Σ: N_F^Σ(Ind_{G_{F′}}^{G_F} ρ) = (𝔡_{F′/F})_Σ^{dim ρ}·Nm_{F′/F}(N_{F′}^{Σ′}(ρ)), with (𝔡_{F′/F})_Σ the part of the relative discriminant prime to Σ. For F = Q, F′ = M quadratic and ψ a finite-order character of G_M: N(Ind_{G_M}^{G_Q} ψ) = |d_M|·Nm_{M/Q}(𝔣(ψ)), at every prime including 2, where 𝔣(ψ) = N_M(ψ) is the Artin conductor of ψ (equal to the conductor of the associated Hecke character by the ClassFieldTheory layer 7 comparison requested in R01.3/artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part); for ℓ-adic ψ the same holds for prime-to-ℓ parts.
hypotheses: L/K separable (always true for perfect k and the extensions arising from G_K); the rational form needs no integrality
the global formula uses the relative discriminant ideal, not the absolute discriminant of F′ unless F = Q
proofSteps: Mackey: Res_{I_K} Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V decomposes over the f double cosets I_K\G_K/G_L into inductions from conjugates of I_L (R01.1/mackey-decomposition), so dim (Ind V)^{I_K} = f·dim V^{I_L} by Frobenius reciprocity.

Swan identity: reduce to a finite Galois M/K through which ρ|P factors, with H = Gal(M/L) ≤ G = Gal(M/K); the Artin character satisfies a_G|_H = δ(L/K)·r_H + f·a_H (Serre LF VI §2 Prop 4; Serre 1961 n° 4 with the Führerdiskriminantenproduktformel), whose proof is the Hilbert formula d(M/K) = Σ_i (|G_i| − 1) and the tower formula for the different (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3); Frobenius reciprocity converts it into the displayed formula.

Global: Res_{G_{F_v}} Ind_{G_{F′}}^{G_F} ρ = ⊕_{w | v} Ind_{G_{F′_w}}^{G_{F_v}} ρ|_{G_{F′_w}} (R01.1/mackey-decomposition with NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5 completions); apply the local formula and the localisation of the different/discriminant (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 6), Σ_{w|v} δ(F′_w/F_v) = v_𝔭(𝔡_{F′/F}) and Σ_w f_w a_w = v_𝔭(Nm 𝔑).
Quadratic case: |d_M| = Nm of the relative discriminant over Q.
acceptance: Q(√−1): N(Ind 1) = N(1 ⊕ χ_{−4}) = 4 = |d|; Q(√2): N(1 ⊕ χ_8) = 8 = |d|; this checks the dyadic wild case
CM: E: y² = x³ − x has conductor 32 = 2^5 (Tate's algorithm gives type III at 2 with v(Δ_min) = 6, Ogg: f_2 = 5); with V_ℓ E ≅ Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} ψ, the formula 32 = 4·Nm(𝔣(ψ)) forces Nm 𝔣(ψ) = 8

nodes.title: Reduction does not increase the conductor at primes different from the coefficient characteristic
nodes.statement: In the local setting of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor (tier (F) or (P)), let ℓ ≠ p, E/Q_ℓ finite with ring of integers O_E and residue field k_E, ρ: G_K → GL(V) continuous on a finite-dimensional E-vector space, Λ ⊂ V a G_K-stable O_E-lattice (R01.1/integral-model) and ρ̄_Λ := Λ/m_EΛ. Then: (a) Sw(ρ̄_Λ) = Sw(ρ) = Sw(ρ̄_Λ^{ss}); (b) a(ρ̄_Λ) = a(ρ) − (dim_{k_E} ρ̄_Λ^{I_K} − dim_E V^{I_K}) ≤ a(ρ), with equality iff Λ^{I_K} ⊗ k_E → (Λ/m_EΛ)^{I_K} is onto, in particular when ρ(I_K) is finite of order prime to ℓ; (c) a(ρ̄_Λ^{ss}) ≤ a(ρ̄_Λ) ≤ a(ρ); a(ρ̄_Λ^{ss}) does not depend on Λ, while a(ρ̄_Λ) can. Global: for ρ: G_F → GL(V) ℓ-adic, N^{(ℓ)}(ρ̄_Λ) divides N^{(ℓ)}(ρ), with quotient ∏_{v ∤ ℓ} 𝔭_v^{dim ρ̄^{I_v} − dim ρ^{I_v}}; in particular N(ρ̄^{ss}) | N^{(ℓ)}(ρ) for residual characteristic ℓ.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p is essential: at places above ℓ no comparison is asserted
the residual conductor uses the actual inertia action of ρ̄_Λ, so it depends on Λ; only the semisimplification is lattice-independent
proofSteps: Swan: H = ρ(P_K) is a finite p-group with ℓ ∤ |H|; for every subgroup H′ ≤ H the idempotent e_{H′} = |H′|^{-1} Σ h lies in O_E[H], so Λ = e_{H′}Λ ⊕ (1 − e_{H′})Λ and rank Λ^{H′} = dim_E V^{H′} = dim_{k_E}(Λ/m_EΛ)^{H′}; insert into the integral formula (DDT Lemma 2.7; Ulmer 2016 §2: δ(ρ^{ss}) = δ(ρ|P_F) = δ(ρ)).

Tame part: Λ^{I_K} = Λ ∩ V^{I_K} is saturated (Λ/Λ^{I_K} is torsion-free), so Λ^{I_K}/m_EΛ^{I_K} → (Λ/m_EΛ)^{I_K} is injective and dim ρ̄^{I_K} ≥ dim V^{I_K}; if |ρ(I_K)| is prime to ℓ the averaging idempotent gives surjectivity.
(c): inertia invariants are left exact, so along a composition series dim (ρ̄^{ss})^{I_K} ≥ dim ρ̄^{I_K}; lattice-independence of ρ̄^{ss} is R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence.
Global: apply (b) at each v ∤ ℓ via R01.2/local-restriction.
acceptance: Steinberg: a(ρ) = 1; for the lattice with N ≢ 0 mod ℓ, ρ̄ is a nonsplit unipotent extension with a(ρ̄) = 1; for a lattice with N ≡ 0 mod ℓ, a(ρ̄) = 0; in both cases a(ρ̄^{ss}) = 0
11a1, ℓ = 5: a_{11}(V_5 E) = 1 and a_{11}(E[5]) = 0 since E[5] is unramified at 11
KW I §8.4 (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.4): a dyadic exponent 1 in characteristic zero bounds v_2(N(ρ̄′)) ≤ 1

nodes.title: Tame and small conductor computations
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of cardinality q and characteristic p, and V a representation as in R01.3/artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part. (a) a(V) = 0 iff V is unramified. (b) If ρ(P_K) = 1 then a(V) = codim V^{I_K}. (c) Steinberg: a two-dimensional Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) with r unramified and N ≠ 0 has a = 1; so does V_ℓ of a Tate curve (ℓ ≠ p). (d) Exponent 2: if dim V = 2, ρ(P_K) = 1 and V^{I_K} = 0 then a(V) = 2; this holds for ρ̄|_{I_K} ≅ ψ ⊕ ψ′ with ψ, ψ′ nontrivial tame characters of I_K (for example ψ′ = ψ^q with ψ ≠ 1 of order prime to p, the good-dihedral case), and for Ind_{G_{K_2}}^{G_K} of a tamely ramified character of the unramified quadratic K_2 not factoring through the norm. (e) One-dimensional: a tamely ramified ramified character has a = 1; over Q_2 the six ramified quadratic characters have a = 2 (fields Q_2(√−1), Q_2(√3)) or a = 3 (fields Q_2(√±2), Q_2(√±6)); over Q_3 a ramified character of order 3 has a = 2 (conductor 9). These are the wild contributions at 2 and 3 that the tame formula (b) would omit.
hypotheses: finite residue field (the examples are over Q_2, Q_3 or with ψ^q)
proofSteps: (a), (b) are R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality (c).
(c): R01.3/conductor-of-a-weil-deligne-representation: a = 0 + 2 − dim (ker N)^{I} = 1; the Tate curve WD representation is of this form (R01.2/weil-deligne-required-examples).
(d): with P_K trivial, a = codim V^{I_K} = 2 − 0.

(e): conductor–discriminant (R01.3/induction-formula-for-conductors) for quadratic L/K: a(χ_L) = δ(L/K) = v(disc), which is 2 or 3 for ramified quadratic extensions of Q_2 and 1 for p odd; the cubic subfield of Q_3(ζ_9) has discriminant exponent 4 = 2·a(χ), so a(χ) = 2.
acceptance: The good-dihedral case of ClassicalSerreModularity Theorem 3.3: N(ρ̄) = q²
Q_2(√−1) and Q_2(√2): exponents 2 and 3
