nodes.title: Chebotarev recognition by Frobenius characteristic polynomials
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of finite places, and Σ a set of finite places of K of Dirichlet density 1 disjoint from S. Let E_1, E_2 be coefficient fields of the standard kinds (finite fields with the discrete topology, or fields of characteristic 0 such as finite extensions of ℚ_ℓ, ℚ̄_ℓ or ℂ with their topologies; residual and characteristic-zero representations are compared only through a common field), and let E be a common extension: either a field containing both, or, for ℓ-adic and residual coefficients, a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ (resp. F_ℓ) inside a fixed ℚ̄_ℓ (resp. F̄_ℓ) containing both. Let ρ_i : G_K → GL(V_i), V_i an n-dimensional E_i-vector space, be continuous (R01.1/continuous-representation) and unramified outside S. Suppose that for every v ∈ Σ the Frobenius characteristic polynomials agree in E[X]: P_v(ρ_1, X) = P_v(ρ_2, X) (R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial, arithmetic Frobenius). Then (V_1 ⊗ E)^ss ≅ (V_2 ⊗ E)^ss as E[G_K]-modules; if each ρ_i ⊗ E is semisimple (automatic for semisimple ρ_i when E/E_i is separable, in particular for finite and characteristic-zero fields), ρ_1 ⊗ E ≅ ρ_2 ⊗ E. Variants: (a) when char E = 0 or char E > n, equality of the traces tr ρ_1(Frob_v) = tr ρ_2(Frob_v) for v ∈ Σ suffices; (b) for n = 2, equality of trace and determinant at v ∈ Σ is equality of P_v and suffices in every characteristic; (c) the same conclusions hold for any profinite Γ and a dense subset D ⊂ Γ in place of the Frobenius elements, with det(X − ρ_1(γ)) = det(X − ρ_2(γ)) for γ ∈ D. Trace equality alone does NOT suffice when 0 < char E ≤ n.
hypotheses: Both representations continuous, of the same dimension n, unramified outside the finite set S; the comparison set Σ has Dirichlet density 1 and avoids S (the representations need only be unramified on Σ).

Characteristic polynomials are compared after the fixed embeddings E_i → E; for ℓ-adic and residual members the common field is reached by R01.1/coefficient-extension (and R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field for ℚ̄_ℓ-valued members).
The conclusion concerns semisimplifications: no splitting of extensions is inferred (a nonsplit extension and its semisimplification have the same characteristic polynomials).
Traces suffice only when n! is invertible in E (characteristic 0 or > n).
proofSteps: Extend coefficients to E (R01.1/coefficient-extension); characteristic polynomials and semisimplifications are compatible with the extension (R01.1/semisimplification).

The functions γ ↦ det(X − ρ_i(γ)) ∈ E[X]_{≤n}, i = 1, 2, are continuous and class functions on G_K and factor through G_K → GL_n(E_1) × GL_n(E_2) (ρ_1, ρ_2), which is unramified outside S; they agree at every Frobenius element at a place above Σ.
R01.5/frobenius-density (c) applied to (ρ_1, ρ_2): the Frobenius elements are dense in the image, so the characteristic polynomials agree on all of G_K (Hausdorff target).

R01.1/brauer-nesbitt (semisimple representations over any field with equal characteristic polynomials on all group elements are isomorphic; supplied through IHG.1 reconstruction and descent) gives (V_1 ⊗ E)^ss ≅ (V_2 ⊗ E)^ss. Equivalently, the determinants det ∘ ρ_i agree as continuous determinants on G_K (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense, via IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation); the representation-level statement is the one exported here.

(a): if n! ∈ E^×, Newton's identities recover det(X − g) from tr(g^k), k ≤ n, and traces agree on all of G_K by step 3 applied to the trace function. (b): for n = 2, P_v = X² − tr·X + det. (c): step 3 with D in place of the Frobenius set.
Counterexample to traces in characteristic p ≤ n: see acceptance.
acceptance: Characteristic two, traces insufficient: let χ : G_ℚ → Gal(ℚ(ζ_7)^+/ℚ) ≅ ℤ/3 ≅ F_4^× be a cubic character. Then 1 ⊕ 1 and χ ⊕ χ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F_4) are semisimple, unramified outside 7, and both have trace 0 everywhere, but at p = 2 (whose class in (ℤ/7)^×/{±1} is nontrivial) P_2(1⊕1) = X² + 1 while P_2(χ⊕χ) = X² + χ(Frob_2)² ≠ X² + 1; they are not isomorphic.

Semisimplicity is needed: for ℓ odd let c : G_ℚ → ℤ_ℓ be the composite of the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ with ℤ_ℓ^× → 1 + ℓℤ_ℓ ≅ ℤ_ℓ (a nonzero continuous homomorphism unramified outside ℓ). Then g ↦ [[1, c(g)],[0, 1]] is a nonsplit extension of 1 by 1 with P_p = (X − 1)² for every p ≠ ℓ; it is not isomorphic to 1 ⊕ 1, only its semisimplification is.

Deligne–Serre Lemme 3.2 is the case K = ℚ, coefficients ℂ, a finite field, or a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, with the trace version in characteristic 0; Dieulefait–Pacetti Remark 4 is the rank-two trace-and-determinant case (b).
Rank two, any characteristic: two odd semisimple ρ̄, ρ̄' : G_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_2) with the same tr and det at all p ∉ S are isomorphic, by (b).

nodes.title: The image algebra, field of definition and Brauer class of an absolutely irreducible representation
nodes.statement: Let k be a field with algebraic closure k̄, Γ a group and ρ : Γ → GL_n(k̄) an absolutely irreducible representation (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible). (1) The field of traces k(ρ) := k(tr ρ(γ) : γ ∈ Γ) ⊂ k̄. (2) The image algebra B(ρ) := the k(ρ)-linear span of ρ(Γ) in M_n(k̄); it is a k(ρ)-subalgebra, central simple over k(ρ) of dimension n², and the inclusion induces B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ ≅ M_n(k̄). (3) The Brauer class β(ρ) := [B(ρ)] ∈ Br(k(ρ)) (Mathlib BrauerGroup, Tau Ceti group structure), and the Schur index s(ρ) := index of B(ρ) = the degree of the division algebra in B(ρ) ≅ M_a(Δ), n = a·s(ρ). These depend only on the isomorphism class of ρ. For a determinant D on k[Γ] whose base change to k̄ is det ∘ ρ (IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation), B(ρ) ≅ k(ρ)[Γ]/ker(D ⊗ k(ρ)) when k(ρ) = k, which is Chenevier's central simple quotient R/ker(D).
hypotheses: ρ absolutely irreducible over k̄ (irreducible suffices since k̄ is algebraically closed).
No condition on the characteristic: the trace form on M_n(k̄) is nondegenerate in every characteristic, which is what makes B(ρ) central simple of the right dimension.
Γ arbitrary (no topology needed); for Galois representations take Γ = G_K or a finite quotient.
proofSteps: B(ρ) is closed under multiplication because ρ(Γ) is a group, and tr(B(ρ)) ⊂ k(ρ).

Burnside: the k̄-span of ρ(Γ) is M_n(k̄) for absolutely irreducible ρ (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 3 density / layer 1 Schur). Choose e_1, …, e_{n²} ∈ ρ(Γ) forming a k̄-basis of M_n(k̄) and let e'_i be the trace-dual basis; for b ∈ B(ρ), b = Σ tr(b e_i) e'_i with tr(b e_i) ∈ k(ρ), so Σ k(ρ) e_i ⊂ B(ρ) ⊂ Σ k(ρ) e'_i, both of dimension n² (BLGGT Lemma A.1.5, proof).
Hence B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ → M_n(k̄) is an isomorphism, so B(ρ) is central simple over k(ρ) (central simplicity is detected after extension to k̄; SemisimpleAlgebras layer 4).

Isomorphic representations have conjugate image algebras (conjugation by an element of GL_n(k̄) commuting with the k(ρ)-structure is a k(ρ)-algebra isomorphism), so β(ρ) is well defined; the Schur index is the index of the Brauer class (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 6).

Comparison with Chenevier Definition-Proposition 2.18(iii): for an absolutely irreducible determinant D on k[Γ] with k(ρ) = k, k[Γ]/ker(D) is central simple of rank n², and the map k[Γ] → M_n(k̄) identifies it with B(ρ).
acceptance: Quaternion group: ρ : Q_8 → ℍ^× ⊂ GL_2(ℂ) has k(ρ) = ℚ (traces 2, −2, 0) and B(ρ) = the rational quaternions (−1, −1)_ℚ; over k = ℝ, B = ℍ and β(ρ) = [ℍ] ≠ 1 (tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one), s(ρ) = 2.
For Γ = GL_2(F_q), ρ the standard representation over k = F_q: B(ρ) = M_2(F_q), β = 1.

uses.how: the realizability criterion is stated through β(ρ_i) and the Schur indices of the constituents
β(ρ) = 1 because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (Deligne–Serre 6.13: no Schur index)
BLGGT Lemma A.1.5's proof: an element with n distinct M-rational eigenvalues forces every Schur index and centre degree to be 1
subrepresentations are defined over M_λ after a finite extension; the obstruction to doing so without extension is this Brauer class
an absolutely irreducible determinant D has R/ker(D) central simple of rank d²

nodes.title: Coefficient descent and its Brauer-class obstruction
nodes.statement: Let k be a PERFECT field (finite fields and fields of characteristic 0), k̄ an algebraic closure, Γ a group, and ρ : Γ → GL_n(k̄) semisimple with det(X − ρ(γ)) ∈ k[X] for every γ ∈ Γ (equivalently, the determinant det ∘ ρ descends to a k-valued determinant on k[Γ], IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring). Write ρ ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^{t} ρ_i^{⊕ m_i} with ρ_i pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible. Then: (1) Gal(k̄/k) permutes the classes [ρ_i] preserving multiplicities, σ(ρ) ≅ ρ for all σ; k(ρ_i) (R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation) is the fixed field of the stabiliser of [ρ_i] and is finite over k. (2) ρ is realizable over k, i.e. ρ ≅ V ⊗_k k̄ for a k[Γ]-module V of dimension n, if and only if the Schur index s(ρ_i) divides m_i for every i. (3) In particular: if every β(ρ_i) ∈ Br(k(ρ_i)) is trivial (e.g. k finite), ρ is realizable over k; if ρ is absolutely irreducible (t = 1, m_1 = 1, so k(ρ) = k), ρ is realizable over k iff β(ρ) = 1 in Br(k), and over a finite extension k' ⊂ k̄ iff k' splits B(ρ). (4) Equivalently in determinant language (Chenevier Theorem 2.16): for the descended determinant D, k[Γ]/ker(D) ≅ ∏ S_i with S_i central simple over k_i = k(ρ_i), D = ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i}, and D is the determinant of a representation Γ → GL_n(k) iff ind(S_i) | m_i for all i. A trace-and-determinant (or characteristic-polynomial) system defined over k does NOT in general descend: the obstruction is the family of classes β(ρ_i) weighted by the multiplicities.
hypotheses: k perfect: over an imperfect field a semisimple representation with k-rational characteristic polynomials can fail to descend for a reason other than the Brauer class (inseparability; see acceptance).
ρ semisimple over k̄ (for a Galois representation, pass to the semisimplification first).
Characteristic polynomials (not traces) in k[X]; in characteristic p ≤ n traces in k do not imply characteristic polynomials in k.
proofSteps: For σ ∈ Gal(k̄/k), σ(ρ) is semisimple with the same characteristic polynomials, so σ(ρ) ≅ ρ by R01.1/brauer-nesbitt; hence Gal(k̄/k) permutes the isotypic constituents preserving m_i. Absolutely irreducible representations are determined by their traces (Burnside density makes the traces of non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible representations linearly independent), so the stabiliser of [ρ_i] is Gal(k̄/k(ρ_i)); k perfect makes k(ρ_i)/k separable and finite.

For each Galois orbit, B(ρ_i) is central simple over k(ρ_i) (R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation). The simple k[Γ]-module W_i attached to the orbit is the simple module of B(ρ_i) viewed over k; W_i ⊗_k k̄ ≅ ⊕_{τ : k(ρ_i) → k̄} τ(ρ_i)^{⊕ s(ρ_i)} (Chenevier Theorem 2.16 with q_i = 1, and the Wedderburn decomposition of SemisimpleAlgebras layer 2).

Every k-form V of ρ is semisimple (k perfect) and so a sum of the W_i; comparing multiplicities of ρ_i gives ρ realizable iff s(ρ_i) | m_i for all i, which is (2). (3) follows: β(ρ_i) = 1 means s(ρ_i) = 1; finite k(ρ_i) has trivial Brauer group (tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite); in the absolutely irreducible case B(ρ) ⊗ k' splits iff k' splits it (tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_mem_ker_baseChange_iff_isSplittingField).

(4) is the same computation in Chenevier's language: det_{S_i} restricted to the simple module of S_i is det_{S_i}^{s_i}, so a k-representation with determinant ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i} exists iff s_i | m_i.

Do not use the second characterisation in Chenevier's Definition 2.19 ('R/ker(D) a product of matrix algebras') for realizability: it is strictly stronger (source issue ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E501).
acceptance: Quaternion obstruction over ℝ: ρ : Q_8 → GL_2(ℂ) has characteristic polynomials (X ∓ 1)² and X² + 1 in ℝ[X] and is absolutely irreducible, but B(ρ) = ℍ and [ℍ] ≠ 1 in Br(ℝ) (tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one), so ρ is not conjugate into GL_2(ℝ); ρ ⊕ ρ is realizable over ℝ (ℍ with left multiplication), matching s = 2 | m = 2.

Quaternion obstruction over ℚ and ℚ_2: composing G_ℚ → Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ Q_8 (K a quaternion extension of ℚ, e.g. Dedekind's field ℚ(√((2+√2)(3+√6)))) with ρ gives a continuous representation with Frobenius polynomials in ℚ[X] that is not realizable over ℚ or over ℚ_2, but is realizable over ℚ_ℓ for every odd ℓ, because (−1,−1) splits exactly away from 2 and ∞.
Finite fields: a semisimple φ over F_4 with F_2-rational characteristic polynomials descends to GL_n(F_2) (R01.5/finite-field-realisability).

Imperfect field: over k = F_p(t), the character χ : ℤ → k̄^×, 1 ↦ t^{1/p}, gives χ^{⊕p} with characteristic polynomial X^p − t ∈ k[X], but χ^{⊕p} is not realizable over k (a k-form would make the scalar t^{1/p} conjugate to a matrix over k); this is why k is assumed perfect.

The obstruction is a Schur index / Brauer class, absent over finite fields.

nodes.title: Realizability over the field of characteristic-polynomial coefficients (finite fields)
nodes.statement: Deligne–Serre Lemme 6.13. Let Φ be a group, k' a finite field and φ : Φ → GL_n(k') a semisimple representation. Let k ⊂ k' be a subfield containing the coefficients of det(1 − φ(s)T) for all s ∈ Φ. Then φ is realizable over k: there is a representation φ_0 : Φ → GL_n(k) with φ_0 ⊗_k k' ≅ φ. If Φ is a profinite group and φ is continuous (discrete topology), φ_0 can be taken continuous with the same kernel; for Φ = G_K, φ_0 is unramified wherever φ is, with the same Frobenius characteristic polynomials. In particular, for a continuous semisimple ρ̄ : G_K → GL_n(F̄_p) (finite image, R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field), ρ̄ is realizable over the finite field generated by the coefficients of its Frobenius characteristic polynomials P_v(ρ̄, X), v outside the ramification set.
hypotheses: k' finite (so every finite extension of k has trivial Brauer group); φ semisimple.
Characteristic polynomials, not traces, are required to have coefficients in k.
proofSteps: Deligne–Serre's proof: it suffices that φ ≅ σ(φ) for every k-automorphism σ of k', because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite), so there is no Schur index; φ and σ(φ) are semisimple with the same characteristic polynomials, hence isomorphic (R01.1/brauer-nesbitt, Curtis–Reiner 30.16). Formally: R01.5/descent-obstruction (3) with k finite (perfect), over k̄ = F̄_p ⊃ k'.

Continuity and kernel: φ_0 ⊗ k' ≅ φ forces ker φ_0 = ker φ, open when φ is continuous (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); Frobenius characteristic polynomials are unchanged by the isomorphism.

For the Galois corollary, the coefficients of det(1 − ρ̄(s)T) for s in the (finite) image lie in the field generated by the P_v-coefficients because every element of the image is a Frobenius (R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius), exactly as in Deligne–Serre 6.12.
acceptance: For S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2) with its standard representation std and A ∈ GL_2(F_4) not in F_4^×·GL_2(F_2), φ = A·std·A^{-1} has entries outside F_2 but F_2-rational characteristic polynomials (X² + 1 and X² + X + 1 for the non-identity classes), and is conjugate into GL_2(F_2), as the theorem predicts.
Deligne–Serre 6.12: the residual representation of a mod-λ eigenform is realised over k_f, the field generated by the a_p and ε(p).

The hypothesis cannot be weakened to traces: 1 ⊕ 1 and χ ⊕ χ over F_4 (χ cubic) have F_2-rational traces, and χ ⊕ χ is not realizable over F_2 because its characteristic polynomials X² + χ(s)² are not F_2-rational.

sources.match: The statement (k' finite, φ semisimple, k containing the characteristic-polynomial coefficients).
The reason: trivial Brauer group of a finite field, so no Schur index.

nodes.title: Descent from traces and one element with distinct rational eigenvalues (BLGGT Lemma A.1.5)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a group, M a field of characteristic 0 and M̄ an algebraic closure. Let r : Γ → GL_n(M̄) be semisimple. Suppose tr r(γ) ∈ M for all γ ∈ Γ and that for some γ_0 ∈ Γ the characteristic polynomial of r(γ_0) has n distinct roots, all in M. Then r is conjugate to a representation into GL_n(M). If moreover Γ is profinite, r is continuous and M is a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, the M-model can be taken continuous and preserves an O_M-lattice (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices).
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 (traces determine semisimple representations and the trace pairing argument uses tr(B) ⊂ M).
One element with n DISTINCT eigenvalues in M; traces in M alone do not suffice (quaternion example).
r semisimple.
proofSteps: Let B be the M-span of r(Γ) in M_n(M̄). The trace-dual-basis argument shows B ⊗_M M̄ ≅ B_{M̄} ⊂ M_n(M̄), so B is a finite-dimensional semisimple M-algebra and M̄^n a faithful B ⊗ M̄-module (BLGGT proof; R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation step 2 in the absolutely irreducible case).

Wedderburn: B ≅ ⊕_j M_{m_j}(D_j) with D_j central division over Z(D_j) ⊃ M, r_j² = dim_{Z(D_j)} D_j (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 2). As a B ⊗ M̄-module, M̄^n ≅ ⊕_{j,τ} (M̄^{m_j r_j})^{n_{j,τ}}, and tr(B) ⊂ M forces n_{j,τ} = n_j independent of the embedding τ.

An element of B with n distinct M-rational eigenvalues forces r_j = n_j = [Z(D_j) : M] = 1 for all j, so B ≅ ⊕ M_{m_j}(M) and M^n with this action is an M-form of r (R01.5/descent-obstruction (2) with all Schur indices 1).
Continuity and lattices: the M-form is conjugate to r by an element of GL_n(M̄) and so continuous; a compact image preserves a lattice.
acceptance: Q_8 → GL_2(ℚ̄) has traces in ℚ and is not realizable over ℚ; the hypothesis fails because every element has eigenvalues in {±1} (central elements, repeated) or {±i} (not in ℚ): consistent with the lemma.

BLGGT Lemma 5.3.1 (proof, p. 71): after enlarging M so that some r_λ(G_{F¹}) contains an element with n distinct M_λ-rational eigenvalues, every H-subrepresentation of a regular weakly compatible system is defined over O_{M,λ}.
n = 1: every character with values in M̄ and traces in M has values in M; the distinct-eigenvalue element is automatic.

sources.match: The conclusion; the statement and proof were read on the rendered page (r : Γ → GL_n(M̄), tr r(γ) ∈ M, one γ with distinct M-rational eigenvalues).
Its use for subrepresentations of regular weakly compatible systems.

nodes.title: Chebotarev density for compact images: Frobenius equidistribution in Haar measure
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, G a profinite group (e.g. a closed subgroup of GL_n(O_E), E/ℚ_ℓ finite) with normalised Haar probability measure μ (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.haar, unique by isHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure), and ρ : G_K → G a continuous SURJECTIVE homomorphism unramified outside a finite set S of finite places, so that ρ(Frob_v) is a well-defined conjugacy class for v ∉ S. For a conjugation-stable Borel set C ⊂ G let Σ_C = {v ∉ S : ρ(Frob_v) ⊂ C}. (a) If C is open and closed, Σ_C has Dirichlet density μ(C) (and natural density μ(C)). (b) If C is closed, Σ_C has upper Dirichlet density ≤ μ(C); in particular μ(C) = 0 implies Σ_C has Dirichlet density 0. (c) If μ(∂C) = 0, Σ_C has Dirichlet density μ(C). (d) Contrapositive form (CG20 Lemma A.8): if a closed conjugation-stable condition holds at ρ(Frob_v) for v in a set of positive upper density, it holds on a subset of G of positive Haar measure. (e) If G is an open subgroup of GL_n(ℤ_ℓ) (or of GL_n(O_E)) and f is a polynomial function on M_n(E) that does not vanish identically on G, then C = {g ∈ G : f(g) = 0} has μ(C) = 0, so Σ_C has density 0; e.g. for ρ with open image in GL_2(ℤ_ℓ), the primes with tr ρ(Frob_v) = 0 have density 0.
hypotheses: ρ surjective onto G (replace G by the closed subgroup ρ(G_K) otherwise; the Haar measure is that of the image).
Densities are Dirichlet densities (ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7); the natural-density form of (a) uses Chebotarev layer 14.

(e) needs f not identically zero on G; a proper analytic subset with empty interior of a general compact ℓ-adic Lie group is also null (Serre), but that general analytic statement is recorded as a gap.
Only a density-ZERO conclusion for null sets; no effective error term (Serre's Théorème 15 bounds need the effective Chebotarev theorem and are not planned here).
proofSteps: Open normal subgroups U of G form a basis at 1 (profinite). For C open and closed and conjugation-stable, C is a union of cosets of some open normal U (compactness), C = π^{-1}(C_U) for π : G → G/U, and μ(C) = #C_U/#(G/U) because all cosets of U have equal measure (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure).
(a): L = K̄^{ρ^{-1}(U)} is finite Galois with Gal(L/K) ≅ G/U, unramified outside S; v ∈ Σ_C iff Frob_v ∈ C_U; Chebotarev layer 10 (resp. 14) gives density #C_U/#(G/U) = μ(C).

(b): μ is outer regular; for ε > 0 choose open W ⊃ C with μ(W) < μ(C) + ε, then (compactness of C, conjugation-stability) an open normal U with CU ⊂ W; CU is open, closed and conjugation-stable, Σ_C ⊂ Σ_{CU}, so the upper density of Σ_C is ≤ μ(CU) < μ(C) + ε.

(c): apply (b) to the closure of C and to the closure of the complement and use μ(∂C) = 0; upper and lower bounds coincide (hasDirichletDensity_of_upperBound_of_lowerBound, ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7). (d) is the contrapositive of (b).

(e): on GL_n(ℤ_ℓ) Haar measure is a multiple of the additive Haar measure of M_n(ℤ_ℓ) (|det| = 1); the zero set of a nonzero polynomial in N variables over ℚ_ℓ is null for the Haar measure of ℤ_ℓ^N (induction on N with Fubini, a nonzero one-variable polynomial having finitely many roots and Haar measure on ℤ_ℓ having no atoms); restrict to the open subgroup G. tr is not identically zero on any open subgroup of GL_2(ℤ_ℓ) (it is 2 at 1).
acceptance: Serre 1981 introduction: for a non-CM elliptic curve E/ℚ the image of the ℓ-adic representation is open in GL_2(ℤ_ℓ), the trace-zero locus is Haar-null, and so the supersingular-type primes with a_p = 0 have density 0.

CG20 Lemma A.8 (published p. 890): with ℓ-adic image GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ), a fixed linear relation between 1, p, b_p, a_p, a_p² holding on a set of positive density forces the corresponding identity on a subset of GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ) of positive measure, hence (being polynomial) everywhere, which fails by inspection.
Finite G recovers Chebotarev: μ(C) = #C/#G.

Density zero is not emptiness, and an infinite image is needed for null classes: for ρ = χ_ℓ : G_ℚ → ℤ_ℓ^× (surjective, unramified outside ℓ, ρ(Frob_p) = p) and C = {a} with a ≠ ℓ a prime, μ(C) = 0 and Σ_C = {a}, a nonempty set of density 0; for finite G no nonempty conjugation-stable set is null.

sources.locator: Appendix §A.4, proof of Lemma A.8, published p. 890 (author copy Siegel.pdf)
sources.match: The Haar-measure form of Chebotarev used for the ℓ-adic image GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ), cited only as 'By Chebotarev'.
The trace-zero locus C_ℓ is null in G_ℓ, which gives density zero by qualitative Chebotarev (text layer garbles C_ℓ, G_ℓ).
Analytic subsets with empty interior are Haar-null (the general form recorded as a gap).
The effective trace-zero bounds, beyond this node: only the density-zero corollary is planned.

nodes.title: Carayol's lemma: recognition, conjugacy and gluing of lifts with absolutely irreducible residual representation
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m_R and finite residue field k, Γ a profinite group and r, r' : Γ → GL_d(R) continuous with the same residual representation r̄ = r mod m_R = r' mod m_R, assumed absolutely irreducible. (a) If det(X − r(γ)) = det(X − r'(γ)) for all γ in a dense subset of Γ — for Γ = G_K and r, r' unramified outside a finite S: for all Frobenius elements at places of a density-one set (R01.5/frobenius-density) — then r' = g r g^{-1} for some g ∈ ker(GL_d(R) → GL_d(k)), unique up to multiplication by 1 + m_R. (b) (Symplectic form, CG20) If r, r' take values in GSp_{2m}(R) for a fixed alternating form J with the same multiplier character ν, then g can be chosen in ker(GSp_{2m}(R) → GSp_{2m}(k)). (c) (Gluing) Let (𝔞_j)_{j≥1} be a decreasing sequence of open ideals of R forming a basis of neighbourhoods of 0, D ⊂ Γ dense, and (P_γ)_{γ∈D} ⊂ R[X] monic of degree d. If r_j : Γ → GL_d(R/𝔞_j) are continuous lifts of r̄ with det(X − r_j(γ)) = P_γ mod 𝔞_j for γ ∈ D, then there are g_j ∈ ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_j) → GL_d(k)) such that the g_j r_j g_j^{-1} are compatible, and they glue to a continuous r : Γ → GL_d(R) lifting r̄ with det(X − r(γ)) = P_γ, unique up to ker(GL_d(R) → GL_d(k))-conjugacy (and similarly for GSp_{2m} with fixed multiplier). The algebraic input — reconstruction and uniqueness of a representation over a henselian local ring from a determinant whose residual determinant is split and absolutely irreducible — is IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1 (Chenevier Theorem 2.22); this node supplies the continuity, Frobenius-density and symplectic refinements.
hypotheses: r̄ absolutely irreducible (split: defined over the finite residue field k). Without it the conclusion fails (scalar or reducible residual representation, see acceptance).
R complete Noetherian local with finite residue field; the m_R-adic topology; r, r' continuous.
Characteristic polynomials, not traces (traces suffice when d! ∈ R^×, by IHG.0/determinant-trace-injective).
(b) uses the same J and the same multiplier ν for r and r'.
proofSteps: Continuity and density: the characteristic-polynomial maps γ ↦ det(X − r(γ)), det(X − r'(γ)) ∈ R[X] are continuous and agree on a dense set, hence everywhere (R01.5/frobenius-density; R is Hausdorff). So det ∘ r = det ∘ r' as continuous determinants on R[Γ] (IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense, IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation).

Algebra (IHG.1, Chenevier Theorem 2.22(i)): for the common determinant D, D mod m_R is split and absolutely irreducible, so the Cayley–Hamilton quotient R[Γ]/CH(D) ≅ M_d(R) with D = det. Both r and r' factor through it (matrix representations are Cayley–Hamilton, IHG.1/cayley-hamilton) and induce surjective, hence bijective, R-algebra endomorphisms of M_d(R) (residually surjective by Burnside, then Nakayama); an R-algebra automorphism of M_d(R) over a local ring is inner (Skolem–Noether over local rings, requested from IHG.1), so r' = g r g^{-1} with g ∈ GL_d(R).

Normalising g: ḡ commutes with r̄(Γ), so ḡ = c ∈ k^× by Schur's lemma for the absolutely irreducible r̄; replacing g by [c]^{-1}g ([c] ∈ R^× a lift) gives g ∈ 1 + M_d(m_R). Uniqueness: End_{R[Γ]}(r) = R (Nakayama plus residual Schur), so g is unique up to (1 + m_R).

(b): g^T J g is an r-invariant alternating form with multiplier ν: r(γ)^T(g^T J g)r(γ) = g^T r'(γ)^T J r'(γ) g = ν(γ) g^T J g. Such forms are Hom_{R[Γ]}(r, r^∨ ⊗ ν), free of rank one over R generated by J (step 3 applied to r^∨ ⊗ ν ≅ r via J), so g^T J g = cJ with c ∈ R^×, c ≡ 1 mod m_R; thus g ∈ GSp_{2m}(R) with multiplier c and ḡ = 1.

(c): by (a) applied over R/𝔞_j, r_{j+1} mod 𝔞_j and r_j are conjugate by an element of ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_j) → GL_d(k)); lift it to ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_{j+1}) → GL_d(k)) (1 + M_d(m) surjects) and conjugate r_{j+1}; inductively the system is compatible, and r = lim r_j is continuous for the inverse-limit topology, which is the m_R-adic topology because the 𝔞_j form a neighbourhood basis. The characteristic polynomials are the limits P_γ. Uniqueness follows from (a).
acceptance: Scalar residual representation (absolute irreducibility is necessary): r̄ = 1 ⊕ 1 over F_p, R = F_p[ε]/(ε²), r = 1 ⊕ 1 and r'(γ) = [[1, ε c(γ)],[0, 1]] for a nonzero continuous homomorphism c : Γ → F_p; both have characteristic polynomial (X − 1)² everywhere, but r' is not conjugate to r (r is central, r' is not).
Reducible non-scalar residual: r̄ = 1 ⊕ ε̄ with a nonsplit extension lift and the split lift 1 ⊕ ε over the same R have the same characteristic polynomials and are not conjugate.
CG20 Theorem 6.13 (published p. 842): it suffices to construct for each m a GSp_4-valued representation over T/I_m with the prescribed characteristic polynomials; (b) and (c) glue them over T.
d = 1: two continuous characters with equal values on a dense set are equal; g ∈ 1 + m_R arbitrary.

sources.match: The algebraic reconstruction over a henselian local ring, without requiring an algebraically closed residue field (only split and absolutely irreducible); owned by IHG.1.
Existence and uniqueness of the lift (stated there with algebraically closed residue field; Theorem 2.22 removes this via 'split').
The gluing use: Galois representations over T/I_m glued over T, compatibility up to conjugation being Carayol's lemma (uncited in the paper).

nodes.title: Semisimplicity criteria from Frobenius annihilation for GSp4-valued ρ (BCGP25 §4.11)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, ρ : G_ℚ → GSp_4(Q̄_p) and s : G_ℚ → GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous (n ≥ 1), unramified outside a finite set (so that they take values in GL over a finite extension E/ℚ_p, R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field). For g ∈ G_ℚ write char_ρ(g)(X) = det(X − ρ(g)). Suppose that for a set of primes l of Dirichlet density 1 at which both are unramified, char_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l)) = 0 in M_n(Q̄_p). (a) (BCGP25 Proposition 4.11.1, a case of Nekovář's Proposition 3.10) If the Zariski closure of ρ(G_ℚ) contains Sp_4, then s ≅ ρ^{⊕m} for some m ≥ 1. (b) (Proposition 4.11.2) If the Zariski closure of ρ(G_ℚ) contains SL_2 × SL_2, ρ is absolutely irreducible but becomes reducible on an index-two subgroup G_E, then s ≅ ρ^{⊕m} for some m ≥ 1. In both cases the first step is: char_ρ(g)(s(g)) = 0 for EVERY g ∈ G_ℚ (Chebotarev and continuity), hence on the Zariski closure of the image of (ρ, s).
hypotheses: Annihilation by the full characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_l), on a density-one set — not merely equality of traces.
The image hypotheses on the Zariski closure (Sp_4 in (a); SL_2 × SL_2 with absolute irreducibility and reducibility on an index-two subgroup in (b)) are essential.
The conclusion includes semisimplicity of s: s is a direct sum of copies of ρ, not merely an iterated extension.
proofSteps: Density step: g ↦ char_ρ(g)(s(g)) is a continuous M_n(E)-valued function on G_ℚ vanishing at the Frobenius elements of a density-one set, hence identically (R01.5/frobenius-density (c)); being polynomial in the matrix entries of (ρ(g), s(g)), it vanishes on the Zariski closure of (ρ, s)(G_ℚ).

(a): with Σ the Frobenius set, hypothesis (C') of Nekovář Proposition 3.10 holds; the Lie algebra of ρ(G_ℚ) is sp_4 or gsp_4 acting through the standard (minuscule) representation, so Nekovář's case (3) gives s ≅ ρ^{⊕m} (BCGP25 proof). Nekovář's proposition is not freely available and was not read; recorded as a gap.

(b): restrict to G_E, ρ|_{G_E} = ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c. For an irreducible subquotient t of s|_{G_E}, Goursat's lemma on the Zariski closure of t ⊕ ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c and the annihilation identity show that the kernel of the projection to the closure of t is unipotent, hence trivial; so t is a quotient of the SL_2 × SL_2 representation and t ∈ {ϱ, ϱ^c}.
No self-extensions of ϱ (or ϱ^c) occur in s|_{G_E}: a generic element of ϱ^c acts invertibly on ϱ, and the GL_2 version of Nekovář's criterion (Blasius–Rogawski) applies.

Remaining case 0 → ρ → W → ρ → 0 nonsplit: Shapiro's lemma splits Ext¹_{G_E}(ϱ, ϱ^c) into H¹(ℚ, A) ⊕ H¹(ℚ, A ⊗ χ), A = s(ϱ) ⊗ η^{-1} the Asai representation twisted by the inverse similitude; a nonsplit extension U of ℚ_p by A cannot have a dense set of semisimple elements, because elements of G_ℚ ∖ G_E act on A with eigenvalues 1, −1, λ, λ^{-1} (corrected from the printed 1, −1, λ, −λ: source issue E502), contradicting the annihilation identity and the minimal-polynomial argument.
acceptance: BCGP25 §4.11 application: for ρ the GSp_4 representation of a non-CM abelian surface with big Zariski closure and s an Eichler–Shimura subquotient of étale cohomology annihilated by Frobenius characteristic polynomials, s ≅ ρ^{⊕m}.

Nonexample showing the role of annihilation: s = ρ ⊗ [[1, c],[0, 1]] with c : G_ℚ → ℤ_p ⊂ Q̄_p the composite of χ_p with ℤ_p^× → 1 + pℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p (p odd; c(Frob_l) ≠ 0 for every l ≠ p), a nonsplit self-extension of ρ, has char_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l)) ≠ 0 at Frobenius elements with ρ(Frob_l) regular semisimple, because s(Frob_l) is not semisimple there; it is excluded by the hypothesis.

Consistency and twists: s = ρ ⊕ ρ satisfies the hypothesis by Cayley–Hamilton and m = 2; s = ρ ⊗ χ with χ a nontrivial quadratic character fails it at every Frob_l with χ(Frob_l) = −1 for which the eigenvalue multiset of ρ(Frob_l) is not stable under negation, a set of positive density by R01.5/haar-measure-chebotarev, so twists are excluded.

sources.match: The annihilation hypothesis on a density-one set.
The conclusion.
Proposition 4.11.1 rests on Nekovář [Nek18, Prop. 3.10] (Ann. Sci. ÉNS 2018), not read.
The printed eigenvalue list, corrected to 1, −1, λ, λ^{-1} (E502).

nodes.title: Potentially abelian representations are induced from a character orbit (Clifford part of BCGP25 Lemma 10.2.3)
nodes.statement: Let F be a field (in the applications a number field), E an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (e.g. Q̄_p with its topology), and ρ : G_F → GL_n(E) a continuous irreducible representation. Suppose L/F is a finite Galois extension with ρ(G_L) abelian. Then: (1) ρ|_{G_L} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^{b} χ_i^{⊕a} with ab = n and χ_1, …, χ_b : G_L → E^× pairwise distinct continuous characters; (2) Gal(L/F) acts on {χ_i} by χ_i^σ(g) = χ_i(σ̃ g σ̃^{-1}) (σ̃ any lift of σ), transitively; (3) with K_i the fixed field of the stabiliser Gal(L/K_i) of χ_i, [K_i : F] = b and there is an irreducible continuous representation V_i of G_{K_i} with V_i|_{G_L} ≅ χ_i^{⊕a} and ρ ≅ Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F} V_i (R01.1/continuous-induction); (4) b = 1 iff ρ(G_L) consists of scalars, and then the projective image of ρ is finite (a quotient of Gal(L/F)); conversely, if the projective image is finite, b = 1 for L the fixed field of the kernel of the projective representation. The de Rham / algebraic Hecke character conclusions of BCGP25 Lemma 10.2.3 (non-parallel weight, b > 1 and CM subfields when ρ is not finite up to twist) are NOT part of this node.
hypotheses: ρ irreducible and continuous; characteristic 0 coefficients, algebraically closed (so the abelian semisimple restriction diagonalises).
L/F finite Galois (G_L open normal in G_F).
No p-adic Hodge theory: de Rham hypotheses and algebraic Hecke characters are routed to the owners named in the notes.
proofSteps: ρ|_{G_L} is semisimple (restriction of an irreducible characteristic-zero representation to an open normal subgroup, R01.1/semisimplicity-under-restriction-and-induction, Clifford); its image is abelian and E algebraically closed, so it is a sum of characters.

For σ ∈ G_F, ρ(σ) maps the χ-eigenspace of G_L to the χ^σ-eigenspace; the sum of eigenspaces over one Gal(L/F)-orbit is G_F-stable, so irreducibility forces a single orbit, and the multiplicities a are constant on it (Clifford's theorem, tauceti InductionRestriction layer 5, applied to the finite quotient through which the permutation action factors).

The χ_i-eigenspace V_i is stable under G_{K_i}; orbit–stabiliser gives [K_i : F] = b; Frobenius reciprocity gives a nonzero map ρ → Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F} V_i, an isomorphism by irreducibility and dimension count (n = b·a), and then V_i is irreducible.

(4): b = 1 means G_L acts by a single character, i.e. by scalars, so the projective image is a quotient of Gal(L/F); conversely, if the projective image is finite, its kernel is an open normal subgroup G_{L'} acting by scalars, and for L' the decomposition has b = 1.
acceptance: Dihedral case n = 2: ρ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ψ with K/F quadratic and ψ ≠ ψ^c restricts to ψ ⊕ ψ^c on G_K: b = 2, a = 1, K_i = K.
Finite image: ρ with finite image, L the fixed field of ker ρ ∩ (centre preimage): if ρ(G_L) is scalar, b = 1 and the projective image is finite.

a > 1 occurs: for K/ℚ a quaternion extension and ρ : G_ℚ → Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ Q_8 ⊂ GL_2(ℂ) the 2-dimensional irreducible representation, take L the biquadratic subfield fixed by the centre {±1}; ρ(G_L) = {±1} is scalar, so b = 1, a = 2, and the projective image Q_8/{±1} ≅ (ℤ/2)² is finite.

sources.match: The character orbit and the transitive Galois action.
The induction step.
The finite-projective-image step uses H²(F, Q̄_p^×) = 0 (Tate) and projective lifting, owned by ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 and G7/lifting-projective-representations, not by this node.

nodes.title: Recognition of lisse sheaves on a curve over a finite field from a dense open subset
nodes.statement: Let F_q be a finite field of characteristic p, C a smooth geometrically connected curve over F_q, U ⊂ C a nonempty (hence dense) open subscheme, ℓ ≠ p, and E a field of characteristic 0 that is a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ (or Q̄_ℓ). Let V_1, V_2 be lisse E-sheaves of rank n on C, i.e. continuous representations of π_1(C, c̄) on n-dimensional E-vector spaces. If det(1 − Frob_x t | V_{1,x̄}) = det(1 − Frob_x t | V_{2,x̄}) in E[t] for every closed point x ∈ |U| (geometric or arithmetic Frobenius, the same for both), then V_1^ss ≅ V_2^ss as representations of π_1(C); if V_1, V_2 are semisimple, V_1 ≅ V_2. This is the step 'by the Chebotarev density Theorem, the semisimplifications … are isomorphic' in the proof of Kisin–Zhou Proposition 5.3.5.
hypotheses: C normal and connected (smooth geometrically connected), U dense open; equality at every closed point of U.
Common coefficient field E of characteristic 0 (for different ℓ the comparison is of polynomials with coefficients in a number field, after which a single ℓ is used).
Conclusion only for semisimplifications.
proofSteps: π_1(U) → π_1(C) is surjective for a dense open U of a normal connected scheme (IG.1 owner of the arithmetic fundamental group sequence and Frobenius at closed points).

Closed-point Chebotarev on curves over finite fields (DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.3, which owns the function-field closed-point density statement with the constant-field degree congruences): the Frobenius elements Frob_x, x ∈ |U|, together with their conjugates, are dense in π_1(U); hence their images are dense in π_1(C).

The characteristic-polynomial maps π_1(C) → E[t] of V_1, V_2 are continuous class functions agreeing on a dense set, hence everywhere (as in R01.5/recognition-by-characteristic-polynomials-and-coefficient-descent (c)); det(1 − g t) and det(1 − g^{-1} t) determine each other, so the Frobenius convention is irrelevant.
R01.1/brauer-nesbitt gives V_1^ss ≅ V_2^ss; semisimple sheaves are equal to their semisimplifications.
acceptance: Semisimplicity is required: on C = P¹ ∖ {0, ∞} over F_q, the representation g ↦ [[1, deg(g)],[0, 1]] (deg : π_1(C) → Ẑ → ℤ_ℓ the degree map) is a nonsplit extension of the trivial sheaf by itself with det(1 − Frob_x t) = (1 − t)² at every closed point, the same as the trivial rank-two sheaf.

Kisin–Zhou Proposition 5.3.5: K^C_{ℓ'} and L^C_{ℓ'} agree on closed points of a dense open U ⊂ C, so their semisimplifications agree on C and the conjugacy classes ϑ(γ_{y,ℓ}) and ϑ(γ_{y,ℓ'}) coincide at the point y ∈ C(F_q) outside U.
U = C recovers recognition at every closed point; the content is that points of C ∖ U are controlled by continuity.

sources.match: The curve recognition step, from equality on closed points of a dense open U ⊂ C.
The reduction to a dense open subset of the curve.

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic Tate module of an abelian variety as a continuous Galois representation
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. For n ≥ 0 put A[ℓ^n] := ker([ℓ^n] : A → A), a finite étale K-group scheme of order ℓ^{2gn} (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3), and A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K̄) its group of geometric points, with the transition maps [ℓ] : A[ℓ^{n+1}](K^sep) → A[ℓ^n](K^sep). Define T_ℓA := lim_n A[ℓ^n](K^sep), with the inverse-limit topology of the discrete finite groups, V_ℓA := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} Q_ℓ, and the prime-to-char K adelic module T̂A := lim_N A[N](K^sep) (N invertible in K) = ∏_{ℓ ≠ char K} T_ℓA. Then: (a) each A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is a free Z/ℓ^n-module of rank 2g, the transition maps are surjective, and T_ℓA is a free Z_ℓ-module of rank 2g whose inverse-limit topology is the ℓ-adic topology (equivalently Mathlib's module topology, IsModuleTopology Z_ℓ); (b) the projection induces a canonical G_K-equivariant isomorphism T_ℓA/ℓ^n T_ℓA ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep); (c) G_K acts Z_ℓ-linearly on T_ℓA through its coordinatewise action on A[ℓ^n](K̄), the action map G_K × T_ℓA → T_ℓA is jointly continuous, and so (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) is an object of ContinuousRep G_K Z_ℓ (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation) of rank 2g, with V_ℓA its coefficient extension to Q_ℓ; (d) the kernel of G_K → Aut(A[ℓ^n](K^sep)) is the open subgroup G_{K(A[ℓ^n])} fixing the finite Galois extension K(A[ℓ^n]) generated by the coordinates of the ℓ^n-torsion points, and ρ_{A,ℓ} factors through Gal(K(A[ℓ^∞])/K); (e) a different choice of algebraic closure changes (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) by a canonical isomorphism, and conjugating the embedding K^sep ⊆ K̄ by τ ∈ G_K changes it by the isomorphism x ↦ τx. A choice of Z_ℓ-basis gives the framed form ρ_{A,ℓ} : G_K → GL_{2g}(Z_ℓ) (R01.1/framed-representation), well defined up to GL_{2g}(Z_ℓ)-conjugacy. The Tate module is covariant in A. It is not defined for ℓ = char K (there A[ℓ](K^sep) has order at most ℓ^g).
hypotheses: K any field; ℓ a prime different from char K (for ℓ = char K the construction is not made: A[ℓ](K^sep) has order ≤ ℓ^g)
A an abelian variety over K of dimension g in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety)
torsion points are taken over K^sep (equivalently K̄), never over K
G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K (automorphisms of AlgebraicClosure K) with the Krull topology
proofSteps: Order and étaleness: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 proves [n] finite locally free of rank n^{2g} and étale when n is invertible on the base; over K with ℓ ≠ char K, A[ℓ^n] is finite étale of order ℓ^{2gn}, so #A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = ℓ^{2gn} and the K^sep- and K̄-points agree (Milne AV, Remark 7.3, p. 34).
Structure: applying the count to every m | ℓ^n and the structure theorem for finite abelian groups gives A[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ (Z/ℓ^n)^{2g} (Milne AV, Remark 7.3, p. 34).

Surjective transitions: [ℓ] : A → A is a finite étale surjective isogeny (A3), so every K^sep-point of A[ℓ^n] lifts to a K^sep-point of A[ℓ^{n+1}]; the inverse limit of free Z/ℓ^n-modules of rank 2g along surjections reducing compatibly is free of rank 2g over Z_ℓ with T_ℓA/ℓ^n ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep) (Milne AV, Proposition 10.5, p. 45).

Galois action: σ ∈ G_K acts on A(K̄) through the functoriality of points along the K-automorphism σ (coordinates); it commutes with [ℓ^n], so preserves A[ℓ^n](K̄) and commutes with the transition maps; hence it acts Z_ℓ-linearly on T_ℓA.

Continuity: each A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is finite and pointwise defined over the finite Galois extension K(A[ℓ^n]), so the action on it factors through the finite quotient Gal(K(A[ℓ^n])/K) and is continuous for the discrete topology (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); joint continuity on the inverse limit follows level by level, and the module topology on the finite free Z_ℓ-module T_ℓA is its inverse-limit topology.

Independence of choices: an isomorphism of algebraic closures over K transports torsion points and Galois actions compatibly; this is the transport-of-structure argument of R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist applied to the isomorphism of profinite groups it induces.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve (g = 1) the construction recovers Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2's T_ℓE, free of rank 2 (node elliptic-tate-module-comparison).

For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, E[2](Q̄) = {O, (0,0), (1,0), (−1,0)} consists of rational points, so T_2E/2T_2E ≅ (Z/2)² with trivial G_Q-action, while ρ_{E,2} itself is nontrivial (its determinant is χ_2, node determinant-and-oddness).

The analogous construction for the multiplicative group, lim μ_{ℓ^n}(K^sep), is the Tate twist Z_ℓ(1) of R01.1/tate-twist, with G_K acting through the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter): this is the χ_ℓ example of the roadmap.

nodes.title: Finite torsion, the residual representation and rational cyclic isogenies
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. (a) For every n ≥ 1 the G_K-module T_ℓA/ℓ^nT_ℓA is canonically isomorphic to A[ℓ^n](K^sep) with its pointwise action; in particular the residual representation ρ̄_{A,ℓ} := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} F_ℓ (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification) is the G_K-module A[ℓ](K^sep) of dimension 2g over F_ℓ. (b) For every G_K-stable Z_ℓ-lattice Λ ⊂ V_ℓA, (Λ/ℓΛ)^ss ≅ A[ℓ](K^sep)^ss as F_ℓ[G_K]-modules (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence). (c) Let E be an elliptic curve over K (Weierstrass, IsElliptic). The G_K-stable F_ℓ-lines L ⊂ E[ℓ](K^sep) are exactly the K-rational cyclic subgroups of order ℓ, i.e. the kernels of the cyclic K-rational isogenies of degree ℓ out of E (the quotient E → E/L of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3); so ρ̄_{E,ℓ} is reducible over F_ℓ iff E admits a K-rational isogeny of degree ℓ. On such a line G_K acts through a character ψ : G_K → F_ℓ^×, and on the quotient E[ℓ]/L through χ̄_ℓ ψ^{−1} (node determinant-and-oddness); ψ need not be trivial, so reducibility of ρ̄_{E,ℓ} does not imply that E has a K-rational point of order ℓ.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K
in (c), the line L is a subgroup of the K^sep-points; its K-rationality means stability under G_K, not pointwise rationality
proofSteps: (a) is part (b) of node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety, restated for consumers; n = 1 is the comparison of the residual representation with the existing pointwise action requested by the stage.
(b) Λ and T_ℓA are both G_K-stable lattices in V_ℓA; R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence gives (Λ/ℓΛ)^ss ≅ (T_ℓA/ℓT_ℓA)^ss, and (a) identifies the latter.

(c) A G_K-stable line L is a finite subgroup of E(K^sep) stable under G_K, hence the K^sep-points of a finite étale K-subgroup scheme (Galois descent for finite étale schemes); the quotient isogeny E → E/L of A3 is defined over K with kernel L. Conversely the kernel of a K-rational isogeny of degree ℓ (ℓ ≠ char K, so the kernel is étale of order ℓ) is a G_K-stable line. The character ψ is the action on L ≅ F_ℓ; the quotient character follows from det ρ̄_{E,ℓ} = χ̄_ℓ (node determinant-and-oddness).

Non-triviality of ψ: E and its quadratic twist E^d (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf) have the same stable lines with ψ replaced by ψ·ε_d for the quadratic character ε_d, so a rational point of order ℓ on E (ψ = 1) gives ψ = ε_d ≠ 1 on E^d for d not a square.
acceptance: The curve 11a3, y² + y = x³ − x², has a rational point (0, 0) of order 5, so ρ̄_{E,5} has a stable line with trivial character ψ = 1 and quotient character χ̄_5 (Δ = −11).

Its quadratic twist by d = −1 still has a G_Q-stable line in E[5] (the twist of the same line) but its character is the nontrivial character ε_{−1} of Q(i)/Q, so the twisted curve has a rational 5-isogeny but no rational point of order 5 in that line.
For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, ρ̄_{E,2} is trivial (all of E[2] is rational) and every line in E[2] is G_Q-stable: three rational 2-isogenies.

nodes.title: Comparison with the Tate module of a Weierstrass curve (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, W a Weierstrass curve over K with [W.IsElliptic], E_W the elliptic curve it defines (the projective closure of W.toAffine, an abelian variety of dimension 1 whose L-points are W⁄L.Point functorially in the field L/K), and ℓ a prime ≠ char K. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2 constructs E[N] = Submodule.torsionBy ℤ (W⁄K^sep).Point N ≃+ (ZMod N)², the Weil pairing e_N valued in rootsOfUnity N K^sep, the Tate module T_ℓW := lim E[ℓ^n] with its continuous G_K-representation into Module.Aut Z_ℓ (T_ℓW) and det = χ_ℓ. Then the identification E_W(K^sep) = (W⁄K^sep).Point induces, for every n, a G_K-equivariant group isomorphism E_W[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ Submodule.torsionBy ℤ (W⁄K^sep).Point ℓ^n compatible with the transition maps, hence an isomorphism T_ℓ(E_W) ≅ T_ℓW of continuous Z_ℓ[G_K]-modules, under which: (i) Tau Ceti's isogeny map TauCeti.Isogeny.toPointHom of φ : W₁ → W₂ corresponds to T_ℓ of the induced homomorphism E_{W₁} → E_{W₂}; (ii) Tau Ceti's e_{ℓ^n} corresponds to the polarization pairing e^λ_{ℓ^n} of node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules for the canonical principal polarization λ : E → E^∨, P ↦ class of (P) − (O), up to the inversion e ↦ e^{−1} fixed once by a named comparison lemma; (iii) the determinant theorem of Layer 2 and node determinant-and-oddness give the same character χ_ℓ. Consequently every statement of this layer about T_ℓA for abelian varieties applies to Tau Ceti's T_ℓW, and every Layer-2 statement about T_ℓW applies to T_ℓ(E_W).
hypotheses: W elliptic over a field K; ℓ ≠ char K
the identification of E_W with an abelian variety of dimension 1 together with E_W(L) = W⁄L.Point is an input recorded as a gap (no owner located)
proofSteps: Both inverse systems are built from the same groups: E_W(K^sep)[ℓ^n] and the ℓ^n-torsion submodule of (W⁄K^sep).Point coincide under the point identification, and multiplication by ℓ corresponds because the group laws coincide.

Galois equivariance: σ acts on both sides by acting on coordinates (Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ), so the identification is G_K-equivariant at each level and hence on the limits; continuity is level-wise on both sides.

Isogenies: a Tau Ceti isogeny is a coordinate-ring pullback; on points it induces the same map as the morphism of abelian varieties it defines (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 0 place dictionary and Layer 1 toPointHom).

Weil pairing: both pairings are characterised by compatibility with isogenies and duals (e_N(φP, Q) = e_N(P, φ̂Q), Milne AV Proposition 13.2(a)) and agree up to the universal sign/inversion convention, which is fixed by evaluating both on a single curve.
Determinant: both equal χ_ℓ since both pairings are perfect alternating and Galois-equivariant into Z_ℓ(1).
acceptance: For W : y² = x³ − x over Q, both constructions give the same mod-2 reduction: the four rational points O, (0,0), (±1,0), with trivial G_Q-action.

For the Tate curve E_q over a p-adic field with ℓ ≠ p, both constructions give the extension 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE_q → Z_ℓ → 0 from Tau Ceti Layer 4's uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) (node required-examples).

nodes.title: Functoriality: homomorphisms, products, isogenies and base change
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. (a) Every homomorphism α : A → B of abelian varieties over K induces a Z_ℓ-linear G_K-equivariant map T_ℓα : T_ℓA → T_ℓB, (x_n) ↦ (α(x_n)); T_ℓ(id) = id, T_ℓ(βα) = T_ℓβ ∘ T_ℓα, T_ℓ(α + α′) = T_ℓα + T_ℓα′, so Hom_K(A, B) → Hom_{Z_ℓ[G_K]}(T_ℓA, T_ℓB) is a group homomorphism and End_K(A) → End_{Z_ℓ[G_K]}(T_ℓA) a ring homomorphism, which extends Z_ℓ-linearly to Hom_K(A, B) ⊗ Z_ℓ. (b) For the product A × B (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.prod), (T_ℓpr_1, T_ℓpr_2) : T_ℓ(A × B) → T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB is an isomorphism of continuous representations. (c) Let φ : A → B be an isogeny (finite surjective, Tau Ceti IsIsogeny) of degree d. Then T_ℓφ is injective and there is a canonical G_K-equivariant isomorphism coker(T_ℓφ) ≅ (ker φ)(K^sep)[ℓ^∞]; in particular #coker(T_ℓφ) = d_ℓ, the ℓ-part of d, and V_ℓφ : V_ℓA → V_ℓB is an isomorphism of Q_ℓ[G_K]-modules. If ℓ ∤ d, T_ℓφ is an isomorphism and φ induces G_K-isomorphisms A[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ B[ℓ^n](K^sep) for all n. If ψ : B → A satisfies ψφ = [m], then T_ℓψ ∘ T_ℓφ = m. (d) For a field extension L ⊆ K̄ of K, T_ℓ(A_L) = T_ℓA|_{G_L} (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.baseChange). (e) For a field isomorphism τ : K → K′ extended to τ̄ : K̄ → K̄′, transport of structure gives a Z_ℓ-isomorphism T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓ(A^τ) intertwining ρ_{A,ℓ}(σ) with ρ_{A^τ,ℓ}(τ̄στ̄^{−1}).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K
in (c) the degree d is the rank of the finite group scheme ker φ (its p-primary part may be infinitesimal in characteristic p; only its ℓ-primary part, which is étale, enters coker T_ℓφ)
proofSteps: (a) α commutes with [ℓ^n] and with the Galois action on coordinates; additivity holds level-wise because the group law on Hom(A, B) is pointwise (Milne AV, §10, p. 45).
(b) A × B represents the product functor on points, so (A × B)[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K^sep) × B[ℓ^n](K^sep) compatibly with transitions and Galois.

(c) Put G = ker φ, a finite K-group scheme of order d (A3). On K^sep-points, 0 → G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] → A[ℓ^∞](K^sep) → B[ℓ^∞](K^sep) → 0 is exact (φ is surjective on K^sep-points and A[ℓ^∞] is divisible). Applying the snake lemma to multiplication by ℓ^n and passing to the limit (Hom(Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ, −) is left exact and G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] is finite, so T_ℓG = 0) gives 0 → T_ℓA → T_ℓB → G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] → 0. The ℓ-primary part of G is étale since ℓ is invertible, so its order is d_ℓ (Milne AV, proof of Proposition 10.20, p. 52, uses exactly #Coker(T_ℓβ) = #Ker(β)(ℓ)).

The quasi-inverse: the kernel of φ is killed by m = exponent, so φ factors [m] through A/G ≅ B and ψ exists with ψφ = [m] (A3, isogenies and quotients); then T_ℓψ T_ℓφ = T_ℓ[m] = m; hence V_ℓφ is invertible (Milne AV Ch. IV, Corollary 3.6, p. 142).
(d) and (e) are transport of structure, using R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist for the restricted and conjugated representations.
acceptance: For the 5-isogeny φ : E = 11a3 → E′ with kernel the rational subgroup ⟨(0,0)⟩, T_5φ is injective with cokernel Z/5 and V_5φ is an isomorphism; for ℓ ≠ 5, T_ℓφ is an isomorphism and E[ℓ] ≅ E′[ℓ] as G_Q-modules.
For [m] : A → A, coker T_ℓ[m] = T_ℓA/m T_ℓA ≅ A[m](K^sep)[ℓ^∞] has order m_ℓ^{2g} = (ℓ-part of deg [m] = m^{2g}).
For A = E_1 × E_2 a product of elliptic curves, T_ℓA = T_ℓE_1 ⊕ T_ℓE_2 has rank 4 and det = χ_ℓ² (node determinant-and-oddness).

nodes.title: The Weil pairing on Tate modules, polarization pairings and the similitude character
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let A^∨ be the dual abelian variety and Z_ℓ(1) = lim μ_{ℓ^n}(K^sep) the Tate twist (R01.1/tate-twist), on which G_K acts through χ_ℓ = cyclotomicCharacter K̄ ℓ. From A3's perfect Weil pairings e_{ℓ^n} : A[ℓ^n] × A^∨[ℓ^n] → μ_{ℓ^n}, which satisfy e_{ℓ^{n+1}}(a, a′)^ℓ = e_{ℓ^n}(ℓa, ℓa′), define e_ℓ : T_ℓA × T_ℓA^∨ → Z_ℓ(1), e_ℓ((a_n), (a′_n)) := (e_{ℓ^n}(a_n, a′_n))_n. Then e_ℓ is Z_ℓ-bilinear, perfect (it induces an isomorphism T_ℓA^∨ ≅ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(T_ℓA, Z_ℓ(1)) = (T_ℓA)^∨(1) of continuous representations, R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist) and Galois-equivariant: e_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e_ℓ(x, y) for σ ∈ G_K, writing Z_ℓ(1) additively. For a homomorphism λ : A → A^∨ put e^λ_ℓ(x, y) := e_ℓ(x, T_ℓλ(y)). Properties: (i) adjunction e_ℓ(x, T_ℓα^∨(y)) = e_ℓ(T_ℓα(x), y) for α : A → B, x ∈ T_ℓA, y ∈ T_ℓB^∨; (ii) if λ = φ_L for a line bundle L (in particular if λ is a polarization), e^λ_ℓ is alternating; (iii) for a polarization λ of degree d, e^λ_ℓ ⊗ Q_ℓ is nondegenerate, and e^λ_ℓ is perfect over Z_ℓ iff ℓ ∤ d (always when λ is principal); (iv) for α ∈ End(A) ⊗ Q and the Rosati involution α ↦ α^† of λ, e^λ_ℓ(αx, y) = e^λ_ℓ(x, α^†y); (v) for polarizations λ, μ of A, B, e^{λ×μ}_ℓ is the orthogonal sum on T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB; (vi) consequently ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) ⊂ GSp(V_ℓA, e^λ) with similitude character (multiplier) χ_ℓ, and for principal λ, ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) ⊂ GSp(T_ℓA, e^λ) ≅ GSp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) after a symplectic basis. Reducing mod ℓ^n recovers A3's pairings e_{ℓ^n} and e^λ_{ℓ^n}.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K
polarizations and the dual abelian variety are imported (A3 for the pairings; Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer E and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 for A^∨ and φ_L)
the target keeps the Tate twist Z_ℓ(1); it is never identified with Z_ℓ without a chosen compatible system of roots of unity
proofSteps: Compatibility of levels: e_{ℓ^{n+1}}(a, a′)^ℓ = e_{ℓ^n}(ℓa, ℓa′) (Milne AV Lemma 13.1, p. 57; A3 for the scheme-theoretic pairing), so the sequence (e_{ℓ^n}(a_n, a′_n)) is an element of lim μ_{ℓ^n} = Z_ℓ(1).
Perfectness: each e_{ℓ^n} is perfect (A3, Cartier duality A^∨[n] = A[n]^D), and a compatible system of perfect pairings of free Z/ℓ^n-modules of rank 2g gives a perfect pairing of the limits.
Galois equivariance: A3's pairing is a morphism of K-group schemes, so e_{ℓ^n}(σa, σa′) = σ(e_{ℓ^n}(a, a′)) = e_{ℓ^n}(a, a′)^{χ_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n} by Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.spec.
(i), (ii), (iv): Milne AV Proposition 13.2 (a)–(d), p. 58; (iv) follows from (i) and the definition α^† = λ^{−1}α^∨λ.
(iii): ker(T_ℓλ ⊗ Q_ℓ) = 0 because λ is an isogeny (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (c)); over Z_ℓ the discriminant of e^λ_ℓ is #coker T_ℓλ = d_ℓ.
(vi): from equivariance, e^λ_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ) e^λ_ℓ(x, y), which is the definition of a similitude with multiplier χ_ℓ(σ).
acceptance: χ_ℓ example: for an elliptic curve, the polarization pairing e_ℓ : T_ℓE × T_ℓE → Z_ℓ(1) is perfect alternating, so ∧²T_ℓE ≅ Z_ℓ(1) and det ρ_{E,ℓ} = χ_ℓ (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2's determinant theorem).

For E : y² = x³ − x over Q and ℓ = 2, the mod-2 pairing on E[2] = {O, P_1, P_2, P_3} takes the value −1 on every pair of distinct nonzero points and 1 on the diagonal: it is alternating and nondegenerate on (Z/2)².

nodes.title: Determinant of the Tate module and oddness over real places
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let λ be a polarization of A (abelian varieties over a field are projective, so one exists). (a) det_{Q_ℓ} ρ_{V_ℓA} = χ_ℓ^g, and if ℓ ∤ deg λ (e.g. λ principal) ∧^{2g}_{Z_ℓ} T_ℓA ≅ Z_ℓ(g), i.e. det_{Z_ℓ} ρ_{A,ℓ} = χ_ℓ^g. (b) For an elliptic curve E: ∧²T_ℓE ≅ Z_ℓ(1), det ρ_{E,ℓ} = χ_ℓ, and det ρ̄_{E,ℓ} = χ̄_ℓ = modularCyclotomicCharacter (the mod-ℓ cyclotomic character) on E[ℓ](K^sep). (c) Oddness: suppose ι : K → R is a real place, extend ι to K̄ → C, and let c ∈ G_K be the induced complex conjugation (c² = 1, χ_ℓ(c) = −1). Then for every prime ℓ (including ℓ = 2) the ±1-eigenspaces V^± of ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) are Lagrangian for e^λ_ℓ ⊗ Q_ℓ, both of dimension g; hence tr ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = 0 and det ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = (−1)^g. For an elliptic curve, det ρ_{E,ℓ}(c) = −1, i.e. ρ_{E,ℓ} is odd in the roadmap's convention (det ρ(c) = −1 at every real place; the definition is stated in stage R01.4, which may cite this node as its instance), and for ℓ odd ρ̄_{E,ℓ}(c) is conjugate to diag(1, −1). For ℓ = 2, det ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1 = −1 holds automatically and ρ̄_{E,2}(c) may be trivial. (d) Over a number field K, det ρ_{E,ℓ}(Frob_v) = q_v for every place v ∤ ℓ at which ρ_{E,ℓ} is unramified (R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters: χ_ℓ(arithmetic Frob_v) = q_v).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K
in (c), K has a real place and c is a complex conjugation attached to it; oddness is a statement about every such c
in (a) the integral statement needs ℓ ∤ deg λ; the rational one holds for every polarization
proofSteps: (a) By node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules (vi), ρ(σ) is a similitude of the nondegenerate alternating form e^λ_ℓ with multiplier χ_ℓ(σ); for a symplectic similitude h of multiplier μ on a 2g-dimensional space, det h = μ^g (det h² = μ^{2g} from h^t J h = μJ, and the sign is fixed by the Pfaffian: Pf(h^t J h) = det h · Pf J). Integrally, when e^λ_ℓ is perfect, the Pfaffian of a symplectic basis identifies ∧^{2g}T_ℓA with Z_ℓ(g).

(b) is (a) for g = 1 with the canonical principal polarization; reduction mod ℓ gives det ρ̄ = χ̄_ℓ (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.toZModPow relates χ_ℓ mod ℓ to modularCyclotomicCharacter). Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2 states the same determinant theorem for its T_ℓW (node elliptic-tate-module-comparison).

(c) c acts on roots of unity by inversion, so χ_ℓ(c) = −1 (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.spec). For x, y ∈ V^+: e(x, y) = e(cx, cy) = χ_ℓ(c)e(x, y) = −e(x, y), so 2e(x, y) = 0 and e(x, y) = 0 since Q_ℓ(1) is torsion-free; likewise for V^−. Since c² = 1 and char Q_ℓ = 0, V = V^+ ⊕ V^−; two isotropic subspaces of a 2g-dimensional nondegenerate alternating space have dimension ≤ g, so both are Lagrangian of dimension g. Hence tr = g − g = 0 and det = (−1)^g. For ℓ odd the same argument works on E[ℓ] over F_ℓ (2 is invertible), giving eigenvalues 1, −1.
ℓ = 2 caveat: over F_2, −1 = 1 and the argument shows nothing; for y² = x³ − x every 2-torsion point is real, so ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1.
(d) is (b) evaluated at a Frobenius element, using R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial (well defined at unramified places).
acceptance: E/Q any elliptic curve: Milne EC, p. 224, the Weil pairing gives ∧²E_ℓ ≅ μ_ℓ and the representation on E_ℓ is odd (det ρ̄(c) = −1).

For E : y² = x³ − x and ℓ = 2, ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1 although det ρ_{E,2}(c) = −1 in Z_2^×: oddness of ρ_{E,2} is a statement in characteristic 0, and the residual condition ρ̄(c) ≠ 1 is a separate hypothesis.
For A = E_1 × E_2 over Q, det ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = (−1)² = 1 and tr ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = 0: the correct dimension-general oddness statement is tr(c) = 0 (eigenvalues ±1 each with multiplicity g), not det(c) = −1.
Serre 1972, §5.2, p. 304: φ_ℓ(G) contains the element c with eigenvalues {1, −1} given by complex conjugation, so for ℓ ≠ 2 the image is never contained in a non-split Cartan subgroup.

nodes.title: Unramifiedness and the Frobenius polynomial at a place of good reduction
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, v a finite place of F with completion F_v (Tau Ceti NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 5), valuation ring O_v, residue field k_v = F_{q_v} of characteristic p, and fix a decomposition group D_w ⊆ G_F and inertia I_w at a place w | v of F̄ (R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place). Let A be an abelian variety of dimension g over F with good reduction at v: A_{F_v} is the generic fibre of an abelian scheme 𝒜 over O_v, with special fibre A_v := 𝒜 ⊗ k_v. Let π_v ∈ End(A_v) be the q_v-Frobenius endomorphism (raising coordinates to the q_v-th power) and ℓ ≠ p. Then: (a) V_ℓA is unramified at v (R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set): I_w acts trivially on T_ℓA. (b) Reduction 𝒜[ℓ^n](O_v^{sh}) gives a D_w-equivariant isomorphism r : T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓA_v, where D_w acts on the right through D_w → Gal(k̄_v/k_v). (c) Every arithmetic Frobenius Frob_w ∈ D_w (lifting x ↦ x^{q_v}) acts on T_ℓA as r^{−1} ∘ T_ℓ(π_v) ∘ r; a geometric Frobenius acts as the inverse. (d) Hence the Frobenius characteristic polynomial P_v(V_ℓA, X) := det(X − ρ_{A,ℓ}(Frob_w) | V_ℓA) of R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial equals det(X − V_ℓπ_v | V_ℓA_v), depends only on v (not on w or the Frobenius lift), and has constant term q_v^g and the functional equation X^{2g}P_v(q_v/X) = q_v^g P_v(X) (from the Weil pairing). (e) For elliptic curves (g = 1, A = E_W for a Weierstrass W whose minimal model over O_v has Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction): P_v(X) = X² − a_v X + q_v with a_v = WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace of the reduction = q_v + 1 − #Ẽ(k_v) ∈ Z, independent of ℓ ≠ p. (f) For general g, P_v(X) is the characteristic polynomial P_{π_v} of the endomorphism π_v in the sense of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6: monic of degree 2g in Z[X] and independent of ℓ ≠ p — this integrality and ℓ-independence is imported (gap: owner A6 is currently downstream of this stage). Convention: with H¹ := V_ℓA^∨, det(1 − T·Φ_w | H¹) = det(1 − T·Frob_w | V_ℓA) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T) for a geometric Frobenius Φ_w (the roadmap's convention), whereas det(1 − T·Φ_w | V_ℓA) = Q_v(T/q_v) with Q_v(T) := T^{2g}P_v(1/T) (by the functional equation in (d)); the latter is not the Euler factor.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p = char k_v (for ℓ = p the representation is in general ramified even with good reduction: PadicHodgeTheory R06.6 treats it)
good reduction means existence of an abelian scheme model over O_v; for elliptic curves this is Mathlib's HasGoodReduction of the minimal model
the conductor comparison (Ogg) is not stated here: it is ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3, which imports this stage
the converse (unramified ⇒ good reduction, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich) is NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5, which consumes this stage, and Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 for elliptic curves
proofSteps: (a),(b): by A3 applied over the base O_v, 𝒜[ℓ^n] is finite étale over O_v (ℓ^n invertible). A finite étale scheme over the henselian O_v^{sh} (strict henselisation, residue field k̄_v) has all its geometric generic points defined over F_v^{ur} and they reduce bijectively to k̄_v-points (Milne AV Ch. IV, proof of Theorem 3.5, p. 141: A(K_v^un)_{ℓ^n} = A_0(k^al)_{ℓ^n} has ℓ^{2n dim A} elements); hence I_w acts trivially and reduction is a D_w-isomorphism, compatible with [ℓ] and so with limits.

(c): for x ∈ A_v(k̄_v), the arithmetic Frobenius of Gal(k̄_v/k_v) raises coordinates to the q_v-th power, which is π_v(x) (Milne AV Ch. II, §1, p. 75, the Frobenius map on points; Ch. IV, p. 142: 'Frob_w acts on V_ℓA as π'); transport by r.

(d): conjugate Frobenius lifts differ by elements of I_w (trivial action) and conjugation in G_F, so the characteristic polynomial depends only on v (R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial). The constant term: det ρ(Frob_w) = χ_ℓ(Frob_w)^g = q_v^g (node determinant-and-oddness (a) and R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters). The functional equation: ρ(Frob_w) is a similitude of multiplier q_v for e^λ_ℓ, so its eigenvalues are stable under α ↦ q_v/α with multiplicities.

(e): for g = 1: det(V_ℓπ_v) = q_v by (d). Trace: det(1 − V_ℓπ_v) = deg(1 − π_v) because det(V_ℓβ) = deg β for β ∈ End(E) (Weil pairing: e(βx, βy) = e(x, β̂βy) = deg β · e(x, y), Milne EC Prop. III.3.22, p. 100), and deg(1 − π_v) = pointCount of the reduction (Tau Ceti TauCeti.Isogeny.degree_oneSubFrobeniusIsogeny_eq_pointCount); so 1 − tr + q_v = #Ẽ(k_v) and tr = q_v + 1 − #Ẽ(k_v) = frobeniusTrace (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace_eq_card_point; Milne EC Ch. IV, p. 150 and Ch. V Proposition 8.3, p. 224; DDT Proposition 2.11(a), p. 56). Both are integers independent of ℓ.

(f): P_{π_v} = det(X − V_ℓπ_v) with integer coefficients independent of ℓ is Milne AV Proposition 10.20 (p. 50), planned as AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module; the stage edge R01.6 → A6 currently forbids citing it (gap and restructure proposal).
acceptance: Supersingular good reduction: E : y² = x³ + 1 over Q at p = 5 (p ≡ 2 mod 3, Δ = −432 prime to 5): #Ẽ(F_5) = 6, a_5 = 0, P_5(X) = X² + 5; likewise a_11 = a_17 = a_23 = 0 — a_p = 0 for supersingular good reduction at p ≥ 5 by the Hasse bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p and p | a_p (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3).
E : y² = x³ − x over Q: a_3 = 0, a_5 = −2, a_7 = 0, a_13 = 6, so P_5(X) = X² + 2X + 5 and P_13(X) = X² − 6X + 13, the same for every ℓ ≠ p.
Milne AV Ch. IV, p. 142: P_v(A, t) is the characteristic polynomial of Frob_w acting on V_ℓA, defined as the Frobenius polynomial of the reduction.

nodes.title: Comparison with Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, W an elliptic Weierstrass curve over F, p a height-one prime of O_F (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum), R = p.adicCompletionIntegers F, K = p.adicCompletion F, q = #(O_F/p), and ℓ a prime not dividing q. Mathlib defines localPolynomial R (W.baseChange K) ∈ Z[X] from the minimal model W′ = (W.baseChange K).minimal R as 1 − aX + qX² with a = q + 1 − Nat.card (W′.reduction R).toAffine.Point if W′ has good reduction, 1 − X if split multiplicative, 1 + X if nonsplit multiplicative, 1 otherwise. Then: (a) if W′ has good reduction, a equals Tau Ceti's frobeniusTrace of W′.reduction R (since the reduction is elliptic, WeierstrassCurve.pointCount_eq_card_point), and localPolynomial R (W.baseChange K) = det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓE) = det(1 − X·Φ_v | V_ℓE^∨) = L_v(V_ℓE^∨, X), the local Euler factor of R01.2/local-euler-factor of H¹ = V_ℓE^∨ (node local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety), for every ℓ ∤ q; (b) if W′ has split multiplicative reduction, localPolynomial = 1 − X = det(1 − X·Φ_v | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v}); if nonsplit multiplicative, localPolynomial = 1 + X = det(1 − X·Φ_v | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v}); (c) consequently, for the places of good or multiplicative reduction, Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LFunction has the Euler factors of the Galois representation V_ℓE^∨. At additive places localPolynomial = 1, and the equality with det(1 − XΦ_v | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v}) needs (V_ℓE)^{I_v} = 0, which rests on the Néron model (connected component of the special fibre unipotent) and is NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5/local-euler-polynomial, downstream of this stage; it is not asserted here.
hypotheses: ℓ ∤ q; the residue field is finite, so Mathlib's Nat.card junk value 0 for infinite residue fields does not occur

the multiplicative cases use Tate's uniformisation over K (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4) and the theorem that an elliptic curve with split multiplicative reduction over K is K-isomorphic to a Tate curve E_q (requested from that layer)
the variable X of localPolynomial is the variable T of det(1 − T·Φ); substituting q^{−s} gives the Dirichlet-series factor
proofSteps: (a) Good reduction: node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (e) gives det(X − Frob_v | V_ℓE) = X² − aX + q with a = frobeniusTrace(W′.reduction R); hence det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓE) = 1 − aX + qX², which is Mathlib's good-reduction branch after pointCount_eq_card_point identifies Mathlib's Nat.card of the affine point type (point at infinity included) with Tau Ceti's pointCount. Transposition: geometric Frobenius on V^∨ is the transpose of arithmetic Frobenius on V, so the two determinants agree; the minimal model is used on both sides (Mathlib's localPolynomial minimises first; good reduction of the curve is HasGoodReduction of the minimal model).

(b) Split multiplicative: E_K ≅ E_q (Tate; ATAEC V.5.3), and the uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) gives 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE → Z_ℓ → 0 with inertia acting through a nontrivial unipotent (the Kummer class of q, v(q) > 0, has infinite-order image on inertia); so (V_ℓE)^{I_v} = Q_ℓ(1) and, dually, (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v} = Q_ℓ (trivial), on which Φ_v acts by 1: the factor is 1 − X (DDT Proposition 2.12(a), p. 56). Nonsplit: E is the quadratic twist of a split curve by the unramified quadratic character δ (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf, EllipticCurves Layer 5), so Φ_v acts by δ(Φ_v) = −1: the factor is 1 + X.
(c) Mathlib's LFunction is the Euler product of localEulerFactor over all primes; at good and multiplicative primes the factors agree by (a), (b).

nodes.title: The local Euler factor of an abelian variety at a finite place
nodes.statement: Let F_v be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_{q_v} of characteristic p (or a number field F with a finite place v, through R01.2/local-restriction), A an abelian variety over F_v of dimension g, and ℓ ≠ p. Put H¹_ℓ(A) := V_ℓA^∨ = Hom_{Q_ℓ}(V_ℓA, Q_ℓ) with the dual action (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist). Define L_v(A, T) := det(1 − T·Φ_v | H¹_ℓ(A)^{I_v}) ∈ Q_ℓ[T], Φ_v a geometric Frobenius (R01.2/local-euler-factor applied to the ℓ-adic representation H¹_ℓ(A), equivalently to its Weil–Deligne representation through R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor, where (ker N)^{I_v} = H¹_ℓ(A)^{I_v}). Equivalently L_v(A, T) = det(1 − T·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v}) with the arithmetic Frobenius on inertia coinvariants. Properties: (a) well defined: independent of the choice of Φ_v and of the decomposition group; (b) at a place of good reduction (ℓ ≠ p), L_v(A, T) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T) = det(1 − T·π_v | V_ℓA_v) with P_v of node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial; for elliptic curves it lies in Z[T] and is independent of ℓ, for general g likewise once the A6 input of that node is available; (c) isogeny invariance: if A and B are F_v-isogenous then L_v(A, T) = L_v(B, T); (d) multiplicativity: L_v(A × B, T) = L_v(A, T)L_v(B, T); (e) degree ≤ 2g, with equality iff V_ℓA is unramified. For a number field F, the partial L-function of A outside a finite set S ⊇ {bad places} is the formal Euler product ∏_{v ∉ S} L_v(A, q_v^{−s})^{−1}. Independence of ℓ at places of bad reduction, and integrality there, are not asserted: they are NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5 (semistable reduction and the Néron model), which consumes this stage.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p
the definition is a priori ℓ-dependent at bad places
Φ_v geometric; the arithmetic version uses coinvariants of V_ℓA
proofSteps: Definition: R01.2/local-euler-factor gives det(1 − T·r(Φ_v) | (ker N)^{I_v}) for a Weil–Deligne representation and, for an ℓ-adic representation with ℓ ≠ p, the Grothendieck monodromy functor identifies (ker N)^{I_v} with the inertia invariants (R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor).
Coinvariant form: (V^∨)^{I} = ((V)_{I})^∨ and the geometric Frobenius acting on V^∨ by f ↦ f ∘ Φ_v^{−1} is the transpose of the arithmetic Frobenius on V, so the determinants agree.
(b): V_ℓA is unramified (node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (a)), so the invariants are all of H¹ and det(1 − TΦ_v | V^∨) = det(1 − T Frob_v | V) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T).

(c): an isogeny induces an isomorphism V_ℓA ≅ V_ℓB of Q_ℓ[G_{F_v}]-modules (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (c)); (d): node functoriality (b); (e): dim H¹^{I} ≤ 2g with equality iff I acts trivially on V^∨, i.e. on V.
acceptance: Elliptic curves: L_v(E, T) agrees with Mathlib's localPolynomial at good and multiplicative places (node comparison-with-weierstrass-local-polynomial).
For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, L_5(E, T) = 1 + 2T + 5T² and L_13(E, T) = 1 − 6T + 13T².

Faltings' L-series (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4/isogeny-criterion-by-rational-tate-modules-and-local-factors) uses det(1 − (Nv)^{−s} F_v | T_l(A)) at good places with F_v the arithmetic Frobenius: this is L_v(A, (Nv)^{−s}) by the coinvariant form.
