nodes.title: Tate modules with endomorphism coefficients and their λ-adic components
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let E ⊆ End⁰_K(A) := End_K(A) ⊗ Q be a number field (a Q-subalgebra that is a field, same unit) of degree d, and O := E ∩ End_K(A) its order. (a) O ⊗ Z_ℓ acts on T_ℓA and E ⊗ Q_ℓ on V_ℓA through node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (a), commuting with ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) because the endomorphisms are defined over K. (b) E ⊗_Q Q_ℓ = ∏_{λ|ℓ} E_λ via the idempotents e_λ, so V_ℓA = ⊕_{λ|ℓ} V_λA with V_λA := V_ℓA ⊗_{E⊗Q_ℓ} E_λ = e_λV_ℓA, each a continuous E_λ-linear representation ρ_{A,λ} : G_K → Aut_{E_λ}(V_λA) (R01.1/continuous-representation over the coefficient field E_λ). (c) If V_ℓA is free over E ⊗ Q_ℓ (true with rank 2g/d: Milne AV Prop. 10.23, planned as AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/trace-and-degree-on-a-subfield — imported, gap), each V_λA has E_λ-dimension 2g/d; GL₂-type (d = g): dim 2; CM type (d = 2g): dim 1. (d) If O_E ⊆ End_K(A), T_λA := T_ℓA ⊗_{O_E⊗Z_ℓ} O_{E,λ} is a G_K-stable O_{E,λ}-lattice in V_λA and its reduction T_λA/λT_λA is the λ-torsion A[λ](K^sep) := {x ∈ A[ℓ](K^sep) : αx = 0 for all α ∈ λ}, a G_K-module over O_E/λ (the residual λ-adic representation); freeness of T_ℓA over O_E ⊗ Z_ℓ is not asserted in general (it holds for ℓ prime to the index of the endomorphism order, e.g. Serre–Tate). (e) Determinant and oddness of λ-components: if E is totally real and the Rosati involution of a polarization λ_0 is the identity on E, then e^{λ_0}_ℓ is E-balanced (e(αx, y) = e(x, αy)), V_λA ⊥ V_λ′A for λ ≠ λ′, each V_λA carries a nondegenerate E_λ-bilinear alternating form with similitude character χ_ℓ, so for GL₂-type det_{E_λ}ρ_{A,λ} = χ_ℓ, and at a real place each V_λA is odd: det_{E_λ}ρ_{A,λ}(c) = −1. For a CM field E the determinant is εχ_ℓ with ε of finite order (Ribet 1992, Lemma 3.1); that refinement uses Hodge–Tate theory and is not asserted here. (f) Frobenius: at a good place v ∤ ℓ, ρ_{A,λ}(Frob_v) is the E_λ-linear map induced by π_v, which commutes with E acting on A_v; its E_λ-characteristic polynomial is the image of the E-characteristic polynomial of π_v ∈ End⁰(A_v) (imported with (c)). (g) Over a smaller field: if the endomorphisms are defined only over a finite Galois extension L/K, V_ℓA is an E ⊗ Q_ℓ[G_L]-module and G_K acts semilinearly through Gal(L/K) → Aut(E).
hypotheses: E ⊆ End⁰_K(A): the endomorphisms are defined over K (otherwise use (g))
ℓ ≠ char K
integral statements require O_E ⊆ End_K(A)
proofSteps: (a) Functoriality of T_ℓ in endomorphisms (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (a)), extended Q_ℓ-linearly; Galois commutation because α ∈ End_K(A) commutes with the coordinate action of G_K.
(b) Chinese remainder decomposition E ⊗ Q_ℓ = ∏ E_λ; each summand e_λV_ℓA is G_K-stable because e_λ commutes with ρ.
(c) Rank: V_ℓA is free over E ⊗ Q_ℓ of rank 2g/d (Milne AV Prop. 10.23; Ribet 1992, §2 for GL₂-type: 'free of rank two over E ⊗ Q_ℓ').

(e) For α ∈ E, α^† = α gives e(αx, y) = e(x, αy) (node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules (iv)); then e(e_λx, e_λ′y) = e(x, e_λe_λ′y) = 0 for λ ≠ λ′. A Q_ℓ-bilinear E-balanced alternating form on V_λ is Tr_{E_λ/Q_ℓ} of a unique E_λ-bilinear alternating form, nondegenerate since e is; the similitude property passes to it; for a 2-dimensional symplectic space det = multiplier. Oddness: the argument of node determinant-and-oddness (c) applied inside each V_λ (c commutes with E) gives V_λ^± isotropic of E_λ-dimension 1.
(d) λ-torsion: T_λA/λT_λA = (T_ℓA/ℓT_ℓA) ⊗_{O_E/ℓ} O_E/λ = A[ℓ] ⊗ O_E/λ, which is the λ-torsion by the Chinese remainder theorem for O_E/ℓ.
(f) node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (c), with π_v commuting with the reductions of the endomorphisms.
acceptance: CM curve over Q (required example): E : y² = x³ − x has CM by Z[i], defined over Q(i) but not over Q. Over K = Q(i), V_ℓE is free of rank 1 over Q(i) ⊗ Q_ℓ (Serre 1972 §4.5: T_ℓ free of rank 1 over R_ℓ), so ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_{Q(i)}) ⊆ (Z[i] ⊗ Z_ℓ)^×, an abelian group, the Cartan subgroup. Over Q, complex conjugation c satisfies c·i = −i·c (semilinearity (g)), so ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) lies in the normaliser of that Cartan, with ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) ⊄ Cartan; for ℓ = 5 (split in Q(i)) V_5E = V_λ ⊕ V_λ̄ over Q(i), two characters of G_{Q(i)} swapped by c, so V_5E ≅ Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} ψ_λ (R01.1/continuous-induction) with ψ_λ the λ-adic avatar of the Hecke character of E (owned by ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4).

Consistency with a_p = 0: for p ≡ 3 mod 4 (inert in Q(i)), Frob_p ∈ G_Q \ G_{Q(i)} acts by an element of the non-identity coset of the Cartan normaliser, which has trace 0 — matching a_3 = a_7 = a_11 = a_19 = a_23 = 0 computed for y² = x³ − x.

GL₂-type: for A_f attached to a weight-two newform f with trivial character, E = K_f is totally real, the Hecke algebra acts by Rosati-fixed endomorphisms, and each V_λ(A_f) is two-dimensional with determinant χ_ℓ (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.6 consumes this).

nodes.title: Galois generic and p-Galois generic abelian varieties
nodes.statement: Let k be a number field and (A, λ) a principally polarized abelian variety over k of dimension g ≥ 1. For a prime p, ρ_{A,p} : G_k → GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p) (node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules (vi)) is the action on the p-power torsion; a symplectic Z_p-basis identifies GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p) with GSp_{2g}(Z_p), uniquely up to conjugation. A is p-Galois generic if ρ_{A,p}(G_k) is open in GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p)(Z_p) (equivalently, being closed, of finite index). Let ρ̂_A : G_k → ∏_p GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p) = GSp(T̂A, e^λ) ≅ GSp_{2g}(Ẑ) be the action on all torsion (adelic Tate module, node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety). A is Galois generic if ρ̂_A(G_k) is open in GSp_{2g}(Ẑ). Both notions are independent of the choice of symplectic basis. Galois generic implies p-Galois generic for every p (projection to a factor is open); the converse implication (Cadoret) and isogeny/conjugation invariance are statements of AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian G0, which consumes this definition.
hypotheses: k a number field
λ a principal polarization (for g = 1 the canonical one; then GSp_2 = GL_2)
proofSteps: The images are compact (G_k is profinite and ρ continuous), hence closed; a closed subgroup of a profinite group is open iff of finite index.
Basis independence: two symplectic bases differ by an element of GSp_{2g}(Z_p) (resp. GSp_{2g}(Ẑ)), and conjugation preserves openness.
Galois generic ⇒ p-Galois generic: the projection GSp_{2g}(Ẑ) → GSp_{2g}(Z_p) is a continuous open surjective homomorphism, and the image of an open subgroup under an open map is open.
Base change: for a finite extension k′/k, G_{k′} is open of finite index in G_k, so (p-)Galois genericity over k and over k′ are equivalent.
acceptance: g = 1: GSp_2 = GL_2, and a non-CM elliptic curve over Q is p-Galois generic for every p (Serre's open image theorem; the theorem itself is owned downstream by AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian G0/serre-open-image, since its proof uses Faltings' theorems).

A CM elliptic curve (e.g. y² = x³ − x over Q) is never p-Galois generic: its image lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup (node tate-module-with-endomorphism-coefficients), which has infinite index in GL_2(Z_p).

nodes.title: Serre: independence and connectedness of the ℓ-adic images after a finite extension
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K, ρ̂ : G_K → ∏_ℓ GL(T_ℓA) its adelic representation (node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety), and for a subgroup U ⊆ ∏_ℓ GL(T_ℓA) let U_ℓ be its image in GL(T_ℓA). Say U satisfies the ℓ-independence property if U = ∏_ℓ U_ℓ (Richard–Yafaev, Def. 2.4), and U_ℓ is Zariski connected if its Zariski closure in GL(V_ℓA) (a Q_ℓ-algebraic group) is connected. Then there is a finite extension L/K such that U := ρ̂(G_L) (1) satisfies the ℓ-independence property and (2) has every U_ℓ Zariski connected; moreover the kernel of G_K → G_ℓ/G_ℓ° (G_ℓ the Zariski closure of ρ_ℓ(G_K)) is independent of ℓ. These are Serre's theorems as Richard–Yafaev Theorem 4.9 cites them. The third clause of that theorem, U ⊆ M(Ẑ) for the Mumford–Tate group M, rests on Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, whose owners (ShimuraData D1, AutomorphicBundles B1) consume this stage; it is not stated here (gap and restructure proposal R01.6-RS3).
hypotheses: K a number field
the proofs of (1) and (2) cited by the source were not read; their inputs that might lie downstream of this stage are recorded as a gap
proofSteps: (2) Serre (Œuvres IV nos. 133, 135; Larsen–Pink 1992, 6.14, as cited by Richard–Yafaev): the component group of the Zariski closure G_ℓ of ρ_ℓ(G_K) defines a finite quotient G_K → G_ℓ/G_ℓ° whose kernel is independent of ℓ; its proof compares Frobenius characteristic polynomials across ℓ (node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial) through Chebotarev density (Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10). Take L ⊇ the fixed field of that kernel.

(1) Serre (Œuvres IV no. 136, Th. 1; Serre 2013, §3.1, as cited): a criterion for a family of ℓ-adic representations to become independent after a finite extension, verified for abelian varieties using bounded ramification (R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence) and the ℓ-independence of Frobenius polynomials.

Placement check: if the cited proofs of (1) or (2) use Faltings' semisimplicity (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4) or semistable reduction (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3), both downstream of R01.6, the theorem must move to a stage downstream of them (restructure proposal R01.6-RS2).
acceptance: For a non-CM elliptic curve over Q, U is open in ∏ GL_2(Z_ℓ) (Serre 1972) and every U_ℓ is Zariski dense in GL_2, hence connected with L = Q; ℓ-independence holds only after a finite extension (the Serre curve phenomenon: Q(√Δ) ⊆ Q(ζ_N) entangles the 2-adic and N-adic images).

For a CM elliptic curve over Q with CM field F, the Zariski closure of U_ℓ for L = Q is the normaliser of a torus, which is disconnected; after L ⊇ F it is the torus Res_{F/Q}G_m ⊗ Q_ℓ, connected — the finite extension in (2) is needed.

sources.match: Statement of the three properties after a finite extension L/K, with references.
Zariski connectedness of the ℓ-adic images, citing Serre Œuvres IV 133, 135 and Larsen–Pink 6.14.
ℓ-independence: U = ∏_p U_p with U_p ≤ M(Q_p).

nodes.title: Specialization of Tate modules and Galois images in a family (Noot, after Serre)
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of finite type over Q, S a normal absolutely irreducible F-variety with function field K = F(S), η : Spec K → S the generic point, X/S an abelian scheme of relative dimension g. For every closed point σ of S, with a point σ̄ of the normalisation S̄ of S in K̄ over it and decomposition group D_σ ⊆ G_K, the specialisation maps s_n : X_η[n](K̄) ≅ X[n](S̄) ≅ X_σ[n](F̄) are group isomorphisms (X[n] is finite étale over S, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3), compatible in n and D_σ-equivariant, where D_σ acts on the right through D_σ ↠ Gal(F̄/F(σ)); their limit is a D_σ-equivariant isomorphism T_ℓX_η ≅ T_ℓX_σ for every ℓ (and on adelic Tate modules), so ρ_{X_η,ℓ}(D_σ) = ρ_{X_σ,ℓ}(Gal(F̄/F(σ))) ⊆ ρ_{X_η,ℓ}(G_K). This is Noot §1.2 and the diagram Richard–Yafaev use in the proof of Proposition 4.8. Serre's complement (Noot Prop. 1.3: for each ℓ some closed point σ gives equality of images) needs Hilbert irreducibility for compact ℓ-adic Lie quotients, owned by InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, which lies downstream of this stage; it is not stated here (restructure proposal R01.6-RS4). The consequence End_K̄(X_η) = End_F̄(X_σ) (Noot Cor. 1.5) uses Faltings' theorem over fields of finite type and belongs to FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.
hypotheses: F of finite type over Q (characteristic 0, so all X[n] are finite étale over S)
X/S an abelian scheme; an abelian variety over K is first spread out to such an X over a dense open of a model (Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0E, spreading out)
proofSteps: X[n] → S is finite étale (A3, n invertible since char F = 0); a point of X_η[n](K̄) extends uniquely to an S̄-point (finiteness), and specialising at σ̄ is a bijection onto X_σ[n](F̄) (étaleness) (Noot §1.2, p. 163). Compatibility with D_σ: D_σ preserves σ̄ and acts on the residue field through Gal(F̄/F(σ)). Pass to limits as in node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety.

Richard–Yafaev's use (proof of Prop. 4.8): F := Q in Noot's notation, a number field F′ ⊆ K̄ and A_{F′} with T_A ≅ T_{A_{F′}}, the commutative diagram giving ρ(D_{F′}) = ρ′(Gal(F̄′/F′)) — which is (a) — and the endomorphism identity (10), which is Noot Cor. 1.5 and depends on Faltings ([FW, VI, 3]).
acceptance: Legendre family X : y² = x(x − 1)(x − t) over S = A¹ \ {0, 1} over Q: specialising at t = −1 gives y² = x³ − x, whose ℓ-adic image is contained in a Cartan normaliser, a proper subgroup of the generic image (open in GL_2(Z_ℓ) after Igusa); so (a) gives only an inclusion ρ_σ(G_{Q}) ⊆ ρ_η(G_K); the equality of images of Serre's complement fails at such CM points.
Noot §1.2: the identification T_lX_η ≅ T_lX_σ and the diagram with D_σ ↠ Gal(F̄/F(σ)) is exactly (a) (read on the page image, p. 163).

sources.match: Specialisation of torsion and Tate modules along a closed point, D_σ-equivariantly.

nodes.title: Required examples: χ_p, the split Tate curve, supersingular good reduction, a CM curve over Q, Frobenius conventions
nodes.statement: (1) χ_p: the Tate module of μ_{p^∞} is Z_p(1) with G_Q acting through χ_p, χ_p(Frob_ℓ) = ℓ for ℓ ≠ p, χ_p(c) = −1, HT(χ_p) = +1; it is det T_pE for every elliptic curve E/Q (node determinant-and-oddness). (2) Split Tate curve: for a p-adic field K, q ∈ K^× with |q| < 1 and ℓ ≠ p, Tau Ceti's uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) gives 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE_q → Z_ℓ → 0, the extension class being the Kummer class of q; inertia acts through a nontrivial unipotent (so V_ℓE_q is ramified, with (V_ℓE_q)^{I} = Q_ℓ(1)), the Frobenius polynomial on V_ℓ^{I} is X − q_K and L(E_q, T) = 1 − T; example 11a3 at 11. (3) Supersingular good reduction: y² = x³ + 1 over Q at p ∈ {5, 11, 17, 23} has a_p = 0 and P_p(X) = X² + p; in general good supersingular reduction at p ≥ 5 forces a_p = 0 (p | a_p and |a_p| ≤ 2√p < p). (4) CM curve over Q: y² = x³ − x (CM by Z[i]): ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) lies in the normaliser of the Cartan subgroup (Z[i] ⊗ Z_ℓ)^×, ρ_{E,ℓ}|_{G_{Q(i)}} is abelian (the λ-adic Hecke character), V_ℓE ⊗ Q̄_ℓ ≅ Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} ψ, and a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4. (5) Frobenius conventions on a finite field: for E/F_q with a = q + 1 − #E(F_q), the arithmetic Frobenius φ : x ↦ x^q acts on T_ℓE as π (characteristic polynomial X² − aX + q), the geometric Frobenius φ^{−1} as π^{−1} (X² − (a/q)X + 1/q), and on H¹ = V_ℓE^∨ the geometric Frobenius has characteristic polynomial X² − aX + q, so det(1 − TΦ | H¹) = 1 − aT + qT² is the local factor; for y² = x³ − x over F_5: X² + 2X + 5, X² + (2/5)X + 1/5, X² + 2X + 5 and 1 + 2T + 5T².
hypotheses: the CM and Hecke-character statements of (4) are owned by ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4; this node only computes them on the Tate module
proofSteps: (1): R01.1/tate-twist and R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters; det by node determinant-and-oddness (b).

(2): Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 (Tate curve, uniformisation, Galois equivariance); the ℓ^n-torsion of K̄^×/q^Z is generated by μ_{ℓ^n} and an ℓ^n-th root of q; Kummer theory shows inertia acts unipotently and nontrivially since v(q) > 0 (DDT Prop. 2.12); the local factor by node comparison-with-weierstrass-local-polynomial (b).
(3): node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (e) and the point counts; Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3 (supersingular iff p | a_p over F_p, Hasse bound).

(4): node tate-module-with-endomorphism-coefficients (acceptance), Serre 1972 §4.5; induction by R01.1/continuous-induction; a_p = 0 for inert p since Frob_p lies in the non-identity coset of the normaliser, of trace 0.
(5): node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (c) over the finite field itself (A = E over F_q, good reduction trivially), node local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety for the transpose.
acceptance: Point counts (Tau Ceti pointCount convention, singular point included): y² = x³ − x has a_3 = 0, a_5 = −2, a_7 = 0, a_13 = 6; y² = x³ + 1 has a_5 = a_11 = a_17 = a_23 = 0, a_7 = −4, a_13 = 2; 11a3 (y² + y = x³ − x²) has a_11 = 1 (split multiplicative) and a_5 = 1.
Milne EC, Ch. IV, p. 158: for the CM curve X³ + Y³ + Z³ = 0 and p ≢ 1 mod 3, #E(F_p) = p + 1 and a_p = 0 'for half the primes'.

sources.match: CM curves have a_p = 0 for half the primes.

nodes.title: Tensor, symmetric and exterior powers of continuous representations
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group, A a topological commutative ring and (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A M (R01.1: M finite projective of constant rank n with its module topology, jointly continuous action). For d ≥ 0 define (i) T^d ρ on M^{⊗d} = ⨂_{i∈Fin d} M (g ↦ ρ(g)^{⊗d}); (ii) Sym^d ρ on Sym[A]^d M (the quotient of M^{⊗d} by the permutation relation, Mathlib SymmetricPower) by the Tau Ceti action Representation.symmetricPower ρ d; (iii) ∧^d ρ on ⋀[A]^d M (Mathlib exteriorPower) by the Tau Ceti action Representation.exteriorPower ρ d. Each is again an object of ContinuousRep Γ A: the module is finite projective of rank n^d, binom(n+d−1, d) and binom(n, d) respectively, it carries its module topology, and the action is jointly continuous. These constructions are functorial in Γ-equivariant A-linear maps, commute with coefficient extension along continuous A → B and with restriction along continuous group homomorphisms. Characteristic-polynomial identities: if ρ(g) has characteristic polynomial ∏_{i=1}^n (X − α_i) over some A-algebra B in which it splits, then det(X − Sym^d ρ(g)) = ∏_{i_1≤…≤i_d}(X − α_{i_1}⋯α_{i_d}) and det(X − ∧^d ρ(g)) = ∏_{i_1<…<i_d}(X − α_{i_1}⋯α_{i_d}); in general the coefficients of these polynomials are universal integer polynomials in the coefficients of det(X − ρ(g)). ∧^n ρ ≅ det ρ (a rank-one ContinuousRep), ∧^d ρ = 0 for d > n, and when 2 ∈ A^× the symmetriser and antisymmetriser give ρ^{⊗2} ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊕ ∧^2 ρ.
hypotheses: M finite projective over A (a framed M = A^n is the special case where a basis is chosen); for the rank formulas A ≠ 0 and M of constant rank n

No invertibility of d! is assumed for the construction; Sym^d is the quotient (coinvariant) symmetric power, not the invariant symmetric tensors or the divided power Γ^d, which differ from it when d! ∉ A^×

The characteristic polynomial identities are statements about Γ acting through ρ; at an unramified place v they give P_v(Sym^d ρ, X) and P_v(∧^d ρ, X) from P_v(ρ, X) with the arithmetic-Frobenius convention of R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial
proofSteps: Underlying abstract representations: use Representation.symmetricPower and Representation.exteriorPower (Tau Ceti, RepresentationTheory/SymmetricPower.lean and ExteriorPower.lean), which give the action through SymmetricPower.map and exteriorPower.map; tensor powers through iterated Representation.tprod (Mathlib).

Finite projectivity and rank: for M free with basis b, Module.Basis.symmetricPower and Module.Basis.exteriorPower give bases indexed by multisets Sym κ d and d-element subsets, so SymmetricPower.finrank_eq and exteriorPower.finrank_eq give the ranks; for projective M localise at primes (or write M as a direct summand of A^N and use functoriality of the three constructions in split idempotents) and use compatibility with base change.

Continuity: M^{⊗d}, Sym^d M and ∧^d M are finite A-modules and carry the module topology (IsModuleTopology); every A-linear map between finite modules with the module topology is continuous, and the action map Γ × M^{⊗d} → M^{⊗d} is jointly continuous because in a basis of a free module containing M as a summand its matrix entries are polynomials in the entries of ρ(g), which are continuous by R01.1/continuous-representation; Sym^d and ∧^d are continuous quotients of M^{⊗d}.

Characteristic polynomials: for a split endomorphism choose (after a faithfully flat or splitting extension, e.g. A → A[α_1,…,α_n] universal splitting algebra) a triangular basis; SymmetricPower.map_basis_symmetricPower_of_apply_basis and the exterior analogue show the induced map is triangular with diagonal entries the monomials α_{i_1}⋯α_{i_d}; descend coefficients since the universal splitting algebra is free over A. SymmetricPower.trace_map_of_apply_basis gives the trace case.

∧^n ρ ≅ det ρ: exteriorPower.finrank_eq gives rank one, and ∧^n f acts by det f on the top exterior power; ∧^d M = 0 for d > n by the basis count. Tensor-square decomposition when 2 is invertible: the idempotents (1 ± swap)/2 on M^{⊗2} commute with ρ(g)^{⊗2}; compare with TauCeti.tensorSquareFDRepIso over ℂ (Tau Ceti ClassicalGroups layer 1), whose proof is the same.
acceptance: Computation: for ρ = 1 ⊕ χ (χ a character) Sym^d ρ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^d χ^i and ∧^2 ρ ≅ χ; for ρ the p-adic Tate module of an elliptic curve (R01.6), ∧^2 ρ ≅ Z_p(1) (Weil pairing).
At an unramified place, P_v(Sym^2 ρ, X) for ρ of rank two with P_v(ρ, X) = X^2 − aX + b is X^3 − (a^2 − b)X^2 + b(a^2 − b)X − b^3.

Non-example in characteristic p: for k = F_p, the GL_2(k)-module Sym^p k^2 is not isomorphic to its dual twisted by det^p (it contains the Frobenius twist k^{2,(1)} spanned by x^p, y^p as a submodule but not as a quotient); the dual of Sym^d is the divided power Γ^d.

nodes.title: Tensor induction from an open subgroup (Asai representation in index two)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, H ≤ Γ an open subgroup of index m, A a topological commutative ring and (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep H A V of rank n. Choose a left transversal t_1,…,t_m of Γ/H and let Φ_t : Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m be the monomial homomorphism, g t_i = t_{π_g(i)} h_i(g) with h_i(g) ∈ H (ProfiniteCohomology layer 13, milestones 1–2). The tensor induction ⊗-Ind_H^Γ ρ is V^{⊗m} = ⨂_{i=1}^m V with g acting by g·(v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ v_m) = ⊗_i ρ(h_i(g)) v_{i} placed in slot π_g(i). It is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A of rank n^m; a different transversal gives a canonically isomorphic representation; it is functorial, multiplicative (⊗-Ind(ρ ⊗ ρ′) ≅ ⊗-Ind ρ ⊗ ⊗-Ind ρ′), compatible with coefficient extension and transitive in towers. If H is normal, its restriction to H is ⊗_{i} ρ^{t_i} (with ρ^{t}(h) = ρ(t^{-1} h t)). Trace formula: for g ∈ Γ with cycles C_1,…,C_r of π_g on Γ/H, of lengths ℓ_j and starting coset t_{i_j}H, tr(⊗-Ind ρ)(g) = ∏_j tr ρ(t_{i_j}^{−1} g^{ℓ_j} t_{i_j}). For m = 2, H = G_K ⊂ G_F = Γ (K/F quadratic), As(ρ) := ⊗-Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ is the Asai representation: As(ρ)|_{G_K} ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^σ, and As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} is the other extension of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ to G_F.
hypotheses: H open (so of finite index); no invertibility hypothesis on A
the isomorphism class is independent of the transversal, the representation on a fixed model is not
As(ρ) and As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} are different extensions of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ; sources that do not distinguish them must say so
proofSteps: Monomial homomorphism Φ_t : Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m and its continuity for open H: ProfiniteCohomology layer 13 milestones 1–2 (requested); the action of the permutation wreath product H^m ⋊ S_m on V^{⊗m} (factors permuted, H^m acting factorwise) is a group action because the place-permutation action of S_m on PiTensorProduct commutes appropriately with ⊗_i ρ(h_i).
Change of transversal t′_i = t_i u_i (u_i ∈ H): the map ⊗_i ρ(u_i)^{−1} intertwines the two actions; canonicity follows from the cocycle identity of Φ under change of transversal.
Continuity: the matrix entries of ⊗-Ind ρ(g) are products of entries of ρ(h_i(g)), and g ↦ (h_i(g), π_g) is locally constant in π and continuous in h because H is open.

Restriction to normal H and the trace formula: compute Φ_t on H (π_h = id, h_i(h) = t_i^{−1} h t_i) and, for general g, the trace of a permuted tensor product is the product over cycles of traces of the cycle products (standard; CG20 and BCGP21 use only m = 2).
Asai case m = 2: As(ρ)|_{G_K} = ρ ⊗ ρ^σ by the restriction formula; the action of a lift of σ is the swap composed with ρ(σ^2) in one factor, as in CG20's explicit realisation.
acceptance: CG20, proof of Example 4.11: for K/Q imaginary quadratic and ρ: G_K → GL_2(F_p) with det ρ = ε^{1−k}, ad⁰(Ind_K^Q ρ) ≅ As(ρ) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ) up to replacing As by its quadratic twist; the element c·(g, h) with g = diag(x, x^{−1}), h = diag(y, y^{−1}) acts on As with eigenvalues xy, (xy)^{−1}, ±1.
BCGP21 §7.5.16: for W = Ind_H^G V with V two-dimensional, ∧^2 W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ (characteristic ≠ 2).
Degenerate: for m = 1, ⊗-Ind_Γ^Γ ρ = ρ; for V = A the trivial rank-one representation, ⊗-Ind V is trivial; for a character ψ of H, ⊗-Ind ψ = ψ ∘ Ver_{Γ→H} (the transfer).

nodes.title: Restriction of scalars of the coefficients
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a continuous homomorphism of topological commutative rings making B a finite projective A-module of constant rank r with the module topology (B's topology is the A-module topology), and let (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ B M of rank n. The restriction of scalars Res_{B/A} ρ is M regarded as an A-module with the same action; it is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A M of rank rn. Characteristic polynomials: det_A(X − ρ(g) | M) = N_{B[X]/A[X]}(det_B(X − ρ(g) | M)). If B is étale over A and A → A′ splits B (B ⊗_A A′ ≅ ∏_{σ ∈ Hom_A(B, A′)} A′), then (Res_{B/A} ρ) ⊗_A A′ ≅ ⊕_σ ρ ⊗_{B,σ} A′. For finite extensions E′/E of coefficient fields finite over Q_ℓ, Res_{E′/E} is the forgetful functor from E′-linear to E-linear continuous representations. Restriction of scalars along the base field (an abelian variety Res_{L/K} A) is not this construction: on Galois representations it is induction (R01.1/continuous-induction).
hypotheses: B finite projective over A with the A-module topology (true for finite extensions of complete DVRs and of finite fields)
the norm formula uses B[X] finite projective over A[X]
the splitting statement needs B étale over A
proofSteps: The A-module M is finite projective since B is finite projective over A; the module topology over A agrees with that over B (transitivity of module topologies for finite modules), so joint continuity is unchanged.

Norm formula: for M free over B use the block matrix of ρ(g) over A obtained from an A-basis of B; det of the A-linear map equals N_{B/A} of the B-determinant (Mathlib Algebra.norm transitivity, det of restriction of scalars); for projective M localise.
Splitting: B ⊗_A A′ ≅ ∏_σ A′ gives M ⊗_A A′ ≅ M ⊗_B (B ⊗_A A′) ≅ ⊕_σ M ⊗_{B,σ} A′, Γ-equivariantly.
acceptance: For E′ = Q_ℓ(√u) unramified quadratic over E = Q_ℓ and a character ψ : Γ → E′^×, Res_{E′/E} ψ is two-dimensional with characteristic polynomial X^2 − Tr(ψ(g))X + N(ψ(g)), and after extending scalars to E′ it is ψ ⊕ ψ^{Frob}.
For A = B the construction is the identity; for B = A^r (r copies) Res is the direct sum of the r components.

nodes.title: The adjoint representation, the trace kernel and the quotient by scalars
nodes.statement: Let (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A M of rank n ≥ 1. (i) ad ρ is End_A(M) with g·X = ρ(g) X ρ(g)^{−1} (Mathlib Representation.linHom ρ ρ), an object of ContinuousRep Γ A of rank n^2, canonically ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^∨. (ii) The scalars A·1 ⊂ ad ρ form a trivial subrepresentation; the quotient ad ρ / A·1 (the pgl-module) is a ContinuousRep of rank n^2 − 1. (iii) The trace tr : ad ρ → A is Γ-equivariant onto the trivial representation; ad⁰ ρ := ker tr (the sl-module) is a ContinuousRep of rank n^2 − 1. (iv) The trace pairing (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) on ad ρ is perfect and Γ-invariant, and induces a Γ-isomorphism ad⁰ ρ ≅ (ad ρ / A·1)^∨ for every A. (v) If n ∈ A^×, then ad ρ = A·1 ⊕ ad⁰ ρ, the composite ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ → ad ρ/A·1 is an isomorphism, and the trace pairing restricts to a perfect pairing on ad⁰ ρ, so ad⁰ ρ is self-dual. (vi) If A is a field of characteristic p with p | n, then A·1 ⊂ ad⁰ ρ, so ad⁰ ρ contains the trivial representation, ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ/A·1 has kernel and cokernel of rank one, and the trace pairing on ad⁰ ρ is degenerate with radical A·1. The three modules ad ρ, ad⁰ ρ and ad ρ/A·1 are kept distinct throughout. (vii) Lie-algebra form: when M = A^n these are gl_n, sl_n and pgl_n := gl_n/scalars with the adjoint action of GL_n(A) through ρ. (viii) For a Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) on V (R01.2), ad(r, N) := (ad r, [N, −]) on End(V), a Weil–Deligne representation.
hypotheses: M finite projective of constant rank n ≥ 1
no hypothesis on n for (i)–(iv); n ∈ A^× for (v)
in (viii) the Weil–Deligne relation for ad follows from that of (r, N)
proofSteps: Use Representation.linHom ρ ρ (Mathlib) for the action; continuity of the action map as for ρ ⊗ ρ^∨ (G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers and R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist); over a normed field ContRepresentation.linHom (Tau Ceti) is the continuous counterpart and agrees in finite dimension.

Equivariance of the trace: tr(ρ(g) X ρ(g)^{−1}) = tr X. The trace form is nondegenerate on matrices over any commutative ring (TauCeti.traceBilinForm_nondegenerate); for finite projective M localise to the free case, so the trace pairing on End_A(M) is perfect.
Duality (iv): the annihilator of A·1 under the trace pairing is ker tr = ad⁰, so the perfect pairing on ad induces ad⁰ ≅ (ad/A·1)^∨.
Splitting (v): X ↦ (tr X / n)·1 is an equivariant projection onto A·1 with kernel ad⁰; nondegeneracy on ad⁰ follows from (iv) and ad⁰ ≅ ad/A·1.
(vi): tr(1) = n = 0 in A, so 1 ∈ ad⁰ and tr(1·Y) = tr Y = 0 for Y ∈ ad⁰.
(viii): if r(w) N r(w)^{−1} = q^{v′(w)} N (R01.2 normalisation) then r(w)[N, X]r(w)^{−1} = q^{v′(w)}[N, r(w)Xr(w)^{−1}], and [N, −] is nilpotent.
acceptance: For n = 2 and 2 ∈ A^×, ad⁰ ρ ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊗ det ρ^{−1}; this is the Galois side of the Gelbart–Jacquet relation Ad(π) = Sym^2(π) ⊗ ω_π^{−1} used by GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4.
For n = p = char k (e.g. n = 2, k = F_2), the identity matrix lies in sl_2(k), so H^0(H, ad⁰) ≠ 0 for every subgroup H; this is why ACC+ note that no subgroup of GL_n(k) is enormous when p | n.
CHT08 §2.1: for 𝒢_n-valued r, ad extends to 𝒢_n on gl_n with ad(j)(x) = −ᵗx, and over Z[1/2] the 𝒢_n-invariants of gl_n vanish (G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group).

nodes.title: Similitude groups GSp and GO of a perfect form, with multiplier
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M a finite projective R-module with a perfect bilinear form B : M × M → R that is ε-symmetric (B(x, y) = εB(y, x), ε ∈ {±1}; for ε = −1 require B alternating, B(x, x) = 0). The similitude group scheme GAut(M, B) over R has points GAut(M, B)(R′) = {(g, ν) ∈ GL(M ⊗ R′) × R′^× : B(gx, gy) = ν B(x, y)}; ν is a character (the multiplier); since B is perfect, ν is determined by g. Write GSp(M, B) for ε = −1 and GO(M, B) for ε = +1, and Sp, O for the kernels of ν. Matrix forms: GSp_{2m} := GSp(R^{2m}, J_{2m}) with J_{2m} = (0, 1_m; −1_m, 0) (BLGGT §1.1), GO_n := GO(R^n, 1_n), and for the paper-specific normalisations GSp_4 with BCGP21's J = (0, s; −s, 0), s = (0 1; 1 0), and with CG20's antidiagonal J; BCG25's G_n is GSp_n (n even, A_n = J_n) or GO_n (n odd, A_n = 1_n). Lie algebras: gsp/go = {X : B(Xx, y) + B(x, Xy) = c B(x, y), c ∈ R}, with sp/so the kernel of dν. If 2 ∈ R^×, gsp(M, B) = sp(M, B) ⊕ R·1, the scalar line being central with trivial adjoint action, and dν(1) = 2. A determinant constraint: g ∈ GSp_{2m}(R) has det g = ν(g)^m, and g ∈ GO_n(R) has (det g)^2 = ν(g)^n.
hypotheses: B perfect (the map M → M^∨, x ↦ B(x, −), is an isomorphism), not merely nondegenerate
alternating forms are required for the symplectic case so that characteristic 2 is covered; then rank M is even
the splitting gsp = sp ⊕ scalars needs 2 ∈ R^×
proofSteps: The functor of points is represented by a closed subgroup scheme of GL(M) × G_m: in a basis it is cut out by the entries of g B ᵗg − ν B (BLGGT and CHT use gJᵗg or ᵗgJg, equivalent since J^{−1} = −J); this extends Tau Ceti's ConstantForm construction (the case ν = 1: TauCeti.ConstantForm.groupScheme, TauCeti.Symplectic.groupScheme, TauCeti.Orthogonal.groupScheme) by the extra G_m coordinate, i.e. the Hopf ideal generated by the entries of X C Xᵀ − t C in O(GL_n × G_m) (Tau Ceti Hopf-ideal/closed-subgroup classification).
Points: Sp_{2m}(R) is Mathlib's Matrix.symplecticGroup for its J = fromBlocks 0 (−1) 1 0 after the change of basis J ↦ −J; O_n(R) is Matrix.orthogonalGroup.
Multiplier is a homomorphism and determined by g: perfectness of B.
Lie algebra splitting for 2 ∈ R^×: X ↦ X − (c/2)·1 (CG20 E18 reasoning); Ad(g) fixes scalars, and Ad(g) preserves c because ν(g) cancels.
det g = ν^m on GSp_{2m}: Pfaffian identity Pf(gJᵗg) = det(g) Pf(J); (det g)^2 = ν^n on GO_n by taking determinants of gᵗg = ν·1.
acceptance: GSp_2 = GL_2 with ν = det (every 2×2 matrix satisfies gJᵗg = det(g) J).
For R = F_7 and n = 7, the form B_6 on Sym^6 F_7^2 of G7/symmetric-power-polarization is identified up to scalar with 1_7, so Sym^6 of a GL_2(F_7)-valued representation lands in GO_7(F_7).
For p > 2 and k a field of characteristic p, gsp_4(k) = sp_4(k) ⊕ k·1_4 has dimension 11 = 10 + 1 with trivial action on the scalar line (CG20, corrected).

nodes.title: Polarized representations: an actual pairing, a multiplier and a sign
nodes.statement: (a) Group-theoretic form. Let Γ be profinite, Δ ≤ Γ an open subgroup of index 2, A a topological commutative ring and (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Δ A M of rank n. For c ∈ Γ ∖ Δ with c^2 = 1, a polarization of ρ at c is a pair (μ, ⟨ , ⟩) of a continuous character μ : Γ → A^× and a perfect A-bilinear pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : M × M → A such that ⟨ρ(σ)x, ρ(cσc)y⟩ = μ(σ)⟨x, y⟩ for all σ ∈ Δ, x, y ∈ M, and ⟨x, y⟩ = ε⟨y, x⟩ for a sign ε = ε_c ∈ {±1} (for ε = −1 the pairing is required to be alternating when 2 ∉ A^×). (b) Number fields (BLGGT §2.1). Let F be CM or totally real with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; for F imaginary take Γ = G_{F⁺}, Δ = G_F; for F = F⁺ take Δ = Γ = G_F (then cσc ∈ G_F). A polarized representation of G_F is (ρ, μ) with ρ ∈ ContinuousRep G_F A M and μ : G_{F⁺} → A^× continuous, together with, for some real place v of F⁺ and complex conjugation c_v ∈ G_{F⁺} at v, a sign ε_v and a pairing as in (a) at c = c_v; when F is imaginary one further requires ε_v = −μ(c_v). (c) CHT form: for any γ_0 ∈ Γ ∖ Δ (no condition γ_0^2 = 1), a triple (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩) with μ(δ)⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨ρ(δ)x, ρ(γ_0 δ γ_0^{−1})y⟩ for δ ∈ Δ and ⟨x, ρ(γ_0^2)y⟩ = −μ(γ_0)⟨y, x⟩; for γ_0 = c_v this is (b) with ε_v = −μ(c_v). The pair (ρ, μ) is polarizable if some pairing exists; essentially conjugate self-dual (ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ|_{G_F}) is the weaker condition with no pairing. A polarized representation is the data (ρ, μ, v, ⟨ , ⟩), not the property.
hypotheses: ⟨ , ⟩ perfect: the map M → M^∨ is an isomorphism (over a field, nondegenerate)
the coefficient ring is arbitrary (fields E/Q_ℓ, finite fields, complete local Noetherian rings, Q̄_ℓ), so the same definition serves l-adic, mod l and deformation-theoretic uses
for F imaginary the condition ε_v = −μ(c_v) is part of the definition; for F totally real it is not imposed (ρ then factors through GSp or GO according to μ(c_v) = −ε_v or μ(c_v) = ε_v)
mod l with l = 2: alternating and symmetric pairings differ, so ε alone does not determine the type; the alternating requirement is recorded
proofSteps: Well-definedness and independence of v: G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (change of place ⟨x, y⟩_{v′} = ⟨x, ρ(c_v c_{v′})y⟩_v, ε_{v′} = μ(c_v c_{v′})ε_v).
Equivalence of (b) and (c) for F imaginary and with 𝒢_n-valued extensions: CHT08 Lemma 2.1.1, recorded in G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group.
Totally real case: ⟨x, y⟩′ := ⟨x, ρ(c_v)y⟩_v is G_F-equivariant up to μ and has symmetry εμ(c_v), giving the GSp/GO factorisation (BLGGT §2.1 bullet three).

nodes.title: Sign, change of place, determinant and parity constraints of a polarization
nodes.statement: Let (ρ, μ) be polarized at a real place v of F⁺ with pairing ⟨ , ⟩_v and sign ε_v (G7/polarized-representation), ρ of rank n over A. (1) Change of place: for another real place v′, ⟨x, y⟩_{v′} := ⟨x, ρ(c_v c_{v′})y⟩_v polarizes (ρ, μ) at v′ with ε_{v′} = μ(c_v c_{v′})ε_v; for F imaginary the condition ε_{v′} = −μ(c_{v′}) then holds at every v′. (2) Determinant: det ρ(c_v σ c_v)·det ρ(σ) = μ(σ)^n for σ ∈ G_F; for F totally real (det ρ)^2 = μ^n, and if moreover ρ is symplectic (μ(c_v) = −ε_v) then n is even and det ρ = μ^{n/2}. (3) Parity: if ⟨ , ⟩′ := ⟨ , ρ(c_v)·⟩ (F totally real) or the pairing itself (CHT, γ_0^2 = 1) is alternating and perfect on a free module over a nonzero ring, n is even. (4) Uniqueness and the intrinsic sign: if A = k is a field and ρ is absolutely irreducible with ρ^{c} ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ|_{G_F}, then a pairing satisfying the covariance identity exists, is unique up to k^×, and its symmetry sign is determined by (ρ, μ): ρ(γ^2)ᵗb_γ = ±μ(γ)b_γ with the sign −sgn(ρ, μ) independent of γ ∈ G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F; (ρ, μ) is polarized iff sgn(ρ, μ) = 1, and otherwise (ρ, μδ_{F/F⁺}) is (BLGGT §1.1, CHT Lemma 2.1.4). The 𝒢_n-valued extensions of ρ up to GL_n(k)-conjugacy are a torsor under k^×/(k^×)^2. (5) Similitude ambiguity (GSp_4, BCGP21 Lemma 8.3.1): if ρ : G_K → GL_4(Q̄_p) is irreducible and preserves symplectic forms with similitude characters ν and νψ, ψ ≠ 1, then ψ has finite order and ρ is reducible over a quadratic subfield of the field cut out by ψ.
hypotheses: (4) requires absolute irreducibility; for reducible ρ the pairing need not be unique and the sign need not be defined
in (2) the symplectic conclusion det ρ = μ^{n/2} is the Pfaffian identity and holds over any ring; (det ρ)^2 = μ^n alone does not determine det ρ
(5) is stated over Q̄_p for a number field K as in the source
proofSteps: (1): direct computation using c_{v′} c_v ∈ G_F and the covariance identity; BLGGT §2.1 first bullet.

(2): take determinants in the matrix form ᵗρ(σ) P ρ(cσc) = μ(σ) P of the covariance identity (P the Gram matrix); in the totally real case use G7/similitude-groups (det g = ν^m on GSp_{2m}, (det g)^2 = ν^n on GO_n).
(3): an alternating matrix of odd size has determinant 0 over any commutative ring.
(4): BLGGT §1.1 (Schur's lemma applied to ρ(γ^2δγ^{−2}) computed two ways) and CHT08 Lemma 2.1.4 (existence of the 𝒢_n-valued extension, and the k^×/(k^×)^2 classification by α ↦ r_α).
(5): BCGP21 Lemma 8.3.1: ν ⊕ νψ ⊂ Hom(V^*, V) gives V ≅ V(ψ), so ψ^4 = 1 by determinants, and a quadratic η with V ≅ V(η) makes V reducible over the fixed field of η by Schur.
acceptance: n = 1, F imaginary: (ψ, μ) polarized forces μ(c_v) = −1 at every v, consistent with (1) since μ(c_v c_{v′}) = 1.
F totally real, n = 2, symplectic: det ρ = μ (GSp_2 = GL_2).
BLGGT §1.1 rank-one example: for χ with χχ^{γ_0} = μ|_Δ and χ(γ_0^2) = −μ(γ_0), (χ, μ) is a 𝒢_1-valued homomorphism with ν = μ.

nodes.title: Operations on polarized representations: dual, twist, tensor, powers, restriction, coefficients
nodes.statement: Let F be CM with F⁺ ≠ F (imaginary case) and δ := δ_{F/F⁺} : G_{F⁺} → {±1} the quadratic character, so δ(c_v) = −1. For polarized (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩, ε) and (ρ′, μ′, ⟨ , ⟩′, ε′) of G_F over A at the same c_v (G7/polarized-representation) define: (1) dual: (ρ^∨, μ^{−1}) with the transported pairing ⟨φ^{−1}f, φ^{−1}g⟩ (φ : M → M^∨ the pairing map), sign ε; (2) twist by a continuous character χ : G_F → A^×: (ρ ⊗ χ, μ·(χ ∘ Ver)) with the same pairing, where Ver : G_{F⁺}^{ab} → G_F^{ab} is the transfer, so (χ ∘ Ver)|_{G_F} = χχ^c and (χ ∘ Ver)(c_v) = 1; sign ε; (3) tensor product: (ρ ⊗ ρ′, μμ′δ) with pairing ⟨x ⊗ x′, y ⊗ y′⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩⟨x′, y′⟩′, sign εε′; (4) exterior powers, k ≥ 1: (∧^k ρ, μ^k δ^{k−1}) with the determinant pairing ⟨x_1∧…∧x_k, y_1∧…∧y_k⟩ = det(⟨x_i, y_j⟩), sign ε^k, for every A; (5) symmetric powers, k ≥ 1, when k! ∈ A^×: (Sym^k ρ, μ^k δ^{k−1}) with the permanent pairing (1/k!)Σ_{s∈S_k}∏_i⟨x_i, y_{s(i)}⟩, sign ε^k; (6) direct sum of two polarizations with the same μ and ε at the same c_v: orthogonal sum; (7) restriction to a CM field L ⊃ F with L = L⁺F (L⁺ ⊃ F⁺ the maximal totally real subfield of L): (ρ|_{G_L}, μ|_{G_{L⁺}}) with the same pairing at a real place of L⁺ above v; (8) coefficient extension along continuous A → B: (ρ ⊗_A B, μ ⊗ B, ⟨ , ⟩ ⊗ B). In each case the output satisfies the CM sign condition. For F totally real the same formulas hold with δ replaced by 1 and the GSp/GO type changing by ε. The quadratic correction δ is invisible on G_F and is required at c_v.
hypotheses: F imaginary CM, both inputs polarized at the same c_v (use G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (1) to move places)
(5) needs k! ∈ A^×: for k ≥ char A the permanent pairing is degenerate (G7/symmetric-power-polarization)
(6): with different multipliers or signs the block pairing is not a polarization of one pair
(7): for a CM extension L/F the real places of L⁺ above v give complex conjugations conjugate in G_{L⁺} to c_v
proofSteps: Each output pairing is perfect: (1) by transport; (3) tensor product of perfect pairings on finite projective modules; (4) ∧^k of a perfect pairing is perfect (∧^k M^∨ ≅ (∧^k M)^∨ for finite projective M); (5) perfect when k! ∈ A^× (symmetrisation is then a split projection).
Covariance: multiplicative in the factors; on G_F, δ is trivial, so the covariance multiplier is μμ′ (resp. μ^k).
Sign: transposition multiplies by εε′ (resp. ε^k by expanding det or perm of the transposed matrix).

CM sign condition: −(μμ′δ)(c_v) = −(−ε)(−ε′)(−1) = εε′; −(μ^kδ^{k−1})(c_v) = −(−ε)^k(−1)^{k−1} = ε^k; for twists, (χ ∘ Ver)(c_v) = 1 since the transfer of an involution outside G_F is trivial (computed on the transversal {1, c_v}).

Restriction and coefficient extension: immediate from the definitions; BLGGT §1.1 records the corresponding statements for 𝒢_n-valued maps (multiplier of r ⊗ r′ differs from μμ′ by the nontrivial character of Γ/Δ).
acceptance: Two totally odd inputs give a totally odd tensor product: ε = ε′ = 1 ⇒ εε′ = 1 (R24.5 consumer statement).

For ρ = ψ a polarized character (ε = 1, μ(c_v) = −1), ψ ⊗ ψ has multiplier μ^2δ with (μ^2δ)(c_v) = −1, again totally odd; without δ the multiplier μ^2 would have value +1 at c_v and violate the CM sign condition.
k = 0 convention: the unit representation A with pairing (a, b) ↦ ab and multiplier δ is polarized with sign +1, which is the value of μ^kδ^{k−1} at k = 0 because δ^{−1} = δ.

nodes.title: Oddness at real places: polarized sign, similitude value and eigenspace balance
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and v a real place; c_v ∈ G_F denotes a complex conjugation at v (the image of complex conjugation under G_ℝ → G_F for an embedding F̄ → ℂ extending v; its conjugacy class [c_v] depends only on v). (a) Polarized oddness (BLGGT §2.1): a polarized (ρ, μ) of G_F, F CM or totally real, is totally odd if ε_v = 1 for every real place v of F⁺; when F is imaginary this is equivalent to μ(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞. (b) Group-valued oddness: a continuous r : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(A) with r^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(A)) = G_F (F imaginary) is totally odd if ν(r(c_v)) = −1 for all v; r : G_F → GSp_{2m}(A) (F totally real) is odd if ν(r(c_v)) = −1 for all v; r : G_F → GO_n(A) is odd if ν(r(c_v)) = +1 for all v. (c) Rank one (ACC+ §1.2): a continuous character μ : G_K → A^× of a totally real K is totally odd if μ(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞. (d) Unpolarized balance (CG18 §8.4, corrected): for V of dimension n over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, V is odd at a real place v if the (±1)-eigenspaces of ρ(c_v) have dimensions differing by at most one (no condition at complex places). In characteristic 0 this is Tr ρ(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}; in characteristic ℓ the trace criterion is equivalent to it exactly when ℓ > n + 1 (n even) or ℓ > n (n odd). (e) Rank two: for n = 2 and characteristic ≠ 2, (d) at v ⇔ det ρ(c_v) = −1 ⇔ (ρ, det ρ) is odd as a GSp_2-valued representation, which is R01.4/odd-representation. Oddness in dimension n is the sign condition (a)/(b), not the rank-two determinant test.
hypotheses: a polarization (or a similitude-group valued representation) is required for (a), (b); (d) is a separate unpolarized notion, used by CG18 for GL_n
characteristic ≠ 2 in (d) so that c_v is diagonalisable with eigenvalues ±1
in characteristic 2 the rank-two condition 'ρ̄(c) ≠ 1' is a different condition and is R01.4's
proofSteps: (a)⇔(μ(c_v) = −1) for F imaginary: ε_v = −μ(c_v) by definition.

Consequences (CHT08 Lemma 2.1.3): for r : Γ → 𝒢_n(k), char k ≠ 2, c ∈ Γ ∖ Δ with c^2 = 1, dim_k gl_n^{c=η} = n(n + ην(r(c)))/2; for totally odd r the c-invariants of ad have dimension n(n − 1)/2. For GSp_4 with ν(c) = −1 and p > 2, r(c) is conjugate to diag(1, 1, −1, −1) with isotropic eigenspaces and dim H^0(⟨c⟩, sp_4) = 4 (CG20, Proposition 4.9 use).

(d): if c_v has eigenspaces of dimensions a, b, then dim H^0(⟨c_v⟩, ad⁰ V) = a^2 + b^2 − 1, minimal exactly when |a − b| ≤ 1, which gives CG18's formula Σ_{v|∞} dim H^0(F_v, ad⁰ V) = [F:Q] n(n−1)/2 + l_0; Tr ρ(c_v) = a − b computed in the field (sourceIssues E702).
(e): for n = 2 the eigenvalue multiset {1, −1} is the balanced case and has determinant −1; GSp_2 = GL_2 with ν = det.
acceptance: An odd ρ : G_Q → GL_2(E) restricted to an imaginary quadratic F is totally odd polarized with multiplier det ρ (pairing det(x, ρ(c)y)).
The cyclotomic character χ_ℓ of a totally real field is totally odd (χ_ℓ(c_v) = −1); the trivial character is not.
Non-example to the trace test (CG18 E164): over F_3 with n = 2 and ρ(c) = 1, Tr ρ(c) = 2 = −1 but the eigenspaces have dimensions 2 and 0, so V is not odd; similarly n = 4, F_5, ρ(c) = ±1.

nodes.title: The group scheme 𝒢_n and the dictionary with polarized triples
nodes.statement: 𝒢_n is the group scheme over Z given as the semidirect product of 𝒢_n^0 = GL_n × GL_1 by {1, j}, with j(g, μ)j^{−1} = (μ ᵗg^{−1}, μ); the multiplier ν : 𝒢_n → GL_1 sends (g, μ) ↦ μ and j ↦ −1; 𝒢_n^0 is the identity component. The adjoint action on gl_n = Lie GL_n ⊂ Lie 𝒢_n is ad(g, μ)(x) = gxg^{−1}, ad(j)(x) = −ᵗx. Dictionary (CHT08 Lemma 2.1.1): for a group Γ with an index-two subgroup Δ (open if Γ is topological), a ring R and γ_0 ∈ Γ ∖ Δ, homomorphisms r : Γ → 𝒢_n(R) inducing Γ/Δ ≅ 𝒢_n/𝒢_n^0 correspond bijectively to triples (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩) with ρ : Δ → GL_n(R), μ : Γ → R^×, ⟨ , ⟩ perfect on R^n, ⟨x, ρ(γ_0^2)y⟩ = −μ(γ_0)⟨y, x⟩ and μ(δ)⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨ρ(δ)x, ρ(γ_0δγ_0^{−1})y⟩; here μ = ν ∘ r, ⟨x, y⟩ = ᵗx A^{−1} y where r(γ_0) = (A, −μ(γ_0))j, and continuous r correspond to continuous ρ. Auxiliary maps: ⊗ : (𝒢_n × 𝒢_m)^+ → 𝒢_{nm}, (g, a) × (g′, a′) ↦ (g ⊗ g′, aa′), j × j ↦ j; I : 𝒢_n → GSp_{2n}; for a similitude group G_n with form matrix A_n (G7/similitude-groups) the injection G_n × {±1} → 𝒢_n, (g, 1) ↦ (g, ν(g)), (g, −1) ↦ (g, ν(g))·(A_n^{−1}, (−1)^{n+1})j, with ν(r((g, s))) = ν(g)s^n, and hence r_ψ : G_Q → 𝒢_n(R) for ψ : G_Q → G_n(R) and an imaginary quadratic F (BCG25 (2.1.2)); the rank-one maps (χ, μ) : Γ → 𝒢_1(R); and CHT's induction Ind^{Γ,Δ,χ}_{Γ′,Δ′}.
hypotheses: Γ/Δ ≅ 𝒢_n/𝒢_n^0 is part of the hypothesis on r (r(Δ) ⊂ 𝒢_n^0 and r(Γ ∖ Δ) ⊂ 𝒢_n^0 j)
the convention for GSp/GO is gA_nᵗg = ν(g)A_n; with ᵗgA_ng = νA_n the same group results
𝒢_n-invariants of gl_n vanish only over Z[1/2]
proofSteps: Group-scheme structure: the semidirect product of two affine group schemes by an automorphism of order 2 (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 0 functor of points; product and constant group {1, j}).

Lemma 2.1.1 (CHT08 p. 7): write r(γ_0) = (A, −μ(γ_0))j; the relation r(γ_0)r(δ)r(γ_0)^{−1} = r(γ_0δγ_0^{−1}) is the covariance identity for ⟨x, y⟩ = ᵗxA^{−1}y, and r(γ_0)^2 = r(γ_0^2) is the symmetry identity; conversely define r(γ_0) from the Gram matrix.

The map (2.1.2) of BCG25 agrees with r̂_Δ of BLGGT §1.1 and CHT Lemma 2.1.2 (r(γ) = (ρ(γ)J^{−1}, (−1)^a μ(γ))j, ν ∘ r = δ_{Γ/Δ}^{a+1}μ); the homomorphism property and ν(r((g, s))) = ν(g)s^n were checked numerically for random similitudes over Q with n = 2, 3, 4, 5 (this job).
⊗ and I are homomorphisms by direct computation (BLGGT §1.1); (χ, μ) is a homomorphism by BLGGT's displayed verification.
Polarized dictionary over CM fields: Γ = G_{F⁺}, Δ = G_F, γ_0 = c_v gives G7/polarized-representation (b) with ε_v = −μ(c_v).
acceptance: n = 1: 𝒢_1-valued r correspond to characters ψ of Δ with ψ^{γ_0} = ψ^{−1}μ|_Δ and ψ(γ_0^2) = −μ(γ_0); with γ_0^2 = 1 this forces μ(γ_0) = −1.
CHT08 Lemma 2.1.3 with c ∈ Γ ∖ Δ, c^2 = 1 and char k ≠ 2: dim gl_n^{c=η} = n(n + ην(r(c)))/2.

nodes.title: Polarization of symmetric powers of a rank-two symplectic representation
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, d ≥ 1 with d! ∈ F^× and 2 ∈ F^×, n = d + 1, V = F^2 with an alternating perfect form h, and r : Γ → GL(V) with h(r(g)x, r(g)y) = μ(g)h(x, y), μ = det r. The normalized symmetrization B_d(u_1⋯u_d, w_1⋯w_d) = (1/d!)Σ_{s∈S_d}∏_j h(u_j, w_{s(j)}) is a well-defined perfect bilinear form on Sym^d V with B_d(Sym^d r(g)u, Sym^d r(g)w) = μ(g)^d B_d(u, w) and B_d(w, u) = (−1)^d B_d(u, w). In a basis x, y with h(x, y) = 1 and v_i = x^{d−i}y^i, B_d(v_i, v_j) = 0 unless i + j = d and B_d(v_i, v_{d−i}) = (−1)^i / binom(d, i). Hence Sym^d r takes values in GSp(Sym^d V, B_d) for d odd (n even) and GO(Sym^d V, B_d) for d even (n odd), with multiplier μ^d. Identification with G_n (G7/similitude-groups): for n even there is P with ᵗP B_d P = J_n; for n odd and F finite of odd characteristic there are P and c ∈ F^× with ᵗP B_d P = c·1_n (scale to match the discriminant square class, then use the classification of nondegenerate quadratic forms over finite fields); over a general field the odd case is an extra hypothesis. When d! ∉ F^× (char F = p ≤ d) the conclusion fails: for p = 7 and d = 7 the space of SL_2(F_7)-invariant bilinear forms on Sym^7 F_7^2 is one-dimensional and spanned by a form of rank 6.
hypotheses: 2 and d! invertible in F (in characteristic p: n ≤ p)
r preserves an alternating perfect form with multiplier det r (automatic for GL_2)
the symmetric identification with 1_n is asserted only over finite fields of odd characteristic (or algebraically closed fields)
proofSteps: Symmetrization is invariant under permuting each argument separately, so B_d descends from V^{⊗d} × V^{⊗d} to Sym^d V × Sym^d V (on the existing Sym^d of G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers); equivariance multiplies each of the d factors h by μ(g).

Monomial computation: B_d(v_i, v_j) counts matchings of i copies of y and d − i copies of x on the left with the right factors; only i + j = d contributes, with value (−1)^i i!(d−i)!/d!. All binomial coefficients are units when d! is, so the antidiagonal Gram matrix is invertible; transposition multiplies by (−1)^d.

Identification: alternating perfect forms have symplectic bases; symmetric forms over finite fields of odd characteristic are classified by rank and discriminant, and scaling by c changes the discriminant by c^n, n odd.

Failure for d ≥ p: computed by this job for p = 7, d = 5, 6, 7, 8 and p = 5, d = 3, 4, 5 by solving gᵗBg = B for the two elementary generators of SL_2(F_p): the invariant forms form a line in each case, of rank 6, 7, 6, 5 (p = 7) and 4, 5, 4 (p = 5); the d!-scaled antidiagonal form (−1)^i i!(d−i)! spans it.
acceptance: d = p − 2 = 5, p = 7 (n = 6): B_5 is alternating of rank 6 and invariant under SL_2(F_7): Sym^5 r lands in GSp_6(F_7) with multiplier μ^5.

d = p − 1 = 6, p = 7 (n = 7): B_6 is symmetric of rank 7; its d!-scaled Gram matrix has all antidiagonal entries −1 (Wilson's theorem), so Sym^6 r lands in GO_7(F_7) with multiplier μ^6 (BCG25 Theorem 3.1 uses n = p with multiplier ε̄^{(1−k)(p−1)} = 1).
d = p = 7: no nondegenerate invariant form exists (rank 6 < 8), so no GSp_8 conclusion; BCG25's multiplier bookkeeping ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄^∨ε̄^{1−n} for n = p − 1, p − 2.
Over F = ℝ with d = 2, B_2 has signature (2, 1), so it is not a scalar multiple of 1_3 up to isometry: keep GO(B_2) unless an identification is supplied.

nodes.title: GSp_4-valued representations: oddness, adjoint modules, and symplectic induction from index two
nodes.statement: Let A be a topological commutative ring with 2 ∈ A^× and F a number field (in the sources totally real or Q). (i) A GSp_4-valued representation is a continuous r : G_F → GSp_4(A) (G7/similitude-groups; BCGP21 or CG20 normalisation of J, compared by an explicit permutation matrix), with similitude character ν ∘ r; it is odd if ν(r(c_v)) = −1 at every real v. For A a field and r odd, r(c_v) is conjugate to diag(1, 1, −1, −1) with Lagrangian eigenspaces and dim H^0(⟨c_v⟩, ad⁰ r) = 4. (ii) Adjoint modules: ad r := gsp_4 with Ad ∘ r (rank 11); ad⁰ r := sp_4 (rank 10) = Lie(Sp_4) = Lie(PGSp_4) = asp⁰ r for 2 ∈ A^×; ad r = ad⁰ r ⊕ A with trivial action on the scalar line A·1_4 (not ⊕ ν); ad⁰ r ≅ Sym^2(r) ⊗ (ν ∘ r)^{−1} and ad⁰ r is self-dual via the trace form. (iii) Symplectic induction (BCGP21 §2.2): let K/F be quadratic with nontrivial character η_{K/F}, σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_K, ρ : G_K → GL(V), V free of rank 2 over a field L, with det ρ = χ|_{G_K} for a character χ of G_F. On W = V ⊕ σV (a model of Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ, R01.1/continuous-induction) choose a nondegenerate alternating form on V, make V ⊥ σV, and set ⟨σv_1, σv_2⟩ = ±χ(σ)⟨v_1, v_2⟩; the two signs give ρ_1, ρ_2 : G_F → GSp(W) with similitude characters χ and χη_{K/F}, and ∧^2 Ind ρ contains χ and χη_{K/F}. In BCGP21's J, the image of {(A, B) ∈ GL_2 × GL_2 : det A = det B} is the set of g ∈ GSp_4 with zero pattern rows (∗,0,0,∗), (0,∗,∗,0), (0,∗,∗,0), (∗,0,0,∗). For ρ with det ρ = ε^{−1}, Ind ρ denotes the symplectic induction with similitude ε^{−1}; for an elliptic curve E/K it is the dual Tate module of Res_{K/F} E with its Weil-pairing polarization. (iv) ad⁰ of an induction (characteristic ≠ 2, ν = χ): ad⁰(Ind ρ)|_{G_K} ≅ (ρ ⊗ ρ^σ) ⊗ χ^{−1} ⊕ ad⁰ ρ ⊕ ad⁰ ρ^σ and ad⁰(Ind ρ) ≅ As(ρ) ⊗ χ^{−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰ ρ up to replacing As(ρ) by As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} (G7/tensor-induction).
hypotheses: 2 ∈ A^× (for ad = ad⁰ ⊕ A and for sp_4 = Lie PGSp_4)
in (iii) det ρ must extend to G_F; the two polarizations differ by η_{K/F}
the Weil-pairing statement is a comparison with R01.6/AbelianSchemes (A3, A6) and is recorded as a use, not proved here
proofSteps: (i): ⟨cv, cw⟩ = ν(c)⟨v, w⟩ = −⟨v, w⟩ makes both eigenspaces isotropic, hence Lagrangian; the centraliser of diag(1,1,−1,−1) in sp_4 is the Siegel Levi gl_2 (CG20 proof of Proposition 4.9).

(ii): G7/similitude-groups (gsp = sp ⊕ scalars for 2 invertible, scalars trivial under Ad); the printed '⊕ ν' (CG20 p. 813) is corrected (sourceIssues E701). Sym^2 W ⊗ ν^{−1} ≅ sp(W) via x·y ↦ (z ↦ ⟨x, z⟩y + ⟨y, z⟩x)/ν, Γ-equivariant up to the multiplier.

(iii): BCGP21 §2.2; consistency of the definition of the form on σV uses σ^2 ∈ G_K and det ρ(σ^2) = χ(σ)^2; equivariance under G_K and σ is a direct check; the block description by writing W = V ⊕ σV in the basis adapted to J.
(iv): compute over G_K using ρ^∨ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ^{−1} (rank two) and descend with G7/tensor-induction (As) and Mackey (R01.1/mackey-decomposition) (CG20 Example 4.11; BCGP21 §7.5.16).
acceptance: BCGP21: for K/F a quadratic extension of number fields and E/K an elliptic curve, Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} of the dual p-adic Tate module of E is GSp_4-valued with similitude ε^{−1}, and is the dual Tate module of Res_{K/F}E.

CG20 Example 4.11: for K/Q imaginary quadratic and ρ̄ : G_K → GL_2(F_p) with det ρ̄ = ε^{1−k}, r̄ = Ind ρ̄ is odd GSp_4-valued and ad⁰(r̄) ≅ As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰(ρ̄) up to the quadratic twist of As.
dim gsp_4 = 11, dim sp_4 = 10, and over F_p, p > 2, the scalar line in gsp_4 is a trivial summand.

nodes.title: Semisimple GSp_4-valued representations are determined by GL_4 × GL_1 (characteristic ≠ 2)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a group and L an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ 2. Two semisimple representations r, r′ : Γ → GSp_4(L) are GSp_4(L)-conjugate if and only if their composites Γ → GSp_4(L) → GL_4(L) × GL_1(L) (underlying representation and similitude character) are GL_4(L) × GL_1(L)-conjugate, i.e. the underlying GL_4-representations are isomorphic and ν ∘ r = ν ∘ r′. In characteristic 2 the statement is false.
hypotheses: L algebraically closed, char L ≠ 2 (BCGP21 states no characteristic hypothesis; sourceIssues E703)
semisimple means semisimple as a GL_4-representation; for char ≠ 2 this is equivalent to GSp_4-complete reducibility
proofSteps: Let V = L^4 with two Γ-invariant-up-to-ν alternating perfect forms B, B′ (the second transported by an isomorphism of GL_4-representations). Decompose V = ⊕_W W ⊗ Hom_Γ(W, V) into isotypic parts; a form with multiplier ν pairs the W-isotypic part with the (W^∨ ⊗ ν)-isotypic part.

For W ≇ W^∨ ⊗ ν the form is determined, up to the action of GL of the multiplicity spaces, by an isomorphism of multiplicity spaces; for W ≅ W^∨ ⊗ ν, with W carrying a unique (Schur) invariant form of sign s_W, the form on the isotypic part is s_W ⊗ (form of sign −s_W on the multiplicity space); over an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ 2 nondegenerate symmetric and alternating forms of a given rank are unique up to isometry.
Hence (V, B) ≅ (V, B′) Γ-equivariantly, i.e. r′ = g r g^{−1} with g ∈ GSp_4(L) (indeed Sp-similar); Gan–Takeda Lemma 6.1 (cited by BCGP21, not read here) gives the same argument.

Characteristic 2 counterexample (BCGP21 E6 review): Γ = SL_2(F_2), V = W ⊗ L^2 with forms B_W ⊗ (0 1; 1 0) and B_W ⊗ I: GL_4-conjugate with equal similitude, not GSp_4-conjugate, because B_W ⊗ I is alternating but the two forms are not isometric under the Γ-commutant.
acceptance: Two GSp_4-valued representations Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ with similitude χ and with χη_{K/F} (G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction) have isomorphic GL_4-representations but different similitude characters, so the lemma does not identify them, as it must not.
For r = ρ_1 ⊕ ρ_2 with ρ_i : Γ → GL_2(L) and det ρ_1 = det ρ_2 = ν (orthogonal sum), any GSp_4-valued r′ with the same GL_4-representation and similitude ν is GSp_4-conjugate to r.

nodes.title: Strongly irreducible representations
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group and (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ K V with K a field (a finite extension of Q_ℓ, Q̄_ℓ, or a finite field). ρ is strongly irreducible if ρ|_{Γ′} is irreducible for every open subgroup Γ′ ≤ Γ. For Γ = G_F, F a field, this says ρ|_{G_L} is irreducible for every finite separable extension L/F inside F^sep; for Γ = G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})} the quantifier runs over finite extensions of F(ζ_{p^∞}). Absolutely strongly irreducible: ρ ⊗_K K̄ strongly irreducible. For K of characteristic 0 and ρ semisimple, ρ ⊗ K̄ is strongly irreducible iff the identity component G_ρ^0 of the Zariski closure of ρ(Γ) acts irreducibly on V ⊗ K̄ (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups).
hypotheses: the quantifier is over all open subgroups (all finite extensions), not only over the given group
irreducible, not absolutely irreducible, unless stated; the absolute variant is a separate predicate
proofSteps: Definition. Characterisation via G^0 (characteristic 0): Γ^0 := ρ^{−1}(G_ρ^0(K̄)) is open of finite index; for open Γ′ the Zariski closure of ρ(Γ′ ∩ Γ^0) is G_ρ^0 (finite-index subgroups of a connected group's dense subgroup are dense: [Bor91, Ch. I §1.2]), and a subspace is ρ(Γ′ ∩ Γ^0)-stable iff it is G_ρ^0-stable; conversely every open Γ′ contains an open subgroup of Γ^0.
acceptance: Non-example: for K/F quadratic and ψ a character of G_K with ψ ≠ ψ^σ, Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ψ is irreducible but not strongly irreducible (its restriction to G_K is ψ ⊕ ψ^σ).

The Tate module V_p E of an elliptic curve with CM by an imaginary quadratic K ⊄ F is irreducible over G_F but reducible over G_{FK}: not strongly irreducible; for E/Q without CM, V_p E is strongly irreducible (Serre's open image theorem gives G_ρ^0 = GL_2).
NT26: for F totally real and π a non-CM RAESDC representation of GL_2(𝔸_F), r_{π,ι} is strongly irreducible ([NT23, Example 2.29], imported by NT26; owned downstream, see notes).

nodes.title: Zariski closures of subgroups and the monodromy group of a representation
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, G an affine group scheme of finite type over K and Σ ⊂ G(K) a subgroup. The Zariski closure Σ̄ ⊂ G is the closed subgroup scheme defined by the Hopf ideal I(Σ) = {f ∈ O(G) : f(σ) = 0 for all σ ∈ Σ} (Tau Ceti's Hopf-ideal/closed-subgroup classification); it is reduced, Σ ⊂ Σ̄(K), and it is the smallest closed subgroup scheme whose K-points contain Σ. For a field K with an algebraically closed extension Ω, closures are formed over Ω and Σ̄_Ω = (Σ̄)_Ω. For (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ K V the monodromy group G_ρ is the Zariski closure of ρ(Γ) in GL(V), with identity component G_ρ^0 (formed after base change to an algebraic closure, TauCeti identityComponent), component group π_0(G_ρ) and Γ^0 := ρ^{−1}(G_ρ^0(K̄)), an open normal subgroup of finite index; for Γ = G_F the field F_ρ^0 := (F^sep)^{Γ^0} is finite Galois over F with Gal(F_ρ^0/F) ≅ ρ(Γ)/(ρ(Γ) ∩ G_ρ^0(K̄)) ≅ π_0(G_ρ)(K̄) (ρ(Γ) is Zariski dense, so it meets every connected component). Facts ([Bor91, Ch. I §§1–2]): (a) for a homomorphism α : H → H′ of affine algebraic groups over an algebraically closed field Ω and a subgroup Σ ⊂ H(Ω), the closure of α(Σ) is α(Σ̄); (b) the closure of the commutator subgroup [Σ, Σ] is the derived group D(Σ̄) ([Bor91, Ch. I §2.4]); (c) in characteristic 0, if ρ is semisimple then G_ρ^0 is reductive (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 6: faithful semisimple representation); (d) in characteristic 0 a connected reductive subgroup of GL_2 acting irreducibly is SL_2 or GL_2, and its image in PGL_2 is PGL_2; (e) a subgroup of PGL_2(Ω) × PGL_2(Ω) surjecting on both factors whose closure is reductive is either dense in PGL_2 × PGL_2 or the graph of an automorphism (Goursat plus simplicity of PGL_2(Ω)), every automorphism of PGL_2 is inner, and a homomorphism of algebraic groups in characteristic 0 bijective on Ω-points is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: closures are defined for subgroups of K-points; for Γ profinite and ρ continuous the closure ignores the topology of Γ
the identity component is geometric (after base change to an algebraically closed field), as in Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 3
(c)–(e) are characteristic-0 statements; (a) holds over any algebraically closed field
proofSteps: I(Σ) is a Hopf ideal: if f vanishes on Σ then Δf vanishes on Σ × Σ, and the map O(G)/I ⊗ O(G)/I → Fun(Σ × Σ, K) is injective (tensor product of injections into function spaces), so Δf ∈ I ⊗ O + O ⊗ I; S(f) and ε(f) similarly. Then Tau Ceti hopfIdealOrderIsoClosedSubgroup gives the closed subgroup scheme.
Base change: I(Σ) ⊗ Ω = I_Ω(Σ) by linear algebra (functions on Σ with values in K vs Ω).

Γ^0 open of finite index: G_ρ^0 has finite index in G_ρ (π_0 finite, Tau Ceti component group results) and ρ(Γ) ∩ G_ρ^0(K̄) is a finite-index subgroup closed in ρ(Γ), hence open since ρ(Γ) is compact.
(a), (b): [Bor91, Ch. I §2.1(f) and §2.4] (cited by NT26; Borel not fetched, the statements are standard and are planned here with these proofs).
(c): a faithful semisimple representation in characteristic 0 forces trivial unipotent radical (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 6, linearly reductive characterisation).
(d), (e): NT26 proof of Lemma 2.2 (Goursat via mathlib Subgroup.goursat on Ω-points; PGL_2(Ω) simple as an abstract group).
acceptance: For ρ = 1 ⊕ χ_ℓ (χ_ℓ the cyclotomic character of G_Q, ℓ-adic), G_ρ = {diag(1, t)} ≅ G_m and G_ρ^0 = G_ρ; for ρ of finite image, G_ρ is the finite constant group ρ(Γ) and G_ρ^0 = 1, F_ρ^0 the field cut out by ρ.
NT26 Lemma 2.2: for ρ strongly irreducible G_F → GL_2(Q̄_p), the closure of Proj ρ(G_F) is PGL_2.
Non-example: over K = F_q, the closure of GL_2(F_q) ⊂ GL_2 is the finite constant group scheme, not GL_2; the dense-subgroup statements (d), (e) are for infinite images in characteristic 0.

nodes.title: Tensor products of symmetric powers with unequal Hodge–Tate differences are strongly irreducible after cyclotomic restriction
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a prime, and ρ, ρ′ : G_F → GL_2(Q̄_p) continuous and strongly irreducible. Suppose there is an embedding τ : F → Q̄_p inducing a place v | p such that ρ|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ′|_{G_{F_v}} are Hodge–Tate with HT_τ(ρ) = {a, b}, HT_τ(ρ′) = {a′, b′} and a − b ≠ ±(a′ − b′). Then (i) the Zariski closure of the image of Proj ρ × Proj ρ′ : G_F → PGL_2(Q̄_p) × PGL_2(Q̄_p) is PGL_2 × PGL_2; (ii) for all m, m′ ≥ 1, (Sym^m ρ ⊗ Sym^{m′} ρ′)|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}} is strongly irreducible.
hypotheses: both representations strongly irreducible (not merely irreducible)
the weight condition a − b ≠ ±(a′ − b′) at one embedding τ; equal differences allow ρ′ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ, where (i) fails
proofSteps: Closure of Proj ρ(G_F) is PGL_2: G_ρ is reductive (faithful irreducible representation), G_ρ^0 acts irreducibly (strong irreducibility, G7/strong-irreducibility), so G_ρ^0 ∈ {SL_2, GL_2} (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups (c), (d)); image in PGL_2 is PGL_2 by fact (a).

Let G be the closure of the image of Proj ρ × Proj ρ′; it is reductive and surjects onto each factor. By Goursat on G(Q̄_p) and simplicity of PGL_2(Q̄_p), either G = PGL_2 × PGL_2 or G(Q̄_p) is the graph of an automorphism; in the latter case the first projection is bijective on points, hence an isomorphism (characteristic 0), every automorphism of PGL_2 is inner, so ad⁰ ρ ≅ ad⁰ ρ′ and their Hodge–Tate weights {a − b, 0, b − a} and {a′ − b′, 0, b′ − a′} at τ agree (Hodge–Tate weights of ad⁰ from PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, tensor/dual compatibility), contradicting the hypothesis (NT26 proof of Lemma 2.2).

Cyclotomic restriction: Gal(F(ζ_{p^∞})/F) is abelian, so the image of G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})} under ρ × ρ′ contains the commutator subgroup of (ρ × ρ′)(G_F); its closure contains the derived group of the closure of (ρ × ρ′)(G_F) (fact (b); NT26's printed product of images is the image of ρ × ρ′, sourceIssues E704), which contains SL_2 × SL_2 because the latter closure surjects onto PGL_2 × PGL_2.

The same holds for every open subgroup of G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})} (finite-index subgroups have the same identity component), and Sym^m ⊗ Sym^{m′} is irreducible for SL_2 × SL_2 in characteristic 0; G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers supplies the representations.
acceptance: NT26 application: ρ = r_{π,ι}, ρ′ = r_{σ,ι} attached to non-CM Hilbert eigenforms of different weights (parallel weight 2 and parallel weight 3 differ: a − b = 1 vs 2), so Sym^m r_π ⊗ Sym^{m′} r_σ is strongly irreducible over F(ζ_{p^∞}).
Failure without the weight hypothesis: ρ′ = ρ ⊗ χ for a character χ has equal weight differences, and Sym^1 ρ ⊗ Sym^1 ρ′ ≅ (Sym^2 ρ ⊕ det ρ) ⊗ χ is reducible.

nodes.title: Lifting projective Galois representations, with Hodge–Tate control in rank two
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and ℓ a prime. (1) (Tate, Conrad) Every continuous ρ̄ : G_F → PGL_n(Q̄_ℓ) lifts to a continuous ρ : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ); more generally for a surjection H′ → H of linear algebraic groups over Q̄_ℓ with kernel a central torus, every continuous G_F → H(Q̄_ℓ) lifts to H′(Q̄_ℓ). Any two lifts to GL_n differ by a continuous character G_F → Q̄_ℓ^×. Every lift is unramified at all but finitely many places if ρ̄ is. (2) (Patrikis, Lemma 2.7.4) If n = 2 and ρ̄ is geometric (unramified almost everywhere and de Rham at places above ℓ, as a projective representation, i.e. ad⁰ of a lift is geometric), there is a lift ρ whose Hodge–Tate–Sen weights at all v | ℓ lie in (1/2)Z, and then Sym^2 ρ and det ρ are geometric. (3) (BCGP21, proof of Proposition 9.2.1) Let F′/F be a quadratic extension of totally real fields and s : G_{F′} → GL_2(Q̄_ℓ) Hodge–Tate of weights (0, 1) at every place above ℓ, such that Proj s extends to a continuous G_F → PGL_2(Q̄_ℓ). Then the extension lifts to r̃ : G_F → GL_2(Q̄_ℓ), unramified almost everywhere and Hodge–Tate of weights (0, 1) at every v | ℓ, with r̃|_{G_{F′}} = s ⊗ ψ for a character ψ of finite order.
hypotheses: F a number field (Tate's theorem H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0 is global); for local fields lifting can be obstructed
coefficients Q̄_ℓ with its ℓ-adic topology; enlarging the coefficient field is essential (Patrikis Remark 2.1.5)
(3) uses that F is totally real (Patrikis Lemma 2.3.17: characters with rational HTS weights have all weights equal)
proofSteps: (1): Patrikis Proposition 2.1.4 (Conrad [Con11, Prop. 5.3]): reduce to kernel G_m, choose an isogeny complement H′_1 with H′_1 ∩ G_m = μ_{n_0}; the obstruction classes c_n ∈ H^2(G_F, Z/n) are compatible and lim_n H^2(G_F, Z/n) = H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0 (Tate; requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4), so the class dies for n large; continuity of the lift and finiteness of the coefficient field via R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field. Almost-everywhere unramifiedness: [Con11, Lemma 5.3] as cited by Patrikis.
Two lifts differ by ρ_2 = ρ_1 ⊗ χ with χ(g) a scalar: χ is a continuous character since ρ_1(g)^{−1}ρ_2(g) is a scalar matrix depending continuously on g.

(2): Patrikis Lemma 2.7.4: twist a lift by a square root ψ of det up to finite order (Lemma 2.3.15) so that ρ ⊗ ρ ≅ (ad⁰ ρ ⊗ χ) ⊕ χ is Hodge–Tate, then Sym^2 ρ and det ρ are de Rham by Wintenberger–Conrad; Hodge–Tate–Sen weights are PadicHodgeTheory's (requested, R06.2).

(3): apply (2) and Patrikis Lemma 2.3.17 to normalise the weights to (0, 1); r̃|_{G_{F′}} and s have the same projectivisation, so differ by a character ψ, which is Hodge–Tate of weight 0 hence of finite order (BCGP21 p. 254).
acceptance: n = 2, projective image dihedral: ρ̄ = Proj Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} θ lifts to Ind θ, and every other lift is Ind θ ⊗ χ.
BCGP21 Proposition 9.2.1, type E[D_n]: s = s_l from a weakly compatible system with s^σ ≅ s ⊗ δ; Proj s extends to G_F by Schur's lemma and lifts as in (3).

Finite-group non-example: the projective representation (Z/2)^2 → PGL_2(Q̄_ℓ) sending the generators to the classes of diag(1, −1) and (0 1; 1 0) does not lift to a homomorphism (Z/2)^2 → GL_2(Q̄_ℓ) (any lifts anticommute); for a Galois group G_F of a number field surjecting onto (Z/2)^2 the inflated projective representation does lift, by (1), with larger image.

nodes.title: From determinants to representations, only through IHG.1, and compatibility with the operations
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite and D an n-dimensional continuous determinant on A[Γ] (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/continuous-determinant). G7 produces a representation from D only in the two situations supplied by IHG.1, with its hypotheses: (a) A = k an algebraically closed field (with its topology): there is a continuous semisimple ρ : Γ → GL_n(k), unique up to isomorphism, with det ∘ ρ = D (Chenevier Theorem 2.12 with continuity); (b) A complete local Noetherian with finite residue field and D̄ := D ⊗ k absolutely irreducible: there is a continuous ρ : Γ → GL_n(A), unique up to GL_n(A)-conjugacy, with det ∘ ρ = D (Chenevier Theorem 2.22). In both cases ρ is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A (R01.1) and the operations of G7 are compatible with determinants: for Φ ∈ {Sym^k, ∧^k, T^k, dual, twist by a character, ad, ad⁰ (n ∈ A^×), ⊗ with another such representation, restriction to open subgroups, coefficient extension} the determinant det ∘ Φ(ρ) depends only on D (and the other inputs' determinants), via the characteristic-polynomial identities of G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers. Polarizations transfer in case (b): if D^c = D^∨·μ|_{G_F} (equality of determinants on G_F) then ρ admits a polarization with multiplier μ or μδ_{F/F⁺}, unique up to A^× (CHT Lemma 2.1.4 for the residual representation, lifted by uniqueness of ρ). No representation is inferred from a determinant that is residually reducible: there D need not be det ∘ ρ for any ρ over A.
hypotheses: IHG.1 hypotheses are kept exactly: algebraically closed field for (a); complete local Noetherian A with residually absolutely irreducible D̄ for (b)
the polarization statement in (b) needs D̄ absolutely irreducible so the pairing is unique up to scalars
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness: IHG.1 (requested; Chenevier Theorems 2.12 and 2.22).

Compatibility: for ρ with det ∘ ρ = D, the characteristic polynomial of Φ(ρ)(g) is a universal polynomial in that of ρ(g) (G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers, G7/adjoint-representations, G7/tensor-induction), and the characteristic polynomials of ρ(g) are the coefficients of D (IHG.0); by Amitsur's formula the determinant of Φ(ρ) is determined by these.

Polarization: D^c = D^∨μ gives ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ by uniqueness in (b); the pairing exists residually by G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (4) and lifts by the same uniqueness applied to the pairing map ρ ≅ (ρ^∨ ⊗ μ)^{c}, i.e. a Γ-isomorphism determined up to A^×.
acceptance: Residually reducible non-example: a non-split extension 0 → χ → ρ_1 → 1 → 0 and ρ_2 = 1 ⊕ χ have the same determinant D, so D does not determine a representation up to isomorphism when D̄ is reducible; G7 constructs nothing from such D.
For ρ = ρ_D in case (b), det(Sym^2 ρ) = (det ρ)^3 for n = 2, computed from D alone.

nodes.title: Adequate, weakly adequate and GHT-adequate subgroups of GL_n over a field of characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, k a field of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, V = k^n and H ⊆ GL_n(k) a finite subgroup. Let ad = M_n(k) = End_k(V) with H acting by conjugation h·X = hXh⁻¹ (the representation G7/adjoint-representations, i.e. Mathlib's linHom of the tautological representation with itself), ad⁰ ⊆ ad the H-submodule of trace-zero matrices, and ad₀ := ad/k·1 the quotient by the scalar line; ad⁰ → ad → ad₀ is an isomorphism exactly when p ∤ n, and the three modules are kept distinct. An element g ∈ H is semisimple if it is diagonalisable over an algebraic closure k̄; as H is finite this holds exactly when the order of g is prime to p. For g ∈ H and α ∈ k̄ write e_{g,α} ∈ M_n(k̄) for the g-equivariant projection of k̄^n onto the generalised α-eigenspace of g along the sum of the other generalised eigenspaces. (a) H is weakly adequate if the semisimple elements of H span M_n(k) as a k-vector space. (b) H is adequate (Thorne 2012, Definition 2.3; equivalently BLGG13, Definition A.1.1) if (A1) H¹(H, k) = 0, i.e. H has no quotient of order p; (A2) H⁰(H, ad⁰) = 0 and H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0; (A3) for every simple k̄[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ ⊗_k k̄ there are g ∈ H and an eigenvalue α ∈ k̄ of g with tr(e_{g,α}·W) ≠ 0. (c) H is GHT-adequate (Thorne 2017, Definition 2.20, taken from Guralnick–Herzig–Tiep) if H¹(H, k) = 0, H¹(H, ad₀) = 0, and for every simple k̄[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad ⊗_k k̄ there are a semisimple g ∈ H and α ∈ k̄ with tr(e_{g,α}·W) ≠ 0. Group cohomology is Mathlib's groupCohomology of the finite group H with coefficients in the k-linear representation. For a representation r̄ : Γ → GL_n(k) and a subgroup Γ' ⊆ Γ, 'r̄(Γ') is adequate' means that the finite subgroup r̄(Γ') ⊆ GL_n(k) is adequate.
hypotheses: k has characteristic p > 0 and H is finite; for an infinite subgroup none of the three notions is defined here
(A3) quantifies over simple submodules of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, not of ad⁰ over k; with k containing every eigenvalue of every element of H this is Thorne's condition over k
adequacy is not absolute irreducibility, not bigness (CHT08, which asks for a multiplicity-one eigenvalue) and not enormous image (G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance)
(b) forces p ∤ n: if p | n the scalar matrices lie in ad⁰ and are H-invariant, so (A2) fails; only (c) can hold when p | n
ad⁰ (trace-zero submodule) and ad₀ (quotient by scalars) are different modules when p | n
proofSteps: Construct ad, ad⁰ and ad₀ from G7/adjoint-representations: ad⁰ is the kernel of Matrix.traceLinearMap (Mathlib LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl as a submodule) and ad₀ is the quotient by the H-stable line k·1; record that ad⁰ ⊆ ad → ad₀ is an isomorphism iff the trace of 1, namely n, is a unit in k.

Define e_{g,α} as the projection onto Module.End.maxGenEigenspace of g at α along the sum of the other maximal generalised eigenspaces (k̄^n is their direct sum because the characteristic polynomial splits over k̄); semisimplicity of g is Module.End.IsSemisimple, equivalently order prime to p for finite H.

GHTT appendix Lemma 1: if H acts irreducibly, (A3) is equivalent to: the semisimple elements of H span ad; the proof takes the annihilator U ⊆ ad of the span of the semisimple elements under the trace pairing, notes U ⊆ ad⁰ (take g = 1) and that U = 0 is the condition. With Burnside's theorem this shows that weak adequacy implies absolute irreducibility (Thorne 2017, after Definition 2.20).
For p ∤ n, ad = k ⊕ ad⁰ as H-modules and ad₀ ≅ ad⁰, so (b) and (c) coincide for absolutely irreducible H (GHT17, introduction: H¹(G,(V*⊗V)/k) is H¹(G, ad⁰) when p ∤ dim V).

Base change: for a field extension k'/k, H^i(H, M ⊗_k k') = H^i(H, M) ⊗_k k' for finite H and finite-dimensional M (the cochain complex is a complex of finite-dimensional k-spaces), and the k-span of a set of matrices has the same dimension after ⊗ k'; so (a), (b), (c) for H ⊆ GL_n(k) are unchanged when k is replaced by k'. BLGG13 Lemma A.1.4 adds invariance under H ↦ k₁^×H for finite k₁ ⊇ k (normal subgroup of index prime to p plus inflation–restriction, Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact).
acceptance: SL₂(F_7) ⊆ GL₂(F_7) is adequate: no quotient of order 7 (perfect, Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top), H⁰(ad⁰) = 0 and H¹(ad⁰) = 0 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients; the computation in scratch gave dim H¹ = 0), and diag(3, 5), the identity, [[0,1],[−1,0]] and [[0,3],[2,0]] are semisimple and span M₂(F_7).

SL₂(F_5) ⊆ GL₂(F_5) is weakly adequate and absolutely irreducible but not adequate, because H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) is one-dimensional; SL₂(F_3) ⊆ GL₂(F_3) is not adequate because SL₂(F_3) → A₄ → Z/3 violates (A1), although H⁰ = H¹ = 0 for ad⁰ there (BLGG13 Proposition A.2.1, Points 5 and 6).

GL₂(F_5) ⊆ GL₂(F_5) is adequate: its abelianisation is F_5^× (order 4), and a direct computation gives H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 (the class of H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) is moved by diag(2,1); it survives only in ad⁰ ⊗ det²). This contradicts BLGG13 v1 Proposition A.2.1 for the projective image PGL₂(F_5) (sourceIssues ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E754) and agrees with Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3.
For p | n no subgroup of GL_n(k) is adequate in sense (b); for example SL₂(F_2) ⊆ GL₂(F_2) has H⁰(ad⁰) = k·1 ≠ 0.
