nodes.title: Verification criteria for adequacy: large characteristic, prime-to-p order, normal subgroups, tensor products, rank two and SL₂(p^r)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, k a field of characteristic p and H ⊆ GL_n(k) a finite subgroup; 'adequate' and 'GHT-adequate' are as in G7/adequate-subgroup. (1) (Guralnick–Herzig–Taylor–Thorne, appendix to Thorne 2012, Theorem 9, cited as Theorem A.9) Suppose H acts irreducibly on k̄^n, let H⁺ be the subgroup generated by the elements of p-power order (then k̄^n is a semisimple H⁺-module) and let d be the largest dimension of an irreducible H⁺-submodule of k̄^n. If p ≥ 2(d+1), then H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, k) = 0 and the semisimple elements of H span ad; hence H is adequate. In particular every absolutely irreducible H ⊆ GL_n(k) is adequate if p ≥ 2(n+1) (Thorne 2012, Lemma 2.4(ii); Newton–Thorne 2026, §2: p > 2n+2). (2) If p ∤ #H and H acts absolutely irreducibly, H is adequate (BLGG13 Remark A.1.2; GHTT Lemma 2(i)). (3) If N ⊴ H is adequate and p ∤ [H : N], then H is adequate (BLGG13 Lemma A.1.3); and if H acts irreducibly and some subgroup of H containing a Sylow p-subgroup of H is GHT-adequate on k^n, in particular if H⁺ is, then H is GHT-adequate (GHT17 Remark 6.1). (4) (BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1, Taylor) For a group Γ and representations r_i : Γ → GL_{n_i}(k̄), i = 1, 2, with r₁(Γ) adequate, r₂|_{ker r₁} irreducible and p ∤ #r₂(Γ), the image (r₁ ⊗ r₂)(Γ) is adequate; the same proof shows: if r₁(Γ) satisfies H¹(r₁(Γ), k̄) = 0, H¹(r₁(Γ), ad) = 0 and the spanning condition, so does (r₁ ⊗ r₂)(Γ) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 3.1). (5) (rank two; BLGG13 Proposition A.2.1 as corrected by sourceIssue E754, in agreement with Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3) If p > 2 and G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_p) is finite and irreducible on F̄_p², then G is adequate unless p = 3 and the image of G in PGL₂(F̄_3) is conjugate to PSL₂(F_3), or p = 5 and that image is conjugate to PSL₂(F_5). (6) (GHT17 Corollary 9.4) A nontrivial absolutely irreducible representation V of SL₂(F_{p^r}) over a field of characteristic p is GHT-adequate unless (i) r = 1 and 1 < dim V = (p ± 1)/2, (ii) p^r ∈ {2, 3, 4} and dim V = p^r, or (iii) p^r = 9 and dim V ∈ {3, 6, 9}.
hypotheses: (1) needs H irreducible and p ≥ 2(d+1) with d computed for H⁺, not for H
(4) needs p ∤ #r₂(Γ) and r₂ irreducible on ker r₁; tensor products of two adequate groups need not be adequate
(5) is for p odd; p = 2 and n = 2 is excluded since then p | n
(6) concerns GHT-adequacy; for p ∤ dim V it is Thorne-adequacy
proofSteps: (1): GHTT Theorem 9. dim V is prime to p (Clifford theory and [CR62, 51.7]); by Proposition 7 (which rests on the classification of finite simple groups) H is r(G(F_p)) for an algebraic group G = G⁰ ⋊ H₀ with G⁰ simply connected semisimple and p ∤ #H₀; H¹(H⁺, Hom(W_i, W_j)) = Ext¹ vanishes by Guralnick 1999, Theorem A, as dim W_i + dim W_j ≤ p − 2; then H¹(H, ad V) = 0 via the index-prime-to-p restriction, and the spanning statement follows from Lemma 3 and Lemma 8 on maximal tori. These two external inputs are recorded as a gap. The 'in particular' is Thorne 2012 Lemma 2.4(ii) with d ≤ n.

(2): BLGG13 Remark A.1.2: (A1) is trivial; p ∤ n since n divides #H (lift to characteristic 0); every element is semisimple and spans by Burnside; H¹ vanishes because #H is invertible (restriction to the trivial subgroup composed with corestriction is multiplication by #H: tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6, cor ∘ res).

(3): BLGG13 Lemma A.1.3 by the inflation–restriction exact sequence (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact) for N ⊴ H with ad^N = k·1, and GHT17 Remark 6.1 (spanning passes to overgroups; H¹ injects under restriction to a subgroup containing a Sylow p-subgroup, by cor ∘ res).

(4): BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1: with H_i = r_i(Γ), K_i = r_i(ker r_{3−i}) and Z the scalars z with (z, z⁻¹) in the image, H/K₂ ≅ H₁/Z; spanning is checked on A₁ ⊗ A₂ using r₂(ker r₁)-spans; H¹ by Hochschild–Serre: H¹(H/K₂, ad(r₁⊗r₂)^{K₂}) = H¹(H₁, ad r₁) = 0 and H¹(K₂, ·) = 0 as p ∤ #K₂.

(5): BLGG13 Proposition A.2.1 case analysis over Dickson's list (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement): p ≥ 7 by (1) with d ≤ 2; prime-to-p projective images by (2); PSL₂/PGL₂(k) with |k| ≥ p² by reduction to SL₂(k) and G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients; p = 3 with PGL₂(F_3) or A₅ adequate; p = 3 with PSL₂(F_3) fails (A1); p = 5 with PSL₂(F_5) fails as H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) ≠ 0. For p = 5 with image PGL₂(F_5): replace G by k^×G and then by GL₂(F_5) (Lemmas A.1.3, A.1.4); H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients (b)), so G is adequate — the opposite of BLGG13's Point 5 (E754).

(6): GHT17 Corollary 9.4: r = 1 is [GHT, Cor. 1.4]; for r > 1, Ext¹_G(V,V) = 0 by Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock [2, Cor. 4.5(a)], H¹(G,k) = 0 as G is perfect and H²(G,k) = 0 unless p^r ∈ {4, 9}; the cases p^r = 4, 9 are computed via tilting modules T(b₀) ⊗ T(b₁)^{(1)}. The AJL Ext computation is not in any library and is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: (1) with n = 2: every irreducible G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_p) is adequate for p ≥ 7 (d ≤ 2 gives p ≥ 6); with n = 4 and H ⊆ GSp₄(k) absolutely irreducible, p ≥ 11 suffices, which is Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni Lemma 7.5.14.
(5) at p = 5: SL₂(F_5) and every G with projective image PSL₂(F_5) are not adequate; GL₂(F_5) is (H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 by the computation recorded in G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients).
(6) with V = Sym^{n−1} of the standard representation of SL₂(F_p), n ≤ p: V is GHT-adequate unless n = (p ± 1)/2 (n > 1); for n = 2 this excludes exactly p = 3 and p = 5, matching (5).

(2) with p odd: the quaternion group Q₈ ⊆ SL₂(F̄_p) acting by its two-dimensional representation is adequate, and so is the image of Q₈ × Q₈ in GL₄(F̄_p) acting on the tensor product (order 32, irreducible); the latter is not enormous (G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance, acceptance), so (2) does not extend to enormous image.

nodes.title: The 'enormous' condition for Taylor–Wiles data, its failure when p divides n, and its invariance under coefficient extension
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, k an algebraic extension of F_p, n ≥ 1, and ad⁰ ⊆ M_n(k) the trace-zero matrices with the conjugation action of GL_n(k) (G7/adjoint-representations). An element h ∈ GL_n(k) is regular semisimple if its characteristic polynomial has n distinct roots in k̄ (equivalently is separable). An absolutely irreducible (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible) subgroup H ⊆ GL_n(k) is enormous over k (Allen et al. 2023, Definition 6.2.29; arXiv v2 Definition 6.2.28) if (1) H has no nontrivial quotient of p-power order; (2) H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0; (3) for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with W^h ≠ 0. The condition depends only on the image of H in PGL_n(k). If p | n, no subgroup of GL_n(k) is enormous, because the scalar matrices lie in ad⁰ and are H-invariant. (Lemma 6.2.30; arXiv v2 Lemma 6.2.29) For an algebraic extension k'/k and H ⊆ GL_n(k), H is enormous over k if and only if it is enormous over k'; hence 'enormous' is used without 'over k'. (Remark 6.2.31) If k contains all eigenvalues of all elements of H, H is enormous iff it satisfies Khare–Thorne 2017, Definition 4.10: (1), (2) and (3') for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ there are h ∈ H with n distinct eigenvalues in k and an eigenvalue α of h with tr(e_{h,α}W) ≠ 0. Relation with adequacy: if k contains all eigenvalues of the elements of a finite enormous H, then H is adequate (Gee–Newton, Remark 3.2.2, via bigness); for n = 2 and p odd, enormous and adequate coincide for irreducible finite H (Gee–Newton, Lemma 3.2.3). Enormous is not a synonym for adequate: for n ≥ 3 adequate groups need not contain any regular semisimple element.
hypotheses: H must be absolutely irreducible as part of the definition, not merely irreducible
condition (3) requires h to be regular semisimple; dropping regularity gives a different condition
the condition cannot hold when p divides n; the source says so explicitly
the equivalence with Khare–Thorne Definition 4.10 holds under the hypothesis that k contains all eigenvalues of the elements of H
in the applications the group is the image of ρ̄ restricted to G_{F(ζ_p)}, not the image of ρ̄ itself
H need not be finite in the definition, although in applications it is the image of a continuous representation into GL_n of a finite field
proofSteps: Lemma 6.2.30 (Allen et al.): only (3) needs attention, and it is equivalent to: for all nonzero k[H]-submodules W ⊆ ad⁰ there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with W^h ≠ 0. In that form enormity over k' implies enormity over k.

Conversely, the property V^h = 0 is closed under direct sums and quotients (V^h ≠ 0 iff the coinvariants V_h ≠ 0, h acting semisimply). For V ⊆ ad⁰ ⊗_k k', σ h v = h σ v for σ ∈ Gal(k'/k) since H ⊆ GL_n(k), so V^h ≠ 0 iff (σV)^h ≠ 0. If W' is a simple k'[H]-submodule with (W')^h = 0 for every regular semisimple h (corrected reading, sourceIssue E752), the submodule generated by all σW' is stable under H and Gal(k'/k), hence by Galois descent is W ⊗_k k' for a k[H]-submodule W; (3) applied to a simple submodule of W gives a regular semisimple h with W^h ≠ 0, hence (W ⊗ k')^h ≠ 0, a contradiction. Conditions (1) and (2) are insensitive to k'/k because group cohomology commutes with the flat base change k → k' (finite-dimensional coefficients) and absolute irreducibility is invariant (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible).

Projective invariance: the conjugation action on ad⁰ factors through the image P of H in PGL_n(k); (1) passes between H and P because the kernel Z = H ∩ k^× consists of elements of order prime to p (k^× has no p-torsion); (2) by inflation–restriction (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact): Z acts trivially on ad⁰ and is a torsion group without elements of order p, so H¹(Z, ad⁰) = Hom(Z, ad⁰) = 0 (ad⁰ is killed by p) and H^i(P, ad⁰) = H^i(H, ad⁰) for i = 0, 1; (3) is unchanged since regularity and fixed vectors are unchanged by scalars.

Remark 6.2.31: with all eigenvalues in k, a regular semisimple h is diagonalisable over k with one-dimensional eigenspaces, and W^h ≠ 0 iff tr(e_{h,α}W) ≠ 0 for some eigenvalue α (the projection to the h-fixed part of ad is X ↦ Σ_α e_{h,α}Xe_{h,α} and the trace pairing identifies W with its dual for ad⁰ when p ∤ n); compare Khare–Thorne Definition 4.10.

Enormous ⇒ adequate (k containing eigenvalues): Gee–Newton Remark 3.2.2 — enormous is big in the sense of CHT08 Definition 2.5.1 (a regular semisimple element has multiplicity-one eigenvalues), and big ⇒ adequate (Thorne 2012 Lemma 2.4(i)); (1) gives H¹(H, k) = 0. For n = 2, Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3: if tr(e_{h,α}W) ≠ 0 for W ⊆ ad⁰ then h has distinct eigenvalues (else e_{h,α} = 1 and tr W = 0).
acceptance: SL₂(F_p) ⊆ GL₂(F_p) is enormous for every p ≥ 7: SL₂(F_p) is perfect (Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top, as F_p has an element a with a² ≠ 1), ad⁰ = Sym² ⊗ det⁻¹ is absolutely irreducible with H⁰ = 0, H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p ≠ 5 (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 2.48; G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients), and h = diag(a, a⁻¹) with a² ≠ 1 is regular semisimple and fixes diag(1, −1) ∈ ad⁰.

SL₂(F_5) is not enormous (H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) is one-dimensional); SL₂(F_3) is not enormous (quotient of order 3, although H⁰ = H¹ = 0 for ad⁰); SL₂(F_2) is not enormous (2 | 2). GL₂(F_5) is enormous (H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0, no quotient of order 5), so a subgroup of an enormous group need not be enormous.
For n = p: the scalar matrix 1 has trace p = 0, so 1 ∈ ad⁰ is H-invariant and (2) fails for every H ⊆ GL_p(k).

Not merely a synonym for adequacy: for p odd the image H of Q₈ × Q₈ in GL₄(F̄_p) acting on the tensor product of two copies of the two-dimensional representation has order 32, is irreducible and hence adequate (G7/adequacy-criteria (2)), but every element g ⊗ h has repeated eigenvalues (products of {±1} or {±i} with {±1} or {±i}), so H has no regular semisimple element and is not enormous.
Lemma 6.2.30 check: SL₂(F_7) is enormous over F_7 and over F_49.

nodes.title: Enormous subgroups of GL_n(O) in characteristic zero (Newton–Thorne) and the Zariski-closure criterion
nodes.statement: Let E/Q_p be a finite extension with ring of integers O, n ≥ 1, and W_E = M_n(E) = ad ⊗_O E with H acting by conjugation. A subgroup H ⊆ GL_n(O) is enormous in the characteristic-zero sense (Newton–Thorne 2023, Definition 2.23) if for every simple E[H]-submodule V ⊆ W_E there are h ∈ H with n distinct eigenvalues in E and an eigenvalue α ∈ E of h with tr(e_{h,α}V) ≠ 0, where e_{h,α} is the h-equivariant projection onto the α-eigenspace. No vanishing of cohomology and no p-power-quotient condition is imposed, and the whole of W_E (not its trace-zero part) is tested. Facts: (Lemma 2.25) such H acts absolutely irreducibly on E^n, so H⁰(H, W⁰_E) = 0. (Lemma 2.28) Suppose H is compact and every h ∈ H has characteristic polynomial split over E. (1) If a closed subgroup H' ⊆ H is enormous, so is H. (2) If the identity component G° of the Zariski closure G ⊆ GL_n of H (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups) contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly on E^n, then H is enormous. Newton–Thorne 2026 (proof of Lemma 4.7) applies (2) through: if the derived subgroup G¹ of G° contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly, and G¹ lies in the Zariski closure of H, then H is enormous. This notion is distinct from the residual notion of G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance: it lives over a characteristic-zero field, has no cohomological conditions, and neither notion is deduced from the other.
hypotheses: E has characteristic zero; the residual notion is a different definition
Lemma 2.28 needs the characteristic polynomials of elements of H to split over E (enlarge E if necessary)
regular semisimple elements of G° (an algebraic group over E), not merely of H, are required in Lemma 2.28(2)
proofSteps: Lemma 2.25: if U = {u ∈ W_E : tr(hu) = 0 for all h ∈ H} is nonzero, a simple submodule V of U violates the definition (tr(e_{h,α}V) = 0 since e_{h,α} is a polynomial in h); so H spans W_E and acts absolutely irreducibly by Burnside's theorem.

Lemma 2.28(1) is immediate from the definition. (2): reduce to G = G°; G(E) spans W_E by absolute irreducibility; the regular semisimple locus G^reg is a nonempty Zariski-open subset and H^reg = H ∩ G^reg is Zariski dense in G; if tr(hv) = 0 for all h ∈ H^reg then tr(gv) = 0 for all g ∈ G, so v = 0; projections e_{h,α} are polynomials in h.

Newton–Thorne 2026, Lemma 4.7: G¹ ⊆ Zariski closure of ρ(G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}) (passage to derived subgroups commutes with Zariski closure, Borel Ch. I §2.4) and G° and G¹ have the same invariant subspaces, so Lemma 2.28 applies to ρ(G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}).
acceptance: Newton–Thorne 2023 Example 2.29: for π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL₂ over a totally real or CM field with Sym²π cuspidal, a model of Sym^{n−1} r_{π,ι} has ρ(G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}) enormous (the Zariski closure contains Sym^{n−1}(SL₂), which has regular semisimple elements and acts irreducibly).

A finite irreducible subgroup with no element of n distinct eigenvalues (the image of Q₈ × Q₈ on the four-dimensional tensor product, now over a p-adic field containing i) is not enormous in this sense; its Zariski closure is finite and contains no regular semisimple element.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers of groups containing SL₂(F_l) are enormous, and the Galois-theoretic consequence after restriction to F'(ζ_l)
nodes.statement: (1) (Gee–Newton, Lemma 3.2.5; Clozel–Harris–Taylor Corollary 2.5.4 with the corrected bound) Let n ≥ 2, p a prime with p > 2n + 1, k an algebraic extension of F_p, k' ⊆ k a finite subfield and H ⊆ GL_n(k) with k^× · Sym^{n−1}GL₂(k') ⊇ H ⊇ Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k'), where Sym^{n−1} : GL₂ → GL_n is the symmetric power of G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers in the monomial basis. Then H is enormous. (2) (Allen et al. 2023, Lemma 7.1.4, with the codomain corrected to GL_n, sourceIssue E751) If n ≥ 2, l > 2n + 1 and H ⊆ GL₂(F̄_l) is a finite subgroup containing SL₂(F_l), then Sym^{n−1}H ⊆ GL_n(F̄_l) is enormous. (3) (Allen et al. 2023, Lemma 7.1.6(2); Qian 2023, Lemma 2.6(1)) Let F/Q be finite with normal closure F̃, m ≥ 1, l > 2m + 3 a prime, r̄ : G_F → GL₂(F̄_l) continuous with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l), and F'/F a finite extension linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F. Then (Sym^m r̄)(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) is enormous. Qian's form (n = m + 1, l > 2n + 5) is the special case with a stronger bound; for n = 1 the image is trivial in GL₁ and enormous. (4) (Gee–Newton, Lemma 3.2.4) If n > 2, p > n, k' ⊆ k is a finite subfield and k^× · GL_n(k') ⊇ H ⊇ SL_n(k'), then H is enormous.
hypotheses: the bound is p > 2n + 1 (l > 2m + 3 for Sym^m); Clozel–Harris–Taylor print l > 2n − 1, which fails for n = 2, l = 5 (sourceIssue E756)
(3) needs SL₂(F_l) ⊆ r̄(G_{F̃}) with F̃ the normal closure, and linear disjointness from the field cut out by r̄ itself, not by ad r̄
the subgroup in (3) is the image of G_{F'(ζ_l)}, not of G_{F'}
proofSteps: (1), condition (2) of enormity: as SL₂(k')-modules ad Sym^{n−1} ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} Sym^{2i} ⊗ det^{−i} (G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions (d), valid as 2n − 2 < p), each Sym^{2i} irreducible (G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers (a)); so H⁰(Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k'), ad⁰) = 0, and H¹(SL₂(k'), Sym^{2i}) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 because 2i ≤ 2n − 2 < p − 3 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients (c)); pass from Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k') to H since the index is prime to p up to scalars (inflation–restriction and cor ∘ res, Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact, tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6). Condition (1): PSL₂(k') is simple and the quotient of H by Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k')·(scalars) has order dividing #k'^× · 2. Condition (3): Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.5.2 — the diagonal torus generator t of SL₂(k') has n distinct eigenvalues on Sym^{n−1} (n < p) and each Sym^{2i} meets the t-fixed part D = ⊕ Hom(V_j, V_j) in a line (Gee–Newton: these eigenspaces are one-dimensional, so t is regular semisimple).

(2): Dickson (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement): the image of H in PGL₂(F̄_l) is conjugate to PSL₂(k) or PGL₂(k) for a finite k ⊇ F_l, so F̄_l^× Sym^{n−1}GL₂(k) ⊇ Sym^{n−1}H ⊇ Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k), and (1) applies with k' = k.

(3): linear disjointness gives r̄(G_{F'}) = r̄(G_F) ⊇ r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l); SL₂(F_l) is perfect for l ≥ 5 (Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top) and Gal(F'(ζ_l)/F') is abelian, so r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field); apply (2) with n = m + 1, l > 2n + 1 = 2m + 3.

(4): Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.4 from the proof of Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.5.6 (bigness of groups between SL_n(k') and k^×GL_n(k')), plus a regular semisimple element of SL_n(k'): the companion matrix of X^n + (−1)^n, which has n distinct roots as p > n.
acceptance: n = 2, (2): every finite H ⊆ GL₂(F̄_l) containing SL₂(F_l) is enormous for l ≥ 7; for l = 5 the bound l > 5 fails and indeed SL₂(F_5) is not enormous (H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) ≠ 0), which shows the printed Clozel–Harris–Taylor bound l > 2n − 1 = 3 is too weak.
n = 3, l = 11 (> 7): Sym²(SL₂(F_11)) ≅ SO₃-image in GL₃(F_11) is enormous; ad⁰ Sym² = Sym² ⊕ Sym⁴ (twists) and H¹(SL₂(F_11), Sym^{2i}) = 0 for i = 1, 2 since 2, 4 ≠ 11 − 3.
(3) for an elliptic curve E/Q without CM and l ≥ 7 with r̄_{E,l}(G_Q) = GL₂(F_l), F = F' = Q, m = 1: r̄_{E,l}(G_{Q(ζ_l)}) = SL₂(F_l) is enormous.

nodes.title: H¹(SL₂(F), ad⁰) vanishes unless #F = 5, and the symmetric-power vanishing behind the bound p > 2n + 1
nodes.statement: Let F be a finite field of odd characteristic p and ad⁰ = End⁰(F²) = sl₂(F) with the conjugation action. (a) (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Lemma 2.48) If #F ≠ 5 then H¹(SL₂(F), ad⁰) = 0; also H⁰(SL₂(F), ad⁰) = 0. (b) For F = F_5, H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) is one-dimensional over F_5, while H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 and H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰ ⊗ det²) is one-dimensional; consequently H¹(G, ad⁰) = 0 for every G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_5) whose image in PGL₂(F̄_5) is conjugate to PGL₂(F_5), and H¹(G, ad⁰) ≠ 0 when that image is PSL₂(F_5). (c) (input to Clozel–Harris–Taylor Corollary 2.5.4, with the corrected bound) If n ≥ 2, p > 2n + 1 and F ⊇ F_p is finite, then H¹(SL₂(F), Sym^{2i}(F̄_p²)) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1. In particular H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p ≥ 7 is the case n = 2 of (c) and of (a).
hypotheses: p odd; for p = 2, ad⁰ contains the scalars
#F = 5 is a genuine exception in (a), not an artefact of the proof

(c) needs 2i ≠ p − 3 for all i ≤ n − 1, which p > 2n + 1 guarantees; the module Sym^{p−3} has nonzero H¹ (computed: dim H¹(SL₂(F_p), Sym^a) = 1 for a = p − 3 and 0 for the other 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1, p = 5, 7, 11)
proofSteps: (a): Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 2.48: p ∤ [SL₂(F) : B] for the Borel B, so H¹(SL₂(F), ad⁰) → H¹(B, ad⁰) is injective (cor ∘ res, tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6); H¹(B, M) = H¹(U, M)^{B/U} for the unipotent radical U; filter ad⁰ by B-stable lines M₁ ⊆ M₂ ⊆ M₃ and compute with long exact sequences; #F = 3 is done directly with the norm element, and #F = 9 needs the connecting homomorphism H¹(U, M₃/M₂)^{B/U} → H²(U, M₂/M₁) to be injective. H⁰ = 0 because ad⁰ is irreducible and nontrivial for p odd.

(b): the p = 5 value is Cline–Parshall–Scott table 4.5 (cited by Darmon–Diamond–Taylor and by BLGG13, Point 5); in this job it was checked by computing cocycles on the Cayley graph of each group over F_5 (a direct linear-algebra computation of the cocycle space): dim H¹ = 0, 1, 0, 0, 0 for SL₂(F_p), p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13; dim H¹(GL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p = 3, 5, 7; dim H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰ ⊗ det^j) = 0, 0, 1, 0 for j = 0, 1, 2, 3; dim H¹({det = ±1} ⊆ GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 1. The PGL₂(F_5) statement follows by replacing G with k^×G and then GL₂(F_5) (index prime to 5, inflation–restriction).

(c): Clozel–Harris–Taylor, proof of Corollary 2.5.4: restrict to the Borel and its Sylow p-subgroup U, H¹(SL₂(F), Sym^{2i}) ↪ H¹(U, Sym^{2i})^B, which vanishes by Cline–Parshall–Scott Lemma 2.7(c) when 2i ≤ 2n − 2 < p − 3. The printed hypothesis l > n + 1 there is too weak (it would include n = 2, l = 5, contradicting (b)); Cline–Parshall–Scott was not read in this job and the statement is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: Computed: dim H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0, 1, 0, 0, 0 for p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, matching (a) and the exception p = 5 that Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang's proof of Lemma 4.5.6 excludes.
Computed: H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 but H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰ ⊗ det²) ≠ 0, so the group GL₂(F_5) is adequate and enormous while SL₂(F_5) is neither.
For p = 2, SL₂(F_2) ≅ S₃ acting on the trace-zero matrices (which contain the scalars) has H⁰ and H¹ both one-dimensional, so the odd-characteristic hypothesis is needed.

Computed by this job (direct linear algebra on the cocycle space): for p = 5, 7, 11 and 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1, H¹(SL₂(F_p), Sym^a(F_p²)) is one-dimensional for a = p − 3 and zero otherwise; so (c) holds for F = F_p, p ≤ 11, and the bound p > 2n + 1 is sharp (n = (p − 1)/2 gives 2(n − 1) = p − 3).

nodes.title: Mod p Clebsch–Gordan decompositions: V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V, the two-constituent congruence for Sym^{p+r−1}V, and End(Sym^{n−1}V)
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Γ a group and V a two-dimensional representation of Γ over k; Sym^a is G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers, det = ∧²V, and (·)^ss is R01.1/semisimplification. (a) (Newton–Thorne 2026, (1.3)) If r ≥ 2 and r is invertible in k (in characteristic p: p ∤ r, in particular 1 < r < p), then V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V ≅ Sym^rV ⊕ (det ⊗ Sym^{r−2}V) as representations of Γ; for r = 1, V ⊗ Sym⁰V ≅ V. (b) (Newton–Thorne 2026, (1.1); Clozel–Thorne 2017, (1.1) for p = 7, r = 2, and proof of Theorem 6.2 for r = 2, general l) Let k ⊇ F_p be perfect, 0 < r < p, and let Frob V be the coefficient Frobenius twist of V (R01.1/coefficient-frobenius-twist: matrix entries raised to the p-th power; for a Galois representation, the action of an arithmetic Frobenius lift φ_p on coefficients). Then (Sym^{p+r−1}V)^ss ≅ (det^{⊗r} ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1}V)^ss ⊕ (Frob V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V)^ss; this is an identity after semisimplification only. (c) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 2.1) For every n ≥ 1, (End(Sym^{n−1}V))^ss ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} (Sym^{2i}V ⊗ det^{−i})^ss. (d) (Clozel–Harris–Taylor, proof of Lemma 2.5.2) If char k = p > 2n − 2 and Γ acts through SL₂(F_p) ⊆ SL₂(k), then ad Sym^{n−1}V ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} Sym^{2i}V as representations (not only after semisimplification), each summand irreducible.
hypotheses: (a) needs r invertible in k; it is a genuine isomorphism
(b) is only an isomorphism of semisimplifications; Sym^{p+r−1}V is in general a non-split extension
(b) uses the coefficient Frobenius twist, not restriction to a decomposition group or a Frobenius element of Γ
(c) holds for all n after semisimplification; (d) needs p > 2n − 2
proofSteps: (a): the comultiplication Δ : Sym^rV → V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V, F ↦ x ⊗ ∂_xF + y ⊗ ∂_yF (natural in V, hence Γ-equivariant) and multiplication m : V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V → Sym^rV satisfy m ∘ Δ = r·id (Euler's identity), so r⁻¹Δ splits m; the map det ⊗ Sym^{r−2}V → V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V, (x∧y) ⊗ G ↦ x ⊗ yG − y ⊗ xG, is Γ-equivariant, injective, lands in ker m, and dimensions match (2r − (r+1) = r − 1).

(b): by R01.1/brauer-nesbitt it suffices that both sides have the same characteristic polynomial for each γ ∈ Γ. If γ has eigenvalues a, b on V (in k̄), Sym^{p+r−1}V has eigenvalues a^i b^{p+r−1−i}, 0 ≤ i ≤ p+r−1; det^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1}V contributes the exponents r ≤ i ≤ p − 1, and Frob V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V (eigenvalues a^p, b^p on Frob V) contributes i = p + j and i = j for 0 ≤ j ≤ r − 1; the multisets agree.

(c): same method: End(Sym^{n−1}V) = Sym^{n−1}V ⊗ (Sym^{n−1}V)^∨ has eigenvalues (a/b)^m with multiplicity n − |m| for |m| ≤ n − 1, and ⊕_i Sym^{2i}V ⊗ det^{−i} has eigenvalues (a/b)^m, |m| ≤ i, again with multiplicity n − |m|.

(d): Clozel–Harris–Taylor: semisimplicity of ad Sym^{n−1} as an SL₂(F_p)-module follows from Serre's semisimplicity theorem for small modules ([Se2] there), and Sym^{2i} is irreducible for 2i ≤ p − 1 (G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers (a)); combine with (c). For the Clozel–Thorne case a = 1 of their discussion: if Γ acts through SL₂(F_p) then Frob V ≅ V and Frob V ⊗ V = Sym²V ⊕ det contains det, so the first constituent of (b) is not irreducible.
acceptance: Clozel–Thorne (1.1): p = 7, r = 2 gives Sym⁸V ~ (Frob V ⊗ V) ⊕ det² ⊗ Sym⁴V, dimensions 9 = 4 + 5.
(a) with r = 2: V ⊗ V ≅ Sym²V ⊕ det for p odd; for p = 2 this fails (V ⊗ V is not semisimple for SL₂(F_2) acting on F̄_2², the case r = p excluded by the hypothesis).
(c) with n = 2: End(V)^ss ≅ 1 ⊕ (Sym²V ⊗ det⁻¹)^ss, i.e. ad = k ⊕ ad⁰ after semisimplification, which is an honest splitting exactly when p ≠ 2.

sources.match: (a), displayed for Galois representations.
(b): the twist is on coefficients.
(b) holds only after semisimplification.
The case p = 7, r = 2.
Coefficient Frobenius and determinant.

nodes.title: Irreducibility of small symmetric powers of SL₂(F) and the one-dimensional constituents of their adjoints
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and F a finite field of characteristic p, with SL₂(F) acting on F̄_p² by the standard representation. (a) For 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1, Sym^a(F̄_p²) is an absolutely irreducible representation of SL₂(F); hence if r̄ : Γ → GL₂(F̄_p) has SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(Γ) and 1 ≤ n ≤ p, every twist of Sym^{n−1} r̄ by a character is absolutely irreducible (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 2.1). (b) (ibid., p. 514) Let p be odd. For 0 ≤ i ≤ p − 1, the one-dimensional composition factors of Sym^{2i}(F̄_p²) as an SL₂(F)-module occur with multiplicity at most one, and only for i = 0, for 2i = p + 1 (only when F = F_p) and for 2i = 2p − 2. (c) (ibid., pp. 513–514) Let p > 3, 1 ≤ n ≤ p, r̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F̄_p) continuous with SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_Q), and ρ̄ = Sym^{n−1} r̄ ⊗ ψ for a character ψ. Then every one-dimensional constituent χ of (ad ρ̄)^ss satisfies χ² = 1, and therefore H⁰(G_Q, M(1)) = 0 for every G_Q-subquotient M of ad ρ̄ or of its dual; in particular H⁰(Q, (𝔤⁰_n)^*(1)) = 0 for the Lie algebra 𝔤⁰_n = 𝔰𝔭_n or 𝔰𝔬_n of the similitude group preserved by ρ̄.
hypotheses: (a) fails for a = p: Sym^p contains the Frobenius twist of the standard representation as a proper submodule
(b) is about composition factors (semisimplification), not submodules
(c) needs p > 3 so that the mod p cyclotomic character satisfies ε̄^{−2} ≠ 1
proofSteps: (a): Sym^a for a ≤ p − 1 is the restricted simple module L(a) of SL₂ over F̄_p and stays simple on SL₂(F) for every finite F ⊇ F_p (Steinberg restriction; Clozel–Harris–Taylor proof of Lemma 2.5.2 uses the same fact for F = F_l); twisting by a character preserves absolute irreducibility; the image r̄(Γ) contains SL₂(F_p).

(b): compute composition factors of Sym^{2i} for 0 ≤ 2i ≤ 2p − 2 via G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions (b) for 2i ≥ p (Sym^{p+r−1} has constituents det^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1} and Frob ⊗ Sym^{r−1}); a one-dimensional constituent arises from Sym^{p−r−1} with r = p − 1 (2i = 2p − 2) or from Frob V ⊗ V ⊇ det when F = F_p and r = 2 (2i = p + 1). The Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction checked this with Brauer characters for p = 7, 11, 13 and F = F_{p²}, p = 5, 7.

(c): Boxer–Calegari–Gee: (𝔤⁰_n)^{*,ss} ⊆ (gl_n^*)^ss ≅ gl_n^ss ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} (Sym^{2i} r̄)^ss ⊗ det(r̄)^{−i} (G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions (c)); by (b) the one-dimensional constituents are self-dual characters, and ε̄^{−1} is not self-dual for p > 3 (ε̄ has order p − 1 > 2 on G_Q); H⁰ of a subquotient injects into H⁰ of the semisimplification's one-dimensional part.
acceptance: p = 7, F = F_7: Sym^0 = 1, Sym^8 (2i = p + 1) contains det-type constituent once, Sym^12 (2i = 2p − 2) contains one, and no other Sym^{2i} with i ≤ 6 has a one-dimensional constituent.
(c) fails for p = 3: ε̄^{−1} has order 2 and is self-dual, so the vanishing argument does not apply.

nodes.title: Adequacy of symmetric powers and Frobenius-twisted tensor products of large SL₂ images, with one common threshold
nodes.statement: (1) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, Lemma 2.2) Let p > 5 and r̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F̄_p) continuous with SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_Q). For p − 2 ≤ n ≤ p, the group (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) is GHT-adequate (Thorne 2017, Definition 2.20); for n = p − 2, p − 1 it is adequate in the sense of Thorne 2012. (2) (Newton–Thorne 2026, Lemma 2.3, quoting Thorne 2024, Lemma 7.3; common threshold) Let p ≥ 5 and φ_p ∈ G_{Q_p} a lift of arithmetic Frobenius. There is an integer a₀ = a₀(p) ≥ 3 such that for every a ≥ a₀ and every finite G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_p) containing a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}): (i) for each 0 < r < p, the image of Sym^{r−1} : G → GL_r(F̄_p) is adequate (Thorne 2012, Definition 2.3); (ii) for each 0 < r < p, the image of φ_p Std ⊗ Sym^{r−1} : G → GL_{2r}(F̄_p) is adequate, φ_p acting on the coefficients of the first factor only; (iii) every subgroup of G of index < 2p contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}) and so satisfies (i) and (ii). One a₀(p) is chosen for (i)–(iii) simultaneously; where Newton–Thorne require a > a₀(p), that strict inequality is kept. (3) (from G7/adequacy-criteria (1)) If SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(Γ) and p ≥ 2n + 2, then (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(Γ') is adequate for every Γ' ⊆ Γ with SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(Γ').
hypotheses: (1): n = p is divisible by p, so only GHT-adequacy (quotient by scalars) can hold there
(2)(ii) twists only the first factor by the coefficient Frobenius (R01.1/coefficient-frobenius-twist)
(2)(iii) is the group-theoretic statement of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/large-image-persistence, quoted here for the common threshold
proofSteps: (1): Boxer–Calegari–Gee: SL₂(F_p) is perfect, so SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}); by Dickson (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement) SL₂(F_q) ⊆ r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) for a power q of p with index prime to p up to scalars; by GHT17 Remark 6.1 (G7/adequacy-criteria (3)) it suffices that V = Sym^{n−1}U is GHT-adequate for SL₂(F_q); V is absolutely irreducible as n ≤ p (G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers (a)) and is not in the exceptional list of GHT17 Corollary 9.4 since n ≥ p − 2 > (p+1)/2 for p > 5 (G7/adequacy-criteria (6)). For n < p, p ∤ n and GHT-adequacy is Thorne-adequacy (G7/adequate-subgroup).

(2): Newton–Thorne quote Thorne 2024 Lemma 7.3, which was not read in this job. A proof along the same lines as (1): by Dickson G has projective image PSL₂(F_{p^b}) or PGL₂(F_{p^b}) with b ≥ a, so up to scalars and index prime to p it contains SL₂(F_{p^b}); Sym^{r−1} = L(r−1) and φ_p Std ⊗ Sym^{r−1} = L(1)^{(1)} ⊗ L(r−1) = L(p + r − 1) (Steinberg) are absolutely irreducible of dimensions r and 2r, both prime to p; GHT17 Corollary 9.4 with b ≥ 3 (excluding p^b ∈ {4, 9}) gives adequacy; G7/adequacy-criteria (3) passes to G. (iii) is ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/large-image-persistence; take a₀(p) as the maximum of the thresholds.
(3): Sym^{n−1} of SL₂(F_p) is absolutely irreducible for n ≤ p, so G7/adequacy-criteria (1) applies with d ≤ n.
acceptance: Boxer–Calegari–Gee p = 107, n = 105, 106: (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(G_{Q(ζ_107)}) is adequate for the mod-107 representation of the weight-26 level-one form (whose image contains SL₂(F_107)); this feeds their Theorem 2.4.
The bound in (1) is sharp in the sense of GHT17 Corollary 9.4(i): for n = (p ± 1)/2 > 1, Sym^{n−1} of SL₂(F_p) is not adequate (Ext¹ ≠ 0); e.g. p = 7, n = 3, 4.

nodes.title: Enormous and weakly enormous subgroups of GSp₄(k); vast and tidy GSp₄-valued representations
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p ≥ 3, GSp₄ the similitude group of the symplectic form of G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction with similitude character ν, and ad⁰ = Lie(Sp₄) ⊗ k (dimension 10) with the adjoint action of GSp₄(k). (i) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni 2021, Definition 7.5.2) A subgroup H ⊆ GSp₄(k) is enormous if (E1) H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0; (E2) H acts absolutely irreducibly on k⁴ (so H⁰(H, ad⁰) = 0); (E3) for every simple k̄[H]-submodule W ⊆ k̄ ⊗ ad⁰ there is h ∈ H with 4 distinct eigenvalues in GSp₄(k̄) such that 1 is an eigenvalue of h on W. H is weakly enormous if it satisfies (E2) and (E3). No condition on p-power quotients is imposed (Remark 7.5.4), unlike G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance; and ad⁰ is 𝔰𝔭₄, not the 15-dimensional 𝔰𝔩₄. (ii) (Lemma 7.5.3) Each notion depends only on the image of H in PGSp₄(k); a group containing a weakly enormous subgroup is weakly enormous, which fails for enormous. (iii) (Lemma 7.5.5) For a number field F and continuous ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k) there is δ depending only on F (δ = 1 if p is unramified in F) such that ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is independent of N for N ≥ 1 + δ (p ≥ 5) or N ≥ 2 + δ (p = 3). (iv) (Definition 7.5.6) ρ̄ is vast if either ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is enormous for all sufficiently large N, or ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is weakly enormous for all sufficiently large N and the fixed field L of ad⁰ρ̄ does not contain ζ_p. (v) (Definition 7.5.11) H ⊆ GSp₄(k) is tidy if some h ∈ H has ν(h) ≠ 1 and no two eigenvalues of h (counted in k̄, not necessarily distinct) have ratio ν(h); ρ̄ is tidy if ρ̄(G_F) is tidy; a group containing a tidy subgroup is tidy.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; the decomposition 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ ⊕ k·1 with trivial action on the centre (not ⊕ ν, sourceIssue E759) needs p > 2
(E3) is tested on simple submodules of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, with an element having 4 distinct eigenvalues and eigenvalue 1 on W
vastness concerns the images over F(ζ_{p^N}) for large N, not over F(ζ_p)
proofSteps: Define ad⁰ as the restriction of G7/adjoint-representations to the symplectic Lie algebra (Mathlib Matrix.symplecticGroup for the form J, transported to the form of G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction); 𝔰𝔭₄ ≅ Sym²(k⁴) ⊗ ν⁻¹ for p odd.

Lemma 7.5.3: with P the projective image and Z = H ∩ k^×, H⁰(P, ad⁰) = H⁰(H, ad⁰) and 0 → H¹(P, ad⁰) → H¹(H, ad⁰) → H¹(Z, ad⁰)^P = 0 (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact; #Z prime to p); (E2), (E3) are unchanged by scalars.

Lemma 7.5.5: Gal(F(ζ_{p^N})/F) ↪ (Z/p^N)^× contains 1 + p^δ; p-power elements of GSp₄(k) have order dividing p (p ≥ 5) or p² (p = 3) because they are unipotent with (σ − 1)⁴ = 0; this forces the kernel of Gal(M(ζ_{p^{N+1}})/F) → Gal(M(ζ_{p^N})/F) to be nontrivial for N in the stated range.
Vast and tidy are defined from (i) and from eigenvalues; the inheritance statements are immediate.
acceptance: Sp₄(F_p) is enormous and GSp₄(F_p) is tidy for p ≥ 3 (G7/gsp4-big-image-verification (5)); in particular, for p = 3, an element of order 20 with eigenvalues ζ, ζ³, ζ⁹, ζ²⁷ and ν = −1 witnesses tidiness.

Remark 7.5.4: the image of a surjective ρ̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F_3) with cyclotomic determinant has a quotient of order 3, so it is not enormous in the sense of Allen et al.; the GSp₄ notion omits that condition so that such images (and the p = 3 subgroups of §7.5.20) are allowed.
SL₂(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z ⊆ Sp₄(F_5) is weakly enormous but not enormous (E1 fails through H¹(SL₂(F_5), Sym²) ≠ 0).

uses.how: vastness gives Taylor–Wiles primes through Lemma 7.5.9; tidiness gives an auxiliary place v₀ at which all lifts are unramified and the level is neat

nodes.title: Verification of vast and tidy images in GSp₄: Galois cohomology vanishing, Sp₄(F_p), induced representations, wreath products and the p = 3 computations
nodes.statement: Notation of G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups; k finite of characteristic p ≥ 3. (1) (Lemma 7.5.9) If ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k) is continuous, N ≥ 1, L is the fixed field of ad⁰ρ̄ and either ζ_p ∉ L or ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is enormous, then H¹(Gal(L(ζ_{p^N})/F), ad⁰ρ̄(1)) = 0; so this holds for all large N if ρ̄ is vast. (2) (Lemma 7.5.12) An absolutely irreducible H ⊆ GSp₄(k) with centre of order ≥ 3 is tidy. (3) (Lemma 7.5.13) If p ≥ 5 and Δ = {(A, B) ∈ GL₂(F_p)² : det A = det B} ⊆ H ⊆ GSp₄(F_p), H is tidy. (4) (Lemma 7.5.14) If p ≥ 11 and H ⊆ GSp₄(k) is absolutely irreducible, (E1) and (E2) hold. (5) (Lemma 7.5.15) For p ≥ 3, Sp₄(F_p) is enormous and GSp₄(F_p) is tidy; a surjective ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(F_p) with similitude ε̄⁻¹ is vast and tidy. (6) (§7.5.16) If G ⊆ Sp₄(k) is absolutely irreducible and its representation W becomes reducible on an index-two subgroup H, with W|_H = V ⊕ V^σ and χ the quadratic character of G/H, then ad⁰(W) = Sym²(W) ≅ Ind_H^G ad⁰(V) ⊕ As(V), ∧²W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ, W ⊗ W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ Ind_H^G ad⁰(V) ⊕ As(V) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ, with As(V) the Asai (tensor-induced) representation, As(V)|_H = V ⊗ V^σ (G7/tensor-induction). (7) (Lemma 7.5.17) If As(V) and Ind_H^G ad⁰(V) are absolutely irreducible and G ∖ H contains an element whose order neither divides 4 nor is divisible by p, then G satisfies (E3). (8) (Lemma 7.5.18, corrected proof, E761) SL₂(k) ≀ Z/2Z ⊆ Sp₄(k) is weakly enormous, and enormous if #k ≠ 5. (9) (Lemma 7.5.19) If H/F is quadratic, r̄ : G_H → GL₂(F_5) surjective with det r̄ = ε̄⁻¹, ρ̄ = Ind r̄ : G_F → GSp₄(F_5), ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_5)}) = SL₂(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z and 5 unramified in F, then ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{5^N})}) is weakly enormous for all N ≥ 1, ζ_5 ∉ fixed field of ad⁰ρ̄, and ρ̄ is vast. (10) (§7.5.20, Lemma 7.5.21; finite computations) Exactly 11 of the 162 conjugacy classes of subgroups of Sp₄(F_3) are enormous (orders 40, 128, 160, 192, 240, 320, 384, 384, 1152, 1920, 51840), and the groups G ⊆ GSp₄(F_3) listed in Lemma 7.5.21 (GSp₄(F_3); a group of order 3840; Γ = Δ ⋊ Z/2Z of order 2304 and its two index-3 subgroups of order 768; Ã₅ ⋊ ⟨σ⟩ of order 480) are tidy with G ∩ Sp₄(F_3) enormous. (11) (Lemma 7.5.22, corrected, E762–E764) Let p ≥ 3, K/F quadratic with K unramified at p, r̄ : G_K → GL₂(k) with r̄(G_{K(ζ_p)}) = SL₂(k), σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_K with Proj r̄^σ ≇ Proj r̄ and det r̄^σ = det r̄ = ε̄⁻¹, ρ̄ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} r̄; if p = 3 assume the fixed fields of ker Proj r̄ and ker Proj r̄^σ are linearly disjoint over K(ζ_3). Then ρ̄ is vast and tidy. (12) (Remark 7.5.23, corrected, E765) The Sylow 2-subgroup Q₈ ≀ Z/2Z (order 128) of Sp₄(F_3) is enormous.
hypotheses: (4) needs p ≥ 11 (GHTT with d ≤ 4); for p = 3, 5, 7 the vanishing H¹(Sp₄(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 in (5) is a finite computation
(8) excludes #k = 5 because H¹(SL₂(F_5), Sym²) ≠ 0
(11) for #k > 3 includes the case Proj r̄^σ ≅ τ ∘ Proj r̄ with τ a field automorphism of order 2, which the printed proof omits
proofSteps: (1): Lemma 7.5.9 by inflation–restriction (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact): if ζ_p ∉ L, Gal(L(ζ_p)/L) acts trivially on ad⁰ but by nontrivial scalars on ad⁰(1), killing invariants, and p ∤ [L(ζ_p) : L]; if the image H over F(ζ_{p^N}) is enormous, H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0 and the splitting field M has p ∤ [M : L].
(2), (3): Schur's lemma makes the centre cyclic and scalar; a scalar ζ with ζ² ≠ 1 has ν = ζ² ≠ 1 and all eigenvalue ratios 1. Δ contains scalars of order p − 1 > 2.
(4): G7/adequacy-criteria (1) with d ≤ 4 (GHTT Theorem A.9), whose two external inputs are recorded as gaps.

(5): 𝔰𝔭₄ is absolutely irreducible for Sp₄(F_p), p ≥ 3; an element with distinct eigenvalues λ, ν/λ, μ, ν/μ has eigenvalue 1 on 𝔰𝔭₄ (from λ·(ν/λ)/ν); H¹(Sp₄(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 by (4) for p ≥ 11 and by computer for p = 3, 5, 7 (the authors' published Magma files; a gap until the computation is certified); tidiness by (2) for p > 3 and, for p = 3, an element of order 20 with ν = −1 and eigenvalues ζ, ζ³, ζ⁹, ζ²⁷; vastness because Sp₄(F_p) has no quotient of order p (PSp₄(F_p) simple).
(6): compute over H and use W ≅ W ⊗ χ; As(V) from G7/tensor-induction; induced representations from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction.

(7): g ∈ G ∖ H has eigenvalues (α, α⁻¹, −α, −α⁻¹), distinct when α⁴ ≠ 1; counting in the Grothendieck group of ⟨g⟩: [As(V)] = [−1, 1, α², α⁻²] and [Ind ad⁰(V)] = [1, −1, α², −α², α⁻², −α⁻²], both containing 1.

(8): (E1) by inflation–restriction reduces to H¹(SL₂(k), Sym²(k²)) = 0 for #k ≠ 5 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients (a)); (E2) is clear; (E3) by (7) with g = (a, 1)σ, a ∈ SL₂(k) of order 4 (e.g. [[0,1],[−1,0]]), so g² = (a, a) has order 4 and g has order 8, not dividing 4 and prime to p. The printed proof takes a of order 8, which does not exist when #k ≡ ±3 mod 8 (E761).

(9): the abelianisation of SL₂(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z has order prime to 5, so the image over F(ζ_{5^N}) does not depend on N, and is weakly enormous by (8); the image Γ of ρ̄ is the full preimage of G with [Γ : G] = 4, whose projective image has abelianisation (Z/2)², which does not surject onto Gal(F(ζ_5)/F) = Z/4.
(10): finite group enumeration (the authors' Magma computation, reproduced as a certified finite computation), except (3a), which is (8). Recorded as a gap.

(11): for #k > 3, Goursat (PSL₂(k) simple; Mathlib Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple) and Aut(PSL₂(k)) = PΓL₂(k) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2) show that either the image over K(ζ_p) is SL₂(k)², giving SL₂(k) ≀ Z/2Z over F(ζ_{p^N}) and (8), (9); or Proj r̄^σ ≅ τ ∘ Proj r̄ with τ of order 2, where the image over F(ζ_p) is an index-two extension of {(A, ±τ(A))}, still enormous (V ≇ V^τ; H¹(SL₂(k), Sym²) = 0 as #k ≥ 25; H¹(SL₂(k), V ⊗ V^τ) = 0 for p ≥ 5; (E3) via (7) with g = (C, ±C)·swap, C of order q₀ + 1), and tidiness from ρ̄(g) with r̄(g) = diag(a, −a⁻¹), a a generator of k^× (E763). For k = F_3 the image over F(ζ_{3^N}), N ≥ 2, is SL₂(F_3) ≀ Z/2Z or its normal subgroup of index 3, both enormous by (10) (the abelianisation is Z/6Z, not prime to 3: E764); the p = 3 hypothesis is linear disjointness over K(ζ_3) (E762); tidiness for p = 3 from an element of order 8 with ν = −1 and eigenvalues (ζ, −ζ⁻¹, ζ, −ζ⁻¹).

(12): |Q₈ ≀ Z/2Z| = 128 is prime to 3, so (E1) holds; the natural representation restricted to Q₈ × Q₈ is V_A ⊕ V_B, non-isomorphic and swapped, so (E2) holds; ad⁰ = Ind(χ₁) ⊕ Ind(χ₂) ⊕ Ind(χ₃) ⊕ As(V) with χ_j the nontrivial characters of Q₈/{±1}, pairwise non-isomorphic irreducibles; g = (a, b)σ with ab of order 4 has the four primitive 8th roots of unity as eigenvalues, acts on Ind(χ_j) with eigenvalues ±√χ_j(ab) (containing 1 when ab ∈ ker χ_j) and on As(V) with eigenvalues 1, −1, i, −i; so (E3) holds.
acceptance: (5) for p = 3: GSp₄(F_3) contains an element of order 20 with ν = −1; its eigenvalue ratios ζ², ζ⁸, ζ²⁶ differ from ζ¹⁰ = −1.

(8) for k = F_3: g = (a, 1)σ with a = [[0,1],[−1,0]] has order 8 and eigenvalues the primitive 8th roots of unity; SL₂(F_3) has no element of order 8 (its Sylow 2-subgroup is Q₈), so the printed choice is impossible.
(8) for k = F_5: (E1) fails, consistent with H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) being one-dimensional; Lemma 7.5.19 substitutes weak enormity plus ζ_5 ∉ L.
(10): the class of order 128 in the list of §7.5.20 is the Sylow 2-subgroup of Sp₄(F_3) (51840 = 2⁷·3⁴·5), consistent with (12) and contradicting the last sentence of Remark 7.5.23.

nodes.title: The big image assumption (H1)–(H3) for GSp₄-valued residual representations of G_Q
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, k a finite field of characteristic p, and r̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(k) continuous (G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction). Let ad(r̄) be r̄ composed with the 11-dimensional adjoint representation on 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ and ad⁰(r̄) its composite with 𝔰𝔭₄ (10-dimensional); ad(r̄) = ad⁰(r̄) ⊕ k with the trivial action on the centre k·1 (corrected statement, sourceIssue E759), and ad⁰(r̄)(1) = ad⁰(r̄) ⊗ ε̄. r̄ has big image (Calegari–Geraghty 2020, Assumption 4.1, after Pilloni §5.7) if (H1) the field Q(ad⁰(r̄)) cut out by ad⁰(r̄) does not contain ζ_p; (H2) for every m ≥ 1 there is σ ∈ G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})} such that r̄(σ) has four distinct eigenvalues and σ has 1 as an eigenvalue on each irreducible k̄[G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}]-constituent of ad⁰(r̄) ⊗ k̄; (H3) neither the image Γ of ad⁰(r̄) nor the image of ad⁰(r̄)(1) has a quotient of order p. (H1) depends on more than the group r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}). Relation with Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni: if r̄|G_{Q(ζ_{p^N})} is absolutely irreducible for all N and r̄ has big image, then r̄ is vast (G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups, Definition 7.5.6(2)), since (H2) for each m gives (E3) for the image over Q(ζ_{p^m}) with a single element for all constituents.
hypotheses: p > 2, so that 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ ⊕ k·1
(H2) asks for one σ that works for all irreducible constituents at once, for every m
(H1) is a condition on the field cut out by ad⁰(r̄), not on the image group
proofSteps: Form ad and ad⁰ from G7/adjoint-representations restricted along GSp₄ ⊆ GL₄; the splitting 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ ⊕ k·I₄ holds for p > 2 (if XᵀJ + JX = cJ then X − (c/2)I ∈ 𝔰𝔭₄) and the adjoint action fixes I₄ (E759).
Constituents are taken after extending scalars to k̄ (R01.1/semisimplification); eigenvalues of σ on a constituent are those of the induced endomorphism.

Relation with vastness: (H2) gives, for W a simple submodule of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄ over G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}, an element with distinct eigenvalues and eigenvalue 1 on W, i.e. (E3); with absolute irreducibility (E2) the image over Q(ζ_{p^m}) is weakly enormous; with (H1) this is Definition 7.5.6(2).
acceptance: Image GSp₄(F_p), p ≥ 5, has big image (G7/cg20-big-image-examples (2)).
An induced r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄ as in Calegari–Geraghty Example 4.11(1) has big image; the element must be taken in r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}) (E757).

elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic K give induced r̄ with big image for almost all p

nodes.title: Examples of big image: surjective GSp₄(F_p) images and inductions from imaginary quadratic fields
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5. (1) (Calegari–Geraghty 2020, Example 4.11(1), with corrected proof) Let K/Q be imaginary quadratic with K ⊄ Q(ζ_p), and ρ̄ : G_K → GL₂(F_p) with det ρ̄ = ε̄^{1−k} for some integer k, such that for a complex conjugation c the pair (ρ̄, ρ̄^c) maps G_{K(ζ_p)} onto SL₂(F_p) × SL₂(F_p) (the fields cut out by ρ̄|G_{K(ζ_p)} and ρ̄^c|G_{K(ζ_p)} are linearly disjoint over K(ζ_p)). Then r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄ preserves a symplectic form with multiplier ε̄^{1−k}·(quadratic character as in G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction), ad⁰(r̄)|_{G_K} ≅ (ρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄^c) ⊗ ε̄^{k−1} ⊕ ad⁰(ρ̄) ⊕ ad⁰(ρ̄^c), ad⁰(r̄) ≅ As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε̄^{k−1} ⊕ Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ̄) up to replacing As(ρ̄) by its quadratic twist, r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}) = {diag(A,B) : A, B ∈ SL₂(F_p)} ⊔ {diag(A,B)·r̄(c) : det A = det B = (−1)^{k−1}} (abstractly SL₂(F_p)² ⋊ Z/2Z) for every m ≥ 1, and r̄ has big image. (2) (Example 4.11(2)) If r̄(G_Q) = GSp₄(F_p), then r̄ has big image.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5, so that SL₂(F_p) and Sp₄(F_p) are perfect and PSL₂(F_p) is simple
the element witnessing (H2) must lie in r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}); c itself does not (E757)
only the eigenvalue 1, not −1, is automatic on Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ̄) for elements of the index-two subgroup (E758)
proofSteps: (1), structure: the dual of ρ̄ is ρ̄ ⊗ ε̄^{k−1} (printed with × for ⊗, E760); compute ad⁰ over K and over Q by G7/gsp4-big-image-verification (6) and G7/tensor-induction (Asai).
(1), (H1) and (H3): SL₂(F_p) perfect (Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top) and K ⊄ Q(ζ_p) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field for the cyclotomic bookkeeping).

(1), image over Q(ζ_{p^m}): elements of G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})} ∖ G_K are σc with σ ∈ G_K, ε̄(σ) ≡ −1, so r̄(σc) = diag(ρ̄(σ), ρ̄^c(σ))·r̄(c) with det ρ̄(σ) = (−1)^{k−1}; SL₂(F_p)² is perfect and disjoint from the p-extension K(ζ_{p^m})/K(ζ_p), so every (A, B) with det A = det B = (−1)^{k−1} occurs (E757).

(1), (H2): take A = diag(x, (−1)^{k−1}x⁻¹), B = diag(y, (−1)^{k−1}y⁻¹), x = 2, y = 1; diag(A,B)·r̄(c) has eigenvalues ±(xy)^{1/2}, ±(xy)^{−1/2} on r̄ (distinct as (xy)² = 4 ≠ 1), eigenvalues xy, (xy)⁻¹, 1, −1 on As(ρ̄), and eigenvalue 1 on Ind ad⁰(ρ̄) (every element of GL₂ has eigenvalue 1 on ad⁰, and elements outside the index-two subgroup have both ±1, E758).

(2): r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}) ⊇ Sp₄(F_p) for all m (Sp₄(F_p) perfect, GSp₄(F_p)/Sp₄(F_p) abelian); (H2) as in G7/gsp4-big-image-verification (5): 𝔰𝔭₄ is absolutely irreducible and every element with distinct eigenvalues has eigenvalue 1 on it; (H1): the projective image PGSp₄(F_p) has abelianisation of order 2 while Gal(Q(ζ_p)/Q) is cyclic of order p − 1 ≥ 4; (H3): PGSp₄(F_p) has no quotient of order p and the image of ad⁰(r̄)(1) is an extension of a quotient of PGSp₄(F_p) by a group of order prime to p. Calegari–Geraghty cite Pilloni 2012, Proposition 5.8 instead (not read in this job).
acceptance: (1) mod 13 with x = 2, y = 1 and either sign (−1)^{k−1}: the element has characteristic polynomial T⁴ + 4T² + 1 on r̄ and (T² − 1)(T − 2)(T − 2⁻¹) on As(ρ̄) (check recorded by the Calegari–Geraghty extraction, E28).
(1) for k = 2 (Remark 4.12, elliptic curves): the printed element swap·diag(x, x⁻¹, y, y⁻¹) has blocks of determinant +1 ≠ −1 and does not lie in r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}); the corrected element does.
(2) for p = 5: GSp₄(F_5) surjective image gives big image although SL₂(F_5) is not enormous.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles image conditions: adequate or enormous image over F(ζ_p) and a scalar element outside G_{F(ζ_p)}
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a prime, n ≥ 1 and s̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_p) continuous; its image is finite and lies in GL_n(k) for a finite field k (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field). (a) s̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles image conditions if (TW2) the finite group s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) ⊆ GL_n(F̄_p) is adequate (G7/adequate-subgroup, Thorne 2012 sense) and (TW3) there is σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_{F(ζ_p)} with s̄(σ) scalar. (b) s̄ satisfies the enormous Taylor–Wiles image conditions if s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous (G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance) and (TW3) holds (Allen et al. 2023, Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2, hypotheses (3)–(4)). These are the image-theoretic parts (2) and (3) of the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, Definition 5.2.1; their condition (1), decomposed genericity, is defined at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7 and the full conjunction is formed at PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5. (TW3) is equivalent to ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad s̄}, i.e. ker(ad s̄) ⊄ G_{F(ζ_p)}.
hypotheses: (TW2) is about the image of G_{F(ζ_p)}, not of G_F
(TW3) requires σ outside G_{F(ζ_p)}; in particular it fails when ζ_p ∈ F
decomposed genericity is not part of this node (stage-edge: AG2.7 requires G7)
proofSteps: Finite image: R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients and R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field; restriction to G_{F(ζ_p)} via R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist.

(TW3) ⟺ ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad s̄}: s̄(σ) is scalar iff σ ∈ ker(ad s̄) (Mathlib Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar: the centre of GL_n is the scalars), and ker(ad s̄) ⊄ G_{F(ζ_p)} iff the fixed field of ker(ad s̄) does not contain ζ_p (Galois correspondence).

Twisting: s̄ ⊗ χ has the same ad and the same image up to scalars over F(ζ_p), so both conditions are invariant under twists (G7/adequate-subgroup API isAdequate_units_mul_iff; enormity is projective).
acceptance: n = 1: (TW2) always holds and (TW3) holds iff ζ_p ∉ F.

For a non-CM elliptic curve E/Q and l ≥ 7 with r̄_{E,l}(G_Q) = GL₂(F_l): r̄(G_{Q(ζ_l)}) = SL₂(F_l) is adequate and enormous, and σ with r̄(σ) = 2·I has χ̄_l(σ) = det = 4 ≠ 1, so σ ∉ G_{Q(ζ_l)}; both (a) and (b) hold.

nodes.title: Verification lemmas for the Taylor–Wiles image conditions: disjoint base change, Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B, induced Frobenius eigenvalues, scalar elements for Sym^m
nodes.statement: (1) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, Lemma 5.2.2, image part) Let F/Q be Galois and s̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_p) satisfy the Taylor–Wiles image conditions (G7/taylor-wiles-image-conditions). If H/F is finite and its Galois closure over Q is linearly disjoint over F from the composite of F(ζ_p) and the Galois closure over Q of F̄^{ker s̄}, then s̄(G_H) = s̄(G_F), s̄(G_{H(ζ_p)}) = s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}), and s̄|G_H satisfies the Taylor–Wiles image conditions. (2) (Lemma 5.2.4, image parts) Let F/Q be Galois, r̄_A : G_F → GL₂(F_p) and r̄_B : G_F → GU_m(F_{p²}) ⊆ GL_m(F_{p²}) with r̄_A(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SL₂(F_p) and r̄_B(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SU_m(F_{p²}), s̄ = Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B, p > 2mn + 1, and if m = 2 assume the Galois closures over Q of the fixed fields of the projective representations of r̄_A and r̄_B are linearly disjoint over F(ζ_p) (E768). Then (i) s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} has adequate image; (ii) if det r̄_A = ε̄^{−m} and r̄_B has multiplier ε̄^{1−m}, s̄ has image in GU_{mn}(F_{p²}) with multiplier ε̄^{1−mn} (E769); (iii) if moreover ε̄(G_F) = F_p^×, (TW3) holds for s̄. (3) (Lemma 5.2.5) Let E/Q be cyclic of degree m and linearly disjoint from F, L = EF, ψ : G_L → F_p^× with p ∤ m, r̄_B = Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ψ, and q a rational prime splitting completely in F with r̄_B unramified above q and Frob_q generating Gal(E/Q). For v | q, the eigenvalues of r̄_B(Frob_v) are λ, ζλ, …, ζ^{m−1}λ with ζ a primitive m-th root of unity. (4) (Lemma 5.2.6, image parts, corrected) Let F/Q be Galois, r̄_A as in (2), r̄_B ≅ Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ψ : G_F → GL_m(F_p) as in (3) with r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible (E767), s̄ = Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B and p > 2mn + 1. Then s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} has adequate image, and if det r̄_A = ε̄^{−m}, det r̄_B = ε̄^{−m(m−1)/2} and ε̄(G_L) = F_p^×, (TW3) holds. (5) (Allen et al. 2023, Lemma 7.1.6(1)) Under the standing hypotheses of G7/enormous-symmetric-powers (3) (F/Q finite with normal closure F̃, l > 2m + 3, r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l), F'/F linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄}), if l is unramified in F'/Q then ζ_l ∉ F̄^{ker ad Sym^m r̄}·F', so Sym^m r̄|G_{F'} satisfies (TW3) and, with G7/enormous-symmetric-powers (3), the enormous Taylor–Wiles image conditions.
hypotheses: the decomposed-genericity halves of Lemmas 5.2.2, 5.2.4(1), 5.2.6(1) and of Allen et al. Lemmas 7.1.5, 7.1.6(3)–(5), 7.1.7 are not stated here (routed to PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5)
(4) needs r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible, not merely irreducible (E767)
(2) for m = 2 needs linear disjointness of the Galois closures, not of the fields themselves (E768)
proofSteps: (1): Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 5.2.2: reduce to H Galois over Q; disjointness gives Gal(H·M(ζ_p)/F) ≅ Gal(M(ζ_p)/F) × Gal(H/F), so the images of G_H and G_{H(ζ_p)} equal those of G_F and G_{F(ζ_p)}, and a scalar σ outside G_{F(ζ_p)} gives (σ, 1).

(2)(i): Goursat with Lemma 5.2.3 (simplicity and pairwise non-isomorphism of PSL₂(F_p) and PSU_m(F_{p²}), ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2 for the PSL₂ part) gives Gal(H̃/F(ζ_p)) ≅ PSL₂(F_p)^r × PSU_m(F_{p²})^s; the image of s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} contains Sym^{n−1}SL₂(F_p) ⊗ SU_m(F_{p²}), acting absolutely irreducibly, and adequacy follows from G7/adequacy-criteria (1) as p > 2mn + 1 ≥ 2(mn + 1) − 1 (GHTT Theorem A.9). (ii): multipliers multiply (G7/polarized-representation for unitary multipliers). (iii): choose σ with r̄_A(σ) and r̄_B(σ) scalar and ε̄(σ) ≠ 1, using ε̄(G_F) = F_p^×.

(3): Gal(L/F) ≅ Gal(E/Q) is cyclic of order m; r̄_B ≅ r̄_B ⊗ χ for a character χ of order m through Gal(L/F), and Frob_v maps to a generator, so the eigenvalue multiset is stable under multiplication by ζ = χ(Frob_v).

(4): as (2)(i), with r̄_B of solvable image and order prime to p after Mackey (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne item 140; Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction layer 4) and G7/adequacy-criteria (4) (BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1) for the tensor product; absolute irreducibility of r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)} is needed because adequacy implies it (E767).

(5): reduce to m = 1 (ad Sym^m r̄ factors through ad r̄); Gal(F'(ζ_l)/F') ≅ (Z/l)^× as l is unramified in F', while ad r̄(G_{F'}) = ad r̄(G_F) is PSL₂(k) or PGL₂(k) and has no cyclic quotient of order l − 1 > 2 (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field); then apply the characterisation (TW3) ⟺ ζ_l ∉ F̄^{ker ad} of G7/taylor-wiles-image-conditions.
acceptance: (3) with m = 2: r̄_B = Ind ψ from a quadratic L = EF, Frob_v nontrivial on E: eigenvalues λ, −λ, i.e. trace zero.
(4) without absolute irreducibility fails: for m = 2 with Ind ψ̄ ≅ θ ⊕ θη over F̄_p (θ F_{p²}-valued) the image of s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is not absolutely irreducible, hence not adequate (E767).
(5) for E/Q non-CM with surjective mod l image, l ≥ 7, F = F' = Q: ζ_l ∉ Q̄^{ker ad r̄}, so Sym^m r̄ satisfies the enormous Taylor–Wiles image conditions for l > 2m + 3.

requests.need: Export the reconstruction theorem over algebraically closed fields as a node: for an algebraically closed field k, a group (or monoid) Γ and a d-dimensional determinant D on k[Γ], there is a semisimple representation ρ : Γ → GL_d(k) with D = det ∘ ρ, unique up to isomorphism, and ker ρ = ker D (Chenevier Theorem 2.12). The uniqueness must be proved without quoting Brauer–Nesbitt (Chenevier's proof does quote it), e.g. by evaluating characteristic polynomials on elements of k[Γ] that map to a rank-one idempotent in one matrix factor of the semisimple image algebra. RT-AREA-langlands-1/17.

For K = Q_ℓ (more generally a nonarchimedean local field) and K̄ = PadicAlgCl ℓ: the action of G_K on the residue field F̄_ℓ of the valuation ring of K̄, i.e. the continuous surjection G_K → Gal(F̄_ℓ/F_ℓ), with arithmetic Frobenius lifts as the preimages of x ↦ x^q.
The inertia subgroup I_K as the kernel of G_K → Gal(k̄/k), so that two lifts of arithmetic Frobenius differ by an element of I_K.

For a split connected reductive Ĝ over a nonarchimedean local field E: the action of Ĝ(E) on the building B(DĜ, E); a compact subgroup of Ĝ(E)^0 (elements whose characters are O_E^×-valued) fixes a point; maximal compact subgroups of Ĝ(E)^0 are stabilisers of centroids of facets; the hyperspecial point x_0 with stabiliser Ĝ(O_E); the equivariant embeddings i_{E,E′} : B(DĜ, E) → B(DĜ, E′) for finite E′/E; conjugacy of hyperspecial vertices under Ĝ^ad(E′); and the GL_n lattice model (vertices = homothety classes of lattices).

Inertia I_K, wild inertia P_K and the tame character I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1) with independence of choices, G_K-equivariance and the finite-level Kummer form; arithmetic Frobenius lifts as a coset of I_K; restriction to finite extensions (the factor e on the tame character).
Gal(K^{ur}/K) ≅ Ẑ with arithmetic Frobenius ↦ 1 (built on Mathlib's profinite completion), the unramified extension of each degree, and the unramified quadratic extension Q_{p²}.
The finite-level tame and wild ramification groups G_0 ⊃ G_1 and the tame quotient embedding G_0/G_1 ↪ k^×, compatible with layer 4.
Krasner's lemma, giving F̄_v = F_v·ι(F̄) for an embedding of algebraic closures, and the globalisation of finite extensions of local fields used by Deligne's Lemme 4.13.

The Weil group W_K with Weil topology, weilDegree : W_K → Z (arithmetic normalisation, kernel I_K), weilTransfer and weilDegree_weilTransfer for finite extensions, and localWeilArtinEquiv for K/Q_p finite.

The artinMap normalisation statements (uniformiser ↦ arithmetic Frobenius, normResidue_uniformizer) and conductors of characters, so that R01.2 can state the conversion to Deligne's geometric normalisation.
kroneckerWeber: every finite abelian extension of Q is contained in a cyclotomic field (finite-order characters of G_Q are Dirichlet characters).
Existence, uniqueness modulo inertia and conjugation of IsArithFrobAt Frobenius elements in finite Galois extensions of number fields, and the cyclotomic examples (Frob_p acts as ζ ↦ ζ^p on Q(ζ_N)).
Completions as nonarchimedean local fields (5.1), completionAlgHom (5.2) and decompositionHom with its bijectivity and compatibility with Frobenius and conjugation (5.6).
Mackey's irreducibility criterion for Ind_H^G χ, H normal of index 2, applied to the finite image of a residual local representation.

Brauer's induction theorem: every virtual character of a finite group is a Z-combination of characters induced from one-dimensional characters of (elementary) subgroups; used for the uniqueness and the global step of Deligne's local constants.
The Tate curve E_q over a local field with its Tate parametrisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E(K̄), giving E[ℓ^n] as an extension of Z/ℓ^n by μ_{ℓ^n} with Kummer class of q.

Tate's local ε-factors of quasi-characters (AL.1/local-epsilon-gamma-factors, AL.1/explicit-epsilon-factors, AL.1/local-quasicharacter-conductor) and Hecke's functional equation (AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation), with an explicit dictionary between ε(s, ω, ψ) and Deligne's ε(χ, ψ, dx). AL.1 does not depend on R01.2 (checked in data/atlas.json: AL.1 requires only AL.0 → AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.0).

Lower and upper numbering with Herbrand's quotient theorem (upperRamificationGroup_quotient), Herbrand functions φ, ψ, Hasse–Arf (hasseArf) and the Hilbert different formula / discriminant exponents for finite Galois extensions of a nonarchimedean local field, in mixed and equal characteristic.
I_K and P_K as closed normal subgroups of G_K, with their images in finite quotients equal to G_0 and G_1.
Unramified extensions: I_{K'} = I_K and equality of filtrations for K'/K unramified.

Comparison of characterConductorExp with the ramification conductor: for K/Q_p finite and every n ≥ 0, artinMap(U_K^n) is dense in the image of G_K^n in G_K^ab (U_K^0 = O_K^×), so that a(χ) = characterConductorExp(χ ∘ artinMap) for finite-order characters χ.
The local Weil group W_K with I_K ⊆ W_K open and its degree map.
Completions F_v and decomposition-group embeddings for the local restriction of global representations.
Localisation of the relative different and discriminant: v_𝔭(𝔡_{F'/F}) = Σ_{w|v} δ(F'_w/F_v).
Clifford theory: a G-stable irreducible character of a normal subgroup N extends to G when G/N is cyclic (with layer 7: Schur multiplier of a cyclic group is trivial).
Brauer's induction theorem: every character of a finite group is a Z-combination of characters induced from one-dimensional characters of (elementary) subgroups.
Vanishing of H²(C, C^×) for C cyclic, used to extend stable characters across a cyclic quotient.
The ℓ-adic Tate module of an elliptic curve with its continuous G_K action (through R01.6/elliptic-tate-module-comparison).
For an endomorphism α of an elliptic curve over a field, tr(α | V_ℓ) = 1 + deg α − deg(1 − α), an integer independent of ℓ.

Tate's algorithm with ReductionSymbol, its component count m and discriminant valuations in every residue characteristic, local minimal discriminant v(Δ_min), Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (i)–(ii), and the Tate curve with its Galois-equivariant uniformisation.
Intersection theory and blowups on regular arithmetic surfaces over a DVR.
Existence and uniqueness of the minimal proper regular model of a curve of positive genus over a DVR, with components and multiplicities of the special fibre.
The different exponent (p − 1)(m + 1) of an Artin–Schreier extension of function fields (Stichtenoth III.7.8), as a cross-check of the local computation.

Clifford theory for a normal subgroup over an arbitrary field (restriction of an irreducible representation to a normal subgroup is semisimple, conjugates of constituents permuted); the baseline declaration TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype covers the semisimplicity half.
Group cohomology H⁰ and H¹ of a finite group with coefficients in a finite-dimensional module, long exact sequence (for the characteristic-two module computations).

hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet: for every finite Galois extension L/K of number fields and every conjugacy class C of Gal(L/K), frobeniusPrimeSet K L C has Dirichlet density #C/#Gal(L/K); with its corollaries (infinitude of each class, invariance under finite symmetric difference).
hasNaturalDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet with value #C/#G, for the natural-density form of Haar-measure Chebotarev (a).

HasDirichletDensity, IsUpperDirichletDensityBound, IsLowerDirichletDensityBound, hasDirichletDensity_of_symmDiff_finite, hasDirichletDensity_of_upperBound_of_lowerBound; monotonicity of upper density and: a set of positive density is not contained in a set of density 0 (equivalently a density-one set meets every set of positive density); finite unions of density-zero sets have density zero (BLGGT Lemma A.1.7).

Uniqueness of the arithmetic Frobenius at an unramified prime in Gal(L/K) (layer 2.2) and its compatibility with restriction to Galois subextensions (layer 2.4), applied to restrictions of Frobenius lifts in G_K.
Schur's lemma for finite-dimensional simple modules over algebraically closed fields and Burnside/density (layers 1 and 3) for absolutely irreducible representations of arbitrary groups.
The algebra Wedderburn presentation B ≅ ∏ M_{m_j}(D_j) of a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra over a field, with centres Z(D_j) and the dimension count.

Brauer group with base change, splitting fields and index of a central simple algebra (the index as the degree of the division algebra in its class); the library already has finite-field triviality, Br(ℝ) and splitting criteria.
Clifford's theorem (single orbit, constant multiplicity) for an irreducible representation restricted to a normal subgroup, applied through the finite quotient Gal(L/F).

Chenevier Theorems 2.12, 2.16 and 2.22 as nodes: (i) reconstruction of a semisimple representation from a determinant over an algebraically closed field; (ii) the structure k[Γ]/ker(D) ≅ ∏ S_i, D = ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i} over an arbitrary field; (iii) over a henselian local ring A, for a Cayley–Hamilton determinant whose residual determinant is split and absolutely irreducible, A[Γ]/CH(D) ≅ M_d(A), together with the uniqueness statement: two representations Γ → GL_d(A) with determinant D are GL_d(A)-conjugate (Skolem–Noether for M_d(A), A local).

Closed-point Chebotarev density for a smooth geometrically connected curve U over F_q, as an exported node: for every open normal subgroup N of π_1(U) and every coset gN the closed points x with Frob_x ∈ gN have positive Dirichlet density (with the constant-field degree congruence recorded), hence the Frobenius elements at closed points of U are dense in π_1(U). DWP.3's stage text owns this construction; its packet currently has only DWP.3/exceptional-frobenius-set-has-density-zero, which uses it.

The étale fundamental group of a connected normal F_q-scheme with Frobenius conjugacy classes at closed points, surjectivity of π_1(U) → π_1(C) for a dense open U of a normal connected C, and lisse ℚ_ℓ/E-sheaves as continuous π_1-representations.

For an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over a base S: [n] finite locally free of rank n^{2g}, étale over S[1/n]; quotient isogenies A → A/G by finite locally free subgroups and quasi-inverses ψφ = [m]; the perfect Weil pairing A[n] × A^∨[n] → μ_n compatible in n, Galois/base-change equivariant; the alternating polarization pairing e^λ_n with its perfectness criterion; and the adjunction e_n(αx, y) = e_n(x, α^∨y). R01.6 builds the Tate-module limits from these.

E[N] ≃+ (ZMod N)² over separably closed fields, the Weil pairing e_N (alternating, nondegenerate, Galois-equivariant, compatible with isogenies via the dual), T_ℓE with its continuous Galois representation and det = cyclotomic character.
frobeniusTrace, the Frobenius isogeny and deg(1 − π_q) = #E(F_q); the Hasse bound a_q² ≤ 4q; supersingular iff p | a_q over a finite field.

The reduction map on points over a DVR and the isomorphism E(K^ur)[ℓ^n] ≅ Ẽ(k̄)[ℓ^n] at good reduction (ℓ ≠ char k); Tate's uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄), Galois-equivariant; and the theorem (ATAEC V.5.3) that an elliptic curve with split multiplicative reduction over a complete discretely valued field is isomorphic over K to a Tate curve E_q.
A nonsplit multiplicative curve is the quadratic twist of a split one by the unramified quadratic character (exists_quadraticTwist_hasSplitMultiplicativeReduction).

At field level: the dual abelian variety A^∨, dual homomorphisms, φ_L : A → A^∨ for line bundles, polarizations and their existence (abelian varieties over a field are projective), and the Rosati involution.
Completions F_v of a number field at finite places and the decomposition-group embedding G_{F_v} → G_F.
Unramified extensions of a local field, the residue correspondence and the arithmetic Frobenius.
Chebotarev density for Frobenius conjugacy classes in finite Galois extensions of number fields.
Spreading out: an abelian variety over a field of finite type over F extends to an abelian scheme over a dense open of a normal F-variety with that function field.

Reconstruction with continuity: (a) over an algebraically closed field k, an n-dimensional continuous determinant on k[Γ] is det∘ρ for a continuous semisimple ρ, unique up to isomorphism (Chenevier Thm 2.12); (b) over a complete local Noetherian A with finite residue field and residually absolutely irreducible D̄, D = det∘ρ for a continuous ρ : Γ → GL_n(A), unique up to GL_n(A)-conjugacy (Chenevier Thm 2.22).

Tate's theorem H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0 for a number field F (continuous cohomology of G_F with discrete torsion coefficients, trivial action), in the form lim_n H^2(G_F, Z/n) = 0 (Serre 1977 Thm 4; Patrikis Thm 2.1.1).

Labelled Hodge–Tate weights HT_τ with the multiset rules for ⊗, dual, Sym^m and ad⁰ (HT_τ(ad⁰ ρ) = {a−b, 0, b−a} for HT_τ(ρ) = {a, b}); Hodge–Tate–Sen weights of arbitrary continuous p-adic representations (Sen theory) with the same rules; and the statement (Patrikis Lemmas 2.2.5, 2.2.7, used by NT26 Lemma 4.7) that the Sen operator of a Hodge–Tate ρ|_{G_{K_v}} lies in Lie(G_ρ) ⊗ K̂_v and has n distinct eigenvalues when ρ is Hodge–Tate regular. If Sen theory is outside R06.2, route it to the PadicHodgeTheory stage that owns it.

Milestones 1–2 for an arbitrary open subgroup U ≤ G of finite index l and arbitrary coefficient groups: the permutation wreath product U^l ⋊ S_l and the transversal-dependent continuous monomial homomorphism Φ : G → U^l ⋊ S_l with its change-of-transversal cocycle (used for tensor induction of representations, not for the F_2 norm).
H^2 of a profinite group with discrete torsion coefficients as the obstruction group for lifting through central extensions with finite kernel, compatible with direct limits of coefficients.
Projective representations, factor sets and the obstruction class in H^2 for finite groups, as the finite-level model of the lifting obstruction.

Symmetric and exterior power representations and the tensor-square decomposition (built: Representation.symmetricPower, Representation.exteriorPower); G7 uses them over arbitrary commutative coefficient rings.
Closed subgroup schemes ↔ Hopf ideals, identity component and component group (geometric), finiteness of π_0 for finite-type groups over a field.

Characteristic 0: a smooth affine group with a faithful semisimple representation has reductive identity component; connected reductive subgroups of GL_2 acting irreducibly are SL_2 or GL_2; derived group.
Lie(G) and Ad for GL_n, GSp, GO and their derived subgroups, compatible with the matrix descriptions gl_n, gsp, sp.
Affine group schemes over Z as representable group functors, to define the semidirect product 𝒢_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j}.

For a finite group G (discrete topology), a subgroup U and a G-module M: corestriction H^i(U, M) → H^i(G, M) with cor ∘ res = multiplication by [G : U]; hence restriction is injective on H¹ when [G : U] is invertible on M, and H¹(G, M) = 0 when #G is invertible on M.
Existence of primes with prescribed Frobenius conjugacy class in a finite Galois extension (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemmas 5.2.4–5.2.6 choose Frobenius elements).
Mackey's irreducibility criterion for representations induced from a normal subgroup of a finite group (irreducibility of Ind ψ for r̄_B).
