gaps.title: Ĝ-pseudocharacters, Ĝ-complete reducibility and Lafforgue's reconstruction
gaps.detail: BHKT Definition 4.1 (Ĝ-pseudocharacters), §3 (Ĝ-completely reducible representations and Ĝ-semisimplification) and Theorem 4.5 (after V. Lafforgue: over an algebraically closed field, Ĝ(k)-conjugacy classes of Ĝ-completely reducible ρ biject with Ĝ-pseudocharacters). No atlas stage plans these; part (ii) of the reductive node (independence of the Ĝ-semisimplified reduction for general Ĝ) rests on them. The GL_n case is closed inside R01.1 without them.

gaps.title: Larsen's lemma on hyperspecial points after a totally ramified extension
gaps.detail: M. Larsen, Maximality of Galois actions for compatible systems, Duke Math. J. 80 (1995), Lemma 2.4, as used in the proof of BHKT Theorem 4.8(ii): there are a totally ramified E′/E and a ρ(Γ)-stable point x ∈ B(DĜ, E) with i_{E,E′}(x) hyperspecial. Not planned by ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 as stated. Not needed for Ĝ = GL_n.

gaps.title: Functional equation of Artin L-functions of number fields with global constants
gaps.detail: Deligne's existence proof (Théorème 4.1 via Lemmes 4.12–4.16) uses, for a Galois extension of number fields and a finite-image complex representation V of Gal(K̄/K) twisted by an idele class quasi-character χ, the meromorphic continuation of L(V, χ) = ∏_v L(V_v ⊗ χ_v), the functional equation L(V, χ) = ε(V, χ)L(V^*, ω_1χ^{-1}) with ε(V, χ) of the form A·e^{Bs}, inductivity ε(Ind V_L, χ) = ε(V_L, χ ∘ N_{L/K}) and additivity (Deligne 3.12 (A)–(D), proved from Brauer induction and Hecke's functional equation), together with idele class characters of prescribed local conductors (Lemme 4.14) and globalisation of local Galois extensions at a non-split place (Lemme 4.13). No atlas stage owns Artin L-functions of number fields (FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 is for function fields; AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1 stops at Hecke characters). Proposed owner: an Artin L-function stage of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors after AL.1.

gaps.title: Local constants outside finite extensions of Q_p
gaps.detail: Deligne's Théorème 4.1 also covers archimedean local fields (W_R, W_C, Deligne 2.2.5 and Lemme 4.4) and local fields of characteristic p. The archimedean Weil groups have no owner in the atlas (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 9 is nonarchimedean; LanglandsParameterStacks LP0 is nonarchimedean), and the equal-characteristic reciprocity isomorphism is excluded from ClassFieldTheory layer 9. FSY's global ε-factor uses the archimedean factor ε_k(∞, s); this node supplies only the finite places.

gaps.title: Ramification filtration over a perfect infinite residue field
gaps.detail: LocalFieldsRamification layer 3 supplies lower and upper numbering, Herbrand's quotient theorem and Hasse–Arf only for IsNonarchimedeanLocalField (finite residue field); AlgebraicCurves layer 8 states explicitly that arbitrary-residue-field completions do not claim that supplier. Missing: the same three results for finite Galois extensions of a complete discretely valued field with perfect (e.g. algebraically closed) residue field (Serre, Local Fields IV–V), which tier (P) of R01.3 — F̄_q((t)) and the completion of K^ur, as requested by FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2 — needs. Tier (F) is closed without it; the Artin–Schreier computation itself uses only the lower filtration. Natural owner: a 'Local fields and ramification, Part II' roadmap (see restructure).

gaps.title: Saito's conductor–discriminant theorem and its inputs
gaps.detail: No roadmap in the atlas plans: (1) ℓ-adic étale cohomology H^i(X_K̄, Q_ℓ), H^i(X_k̄, Q_ℓ) of the fibres of a proper regular curve X over a complete DVR together with the specialisation identity dim H¹(X_k̄) = dim H¹(X_K̄)^{I_K} for the minimal regular model of an elliptic curve (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0 is downstream of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations and cannot be used); (2) Deligne's discriminant Δ_{X/S} of a regular relative curve (via the Mumford isomorphism) and its identification with the minimal Weierstrass discriminant in genus one; (3) Saito's theorem −Art(X/S) = ord Δ_{X/S} (Duke Math. J. 57 (1988), Theorem 1 and Cor. 2; not freely available, statement read in Liu 1994). Consequence: R01.3/ogg-formula is closed for residue characteristic p ≥ 5 by the direct case check and open for p ∈ {2, 3}; EllipticCurveModularity R29.4's exact-conductor comparison at 2 and 3 waits on this gap. Proposed owner: a stage of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties or a new arithmetic-surfaces stage upstream of R01.3 that owns étale cohomology of relative curves over a DVR and Deligne's discriminant.

gaps.title: One-dimensional comparison with class field theory
gaps.detail: ClassFieldTheory layer 7 defines characterConductorExp through unit filtrations; the identity artinMap(U_K^n) ↔ G_K^n (Serre, Local Fields XV §2) that equates it with the Artin conductor of this layer is not stated by any layer; requested from ClassFieldTheory layer 7. The local and global theorems of R01.3 do not need it; only the translation of 𝔣(ψ) into the conductor of a Hecke character does.

gaps.title: Dickinson 2001, Lemma 42 (H¹(SL_2(F_{2^r}), M_2(F)) = 0, r ≥ 2) not read
gaps.detail: Statement (c) is quoted from Dickinson, On the modularity of certain 2-adic Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 109 (2001), through KW II Lemma 4.3(5)(i). The paper was not obtained; the proof sketch reduces it to Ext¹(V, V) = 0 for the natural SL_2(F_0)-module, which still needs a source or a computation.

gaps.title: Automorphisms of PSL_2(F_q) and PGL_2(F_q) (Dieudonné / Steinberg) not read in their own source
gaps.detail: Statement (c) (Aut = PΓL_2) is quoted from NT26, CG20 and BCGNT, which cite Dieudonné, La géométrie des groupes classiques, Ch. IV §6, and Steinberg; those sources were not read and the normaliser of PSL_2(F_q) in Sym(q + 1) is not proved here.

gaps.title: Nekovář's semisimplicity criterion [Nek18, Proposition 3.10]
gaps.detail: BCGP25 Proposition 4.11.1 is a special case of Nekovář, Eichler–Shimura relations and semisimplicity of étale cohomology of quaternionic Shimura varieties, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 51 (2018), Prop. 3.10 (minuscule case (3)); the GL_2 version (Blasius–Rogawski) is used in 4.11.2. The paper is not on arXiv and was not read; no roadmap plans it.

gaps.title: Analytic subsets of compact ℓ-adic Lie groups with empty interior are Haar-null
gaps.detail: Serre 1981 §6.4 (p. 168, citing Bourbaki, Variétés §10.1.2) uses that a closed analytic subset with empty interior of a compact ℓ-adic Lie group has Haar measure 0. The polynomial case on open subgroups of GL_n(ℤ_ℓ) is proved in the node; the general analytic case (needed for images such as GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ) when the condition is not polynomial on GL_n-coordinates, and for Zariski-closed images) has no owner and no library support.

gaps.title: Integral, ℓ-independent characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism on V_ℓA (dimension > 1)
gaps.detail: Milne AV Prop. 10.20 (P_α = det(X − V_ℓα), integer coefficients, independent of ℓ) is planned as AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module, whose own prerequisites (A6 degree theory, A3, A4) do not involve R01.6. But the stage AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6 requires ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6 (only through A6/tate-module-of-a-weil-restriction), so citing it would close a stage cycle. The elliptic case (g = 1) is proved in this layer without A6. Closed by restructure proposal R01.6-RS1.

gaps.title: Freeness of V_ℓA over E ⊗ Q_ℓ for a subfield E ⊆ End⁰(A), and E-characteristic polynomials
gaps.detail: Milne AV Prop. 10.23 (V_ℓA free of rank 2g/[E:Q] over E ⊗ Q_ℓ; trace and norm formulas) is AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/trace-and-degree-on-a-subfield, downstream for the same reason as the previous gap. Closed by R01.6-RS1.

gaps.title: Weierstrass curves as abelian varieties of dimension one
gaps.detail: No packet or Tau Ceti layer located that identifies the projective closure of an elliptic Weierstrass curve W/K with a Tau Ceti AbelianVariety of dimension 1 whose L-points are W⁄L.Point functorially in L. Elliptic statements of this layer avoid it (they use Tau Ceti EllipticCurves directly); only the transfer of abelian-variety statements (isogeny cokernels, local Euler factors) to Weierstrass curves needs it. Natural owner: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer E or AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1.

gaps.title: Mumford–Tate containment of the ℓ-adic images (Richard–Yafaev Theorem 4.9, third clause)
gaps.detail: Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, the Galois finiteness on absolute Hodge classes (Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih I, Prop. 2.9) and the Mumford–Tate group as stabiliser of Hodge tensors (I.3.4) are owned by ShimuraData D1 and AutomorphicBundles B1, which consume this stage (through NeronModels R11.5, ShimuraVarieties V5 and B1), so citing them here closes a stage cycle. The clause U ⊆ M(Ẑ) is therefore not stated in R01.6; restructure proposal R01.6-RS3 plans it at a stage downstream of both owners.

gaps.title: Serre's independence and connectedness theorems: original proofs not read; possibly downstream inputs
gaps.detail: Richard–Yafaev cite Serre, Œuvres IV nos. 133, 135, 136, Serre, Comment. Math. Helv. 88 (2013) §3.1, and Larsen–Pink, Invent. Math. 107 (1992) 6.14; none was read in this pass (not freely located in time). If their proofs for abelian varieties use Faltings' semisimplicity (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4) or Grothendieck's semistable reduction (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3), both of which consume R01.6, parts (1)–(2) must move downstream (restructure R01.6-RS2).

gaps.title: Serre's complement to the specialization of Galois images (Noot Proposition 1.3)
gaps.detail: For each ℓ there is a closed point σ with ρ_{X_η,ℓ}(G_K) = ρ_{X_σ,ℓ}(Gal(F̄/F(σ))). Its proof uses Hilbert irreducibility for compact ℓ-adic Lie quotients (Serre, Lectures on the Mordell–Weil theorem, 10.6), owned by InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, which depends on this stage (IG.2 ← IG.1 ← IG.0 ← SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 … ← NeronModels R11.3 ← R01.6). Restructure proposal R01.6-RS4 plans the complement at IG.2.

gaps.title: Gan–Takeda Lemma 6.1 not read
gaps.detail: BCGP21 proves Lemma 2.1.3 by citing the proof of Gan–Takeda (Ann. of Math. 173 (2011)) Lemma 6.1, not fetched here; the proof sketch given is the standard isotypic-component argument.

gaps.title: Guralnick–Herzig–Taylor–Thorne adequacy theorem (appendix Theorem 9 / Theorem A.9)
gaps.detail: The proof uses Proposition 7 of the appendix, which rests on the classification of finite simple groups (Tau Ceti CFSGStatement states the classification but no layer derives the algebraic-group structure of finite linear groups generated by p-elements in small dimension), and Guralnick's 1999 theorem that small modules have no self-extensions (Ext¹ vanishing for dim W_i + dim W_j ≤ p − 2). Neither input is planned by any roadmap.

gaps.title: Ext¹ computations for SL₂(F_{p^r}) behind GHT17 Corollary 9.4
gaps.detail: Corollary 9.4 uses Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock's Ext¹ computations for SL₂(p^r) (r > 1), [GHT, Cor. 1.4] for r = 1, H²(SL₂(F_q), k) = 0 for q ∉ {4, 9}, and tilting-module computations for q = 4, 9. No library or roadmap plans the modular representation theory of SL₂(F_q).

gaps.title: H¹(SL₂(F_q), Sym^{2i}) = 0 for 2i < p − 3 (Cline–Parshall–Scott Lemma 2.7(c))
gaps.detail: Clozel–Harris–Taylor's proof of Corollary 2.5.4 cites Cline–Parshall–Scott (1975), Lemma 2.7(c), for H¹(U, Sym^{2i})^B = 0; that paper was not obtained in this job, and the printed hypothesis (l > n + 1) is too weak. Darmon–Diamond–Taylor's method (restriction to the Borel and a B-stable filtration) proves the case 2i = 2; the general case needs the weight computation of H¹(U, ·)^B. An exact source statement is still to be read; this job verified the prime-field cases p = 5, 7, 11 by computation (H¹(SL₂(F_p), Sym^a) ≠ 0 only for a = p − 3).

gaps.title: Finite group computations of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni §7.5
gaps.detail: H¹(Sp₄(F_p), 𝔰𝔭₄) = 0 for p = 3, 5, 7 (Lemma 7.5.15), the list of the 11 enormous classes among the 162 conjugacy classes of subgroups of Sp₄(F_3) (§7.5.20) and Lemma 7.5.21(1), (2), (3b), (4) are Magma computations; a formal treatment needs certified enumerations of these finite groups and their cohomology.

gaps.title: Thorne 2024, Lemma 7.3 (adequacy of symmetric powers of large SL₂ images)
gaps.detail: Newton–Thorne quote Thorne, A p-adic approach to the existence of level-raising congruences (Proc. LMS 128, 2024), Lemma 7.3, which was not read; the node gives a proof route through GHT17 Corollary 9.4, which itself rests on the gap above.

sourceIssues.locator: §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 843 (Duke published version); arXiv:1907.08691v1 has the same text in the proof of Theorem 6.13
sourceIssues.printed: The proof cites Proposition 6.8 to attach r_{f_i} : G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′_i}) to the eigenform f_i after a finite extension K′_i/K_i. Proposition 6.8 itself supplies r_f : G_Q → GSp4(K′), explaining via a Baire category argument that the field of definition can be a finite extension of K.
sourceIssues.correction: Add: since r̄ is absolutely irreducible, the G_Q-stable O_{K′}-lattices in r_f form a single homothety class; the similitude character is O_{K′}^×-valued by compactness; the dual lattice for the symplectic form is stable, hence a homothetic translate, so after rescaling the lattice (and the form by ϖ if needed) the form is perfect on it and has a symplectic basis, giving r_f : G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′}).
sourceIssues.reason: Proposition 6.8 is a field-valued statement; the integral GSp4(O) model is an additional step (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/self-dual-lattice-for-absolutely-irreducible-residual). It holds under the standing absolute irreducibility of r̄, so the theorem is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition A.2.1 and its proof, Point 5 and Figure 1, arXiv v1 pp. 30–34
sourceIssues.printed: In the l = 5 case, the source places the projective image of G in a conjugate of PGL2 (F5 ) or of PSL2 (F5 ). For Ḡ equal to PGL2 (F5 ), it cites [CPS75, 2.3 (g)] to claim H 1 (G, gln (Fl )) 6= (0), concluding that G lacks adequacy.
sourceIssues.correction: For l = 5 only the projective image PSL₂(F_5) is excluded: if the image of G in PGL₂(F̄_5) is conjugate to PGL₂(F_5), then G is adequate.
sourceIssues.reason: By Lemmas A.1.3–A.1.4 of the same appendix, G is adequate iff GL₂(F_5) is. GL₂(F_5) has no quotient of order 5, 5 ∤ 2, its semisimple elements span M₂(F_5), and H¹(GL₂(F_5), gl₂) = H¹(GL₂(F_5), F_5) ⊕ H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂) = 0: the first because the abelianisation is F_5^× of order 4; the second by a direct cocycle computation over the Cayley graph of GL₂(F_5) (a direct linear-algebra computation by this job), which gives dim H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂ ⊗ det^j) = 0, 0, 1, 0 for j = 0, 1, 2, 3, and dim H¹ = 1 for SL₂(F_5) and for {g : det g = ±1}. So the class in H¹(SL₂(F_5), sl₂) is moved by the outer action of diag(2,1) (it lives in sl₂ ⊗ det²), and inflation–restriction gives H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂) = H¹(SL₂(F_5), sl₂)^{GL₂/SL₂} = 0. This agrees with the Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock description of Ext¹_{GL₂(F_p)}(1, Sym^{p−3} ⊗ det^b) (nonzero only for b ≡ 1 mod p − 1, while sl₂ = Sym² ⊗ det⁻¹), and with Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3.

[R01.6-RS2] If Serre's independence/connectedness proofs need Faltings' semisimplicity or semistable reduction, move parts (1)–(2) of R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness to a stage downstream of FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4 and NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3 (as REV-PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20 routed Serre's open image), keeping the definitions and Deligne's part (3) here.

[R01.6-RS3] Plan the Mumford–Tate containment of Richard–Yafaev Theorem 4.9 (third clause: after a finite extension the adelic image of an abelian variety over a number field lies in M(Ẑ)) at a stage downstream of ShimuraData D1 and AutomorphicBundles B1, importing R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness and R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety.

[R01.6-RS4] Plan Serre's complement to the specialization of Galois images (Noot Prop. 1.3: for each ℓ a closed point with equal ℓ-adic image) at InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, which owns Hilbert irreducibility and already depends on R01.6; it imports R01.6/noot-specialization.

upstreamNotes: Mathlib's ContRepresentation asks only that each operator be continuous; a jointly continuous variant (or a predicate IsContinuousAction on ContRepresentation) for modules with the module topology would be the natural upstream home of TauCeti.ContinuousRep.

Mathlib's LinearMap.det returns 1 on modules without a finite basis; a determinant for finite projective modules via the top exterior power would remove the free-module restriction in determinant formulas.
Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 9 should expose weilDegree's normalisation lemma (arithmetic Frobenius lifts have degree 1) under a stable name; R01.2's Weil–Deligne relation is stated through it.
Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 could export the ℓ-component t_ℓ and the restriction formula t_K|_{I_L} = e·t_L directly; R01.2/ell-adic-tame-character plans them meanwhile.
The absolute upper filtration G_K^u (constructed in R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor from upperRamificationGroup_quotient) is a natural addition to LocalFieldsRamification layer 3.

Tau Ceti Chebotarev layer 10: consumers need the infinite-extension corollary 'Frobenius lifts at a density-one set of places are dense in G_K'; R01.5/frobenius-density derives it from hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet.
Mathlib's ContRepresentation only makes each operator continuous; T_ℓA is packaged as ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations' ContinuousRep (joint continuity) and maps to ContRepresentation by forgetting.
Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup is Aut(AlgebraicClosure K / K); torsion points prime to char K have coordinates in K^sep, so the action is the Gal(K^sep/K) action transported by restriction.

Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial counts Nat.card of Affine.Point of the reduction (point at infinity included); for good reduction this equals Tau Ceti's pointCount (pointCount_eq_card_point).
